If the CRM integration option is enabled in the mailbox settings, leads or deals are created automatically.
If integration is disabled, an employee with access to the mailbox can manually save an email to CRM.
How to link an email to another deal

To link an email to another deal, an employee needs permission to modify these deals. CRM access permissions can be configured by Bitrix24 administrator and an employee with the access permissions to change CRM settings.
Access Permissions in CRM
1. Open the deal to which the email is bound.
2. Click Open in the timeline next to the email.
3. Click More - Change deal .
If there is no Change deal button, you can't bind the email to another deal. This happens after converting a lead to a deal, since the email is linked to both the deal and the lead.
Who can be responsible for an email in a CRM item form
The person responsible for an email in a CRM item form is the employee responsible for this item. All activities related to the email are automatically assigned to this person.

When an email is saved to a CRM item form, a system entry for the new email appears in the timeline along with a scheduled activity. The avatar of the employee who connected the mailbox is displayed next to this entry. This employee can also change mail integration settings.
Why an email shows a different time in Webmail and CRM
The system may show different times for an email depending on:
- When the email was actually received
- When it was entered into CRM
- When an activity based on the email was created in the CRM item form
When the email was received. In Webmail, open the email. The actual time it was received is shown in the upper right corner.
When the email entered CRM. This time is shown in the item form timeline.
When an activity was created from the email. Scheduled activities use the time when the email entered CRM. If the activity is completed, the completion time is shown.
Why an employee does not see an email in the CRM item form

Only employees with access permissions can view the items to which the email is linked. For example, if an email is linked to a deal and a contact, but the employee does not have access permissions to the contact, he/she will not see the email in the deal form.
Access permissions can be configured by Bitrix24 administrators and employees with the permissions to change CRM settings.
Access Permissions in CRM
How the "Route emails from existing clients to assigned CRM managers" option works
If an email comes from a client already in CRM, you can attach it to the existing form. Use the Route emails from existing clients to assigned CRM managers option.
If a responsible employee for the client is specified in the lead and contact distribution queue, a new email from this client will be added to the existing CRM item form.

If no responsible employee is specified in the distribution queue, each email from this client creates a new lead. This lead will be assigned to one of the responsible employees in the queue. Several CRM item forms for one client with different responsible employees will appear in the CRM.
Why an email is not saved in CRM
Error. When attempting to manually save an email in CRM, an error occurs.
Reason. Incoming or outgoing emails from your Bitrix24 account users cannot be saved in CRM. You can only link emails from clients to CRM.
Why you can't send an email from the deal form
Issue. The email button in the deal form is inactive.
Reason. You can only send an email from a deal to a contact or company linked to that deal. Send emails to email addresses from the CRM item form
Solution. Add a contact or company to the deal from the CRM, or create a new one.
Add a customer from CRM. In the Client field, select a contact or company from the list. Make sure the Email field is completed.
Create a new contact.
1. Click More .
2. Select Email .
3. Click Add in the To field.
4. Select Add new email contact .
5. Enter the customer's name and email.
6. Click Save .
Once done, you can send an email from the deal form. The new contact will be added to the CRM but not linked to the deal automatically. To link them, select the contact in the Client field.
Why responding to an incoming email doesn't complete the activity in the CRM item form
The activity doesn’t close automatically, so you can keep the conversation going if needed.
To complete the activity, choose one of the following options:
- Complete the activity manually if the conversation is finished.
- Create a new activity from the incoming email if you plan to continue working with the client on this topic.
Why duplicate contacts may appear when sending an email from a CRM item form
Duplicates are not created when you send an email to a contact already stored in the CRM, even if the contact isn't linked to the current item.

Duplicates are created when you send an email to an address from the email contacts (marked with a blue icon). In this case, the CRM considers the email address as new and creates a duplicate, even if it already exists in another contact form.
To prevent duplicates from appearing:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Settings .
4. Select CRM settings .
5. Open the Other tab.
6. Click Other Settings .
7. Go to the Activity section.
8. Turn off Allow sending emails to any addresses and click Apply .
Now, emails can only be sent to addresses saved in CRM—new duplicates will no longer appear. Select email recipients in CRM
Why a lead is created in CRM even though lead creation is disabled in the mailbox settings
Issue: A duplicate lead is created from an incoming email, even though lead creation is turned off in the mailbox settings.
Reason: The Enable repeat sales mode option is active in your CRM settings. What are repeat leads and deals in Bitrix24
Solution: Turn off repeat sales in CRM.
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Settings .
4. Select CRM settings .
5. Open the Other tab.
6. Click Other Settings .
7. Turn off Enable repeat sales mode .
8. Turn on Enable legacy lead creation mode .
9. Click Apply .
Once you disable repeat sales, this change applies to all communication channels. For example, if a client with a closed lead calls again, a new lead won’t be created.
Now, repeat leads will no longer be created. If a client already exists in CRM and contacts you again:
- If there’s an active deal with this client, the new inquiry will be linked to it.
- If there’s no active deal, the inquiry will be linked to the closed lead.
How to select a CRM item when manually saving an email

When you manually save an email to CRM, you can’t choose which item it will be linked to. The system automatically links the email based on your mailbox and CRM settings. Manage emails with CRM Mailbox settings

titre: View email headers (RFC headers)
sections: View email headers (RFC headers)

An email message header is a hidden part of an email that shows when it was sent and the mail servers it passed through. Bitrix24 support may request email headers to help resolve issues, such as why an email isn't saved to CRM.
In this article, we'll show you how to view email headers in different mail services:
- Gmail
- Outlook
- iCloud
- Yahoo
- Aol
To view the email header, open the mail service and select an email message.
Gmail . Open a message, click the three dots (...), and select Show original.
Outlook . Open a message, click the three dots (...), and select View > View message source.
iCloud . Open a message, click the three dots (...), and select Show All Headers.
Yahoo . Open a message, click the three dots (...), and select View raw message.
Aol . Open a message, click More, and select View Message Source.

titre: List of supported HTML tags in emails
sections: List of supported HTML tags in emails
In Bitrix24 Mail, you can create email templates with HTML HTML defines the structure of web pages. You can use HTML tags to add and format text, images, tables, and videos in your emails. tags.
Use HTML tags to:
- Customize the appearance of your email (fonts, colors, styles)
- Add elements such as tables, lists, and images (for example, a company logo)
How HTML tags work
HTML tags can be single or paired:

- Single tags use one element (for example,
).
- Paired tags include an opening and a closing tag.
Example:

-

— opens a paragraph.

-

— closes a paragraph.
Tags must be placed inside angle brackets <> .
Some tags include attributes. Attributes define how the tag behaves. They are added inside the opening tag as name/value pairs.
Example:
The tag has an attribute src and alt : . An attribute src specifies the path to the file, and alt shows the name of the image if it fails to load.
Tags for email structure
- <html> – defines the HTML document (attribute: xmlns)
- <head> – contains metadata and styles
- <body> – contains all visible content such as a text, images, and links.
Tags for metadata
- <meta> – stores page information (description, keywords)
- <title> – sets the page title
Tags for styles
- <style> – defines internal styles
- <link> connects external style files (attributes: type, rel, href)
Tags for text formatting
- <a> – creates a link (attributes: href, title, name, style, id, class, shape, coords, alt, target)
- <b> , <strong> – bold text (attributes: style, id, class)
- <i> – italic text (attributes: style, id, class)
- <u> – underlined text (attributes: style, id, class)
- <small> – smaller text (attributes: style, id, class)
- <big> – larger text (attributes: style, id, class)

-
– line break (attributes: style, id, class)
- <blockquote> – quoted text (attributes: title, style, id, class)
Tags for structure and grouping
- <div> – groups content blocks (attributes: title, style, id, class, align)
- <span> – formats inline text (attributes: title, style, id, class, align)

-

– creates a paragraph (attributes: style, id, class, align)
Tags to create lists
- <ul> – unordered list (attributes: style, id, class)
- <ol> – ordered list (attributes: style, id, class)
- <li> – list item (attributes: style, id, class)
Tags for tables
- <table> – creates a table (attributes: border, width, style, id, class, cellspacing, cellpadding)
- <tr> – table row (attributes: align, valign, style, id, class)
- <td> – table cell (attributes: width, height, style, id, class, align, valign, colspan, rowspan, bgcolor)
- <th> – table header (attributes: width, height, style, id, class, colspan, rowspan)
- <thead> , <tbody> , <tfoot> – table sections (attributes: align, valign, style, id, class)
Tags for images
- – inserts an image (attributes: src, alt, height, width, title)
Tags for code and advanced formatting
- <code> – formats code (attributes: style, id, class)
- <del> – shows deleted text (attributes: style, id, class)
- <ins> – shows inserted text (attributes: style, id, class)
- <map> – defines clickable areas in an image (attributes: shape, coords, href, alt, title, style, id, class, name)
- <php> – inserts PHP code (attributes: id)
This is the full list of supported HTML tags. Other tags are not supported in Bitrix24 Mail.
To use HTML in your email:
1. Go to Webmail .
2. Click New message .
3. Select HTML .
4. Add your tags and send the email.
In brief
- HTML tags define the structure and formatting of email content.
- Use them to customize layout and add elements like images or tables.
- Only the supported tags listed above work in Bitrix24 Mail.

titre: Add calendar open slots to email
sections: Add calendar open slots to email
Calendar slots lets you create a link to your schedule with available meeting times. Send this link to external users so they can book a convenient time.
Open slots in Bitrix24 calendar
You can automatically add a link to your available time slots when you send emails. This makes it easier to schedule meetings with clients, partners, and counterparties.
Create and send a schedule link
To add a calendar link to an email:
1. Open the email form.
2. Click Time slots .
The recipient can open the link and choose an available meeting time.
Recipients cannot see:
- Meeting names
- Participant names
- Other event details
Disable calendar access for external users
1. Go to the Calendar section.
2. Disable the Open slots option.
If you enable this option again later, Bitrix24 creates a new link automatically. Previous links stop working.
In brief
- Slots are available time periods in your calendar for meetings and appointments.
- You can send a link to your available slots by email.
- Recipients can choose a convenient meeting time from the available slots.
- Recipients cannot view meeting names, participants, or other calendar events.

titre: Track link clicks in outgoing emails
sections: Track link clicks in outgoing emails
You can track when customers click links in emails sent from CRM or marketing campaigns.
To turn on link tracking, open Settings in your Bitrix24 account.
Go to Other settings > Email messages and turn on Track link clicks in outgoing emails .
Use link tracking to analyze your sales and marketing data. You can see which message works best and which offers get customers’ attention.

Sales. After you turn on link tracking, you can automate sales with a trigger. For example, you send a customer an email with a product offer and a link to an order form. When the customer clicks the link, the deal moves to the stage where the trigger is set.

Let’s say your CRM has five stages: Start > Link click > Call > Invoice > Finish. Add a trigger to the second stage. When the customer clicks the link, the deal moves to this stage. This means the customer is interested in the product, and it is time to call them.
You can add a trigger in the Automation section.
Click the plus button, then select Customer communication > Track link clicks .
Configure the trigger and click Save .
Create automation rules and triggers
Marketing. After you turn on link tracking in your Bitrix24 account settings, go to Marketing > Settings .
Open the More tab and turn on Track email reads and link clicks .
You can now track how many people clicked links in your email.
To view conversion statistics, open the Campaigns page.
In brief
- You can track customer clicks on links in emails sent from CRM or marketing campaigns.
- Link tracking is available in CRM and Marketing.
- Conversion tracking in CRM and Marketing works only if link tracking is turned on in your Bitrix24 account settings.
- Use link tracking to analyze sales and marketing data. You can see which message works best and which offers get customers’ attention.

titre: Save an email as an EML file
sections: Save an email as an EML file
If you experience email issues in Bitrix24, our support team may ask you to send the message as an EML file.
This helps us investigate issues like:
- The email won't open
- Attachments are missing
- The email appears differently in Bitrix24 compared to your email provider
An EML file is a saved copy of an email. It includes:
- Message content
- Sender and recipient details
- Subject
- Date
- Attachments
Learn how to save an EML file in common email services:
- Yahoo!
- Gmail
- Outlook
- iCloud
If your email provider is not listed here or does not support the EML format, use Thunderbird as a universal option.
Yahoo!
Open the email in your mailbox.
1. Click Three dots (...) on the right side of the top toolbar.
2. Select View raw message . The message opens in a new window.
3. Right-click and select Save as . The file is saved in TXT format.
Gmail
Open the email in your mailbox.
1. Click Three dots to the right of the email.
2. Select Download message . The email is saved automatically in EML format.
Outlook
Open your mailbox in the web version or the desktop app.
Web version
1. Right-click the email.
2. Click Download .
3. Select Download as EML . The email is saved automatically in EML format.
Desktop app (new Outlook)
1. Right-click the email.
2. Click Save as .
3. Select Save as EML . The email is saved automatically in EML format.
Some older versions of Outlook do not support EML files. In this case, save the email in MSG format and send it to Support instead.
Save an email as MSG in an older version of Outlook
1. Open your mailbox and select the email.
2. Click File in the top-left corner.
3. Select Save as .
4. Save the file.
iCloud
Open the email in your mailbox.
1. Click Three dots (...) in the bottom-right corner.
2. Select Download Message . The email is saved automatically in EML format.
Thunderbird
If your email service does not support EML files, connect your email account to Outlook or Thunderbird. Both apps allow you to save emails in this format.
To save an email as an EML file in Thunderbird:
1. Open the app and select the email.
2. Click More in the top-right corner.
3. Select Save as .
Save the email in EML format or in a similar format, such as MSG, and send the file to Bitrix24 Support. This helps us resolve the issue faster.

titre: Increase the daily limit for sending emails
sections: Increase the daily limit for sending emails

To protect email recipients from spam, email services put limits on the number of emails per day. If you send a lot of emails that don't meet the sender requirements, the limit may be lowered. In this case, you will get a notification in Bitrix24.
To increase the limit, contact the email service support. Once you agree on a new limit with them, adjust it in Bitrix24.
Check the email service requirements . For example, here are the rules for Gmail .
Contact the email service support . Explain your situation to the support team and agree on a new limit.
Set the limit in Bitrix24 . After the email service increases the limit, adjust it in Bitrix24.
1. Go to the Webmail section.
2. Click Settings (⚙️) in the top right corner.
3. Select Mailbox settings .
4. Check the box next to Set daily email limit .
5. Specify how many emails can be sent per day from this mailbox.
In brief
- To protect email recipients from spam, email services put limits on the number of emails per day.
- To increase the limit, read the email service requirements and contact their support.
- After the email service increases the limit, adjust it in Bitrix24.

titre: Tasks in Bitrix24
sections: Tasks in Bitrix24
Task is workspace for managing team work, from simple assignments to large projects. Team members can discuss details in the task chat, share files, and record work results in one place.

Tasks help managers track progress, manage deadlines, and assign responsibilities. For example, a supervisor can create a task called “Run an advertising campaign” and specify the goal, deadline, and responsible employees. The marketer and designer can collaborate in the task chat, share updates, and attach materials. The supervisor can monitor progress without additional meetings or messages.
Simplify task management

Tasks in Bitrix24 include tools that help teams stay organized and complete work on time. Managers can track progress, employees can clearly see their responsibilities, and important information stays in one place instead of getting lost in chats or emails. Create a task
Checklist . Create a checklist to break a task into steps. You can add subitems, assign responsible employees, and attach files.
Tags . Use predefined tags or create your own to organize tasks by topic. Tags help you filter tasks and quickly find the information you need. Tags in tasks and projects
Reminders . Set reminders to receive notifications or email messages to help employees stay on schedule.
Time tracking . Start a timer when you begin working on a task. Time tracking option

Task status summary . Task participants can leave updates and record work results for colleagues, including the assignee, creator, and observers. You can add a summary when creating or editing a task. Record the work result in tasks

Templates . Use templates for recurring work. A template can include the task structure, roles, deadlines, and files. For example, you can create templates for reports or contract approvals. Templates help employees quickly create tasks and follow a standard workflow. Task templates
Search for tasks
Bitrix24 includes filters that help you quickly find tasks.
- Search field : Search by keywords or phrases in the task name or description.
- Roles : Filter tasks by role, such as ongoing, assisting, creating, or following.
- Filters : Use predefined filters or create custom ones, such as Pending , In progress , Pending review , Completed , or Deferred .
Task views
Bitrix24 includes five task views.
- List : View all tasks in one place. Sort tasks by different criteria and track recent updates.
- Deadline : See how much time remains before task deadlines.
- Planner : Organize tasks by deadline, priority, status, and other criteria.
- Calendar : Track deadlines and review workload across different time periods.
- Gantt : View tasks on a timeline to understand schedules and task duration.
List view in tasks Deadline view in Tasks Planner view in Tasks Calendar view in Tasks Gantt chart
Automation
Use automation rules and triggers to automatically create tasks, add participants, and track deadlines. Automation rules and triggers in tasks
Access permissions

Configure access permissions to control which actions employees can perform on tasks, templates, and automation rules. You can create custom roles and assign them to employees or groups. Tasks: Access permissions
Tasks in other Bitrix24 tools

Tasks in Bitrix24 integrate with other tools across the product. For example, you can turn a chat message into a task in a few clicks. The message text becomes the task description, the recipient becomes the assignee, and chat participants become observers.
Collaboration . Create tasks from Messenger, Calendar, Feed, groups, and projects. Convert Feed post into a task Create a task or an event from a message

CRM . Tasks in CRM help teams work together across departments. For example, the Sales department can create a task for the legal team to prepare client documents. Sales managers can track task statuses directly in the kanban view without opening the CRM item. Tasks in CRM
In brief
- Tasks in Bitrix24 help teams organize work and manage projects.
- You can track progress, manage deadlines, and assign responsibilities.
- Tasks include tools for structuring work and organizing information.
- Bitrix24 includes five task views: List , Deadline , Planner , Calendar , and Gantt .
- You can automate tasks with automation rules and triggers.
- Tasks integrate with other Bitrix24 tools, including Chat, Calendar, Feed, groups, and projects.

titre: Working with tasks
sections: Working with tasks
After you create a task, the next steps depend on your role. This article explains how to work with tasks on the web and in the mobile app.
- For assignees
- For creators
Work with a task as an assignee
Open the task by clicking its name. Review the description and deadlines to understand the scope of work.
Check whether the task has the High Priority label in the upper-right corner. This helps you identify tasks that need immediate attention.
If you manage a department, you can delegate the task to another employee to balance the workload.
Click Start to begin working on the task. If time tracking is enabled, click Start time tracker instead. Time tracking option in tasks
You can pause the task or postpone it if you need to continue later.
If the task includes a checklist, mark items as complete as you finish them. You can also add new checklist items if needed.
Use comments to discuss task-related questions. You can also use these communication options:
- Open chat : Create a separate chat for the task. By default, the chat name uses the format Task: *task name* .
- Start video call : Create a chat with all task participants and start a video call.
- Post to Feed : Create a Feed post based on the task. All task participants receive the post.
- Create event : Schedule a meeting for the task. Add the location, date, and time. All task participants receive an invitation.
Set reminders so you do not miss important deadlines. Task reminders
When you finish the task, add the results in the comments and click Finish .
If the task requires a status summary, select a comment and mark it as the task summary.
Open the task in the mobile app. Review the description and deadlines to understand the scope of work.
Check whether the task has the High Priority label in the upper-right corner. This helps you identify tasks that need immediate attention.
If you manage a department, you can delegate the task to another employee to balance the workload.
Tap Start to begin working on the task. This helps task participants quickly see the current status.
If you want to continue the task later, tap the three-dot menu (...) and select Pause .
If the task includes a checklist, mark items as complete as you finish them. You can also add new checklist items if needed.
Open the Comments section to discuss task-related questions.
When you finish the task, add the results in the comments and complete the task.
If the task requires a status summary, tap and hold a comment, then mark it as the task summary.
Work with a task as a creator
As the task creator, you can track progress and update the task when needed. For example, you can add more details or invite additional participants.
Enable the Check task upon completion option so the task moves to the Pending review status after the assignee finishes it. The task stays open until you review the result.
After the review, you can either accept the task or return it for revisions.
You can also leave feedback for the assignee. Choose a positive or negative rating, or leave the task unrated.
As the task creator, you can track progress and update the task when needed. For example, you can add participants or attach files.
Enable the Require task review on close option in the task settings. After the assignee completes the task, it moves to the Pending review status and stays open until you review it.
After the review, tap Approve to accept the task as completed, or tap the X icon to send it back for revision.

titre: New task form
sections: New task form
Teams now discuss work directly in chats more often. They coordinate tasks, plan next steps, and capture decisions there.

We redesigned tasks in Bitrix24 to match this workflow. A task is no longer just a form with fields and comments. It is now a single workspace for discussions, actions, and results. Task chat is now the main place for communication and process management. Teams can call each other, share files, and make decisions without losing context or switching tools.
We also redesigned the task form for this new way of working, where communication is the main way work gets done. Here is what changed and how it helps your team move faster.
New task form: everything in one place

The task form is now cleaner and easier to use. Information is grouped into sections such as description, participants, files, checklists, results, and more. This layout helps you quickly understand the task, review important details, and focus on the work.
The form now includes a built-in chat that keeps the full discussion context. You can review recent changes, start a call, clarify details, and make decisions without leaving the task. Chats in tasks
Benefits of the new task form:
- Create tasks faster. Add only the fields you need, such as a description, deadline, assignee, and checklist. Other sections stay hidden, so the form stays compact and easy to use.
- Use the same layout when creating and viewing tasks. The form looks the same in both cases, so you spend less time searching for fields.

- Communicate and make decisions faster. The task chat makes collaboration easier. Your team can discuss issues the same way they do in a messenger. Feedback comes faster, decisions happen sooner, and work keeps moving.

- Work with files together. Each task now has a dedicated area for documents. All participants can attach and view files there. Nothing gets lost, and you can quickly find and open any document right in the task. If you need a quick discussion, send the file to the task chat.

- Keep deadlines under control. By default, new tasks get a deadline five business days from the creation date, so nothing gets missed. The creator can also choose who can change the deadline and under what conditions, such as blocking postponements or requiring a reason.

- Track results and progress. The task now includes a dedicated Results section. You can add the final result and interim milestones during the work. This helps supervisors and teammates track progress and give feedback quickly.
To quickly find the chat for a specific task, use the search bar.
- Click the search bar above the chat list and start typing the task name. As you type, matching results will appear in the task chat list.
- Select the desired chat from the search results.
Chats in tasks

Task chat is now the center of communication. Your team can discuss work, review results, see changes, and keep the full history of interactions in one place. Because the chat works like a familiar messenger, it makes task work faster and easier. Everything happens in one window, so there is no need to switch between tools.
In the task chat, you can:
- Discuss details. Talk with teammates directly inside the task instead of switching to separate chats or tabs. Ask questions, get answers, and agree on decisions in real time.

- Start calls. Launch audio or video calls right from the task chat to discuss issues and make decisions quickly. After the call, CoPilot Follow-Up creates a transcript and a short summary. CoPilot Follow-Up: AI-powered speech analytics for video calls
- Track changes. Every update appears in the chat, including deadline changes and status updates. This makes it easy to see what changed and where the task stands.
- Highlight important information. Pin key messages or add them to Favorites so you can return to them quickly.
- Keep context. The full history of discussions, actions, and calls stays in one place, so your team always has the latest information.
Comments from the previous task form are available in the chat in read-only mode.
All task chats in one list
We added a new Task Chats section. It is more than a list of chats. It is a simple way to communicate and manage tasks directly from Messenger.
- Work in a familiar messenger layout. The list of task chats with the latest messages appears on the left, and the selected chat opens on the right.
- Reply faster. Discuss tasks directly in chat. New messages appear in the list right away, so you do not need to open every task to check for updates.

- Find the right task quickly. All active tasks you participate in are collected in one list. Chats with new messages move to the top, just like in a messenger, so you can quickly see where your attention is needed.
- Monitor progress. Assignees can track updates, supervisors can follow many discussions at once, and observers can stay informed about changes.
You can open the task chat list in Tasks and Projects > Task Chats and in Messenger > Task Chats. To open the task itself, click the link in the chat header.
Counters and notifications: stay on top of changes
The new notification system combines task counters and chat notifications. It helps you track important events such as new messages, deadline changes, completed checklist items, and more.
When something changes in a task:
1. A new message appears in the task chat, and you get a notification like in a messenger. A counter also appears in the chat list.
2. A counter appears in the Tasks and Projects section to show where there are unread updates.
How to track changes:
1. Watch the counters in Tasks and Projects or in Messenger on the Tasks tab. They show the total number of new events and highlight tasks with updates.
2. Open the task chat list to review new messages and changes in order.
Each participant receives notifications and counters based on their role:
- Assignees and co-assignees get notifications for all changes in their tasks.
- Creators get notifications for key events, such as task completion, checklist completion, or a result being added.
- Observers get notifications about status changes, such as when a task is created or completed.
If someone is mentioned in the chat, they also get a notification and see a counter.

The new task experience is more than an update. It is a new way to work. Everything you need to complete a task is now in one place. Task chat is now the center of task management, where your team discusses details, makes decisions, and tracks changes in real time. Work moves faster, and Bitrix24 helps you bring tasks to completion.

titre: Create a subtask
sections: Create a subtask

Subtasks are useful when you need to keep a close eye on complex tasks. You can break them down into simpler tasks and assign them to different users, making the whole process more flexible and effective.
Here are some ways you can add a subtask:
- When viewing a task, click on More and select Create subtask .
- Or, click Add in the top right corner and choose Create subtask .
- When creating or editing a task, click More and find Subtask of section. Then click Add and select the main task that this will be a subtask of.
- In the task list, click the menu button (≡) and select Create subtask .
- If you're using the Gantt chart, open the task menu and click Create subtask .
There are two additional features you can use when working with subtasks.

- Sometimes, it might be helpful to set the start and end dates for the main task based on the subtasks' dates. To do this, while creating or editing a task, click Options and enable the Derive task dates from subtask dates option. This means the main task will start on the earliest date out of all the subtasks and end on the latest date out of all the subtasks.

- You might want the main task to automatically be marked as complete when all its subtasks are done. To do this, while creating or editing a task, click Options and enable the Auto complete task when all subtasks are completed (and vice versa) option.
If you don't use this option, the subtasks will become separate tasks once the main task is completed.
To add a subtask in the Bitrix24 mobile app, open a task and tap Subtasks . Select an existing task or create a new one.

titre: Quick task creation form
sections: Quick task creation form

Bitrix24 now features a form for quick task creation. You can fill in only the essential information, such as the title, description, and deadline. This is convenient when you need to set a task without extra details.
Go to the Tasks and Projects section and click Create .
Fill in the task fields.
Task name — it will be displayed in the task list. Description — specify what the employee needs to do. Important — click the flame icon to mark the task as important.

Assignee — select the employee who will perform the task. Deadline — specify when the task should be completed. Choose a date from the calendar or select a preset option: today, tomorrow, late this week, in a week, late this month.
Files — attach an image or a document from your computer or Bitrix24 Drive.
Checklists — create a list of steps to complete the task.
Project — add the task to a workgroup or a project.
Once you have filled in the necessary fields, click Create . To access additional task settings, click Detailed form .
Hotkeys that will help you quickly create a task:
- Tab - switch between fields: title > description > performer and so on.
- Enter - open the menu. For example, the Deadline field will open a calendar with date selection.
- Esc - close the task form without saving.
- Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter for Mac) - set task.
In brief

- Bitrix24 now features a form for quick task creation. You can fill in only the essential information, such as the title, description, and deadline. This is convenient when you need to set a task without extra details.
- Go to the Tasks and Projects section and click Create . Fill in the task fields.
- To access additional task settings, click Detailed form .

titre: Limits in tasks on the free plan
sections: Limits in tasks on the free plan
Free plan users can create 100 tasks. The total number includes tasks with all statuses: in progress, completed, deferred, almost overdue.
Some options will become unavailable when you create 101 tasks. You will not be able to:
- Add participants and observers
- Delegate tasks
- Enable Task status summary option
- Use regular tasks and templates with subtasks
- View Supervising and efficiency pages
- Configure access permissions in workgroups and projects
The task limits will be marked with a padlock.

titre: Import tasks
sections: Import tasks
You can move tasks to Bitrix24 from another service using a CSV file. Export your tasks to CSV and upload the file.
To start the import:
1. Go to Tasks and Projects and open Tasks .
2. Click the gear icon on the right.
3. Select Import list .
4. Click From CSV .
The Import Tasks page opens. Scroll down and download the template file to prepare your data.
Make sure the date format in your CSV file matches your Bitrix24 settings. Check it in Account settings > Other settings > Date format .
Upload your CSV file in the Data file (CSV format) field. Then configure these settings:
- Data file encoding : Select the correct encoding. If you are not sure, use Auto-Detect .
- Default task author : Choose who will be listed as the task creator.
- Default assignee : Choose who will be responsible for the tasks.
- Name format : Select how names appear.
- Column separator : Choose the delimiter used in your file.
First row is a header : Specify if the first row contains column names.
Skip empty columns : Ignore empty columns if needed.
Click Next and map the fields.
Review the results. If there are no errors, click Done .
Your task list is now available in Bitrix24.

titre: Group actions with tasks
sections: Group actions with tasks
When you have a lot of tasks for your team, you may need to apply the same action to many of them at once. This is where using group actions can save you time.
Here's how to use group actions:
1. Select tasks by ticking them in the list.
2. Scroll down to the group action tab and click Select action .
3. A drop-down list will appear with different actions you can choose from:
- Ping
- Complete
- Set deadline
- Move deadline forward or backward
- Disable check upon completion
- Change assignee or creator
- Add observer or participant
- Mute or unmute
- Add to favorites or remove from favorites
- Set group (project)
- Delete
1. Specify the additional parameters, if any, and click Apply .
2. Then click Continue to proceed.
To apply an action to all tasks selected by the filter, use the For all option.
- Delete several CRM entities or tasks at once
- Working with tasks

titre: Employee Workload Planning
sections: Employee Workload Planning
Besides Involvement section, you can use Task Reports to track time spent on tasks.
You can estimate how much time should be spent on a task and after its completion, compare that to how much time has actually been spent.
Employee Resource Tracking report shows how long it took for each employee to complete resource tracking enabled tasks. The report can be broken down by projects.
When creating or editing a task, click the Task planned time checkbox and put in an estimated amount of time for the task.

If you'd like to make some modifications to the Employee Resource Tracking report, please Copy report first. Your modifications will be saved as report copy, when default reports will stay in the original format.
The report wizard will show Employee Resource Tracking report conditions which can be modified. Use Add option to add tasks fields to the report columns.
Please note that your employees should use Start time tracker option when working on tasks in order for the time spent on task to be calculated.

titre: Create a task
sections: Create a task

Tasks in Bitrix24 provide a unified space to organize team work: assign tasks and manage projects. The task form allows you to track employee progress, monitor deadlines, distribute responsibilities, and discuss work in the chat.
In this article:
- Create a task
- Fill in the main parameters
- Add participants
- Use additional task features
Go to the Tasks and Projects section > Tasks and click Create. A mini task form will open.
Bitrix24 offers two ways to create a task:

- Short form . Use it for quick and simple assignments. It includes only the essentials: title, description, assignee, and deadline. You can also add files, a checklist, and link it to a project if needed. Quick task creation form
- Detailed form . It is suitable for tasks requiring additional parameters, such as adding observers, participants, and setting reminders.
Follow these three steps to create a detailed task:
1. Fill in the main parameters. Start by specifying the title, description, and deadline.

Title. This is the first thing the assignee sees in the task list. The title should clearly indicate what needs to be done. If you revisit the task a week later, the title alone should be enough to recall its purpose without reading the description.

Description. Briefly provide context and the expected result: what to do, why, and in what format the outcome is needed. Use CoPilot to structure the text, refine wording, or turn the description into a checklist if necessary. CoPilot in Tasks
Deadline and task settings. Specify the date and time by which the task should be completed. You can choose a preset option or select a date from the calendar.
Click Settings (⚙️) next to the deadline to enable additional parameters for monitoring results and deadlines:

- Require approval upon completion — once the assignee completes the task, it will return to the creator for review. The creator can accept the result or send it back for revision. If the creator and assignee are the same person, the task will not return for review. Administrators, the creator’s supervisor, and the assignee’s supervisor can also complete and accept the task.

- Set default deadline for all new tasks — a default deadline, such as five business days, will be applied to each new task. This helps avoid forgetting deadlines and eliminates the need to fill in the field manually.
- Assignee can change deadline — the assignee can reschedule the task’s completion date. You can also configure a reason request for changes and limit the deadline changes by date or frequency.
- Skip weekends — if the deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the task will be due on the next business day according to the company’s schedule.

- Auto complete task when all subtasks are completed, and vice versa — when all subtasks are completed, the main task will automatically close. Similarly, completing the main task will close all its subtasks in Bitrix24.
2. Add participants. Tasks can include several roles, indicating who performs the work, who assists, and who monitors the results.
- Creator — assigns the task and reviews the result. By default, this is the person creating the task.
- Assignee — responsible for completing the task. Each task has one assignee. If multiple assignees are specified, Bitrix24 creates separate tasks for each, and the creator sees them as linked tasks.
- Participants — collaborate with the assignee to complete the task.
- Observers — monitor the task’s progress, view comments and files, but do not perform the work.
To specify Participants and Observers in a task, select the parameters in the lower block with additional options.
3. Use additional features. The full task form includes tools to structure work, keep materials organized, and monitor results.
- Task status summaries — record the outcome in a separate block to avoid losing it in comments and quickly verify task completion. Task status summary option
- Files — attach documents, images, and other materials. All participants work with the latest version, and changes sync with Bitrix24 Drive. New task form
- Checklists — break the task into steps, add sub-items, assign responsibilities, and attach files. Checklists help track progress and ensure nothing is missed. Checklists in tasks
- Projects — link the task to a workgroup or project to keep related tasks and materials in one place. Working with tasks in projects
- Participants and observers — add employees who assist with the task or need to monitor its progress. Participants perform part of the work, while observers see the entire progress.

- Flow — use department flows to automatically distribute similar tasks among employees, reducing the supervisor’s workload. For example, all "Contract review" tasks are sent to the legal department’s flow and distributed automatically. Bitrix24 Flows: Get started
- Tags — group tasks by topics and quickly filter them in the list. Tags in tasks and projects

- Reminders — set reminders for the assignee, creator, or participants to ensure tasks are completed on time. For example, a manager can set a reminder three hours before the deadline to prepare a report. Task reminders

- CRM items — link tasks to deals, leads, contacts, and companies to unify department work. For instance, a sales manager can assign a task to accounting to "Prepare an invoice" and link it to a specific deal. Work with tasks in CRM

- Parent task — use this if the task is part of a larger process. The parent task helps see the context and connections. For example, the task "Prepare a promotion" may include subtasks like design, legal review, and campaign preparation.

- Subtasks — create separate tasks within the main one for independent work stages. For example, in the task "Organize an event," you can create subtasks like "Book a venue," "Prepare the program," and "Gather participants." Create a subtask

- Linked tasks — connect tasks to show when the next work stage should begin. This helps visualize dependencies. For example, the task "Launch an ad campaign" is linked to "Prepare banners." Additional task features
- Gantt — add dependencies between tasks on the Gantt chart to plan projects. For example, website development starts only after the design is approved. Gantt chart
- Deadline planning — specify the start date and duration, and Bitrix24 will calculate the completion date automatically.
- Time tracking — record time spent on tasks automatically or manually. This helps see the team’s actual workload and plan resources more accurately. Time tracking option in tasks
- Custom fields — add your own fields to adapt tasks to your company’s processes. For example, the procurement department can add fields like "Purchase number" or "Vendor." Custom fields for tasks

Use only the tools needed for a specific task. You can add others later. Once everything is set up, click Create . The task will appear in the list, and communication about it will continue in the chat.
In the Bitrix24 mobile app, you can create a task in a few steps. It is convenient for quickly recording assignments without using a computer. Go to the Tasks tab. Tap + to create a new task.
Enter the task title and a brief description to clarify what needs to be done. Select the assignee and set a deadline: today, tomorrow, the end of the week, or choose a date from the calendar.
If needed, use additional task features to add:
- Project — link the task to the appropriate workgroup or project to include it in the team’s tasks.
- Flow — send the task to a department flow for automatic distribution among employees.
- Files — attach documents and images from the gallery, "My files," or Bitrix24 Drive.
- Checklists — break the task into steps and mark completed items.
- Participants and observers — add those assisting with the task or monitoring its progress.
- Tags — label the task for easier filtering in the list.
- Custom fields — fill in additional fields configured for tasks in your company.
- CRM items — link the task to a specific deal, lead, contact, or company.
- Time tracking — enable time tracking or planning if monitoring effort is important.
- Deadline planning — set the start date, end date, and task duration.
Once all parameters are set, tap the arrow icon. The task will appear in the list.
To set task execution and control rules, open the task and tap Three dots (…) > Additional settings . Here, you can enable parameters like:
- Require task status summary . Assignee will have to add a status summary to mark the task as completed.
- Require approval upon completion . After completion, the task will be sent to the creator for review. The owner can accept the result or return the task for revision.
- Allow deadline changes . The assignee can reschedule the deadline without approval. Use this if flexible deadlines are acceptable.
- Skip weekends . The deadline will automatically shift if it falls on a weekend or holiday.
In brief
- Tasks in Bitrix24 help record assignments, distribute roles, and monitor deadlines in one place.
- You can create tasks in a quick or detailed form.
- Tasks include a title, description, assignee, and deadline, with options for control and requiring results before completion.
- Additional task features like checklists, tags, time tracking, and deadline planning help keep materials organized and monitor progress.
- The Bitrix24 mobile app allows you to quickly create tasks, configure parameters, and use additional features.

titre: Limitations in tasks on the Free plan
sections: Limitations in tasks on the Free plan

You can work with tasks in Bitrix24 on any plan, but the free plan has some limitations. Some restrictions apply immediately, such as the inability to enable time tracking in tasks. Additional limits come into effect after creating 100 tasks.
In the first 100 tasks on the free plan, you can:
- Add a task participant or observer
- Delegate a task
- Use the Control task after completion option to approve work on time or send it back for revision
- Make tasks recurring — they will be created automatically on a schedule
- Create templates with subtasks
- Track subordinate tasks in the Supervise section to assess team workload and monitor deadlines
- View task statistics in the Efficiency section: how many tasks are in progress, completed, or overdue

Starting from the 101st task, these features become unavailable. They will be marked with a lock icon in the interface. Restrictions apply only to new tasks, while previously created tasks retain all functionalities. The limit includes the total number of tasks and subtasks created. Deleting old tasks will not restore access to these features.

If you plan to actively use recurring tasks or control tools, keep in mind the 100-task limit on the free plan. To work without restrictions, switch to a commercial Bitrix24 plan. Bitrix24 plans and pricing

titre: Search and filters in Tasks
sections: Search and filters in Tasks

In Bitrix24 tasks, smart search and filters help you quickly sort tasks by assignees, statuses, deadlines, and other parameters. For example, you can select all important tasks or view the ones you assigned.
In this article:
- Use search in tasks
- Work with filters by roles and statuses
- Create custom filters
- Search for favorite tasks
Using search in tasks

Smart search helps you quickly find the task you need. Enter a word or part of a word in the search field. Bitrix24 will display matching tasks. For example, if there is a task titled "Prepare sales report for March," you can type "report", "sales", or part of a word like "sale" to see tasks containing this text in their titles or descriptions.
Working with filters by roles and statuses

Tasks include standard filters for roles and statuses. These filters help you quickly find tasks without manually configuring them. For instance, you can view tasks you are working on or have assigned.
Role filter displays tasks based on your role in them. Select the appropriate role:
- Ongoing — you are the assignee.
- Assisting — you are a participant.
- Set by me — you are the creator.
- Following — you are an observer.
- All roles — any of the above roles.
Status filter helps you view tasks at different stages. Select the desired task status:
- In progress — tasks waiting to be done, being worked on, awaiting review, or postponed.
- Completed — tasks that are finished and closed.
- Deferred — tasks temporarily on hold.
- Overdue — tasks with "Waiting to be done" or "In progress" statuses that have passed their deadlines.
- Almost overdue — tasks with "Waiting to be done" or "In progress" statuses whose deadlines are tomorrow.

By default, the filter shows only tasks where you are involved as an assignee, participant, creator, or observer. To view tasks of other employees, select the Task parameters field and check the box next to Show tasks I don't participate in :
- Bitrix24 administrator — views all tasks.
- Supervisor — views tasks of their subordinates and those they have access to.
- Employee — views tasks they have access to, such as tasks in groups and projects they participate in.
Tasks: Access permissions
Creating custom filters
Frequently used filters can be saved to avoid configuring them repeatedly. For example, you can create a filter for tasks of a specific employee completed during the current week.

1. Click Filter + Search. 2. Select the required fields and specify their values. If the field you need is not listed, click Add field and select the ones you want to use. 3. Click Save filter. 4. Enter a filter name and click Save.

To make filters available to all employees, the Bitrix24 administrator can set them as public. Employees can use these filters but cannot modify or delete them. To do this, click Settings (⚙️) > Apply for all users.
Searching for favorite tasks
Tasks you have added to favorites can be found using a special filter.
1. Click Filter + Search. 2. In the Task parameters field, check the box next to In favorites. 3. Click Search.
In brief
- Bitrix24 tasks include smart search and filters to quickly sort tasks by assignees, statuses, deadlines, and other parameters.
- Smart search helps you find tasks by a word or part of a word in their titles or descriptions.
- Bitrix24 tasks have standard filters for roles and statuses.
- If standard filters are insufficient, create custom ones and save them for future use.
- Tasks added to favorites can be found using the Task parameters > In favorites filter.

titre: Delete multiple CRM entities or tasks at once
sections: Delete multiple CRM entities or tasks at once
When dealing with lots of tasks, it is important to stay organized and clear out information that is no longer needed. You can quickly delete old tasks and CRM data using group actions.
There are two main types of data you might want to delete:
- Tasks . These could be tasks from workflows, dismissed employees' tasks, or tasks that were imported from other systems.
- CRM entities . These could be deals that have been completed or were just for testing, leads that have already been converted, and so on.
Delete multiple tasks at once
Go to the Tasks and Projects section and do the following:
1. Open Tasks and switch to the List view.
2. Select the tasks you want to delete.
3. Click Select Action and choose Delete .
4. Then click Apply .
If you have tasks assigned to dismissed employees, you can either reassign those tasks to other users or close them. If these tasks are just old and not useful, you can delete them.
To delete a dismissed user's tasks,
1. Go to Company and open the Employees tab.
2. Use the Dismissed persons filter to find the employee.
3. Open the dismissed employee profile page and click Tasks .
4. Switch to the List view, select no longer needed tasks, and delete them.
See these topics to learn more:
- Dismiss users
- Delegate the dismissed user's tasks
- Reassign CRM entities from dismissed users
Delete multiple CRM entities at once
Consider the following example of removing multiple CRM entities.
1. Let's say you want to remove some test deals. Go to CRM and open Deals .
2. Switch to the List view and filter your test deals.
3. Then select the test deals you want to remove and delete them.
Read also:
- Search for CRM items using a filter
- CRM Recycle Bin
- Task recycle bin

titre: Configure access permissions in tasks
sections: Configure access permissions in tasks

In Bitrix24 tasks, an employee can be a creator, an assignee, a participant, or an observer. These roles define involvement in a specific task but do not restrict access to changes. If all employees have full access, they can modify or delete tasks, which may lead to errors and delays in work.
Access permissions determine who can edit tasks and templates and who can only assign and complete tasks. This helps avoid accidental changes and maintain order in work.

By default, access permissions can be configured by the Bitrix24 administrator, but they can delegate this right to other employees. To configure permissions, go to Tasks and Projects > More > Access Permissions .
In this article:
- Select standard roles
- Create and configure custom roles
- Set up access permissions
- Assign roles to employees
Select standard roles
Task access permissions include three roles with predefined rights:

- Full access — by default, this role is assigned only to the Bitrix24 administrator, but they can delegate it to other employees. A user with this role can perform any actions with tasks and manage access permissions.

- Supervisor — this role is automatically assigned to department heads in the company structure. They can manage department tasks but cannot configure roles and access permissions. Supervisors always see their subordinates' tasks, even if this right is disabled in the settings.
- Manager — this role is automatically assigned to all employees. Users work only with their tasks and cannot see colleagues' tasks.
Create and configure custom roles
If standard roles do not meet your needs, you can copy, edit, or create new ones.
Create a new role . You can create a role from scratch to configure access permissions for your company's processes.
1. Click Create role and specify its name. 2. Configure the required permissions using the toggles. 3. Click Save .
Copy a role . This helps create a new role with similar permissions without setting it up from scratch.
1. Click Clone role and select the desired role from the list. 2. Specify the name of the new role. 3. Configure access permissions and click Save .
Configure access permissions
In each role's settings, you can define permissions for various tools in the Tasks and Projects section.
Tasks — permissions define what employees can do with tasks.
Permissions for assignees:
- Edit task — change the title, description, deadlines, and other task parameters. Supervisors can always edit their subordinates' tasks, even if this right is disabled in the settings.

- Delegate task — assign them to another employee. Supervisors can always delegate tasks to their subordinates. In other cases, delegation is possible only if the user has the right to assign tasks to those employees.
- Add participant — include additional participants in a task. This requires the right to assign tasks to the selected employee.

- Change assignee — assign another employee. By default, you can select someone from your department. To assign a supervisor or an employee from another department, you need the right to assign tasks to them.
- Edit checklist— modify and delete checklist items. Marking items as completed is possible regardless of this setting.
- Add new checklist items — add new items and edit your own. You cannot modify items added by others.
Permissions for creators:
- Edit completed task — modify a task after the assignee has completed it.
- Delete task — delete tasks created by the employee.
Permissions within your department:
- Assign task to own department's employees — assign tasks to colleagues within the department.
- Assign task to own department's head — assign tasks to the supervisor.
- View all tasks in own department — see tasks of employees and the supervisor. This permission applies to all departments where the user works.
- Edit available tasks in own department— edit department tasks available for viewing.
- Edit available completed tasks in own department — modify completed department tasks available for viewing.
- Delete available tasks in own department — delete department tasks available for viewing.
Permissions for other departments:
- Assign task to other departments' heads — assign tasks to supervisors of other departments.
- Assign task to other departments' employees — assign tasks to employees of other departments.
- View all tasks in other departments — see tasks of employees in other departments without participating in them.
- Edit available tasks in other departments — modify tasks in other departments available for viewing.
- Edit available completed tasks in other departments — modify completed tasks in other departments available for viewing.
- Delete available tasks in other departments — delete tasks of colleagues in other departments available for viewing.
General permissions:
- Export accessible tasks — export a list of accessible tasks to a file.
- Import tasks — upload tasks to Bitrix24 from a file.
Task templates — permissions define what employees can do with templates. This helps maintain a unified work standard and protect templates from accidental changes. Task templates
- Create task templates — create new templates with the required settings.
- View all templates in your department — see templates created by department employees.
- View all templates in other departments — see templates of colleagues in other departments.
- Edit templates in your department — modify templates of colleagues in your department.
- Edit templates in other departments — modify templates in other departments available for viewing.
- Delete templates with access — delete templates available for viewing.

Flows — used to collect similar tasks from different employees in one place. Access permissions settings define who can create new flows, usually supervisors or employees responsible for organizing processes. Bitrix24 Flows: getting started

Automation rules — automate actions in personal tasks, such as sending notifications or creating tasks. By default, any employee can configure automation rules, but this permission can be restricted if necessary. This helps avoid confusion and unnecessary automated actions in tasks. Automation rules and triggers: how to automate task management
Access permissions — define who can modify task access settings. By default, this is available only to the Bitrix24 administrator, but they can delegate this right to other employees.
Assign roles to employees
Click the Plus (+) icon next to the role name. Choose who to assign this role to:
- Recent — displays employees, departments, and groups you have searched for in any Bitrix24 section.
- Groups — predefined user groups that cannot be modified, such as Supervisors, Deputies, etc.
- My groups — select a group or project.
- Employees and departments — select a user or department from the company structure.
- Search — find any employee by entering their name in the search bar.
Summary
- Access permissions define who can manage tasks, templates, flows, and automation rules, and who can only assign and complete tasks.
- By default, access permissions can be configured by the Bitrix24 administrator, but they can delegate this right to other employees.
- Separate task access permissions apply in groups and projects.
- By default, there are three roles in the permissions settings: Full access, Supervisor, and Manager.
- If standard roles do not meet your needs, you can copy, edit, or create new ones.
- If a user has multiple roles with different permission levels, the one granting more capabilities applies.

titre: Work with subtasks
sections: Work with subtasks
If a task is large and consists of several stages, you can divide it into subtasks in Bitrix24. This structure helps distribute work among employees, monitor each step, and see the overall result.
The main task to which subtasks are linked is called the parent task. It unites all related tasks and shows the overall project progress.
Create a subtask
You can create a subtask in Bitrix24 on both the desktop and mobile app.
In the desktop version of Bitrix24, there are two ways to create a subtask.

Add a subtask within the parent task . Subtasks help structure work: each team or employee is responsible for their stage, while the overall result is recorded in the parent task. Specify the main project goal in the parent task and assign an employee responsible for the final result.

1. Open or create a new task that will serve as the parent task. 2. Click Subtasks . 3. Use the search to find one or more tasks to make subtasks or create new ones. 4. All subtasks will appear in the parent task form.
Specify the parent task within the subtask . Each subtask can have only one parent task.
1. Open or create a task that should become a subtask. 2. Click the Parent task button. 3. Use the search to find and select the required task. 4. The parent task will appear in the subtask form.

To automatically close tasks and subtasks, enable the "Auto complete task when all subtasks are completed, and vice versa" option. When all subtasks are completed, Bitrix24 will close the parent task. If you complete the parent task, all related subtasks will also be completed.
In the mobile app, you can create a subtask only within the parent task. Open the parent task, click Subtasks in the carousel menu, and select or create a new one.
Unlink a subtask from the parent task
If a subtask is no longer related to the main project, you can make it independent. This can be done from the parent task form or the subtask form.
In the subtask form , find the Parent task section and click Remove (x) next to the task.
In the parent task form , find the Subtasks section and click Remove (x) next to the required subtask.
In brief
- If a task is large and consists of several stages, you can divide it into subtasks in Bitrix24. This structure helps distribute work among employees, monitor each step, and see the overall result.
- You can create a subtask in Bitrix24 on both the desktop and mobile app.
- To create a subtask, add it to an existing parent task or select a parent task in the form of an already created task.
- Each subtask can have only one parent task.

- Enable the "Auto complete task when all subtasks are completed, and vice versa" option to let Bitrix24 close the parent task when all subtasks are completed. If you complete the parent task, all related subtasks will also be completed.

titre: Custom fields for tasks
sections: Custom fields for tasks
Custom fields let you add task details specific to your company’s workflow. Use them to capture information that is not available in the default task form.
Create a custom field
1. Open the task creation form.
2. Expand Custom fields .
3. Click Add field .
4. Select the field type.
Field types
- String — enter short text, such as notes or labels.
- Number — enter numeric values, such as amounts, prices, or quantities.
- Date/Time — select a date and time, such as a deadline or scheduled event.
- True/False — choose Yes or No .
Field options
You can configure additional settings for each field:
- Required — users must complete the field before they can create the task. If a required field is empty, the system displays a warning.
- Multiple — allows users to add more than one value in the same field.
If a field is required, users must complete it before saving the task. Required fields are marked with a red indicator in the form.
If the Multiple option is enabled, users can enter several values in the same field by clicking Add .
Configure custom fields
Click Settings (⚙️) next to a custom field to manage how it behaves.
Available options:
- Apply field set to all users – makes the custom field available to everyone in your company. If other users customized their task forms, their settings will be replaced.
- Enable field dragging – lets users reorder custom fields using drag and drop.
Learn more about feature availability on the Bitrix24 pricing page. Bitrix24 plans and pricing

titre: CoPilot in Tasks
sections: CoPilot in Tasks

CoPilot, your AI assistant, is available in tasks. It helps you save time when creating tasks for employees. Describe what needs to be done, and CoPilot will generate a clear task description and create a checklist automatically.
Without CoPilot, you need to:
- Write a detailed task description manually.
- Create a checklist to make sure nothing is missed.
- Read and reply to all comments while keeping track of the full context.
With CoPilot, you can:
- Generate a clear task description and split it into steps.
- Create a checklist automatically.
- Analyze comments, highlight key points, and suggest a reply.
Get started with CoPilot in Tasks
You can open CoPilot below the task description field or in comments. To do this, click CoPilot or press the space bar. To work with part of the text, select it and click CoPilot .
Create a task with CoPilot

Add basic information about the task, and let CoPilot expand it and define the required steps. You do not need to worry about typos or complicated wording. CoPilot will improve the text automatically.
Click CoPilot and enter your prompt.

To create a task, use our pre-prompts Pre-prompts are ready-made prompts for CoPilot. They use simple language, but include several requests in one prompt to help CoPilot generate the expected result. . They are grouped by purpose:
Improve task description . Continue the task description, rewrite it in simpler language, create a checklist, or add encouraging wording for employees.
Analyze text . Summarize the text, identify pros and cons, and clarify unclear points.
Modify text . Fix mistakes, simplify the text, translate it into another language, or add emojis.
Change tone of text . Rewrite the text in a more polite or formal style.
Create a checklist with CoPilot

The main advantage of CoPilot in tasks is the ability to create checklists in one click. You do not need to organize the information manually or worry about missing important details. Add the main task information, and CoPilot will generate the checklist automatically.
Click Checklist in the bottom-right corner.
Create your own prompts for CoPilot
In addition to pre-prompts, you can create your own prompts for CoPilot from scratch.
Clearly describe the expected result in your prompt. This helps CoPilot generate more accurate and relevant content.
For example, here is a message from a manager in a team chat:
Here are two example prompts you can use to create a task from this message:
- What needs to be done?
- Explain in detail what needs to be done. Suggest a dress code for the themed event. Create a checklist for the task.
In the first example, CoPilot generates only the basic task information.
In the second example, the result is more detailed because the prompt includes additional instructions.
Add as many details as possible to get better results.
Use CoPilot in task chats

In a task chat, you can interact with CoPilot to ask questions, discuss ideas, or request a summary of the conversation. CoPilot helps you quickly understand the context, suggest ideas, and support discussions directly in the chat.
1. In the message field, type @ and select CoPilot. 2. Enter your question or request, for example: "Summarize the discussion".
CoPilot replies directly in the chat. All task participants can see the response.
In brief
- CoPilot is an AI assistant available in tasks. Describe what needs to be done, and CoPilot will generate a clear task description and checklist automatically.
- The main advantage of CoPilot in tasks is one-click checklist creation. You do not need to organize information manually or worry about missing important details.
- You do not need to learn prompt engineering to use CoPilot. Bitrix24 includes ready-made pre-prompts to help you quickly create tasks and comments.
- You can improve the generated text step by step until you are satisfied with the result. Use pre-prompts or create your own prompts to add more details.

titre: Task features
sections: Task features

Tasks in Bitrix24 help you plan work, assign responsibility, and track deadlines. To create a clear task, add a title, description, and assignee. You can also add stages, attach files, or link the task to a project. This helps the team stay aligned and avoid missed details.

For example, when preparing a marketing campaign, create a task, set the description and deadline, attach materials, and add a checklist. The team can then follow the plan and track progress for each step.
In this article:
- Set a deadline
- Attach files and documents
- Mark a task as important
- Add a checklist
- Set reminders
- Enable time tracking
- Record results
Set a deadline

Deadlines help team members plan their work and understand when tasks are due. In advanced settings, you can control how deadlines work. For example, you can allow or restrict changes, set default deadlines for new tasks, or require review before completion.
Click Settings (⚙️) next to the deadline and enable the necessary options.
Check task upon completion . When the assignee completes the task, it goes to the creator for review. The creator can approve the result or send the task back for revision. Check task upon completion
Set default deadline for all new tasks . Define how many days after creation a task should be due. This applies automatically to new tasks. Use this if your team often works with the same timelines.
Assignee can change deadline . Allow the assignee to update the due date. You can add controls:
- Require a reason for the change
- Limit how many times or how far the deadline can move
Skip weekends . If a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the system moves it to the next workday.
Auto complete task when all subtasks are completed, and vice versa . When all subtasks are complete, the main task closes automatically. Completing the main task also completes all subtasks.
Attach files and documents

Use tasks to store all related materials, such as documents, instructions, or files. For example, in a “Review contract” task, attach the file so teammates can open it directly from the task. This keeps everyone working with the latest version.

Click Files to upload documents or create a new one. Any participant can add files. Files created in Bitrix24 sync with Drive and projects. Changes update everywhere automatically. You can also share files with teammates or external users. Online Documents: Getting Started
Mark a task as important
Mark a task as important when it needs extra attention. For example, urgent updates or time-sensitive requests.
Click the priority icon to highlight the task. It will stand out in the list so assignees can prioritize it. To view only important tasks, use the Priority filter.
Add a checklist
Checklists break a task into smaller steps and help track progress. They show what is done and what is still pending.
- Step-by-step work. For example, updating a website: collect data, edit content, update images, and review results.
- Dividing work among team members. For example, preparing a workspace: set up equipment, grant access, and prepare documents.
Click Checklists and add items. Checklists in tasks
Set reminders
Reminders help you stay on schedule and avoid missed steps. You can set reminders for each participant. Task reminders
For assignees, reminders show when to start or return to work. For creators, they signal when to review results.
Enable time tracking for a task
Use time tracking to record how long work takes. Start the timer when you begin work and pause it when needed.
All time entries save automatically in the task. This helps track effort and review team performance.
Click Time tracking and set the planned time. You can then compare planned and actual time. Time tracking in tasks
Record results
Results capture the outcome of a task in one place. The assignee can add a summary, attach files, or describe the work completed.
If Task status summary is enabled, the assignee must add a result before closing the task. This ensures clear documentation and simplifies review.
You can add results in the task form or in the chat by marking a message as a result. Task status summary
In brief
- Tasks include tools to plan work and track progress.
- You can control deadlines, including restrictions and default settings.
- Tasks store all related files and documents.
- Important tasks stand out with priority markers.
- Checklists break work into clear steps.
- Reminders help keep work on track.
- Time tracking records actual effort.
- Results keep outcomes organized in one place.

titre: Recycle bin in tasks
sections: Recycle bin in tasks

In Bitrix24, deleted tasks are first moved to the recycle bin, where they are stored for 30 days. If a task was deleted by mistake and contains important discussions or files. You can recover it along with the chat history. If the task is no longer needed, it can be permanently deleted from the recycle bin. After 30 days, tasks are automatically removed.
In this article:
- Find deleted tasks
- Restore or permanently delete tasks from the recycle bin.
Find deleted tasks
Each user can only see the tasks they deleted. A Bitrix24 administrator can view deleted tasks of all employees.

1. Go to Tasks and projects > More > Recycle bin . A list of tasks will appear, showing who deleted them and when. 2. To quickly find specific tasks, click Filter + Search . You can search tasks by name or filter them by various parameters, such as the deletion date. 3. If you are a Bitrix24 administrator, you can find deleted tasks of a specific employee using the filter: add the User field and select the desired person.
Recover or delete tasks from the recycle bin
Each user can only restore or delete tasks they deleted. A Bitrix24 administrator can recover or delete tasks of all employees.
1. Go to Tasks and projects > More > Recycle bin. 2. Select one or more tasks and choose the desired action: recover or delete. 3. Confirm the action.
In brief
- In Bitrix24, deleted tasks are first moved to the recycle bin.
- Tasks can be restored or permanently deleted from the recycle bin within 30 days. After that, they are automatically removed.
- Deleted tasks can be found in Tasks and projects > More > Recycle bin.
- Each user can see only the tasks they deleted.
- A Bitrix24 administrator can view deleted tasks of all employees.
- Tasks deleted from the recycle bin cannot be recovered.

titre: Tags in tasks and projects
sections: Tags in tasks and projects
Tags are labels that help group tasks and quickly find the ones you need. They are useful when managing multiple parallel tasks and need to quickly navigate a topic or type of work.
In this article:
- Add tags when creating and editing tasks
- Use tags in projects
- Edit and delete tags
- Search and filter tasks by tags
Adding tags to tasks
1. Go to the Tasks and Projects > Tasks .
2. Create a new task or open an existing one.
3. Click Tags . Select the desired tag from the list or start typing a name to create a new one.
The tag will then appear in the task form.
Tags can also be created in the task description. If you include a word with the # symbol, such as #Contract , Bitrix24 will recognize it as a tag and add it to the general list.
If an incorrect tag is added to a task, you can remove it. Select the tag in the block and delete it.
1. Go to the Tasks tab.
2. Create a new task or open an existing one.
3. Tap Tags . Select the desired tag from the list and tap Select .
