1. To create a new tag, enter the name and tap ➕.
2. Select the new tag from the list and tap Select .
The tags will then appear in the task form.
To remove a tag from a task, tap the tag block, uncheck the unnecessary tag, and tap Select .
How tags work in projects
If a task belongs to a project and you add a tag to it, the tag becomes a group tag—accessible to all project members. This is convenient when tasks are united by a common theme, direction, or stage.
Key principles:
- Tags created within a project are available to all project members.
- Tags created in personal tasks are not displayed in projects.
- If a task is added to a project, its tags are retained—missing tags are automatically added to the project.
- If a task is moved from one project to another, missing tags are transferred to the new project.
Editing and deleting tags

Editing and deleting tags is only available in the web version of Bitrix24. To rename or delete a tag, open the task, click ➕ in the tag block, and select View tags . Choose a tag from the list, click Menu (≡) , and select Rename or Delete .
Filtering tasks by tags
1. In the task list, open the filter, add the Tag field.
2. Select the tags, and click Search . The list will display tasks containing the selected tags.

You can also search for tasks by tags in the task list. Add a tag field: open Settings (⚙️) , check Tags , and click Apply . Then, click the tag name in the list — the filter will be applied automatically.
You can find tasks with the tag using the search bar in tasks.
In brief
- Tags help group tasks and quickly find the ones you need.
- You can add tags when creating or editing a task in Bitrix24 on both desktop and mobile apps.
- In projects, tags become group tags — accessible to all project members.
- Tags can only be edited or deleted in the web version. Personal tags can only be modified by their owner.
- You can search for tasks by tags using the filter in the web version or the search bar in the mobile app.

titre: Checklists in tasks
sections: Checklists in tasks
Checklists help break a task into clear steps, assign responsibility, and monitor progress. This is especially useful for large tasks or those involving multiple employees.

For example, when preparing a marketing campaign, you can create a checklist with items like defining goals, gathering content, launching ads, and analyzing results. This makes it easier for the assignee to plan their work and for the supervisor to track what has been completed and what is still in progress.
You can create multiple checklists within a single task and use them as mini-plans.
- Сreate a checklist
- How it works
Creating a checklist
You can create a checklist in a task using Bitrix24 on both desktop and mobile apps. This can be done in a new task or an existing one.
By default, only the task creator can create and edit checklists. An administrator or an employee with task management permissions can grant these rights to the assignee. Task access permissions
1. Open the task form and click Checklists.
2. Enter a checklist name. This makes it easier to find if there are multiple checklists.
3. Add items. Each item represents a separate action, such as preparing files, verifying calculations, or approving text.
4. Customize items by placing the cursor on the desired line and selecting an action:
- mark the checklist item as important
- attach a file
- set the nesting level of the item. For example, item 2 can include sub-items 2.1, 2.2, and so on. There is no limit to the number of levels
- assign participants and observers to individual checklist items or the entire list
Save your changes.
1. Open the task form and click Checklists.
2. Enter a checklist name. This makes it easier to find if there are multiple checklists.
3. Add items. Each item represents a separate action, such as preparing files, verifying calculations, or approving text.
4. Customize checklist items by tapping the desired line and selecting an action:
- mark the checklist item as important
- attach a file
- set the nesting level of the item. For example, item 2 can include sub-items 2.1, 2.2, and so on. There is no limit to the number of levels
- assign participants and observers to individual checklist items or the entire list
Save your changes.
How it works
You can create multiple checklists within a single task, delete unnecessary items, mark completed ones, and hide those no longer needed.
Add an additional checklist. If multiple employees are working on a task, divide actions into separate lists.
Reorder checklist items. To change the order of items, hold and move them to the desired position.
Adjust item visibility. If there are many items, you can hide completed ones to avoid distractions. This helps focus on what is still in progress.
Click Three dots (...) > Hide completed items . You can always bring back completed items to the checklist later.
Edit items. You can modify multiple items at once. Click Three dots (...) > Group actions . Check the boxes next to the items and select the desired action.
Delete items. You can delete items or the entire checklist. To delete an item, place the cursor next to its name and click the bin icon.
To delete a checklist, click Three dots (...) > Delete.
Add an additional checklist. If multiple employees are working on a task, divide actions into separate lists.
Click Add checklist .
Adjust checklist visibility. If there are many items, you can hide completed ones to avoid distractions and leave only those where you are responsible.
Click Three dots (...) and select the desired action.
Delete items. You can delete items or the entire checklist. To delete the entire checklist, click Three dots (...) > Delete , and to delete an item, highlight the desired line and click the bin icon.
In brief
- Checklists help break tasks into clear steps, assign responsibility, and monitor progress.
- You can create multiple checklists within a single task and use them as mini-plans.
- By default, only the task creator can create and edit checklists.
- You can create a checklist in a task using Bitrix24 on both desktop and mobile apps. This can be done in a new task or an existing one.
- To create a checklist, open the desired task and click Checklists .
- You can create multiple checklists within a single task, delete unnecessary items, mark completed ones, and hide those no longer needed.

titre: Export tasks from Bitrix24
sections: Export tasks from Bitrix24
You can export tasks from Bitrix24 to an .xls file. This is useful when you need to save a task list as a separate file, create a report, or share task data with someone who does not use Bitrix24.
By default, all employees can export tasks. A Bitrix24 administrator can limit this permission in the access settings.
Prepare tasks for export
Before you export, set up the task list and fields so the file includes only the tasks and data you need.
Configure the task list.

1. Go to Tasks and open the List view. 2. Click Filter + Search and enter search parameters or apply a preset filter. For example, to export only tasks that are in progress, click In progress . 3. Click Search . Search and filters in Tasks
Configure task fields.
If you want to export specific task data, such as the modified date or assignee, add those fields to the list first.
1. Click Settings (⚙️) in the top-left corner of the table, next to the column headers. 2. Select the fields you want to add. 3. Click Apply .
Export tasks
1. Open Settings (⚙️) > Export to Microsoft Excel . 2. Choose which task fields to include in the file:
- Only fields in list — exports only the fields currently shown in the task list
- All task fields — exports all fields from the task card.
3. Click Run . Export time depends on the number of tasks. 4. Click Download export file to save the spreadsheet to your computer.
In brief
- Go to Tasks and open the List view.
- If needed, filter the tasks you want to export and choose which fields appear in the table.
- In the top-right corner, open Settings (⚙️) > Export list to Microsoft Excel .
- Choose which task fields to export: only the fields shown in the list, or all fields.
- Click Run .
- When the export is ready, click Download export file .

titre: Recurring tasks
sections: Recurring tasks
Recurring tasks let you automate repeat work. Bitrix24 creates tasks on a schedule, so you don’t have to set them up manually each time.

Set up the task once. Add the title, description, assignee, and schedule. Bitrix24 will generate new tasks based on these settings. For example, an accountant can get a “Submit reports” task every month. A marketer can get a weekly reminder to review campaigns.
Recurring tasks are based on templates. You can update or pause a template at any time.
In this article:
- Create a recurring task
- Set up task recurrence
- Edit or stop a recurring task
- Manage recurring tasks
Create a recurring task
To make a task recurring, create or edit a template:
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > Templates .
2. Open an existing template or click Create .
3. Fill in the main fields such as title, description, assignee, and deadline.
4. Add optional items like files, checklists, or reminders.
5. Turn on Recurring task at the bottom of the form.
A block with recurrence settings will appear.
Set up task recurrence
Use recurrence settings to control when and how Bitrix24 creates new tasks.
Create tasks by template Choose how often Bitrix24 should create tasks:
- Daily: Use this for tasks you handle every day, such as reviewing reports or checking inventory.
- Weekly: Pick specific days of the week. For example, create a task every Tuesday or Friday.
- Monthly: Choose a date or a weekday, such as the 15th or the second Monday. This works well for reports or invoices.
- Yearly: Set a specific date or pattern for annual tasks like audits or renewals.
Recurrence start Defines when Bitrix24 begins creating tasks. By default, tasks start right after you save the settings. You can select a different start date if needed.
Recurrence stop Controls when task creation ends. Choose one of these options:
- Exact date: Stop on a specific date.
- After ... runs: Stop after a set number of tasks.
- Manually: Keep creating tasks until you turn off recurrence.
Create new task at Choose when new tasks appear. By default, Bitrix24 creates tasks at the start of the workday based on your account settings.

Create tasks on weekends and holidays Decide what happens if a task falls on a non-working day. By default, Bitrix24 creates the task on that day. To move it to the next workday, select No . This option is available only for the Daily recurrence period.
When you finish, click Save.
Edit or stop a recurring task
You can update or turn off recurrence at any time.
The following users can change recurrence settings:
- Template creator: The person who creates the template.
- Bitrix24 administrator: Has administrative rights to manage templates.
- Users with Full access to the template: Can view, edit, and manage the template fully.

Users with view-only access cannot edit the template. To allow editing, enable permissions to edit templates in the Tasks and Projects section for their department or others. Tasks: Access permissions
To update or remove recurrence:
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > Templates .
2. Use the filter and select Recurring .
3. Open the template you need.
4. Click the recurrence rule to update the settings.
5. To remove recurrence, click the Cross icon next to it.
After you save changes, Bitrix24 will create new tasks using the updated settings. If you remove recurrence, Bitrix24 will stop creating new tasks.
Manage recurring tasks
After you set up a template, you can track recurring tasks and control access.
View task history
Open the History section to see all tasks created from the template. This helps you check when the last task was created and confirm that recurrence works as expected.
Manage access permissions
Control who can view, edit, or delete the template.
The following users can edit the template:
- Template creator: The person who creates the template.
- Bitrix24 administrator: Has administrative rights to manage templates.
- Users with full access to the template: Can view, edit, and manage the template fully.
- Users with permission to edit templates for their department or other departments: Can edit templates in the Tasks and Projects section.
Users with view-only access can open the template but cannot change it. Task templates
In brief
- Recurring tasks create assignments automatically on a schedule: daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
- Tasks are based on a template, so you set them up once.
- You can define the start date, creation time, and end conditions.
- You can pause or update recurrence in the template. New tasks will follow the updated settings.
- The template stores a history of created tasks.
- Access permissions control who can view, edit, or delete the template.

titre: Task reminders
sections: Task reminders
Task reminders in Bitrix24 help you stay on top of important work stages. They notify you when to start a task, request information, monitor results, and close the task.
For example, an assignee can set a reminder two days before the deadline to return to the task on time, while the creator can set one day before to assess progress.
- Add a reminder
- View and edit reminders
Adding a reminder to a task
Any participant can add a reminder for themselves or colleagues — the assignee, creator, or participants. This can be done when creating or editing a task.
1. Go to the Tasks and Projects section.
2. Open the task form or create a new one.
3. Choose who will receive the reminder: the assignee, creator, participants, or yourself.
4. Specify when to send the reminder:
- On a specific date — set the day and time for the notification.
- Before the deadline — define how much time before the deadline the reminder should be sent.
Select the type of notification the user will receive:
- A notification in Bitrix24.
- An email.
Click Save .
Viewing and editing reminders

All reminders set by an employee are collected in a separate block within the task and are visible only to them. If a reminder is set for another participant, the colleague will not see it in their list but will receive the notification.
1. Click the Reminders block to open the list.
2. Hover over the desired reminder and click to delete it.
3. Click the Reminders block to open the list.
4. Click Add reminder if you want to add another entry. There is no limit to the number of reminders.
In brief
- Task reminders in Bitrix24 help you stay on top of important work stages. They notify you when to start a task, request information, monitor results, and close the task.
- Any participant can set a reminder for themselves or colleagues: on a specific date or a set time before the deadline.
- Notifications are available in Bitrix24 or via email.
- To add a reminder, go to the Tasks and Projects section, open the required task or create a new one. Click the Reminders button, set the parameters, and click Save .
- All reminders set by an employee are saved in the task form. Click the Reminders block to expand the list, edit, delete, or add a new reminder.

titre: Communication in Bitrix24 Tasks
sections: Communication in Bitrix24 Tasks

When a team works on a task, information often gets scattered. Questions happen in direct messages. Files are shared in chats or saved to a drive. Approvals happen over email. This makes it hard for a new team member to catch up. They need to search through different chats and files to find the full picture. As a result, it is often unclear what decisions were made and what stage the task is in.

In Bitrix24, all task-related work stays in one place. Discussions, calls, meetings, and files are all connected to the task. You can also communicate with clients, contractors, and other external participants right inside the task. Nothing gets lost. Your team can quickly find the information they need, and supervisors can review the task history and current status at any time.
Task discussions: a chat for the whole team

The task chat is the main space for communication and task updates. It stores participant messages and system notifications about changes. The chat history shows what decisions were made and where the work stands. New participants can get up to speed quickly, supervisors can check status at any time, and the team always has the latest information.
In the task chat, you can:
- Ask questions and clarify details during the work.
- Add participants to the task.
- Mention colleagues so they get notified right away and can respond faster.
- Attach files such as documents, mockups, and spreadsheets. Everything stays in one place.
- Track activity, such as who changed the deadline, updated the status, or added a message.
- Pin important messages and save them to Favorites for quick access later.

For example, a manager reviews website copy with a copywriter and designer. All edits and versions are discussed in the task chat. When a client asks for an update, no one has to piece the history together from memory. Everything is already in the chat.

External participants . You can invite external participants to the task chat, such as clients, contractors, or freelancers. A guest gets access only to that task. They can view the discussion, post in the chat, and track updates through email notifications. They cannot access any other company data.

For example, a design agency is building a website for a client. The client is added to the task as a guest. They can review the discussion, leave comments in the chat, and receive email notifications. Client communication and internal team discussion stay in one place.

AI in the chat . CoPilot is available in the task chat. Type @ and select it from the list. You can ask it to summarize the discussion, suggest ideas, or answer a question. The reply appears directly in the chat and is visible to all participants.

Task chats . If you work with many tasks, you can track all discussions in the Task chats section. It works much like Messenger. On the left, you see a list of tasks with the latest messages. On the right, you see the chat for the selected task. Tasks with new messages and comments move to the top, so you can quickly spot updates and see where a reply is needed.
This is useful for:
- Supervisors who need to review updates across many tasks
- Assignees who want to track all task updates in one place
- Observers who need to stay informed about changes
You can open the task chats list in Tasks and projects > Task chats or Messenger > Task chats
Notifications and counters for new messages
Each task participant gets notifications based on their role. New messages and task updates are marked with counters, so you can quickly see where action is needed.
What each participant receives:
- Assignees and co-assignees get notifications for all changes in their tasks.
- Creators get notifications about important events, such as when a task is completed, a checklist item is finished, or a result is attached.
- Observers get notifications about task status changes, such as when a task is created or completed.
If someone is mentioned in the chat, they get a notification regardless of their role.
Calls: when chat is not enough

Sometimes it is easier to talk than type. In Bitrix24, you can start an audio or video call directly from the task chat without switching to another section. After the call, you can post the results in the task chat right away so nothing is lost. CoPilot Follow-Up is available in video calls. It automatically creates a transcript and a short call summary. CoPilot Follow-Up: AI-powered speech analytics for video calls

For example, a team cannot agree on a mockup in chat because everyone reads the task differently. They start a video call from the task chat, turn on CoPilot Follow-Up, and resolve everything in ten minutes. The call summary is added to the chat automatically.
Meetings: schedule directly from the task

Sometimes it makes sense to hold a meeting to bring participants up to speed before a task starts or to review progress along the way. You can create a meeting directly from the task chat. Click the paperclip icon and select Meeting . The event is linked to the task and participants receive an invitation.

For example, a designer sends the final mockup, but the developer and manager have questions. Instead of a long back-and-forth in chat, they schedule a meeting directly from the task chat. All three join, review the mockup, and leave with a clear plan.
In brief
- All task communication — discussions, calls, meetings, and file sharing — happens directly in the task, not scattered across chats and emails.
- Discuss questions in the task chat instead of direct messages so the decision history stays in context and is accessible to all participants.
- You can invite external participants to a task — clients, contractors, or freelancers. They communicate in the same chat and receive email notifications, but cannot access any other company data.
- The Task chats section brings all active discussions into one list, just like a messenger.
- Notifications about important events are sent to each participant based on the role, and counters show where action is needed.
- Audio and video calls can be started directly from the task chat. CoPilot Follow-Up is available for group video calls and automatically creates a transcript and a short summary.
- A meeting can be created directly from a chat message without opening the calendar.

titre: Work with tasks in Bitrix24
sections: Work with tasks in Bitrix24
Tasks in Bitrix24 help you stay organized. All assignments and deadlines are in one place, so you do not need to search through chats or keep everything in your head.
Why tasks are useful for assignees:
- Clear instructions — you always know what needs to be done.
- Deadlines stay visible — Bitrix24 reminds you when a deadline is coming up.
- One workspace — discussions, files, and comments stay inside the task.
- No extra reports — the supervisor can track progress without asking for updates.
- Clear results — the full work history and outcome stay in the task.
- Mobile access — you can discuss tasks, check off checklist items, and attach photos from your phone. This is especially helpful for field employees and anyone who often works outside the office.
In this article:
- Work with the task form
- Handle large or unclear tasks
- Collaborate without losing agreements
- Complete a task
Work with the task form

You can find all your tasks in Tasks and Projects > Tasks . It does not matter where a task comes from. It appears here automatically. You do not need to search message threads or remember who sent it.

The task form shows what needs to be done, when it is due, and who is responsible. It includes everything you need to work on the task: the description, files, checklist items, comments, and activity history.

Title . It is a short summary of the task. It helps you quickly understand what the task is about. For example, if the title says "Prepare a sales report," the expected result is a finished document, not just collected data.
Priority . The icon next to the title shows whether the task has high priority. Start with these tasks first.
Description . It explains what needs to be done and what the final result should look like. Read it carefully to avoid rework. If anything is unclear, ask the creator in the task chat.
Creator . This is the person who created the task and will review the result. If you have questions, contact them in the task chat.

Assignee .This is the person who accepts the task and is responsible for completing it on time. If needed, the assignee can delegate the task to another employee. To do this, click Three dots (...) > Delegate.
Deadline . It is the date and time when the task must be completed. If you cannot meet it, do not wait until the task becomes overdue. Write in the task chat and discuss a new deadline.
The creator can move the deadline. The assignee can move it only if task settings allow it. If you change the deadline, add a reason in the chat so the supervisor can see it right away.
Status shows the current stage of the task. You can change it with the buttons in the task form. This helps the team understand the progress without extra messages.
- Pending — all new tasks start with this status. When you click Start , the task moves to In progress . If time tracking is enabled, a timer starts automatically.

- In progress — work on the task is underway. If time tracking is enabled and you need to pause, for example while waiting for materials, click Pause . The timer stops and the task returns to Pending .

- Deferred — click Three dots (...) > Defer if the task does not need action yet. For example, you are waiting for a decision or another task to be completed first. The task leaves the active list but stays in your task list.
- Pending review — if creator control is enabled, clicking Complete moves the task to Pending review . The creator then reviews the result and either accepts it or sends it back for changes.
- Completed — the task is finished and closed. If creator control is not enabled, the task moves to this status as soon as you click Complete .

Task chat . Use the task chat to discuss details and make decisions. You can ask questions, agree on next steps, mention colleagues, and attach files. All messages stay in the task, so you can always go back and review the full history.
System messages also appear in the chat. They show who changed the deadline, updated the status, added a comment, or uploaded a file. This gives you a full timeline from task creation to completion.
Files . You can add files to a task in the Files section or in the task chat. This keeps all related materials in one place.
The creator can attach source materials such as a client brief or a spreadsheet. You can also add files while you work, such as a draft for review.
If a file was added from Bitrix24 Drive and shared for collaborative editing, it can be edited directly from the task or from the shared file list. Changes are saved automatically.
Co-assignees . These are colleagues who help complete the task. There can be several of them, each handling their part of the work, but the main assignee remains responsible for the overall result.

For example, a manager assigns you the task "Prepare a client presentation." The task has two co-assignees: a designer who creates the slides and an analyst who prepares the data. The presentation must be assembled and sent to the client by the deadline, and the assignee is responsible for making that happen.

Observers . These are colleagues who are kept informed about the task. They do not work on it, but need to know how it is progressing. For example, a manager may be an observer on a presentation task to track progress and step in for review when it is ready.

Related tasks. A task can be linked to a project, a deal, or another task. This helps you see the context and maintain connections between processes. For example, if a task is related to a client, link it to the CRM record so you can quickly open the client card or find related documents without searching manually.
Handle large or unclear tasks

Sometimes a task feels too large or is written in a way that makes it hard to know where to start. Do not waste time guessing. Bitrix24 has tools that can help you break things down and move forward with confidence.
Checklist . It helps you complete a task step by step or verify that the result meets the requirements.
Use the checklist as a plan . Break the task into steps so you can move through them in order: prepare materials → review with colleagues → check the final version.

If the creator added a checklist, just follow the steps. If there is no checklist, add one yourself as your working plan. For example, a designer working on "Client Presentation" checks off items like "gather content," "create layout," and "send for approval."
Use the checklist as a quality check . After finishing the task, go through the checklist to make sure everything is in order:
- Documents are formatted using the template
- All files are attached
- Deadlines are set
- Colleagues have been notified
This helps you avoid missing anything and submit the task without revisions.
Additional checklist features:
- You can add a link or file to each item, such as a template, instructions, or mockup.
- You can assign a co-assignee or observer if someone is responsible for a specific step. For example, the designer handles "prepare the mockup" and the marketer is tagged in "review the content."
Checklists are useful in many scenarios:
- Document preparation — collect signatures, verify details, send to the archive
- Marketing — prepare the mockup, hand it off for layout, review the text after edits
- Event planning — book the venue, send invitations, check the equipment
- HR tasks — grant access, schedule a meeting, give a tour to a new employee
Collaborate without losing agreements

Keep all work discussions in the task chat. Messages are saved so you can always go back and see who suggested or agreed to what. For example, a team discusses the copy for a landing page. All edits and approvals happen in the task chat. A new copywriter joins a month later and does not need to read through separate messengers. The full history is right there in one place.

Mention colleagues. To quickly bring a colleague into a discussion, type @ at the start of your message and enter the name. You can mention any task participant. If you need to bring in someone new, first add them to the task in one of the roles.
Add observers and co-assignees. You can add colleagues who are helping with the task or who need to stay informed.
Attach materials. To keep files easy to find, send them to:
- The Files section — they will appear in the task form
- The task chat — they can be found quickly in the sidebar.

Schedule meetings and calls directly from the task chat. If you need to talk something through, you can schedule a meeting or start a call right away. Right-click a message and select Other > Create meeting .

You can also work on tasks in the Bitrix24 mobile app. Leave comments, attach photos or files, mention colleagues, check off checklist items, and update statuses. This is especially convenient for field employees. For example, after a client visit, a field surveyor can attach a photo report from their phone, close the task, and move on without returning to the office. The supervisor sees the result right away.
Complete a task
Complete a task only when it is truly done and there is a result to show.

Record the result. Before closing the task, attach the final file, a link to the document, or a report. If the result cannot be shown as a file, for example if you updated CRM records or held a meeting, write a short comment.
If the Task status summaries option is enabled, you will not be able to close the task without describing the outcome. A prompt will appear asking you to enter the result.
Close the task. When everything is ready, click Complete in the task form. There are two possible outcomes:
- If creator control is enabled — the task moves to Pending review and goes to the creator. They will check the result and either accept it or send it back for revisions.
- If creator control is not enabled — the task immediately moves to Completed .

If you get a revision request. When the creator sends a task back for revision, the task returns to Pending. Read the comments and confirm what needs to change. After you make the updates, click Complete again.
In brief
- Tasks in Bitrix24 help you stay organized. All assignments and deadlines are in one place, so you do not need to search through chats or remember everything yourself.
- You can find all your tasks in Tasks and projects > Tasks. It does not matter where the task came from. Everything appears here automatically.
- The task form clearly shows what you need to do, when it is due, and who is responsible. It includes everything you need to work on the task: description, files, checklists, comments, and history.
- Keep task statuses up to date: Pending , In progress , and Completed. This helps your teammates and supervisor track progress.
- Keep all discussions in the task chat. The full conversation stays with the task, so you can always check who suggested or approved something.
- Add files to the task form or task chat so participants always have the latest version.
- Checklists help you complete work step by step and confirm that the result meets the requirements.
- Mark a task complete only when the work is fully done and you have a final result. Attach the final file or add a comment, then click Finish.
- If the Task status summaries is enabled, the creator reviews the result and either accepts the task or sends it back for revision.

titre: Collaboration: Participants and observers in tasks
sections: Collaboration: Participants and observers in tasks

When a task involves several people, you can keep everyone in one place. This helps you split work by stage or across different teams. Some people complete parts of the task. Others follow progress and step in when needed.

For example, a company is preparing a website post. A marketing specialist creates a task to prepare the content. A copywriter creates the text, an editor reviews it, and a manager tracks progress and helps when needed.

Bitrix24 Tasks supports two collaboration roles: Participants and Observers . These roles show who works on the task and who monitors it. Participants help complete the task. Observers follow the process and join only when needed.
In this article, you will learn how to organize collaboration in a task and what Participants and Observers are responsible for.
Collaboration in a task
To organize teamwork in a task:
- Add people and assign roles: who completes the task, who helps, and who monitors progress and results
- Describe the task and keep all key details in one place so everyone has the same context
- Split work between participants with task checklists and assign responsibilities
- Track progress to see what stage the task is in
Participants help complete the task

Participants are employees who help the assignee work on a task. You can add several participants, and each person is responsible for their own part of the work. The assignee is still responsible for the final result. This makes it easier to divide work across a team.

Prepare a client presentation . A sales team lead creates a task to prepare a presentation. The assignee is the project manager. To handle the slide design, the manager adds a designer as a participant. The manager prepares the content, and the designer formats the presentation.

Write a website article . A manager assigns a copywriter to write an article about the company's new services. An editor is added as a participant to review the text. After that, the copywriter publishes the content.

Launch an ad campaign . A marketer gets a task to launch an ad campaign. They add a targeting specialist as a participant. The marketer prepares the strategy and ad copy, while the specialist sets up the ads.
In all of these cases, employees work in one task, each person has their own responsibilities, and the assignee is accountable for the final result.
Observers monitor the task

Observers are employees who do not work on the task directly but monitor its progress and results. You can involve them when needed. This helps people stay informed and join the task without extra explanation.
Add observers when:
- Colleagues need to follow the task and stay up to date on the details
- Another employee needs the result for the next stage of work
- A manager needs to track deadlines and progress

Create a banner for an ad campaign . A designer is working on a banner task. The marketing manager is added as an observer to track progress, deadlines, and status. This is useful when the manager needs the result for the next step, such as launching the campaign.

Launch a promo code campaign . A Helpdesk specialist is added as an observer. They do not help prepare the campaign, but they need to see the terms and the discussion. While the marketer prepares the campaign details and website copy, the Helpdesk specialist gets the context they need. Later, they can answer customer questions without asking coworkers for details, even after the task is closed.

Prepare an estimate . A manager prepares an estimate for a major client with a 25% discount and adds the CFO and chief accountant as observers. This lets them review the terms in advance and quickly join the discussion about financial details without separate follow-up.
Participants vs. Observers
The main difference between these roles is how a person is involved in the task:
- A Participant completes part of the task
- An Observer follows progress and results
What Participants can do . Participants work on the task together with the assignee and can:
- Discuss task details in the chat
- Receive notifications about all task changes
- Add observers
- Change statuses
- Add intermediate and final results
- Set reminders
- Create and attach subtasks
- Turn on time tracking
- And more
What Observers can do . Observers do not complete the task, but they can follow progress, discussion, and results. For example, they can:
- Add other observers
- Discuss task details in the chat
- Attach files
- Set reminders
- Receive notifications about task status changes
Some task actions depend on access permission settings. For example, checklist editing may be limited.
In brief
- You can bring several employees into one task to split work and track progress.
- Tasks include two collaboration roles: Participants and Observers.
- Participants help the assignee complete the task and are responsible for their part of the work.
- Observers do not work on the task directly, but they monitor progress and results.
- Available actions depend on a person's role in the task and access permission settings.

titre: Task reports: How to analyze team performance
sections: Task reports: How to analyze team performance
Every company needs a clear view of team performance. A department manager needs to know if work is on track. HR needs to see how new hires are doing during probation.
When task data is spread across dozens of forms, it is hard to see the full picture. For example:
- A manager can see that the team is behind schedule, but cannot tell who is overloaded and who still has capacity.
- A director asks for the department's quarterly results, but the data is spread across many tasks, so collecting it by hand takes too long.
- Before starting a new project, the team needs to know whether they have enough capacity, but checking each employee one by one takes too much time.

Task reports bring this information together in one place. You can see how many tasks each person completed, where overdue tasks are building up, and how the team performed over any time period without collecting data manually.
If you need more flexibility, you can export the data and keep working with it there. You can also share it with people who do not have access to Bitrix24.
In this article:
- When to use task reports
- Analyze team performance with reports
- Monitor team work in real time
- When to use export
When to use task reports
Reports do more than support routine monitoring. They also help you spot problems that are easy to miss when you look at tasks one by one.

Uneven workload distribution. A project manager notices that one developer keeps missing deadlines. He opens the resource report by assignee and sees that this developer has three times more active tasks than the rest of the team. The issue is not the employee. The workload is distributed unevenly.

One task type is delayed again and again. If overdue tasks keep appearing month after month in the same task type, you should look into the cause. When you compare reports across different periods, you may find that tasks are underestimated or that approvals take longer than planned.

The team starts a new project without checking current capacity. Before accepting a large new order, a manager checks project involvement and sees that the team is already fully loaded. This helps set realistic timelines instead of making promises the team cannot keep.

Workload changes over time. When you compare reports from different periods, you can spot trends. You can see whether the number of tasks is growing and whether the team is still performing at the same level. This helps you catch rising workload early and decide whether to expand the team before problems begin.
Analyze team performance with reports
Reports in Bitrix24 help when you need to quickly review current data or share it with coworkers.
Go to Tasks and Projects > More > Reports . You will see two report sections: Personal and Standard .

Standard reports are ready-made templates for common analysis tasks. They do not require setup, and the data is always current when you open them. In any standard report, you can use filters to choose a specific employee, task status, or other parameters.
You cannot edit standard reports, but you can copy any report and customize the copy for your needs. Standard reports in tasks
Bitrix24 includes six standard reports.

Involvement in projects . It shows how much time employees spend on tasks in each project and how many tasks they currently have in progress. For example, a manager may see that two out of three developers are fully loaded while the third has almost no active tasks. This makes it easy to rebalance work before deadlines are missed.

Tasks this month . It shows the current situation: how many tasks were created, completed, and are still in progress. For example, a manager checks the report in the middle of the month and sees that only 8 out of 40 tasks are done and 12 are already overdue. This is a signal to address the issue at the next standup instead of waiting until the end of the month.

Efficiency report . It shows how each employee handles tasks: how many were completed on time, how many became overdue, and how tasks were rated. For example, one manager's overdue rate rises from 10% to 35% over two months. The supervisor reviews that manager's task list and finds 30 active assignments, while everyone else has only 10 to 12. The issue is not the employee. The workload is uneven.

Tasks for last month . It shows the previous month's results by status and assignee. For example, a manager notices that the team is missing deadlines more often. He opens the report for the previous month and compares it with an earlier period. The report shows that the number of overdue tasks has almost doubled. This is a reason to investigate before the issue becomes recurring.

Task resource tracking . It shows planned and actual time spent on each task. For example, a task called Prepare a commercial proposal has 2 hours budgeted, but actually takes 6 to 8 hours. The next time this task is planned, a realistic time estimate should be used.

Employee resource tracking . It shows who spends time on tasks and how much. For example, a designer always seems busy, but the report shows that 70% of his time goes to revisions and approvals, and only 30% to creating new materials. This is a reason to rethink the approval process rather than hire a second designer.
Resource tracking reports only show data for tasks that have the Time tracking option enabled.
Personal reports are created using the report builder. You can choose the data, time period, employees, or projects for a specific request.

For example, a marketing manager wants to see only tasks from their department with a negative rating over the last six months. A personal report is the right tool for this — it is built for specific parameters using the report builder.
To create a new report, go to the reports page and click Add report in the top right corner. Create reports on tasks
Monitor team work in real time

The Supervising section helps you track team work throughout the day. It shows key metrics for each direct report: efficiency, number of tasks, and their roles — assignee, task owner, assistant, and observer.

Unlike reports, which help you analyze work over a selected period, the Supervising section shows the current situation. A manager can immediately see who is overloaded and who is available for new tasks.
The section only shows direct reports — employees who have you listed as their manager in the company structure. Company structure: New interface and features

For example, a manager starts the workday by opening the Supervising section and immediately sees that two employees have overdue tasks building up, while a new team member has only one active task. This makes it easy to redistribute work and avoid new delays without building separate reports.

To open the section, go to Tasks and Projects and click Supervising in the top menu. If you have many employees, use filters to quickly find a specific person or sort employees by efficiency and department. Supervising option: How to track subordinates' tasks
When to use export
Export is useful when you need to combine Bitrix24 data with information from other systems, share it with people who do not have access to Bitrix24, or save a separate copy.

Combine data from different systems. Company leadership is preparing a quarterly report that includes task data, sales figures, and expenses from different systems. A department head exports the task report and combines it with the other data in xlsx format.

Save data when a project is complete. A company wraps up a large project. The manager exports the report and stores it alongside the project documentation. If questions come up later about timelines, team workload, or the scope of work completed, the data will be easy to find.
To export a report, open it and click Settings (⚙️) > Export to Microsoft Excel in the top right corner.
In brief
- Task reports give you a complete view of team performance.
- Bitrix24 offers two types of reports: standard reports with six ready-made templates, and personal reports built with the report builder for specific needs.
- Standard reports cannot be edited, but you can copy any of them and customize the copy.
- The Supervising section shows the current status of your direct reports in real time.
- Export data when you need to work with it outside Bitrix24: share it with colleagues who do not have access, combine it with other sources, or save an archived snapshot.

titre: Projects in Bitrix24: How to organize teamwork
sections: Projects in Bitrix24: How to organize teamwork

Projects work best when a team shares one goal and needs to complete several related steps to reach it. These steps can happen one after another or at the same time. They often take a while and involve people from different teams.

For example, a company is launching an online store website. The team needs to agree on the site structure with the client, prepare the design, build the pages, add catalog content, set up payment and delivery, and test everything before launch. Since all of this leads to one outcome, it makes sense to manage it as a project.

In Bitrix24, a project is a shared workspace for the team. Team members can create tasks, discuss work in public and private chats, hold meetings, work with files, and track overall progress. Everything stays in one place, so it is easier to keep context and coordinate work.
In this article:
- How projects differ from tasks
- When to create a project
- Break a project into tasks
- Use tasks, chats, meetings, and files
- Track overall progress
How a project differs from a task
A task helps organize one specific assignment. It has an assignee, a deadline, and a clear result.

A project brings together several related tasks that support one shared goal. Project work usually takes longer, includes multiple stages, and involves a team. Some tasks can run in parallel, while others depend on each other.
For example, preparing a conference agenda is a task. The result is a finished event program.

Hosting an annual partner conference is a project. It includes finding a venue, inviting speakers, opening registration, preparing promotional materials, setting up a live stream, and running the event. Different employees handle different parts, but everyone works toward the same result.
In a project, the team can see not only individual assignments but the full scope of work:
- Which tasks are complete
- What employees are working on now
- Which stages have not started yet
- Where current files are stored
- What decisions the team has made
- Which meetings are scheduled and what agreements were recorded
When to use a project
Create a project when the work has one shared goal and several related stages.
A project is useful when:
- Multiple employees or departments contribute to the result
- There are many tasks and they get lost among other assignments
- Several stages happen at the same time
- The team needs shared files, discussions, and meetings
- It is important to track overall progress
- A client or contractor needs to be involved

For example, when launching a website, the designer prepares mockups, the developer builds the pages, the content manager fills the catalog, and the payments specialist connects the payment system. A project brings these tasks together, so the team can track progress across the full launch, not just one part of it.
If employees are working on unrelated assignments with no shared goal, separate tasks are enough.
Get started with a project
Any employee can create a project. Open the Projects section and click Create .
Enter a name, add members, and choose the project type:
- Public project: visible to all employees, and anyone can join
- Private project: employees can join by invitation only

Choose a name that reflects the outcome. "New website" describes a topic, but not the goal. "Launch the e-commerce website" gives more context because it shows the result and the general direction of the work.
Break a project into tasks
Split the project into clear deliverables that you can assign to team members. For a website launch, do not create one task called "Build the website." Break the work into stages instead:
- Approve the site structure
- Prepare the design
- Build the pages
- Fill the catalog
- Set up payment and delivery
- Test the site before launch
Each task should have a clear result, an owner, and a deadline. This helps employees understand what they need to do. It also helps managers see who owns each part of the project.
If a stage is too large, split it into subtasks. For example, the task "Fill the catalog" can include subtasks for photos, descriptions, and prices.
To add a new task directly in a project, create it from the project card and click Add task .
You can also link an existing task to a project. This is helpful if work started before the project was created and you now want to keep everything in one place.
What's included in a project

A project is a shared workspace for your team. It brings together tasks, chats, meetings, files, and an AI assistant. Your team can work in one place instead of switching between tools or rebuilding context.
A project includes:
- Tasks and subtasks
- The main project chat
- Public and private chats
- Task chats
- Calendar and meetings
- Files and docs

Tasks and subtasks help you turn a project goal into clear deliverables. Each task has an assignee, a deadline, and an expected result. If a phase is too large, you can split it into subtasks and assign them to different employees. This helps everyone understand ownership and makes it easier for a supervisor to track progress.
The main project chat is best for general updates. Use it to notify the team about deadline changes, discuss new client requirements, or make decisions that affect everyone.
Public and private chats help teams discuss specific workstreams. Designers can review layouts, while developers can focus on technical details without distracting other project members.

Task chats are best for specific assignments. They keep questions, interim results, files, and decisions in one place. If a new assignment comes up in the main chat or a group chat, create a task directly from the message so nothing gets lost.
Calendar and meetings help the team plan shared events. A meeting created in the project is added to each participant's calendar automatically, so you do not need to invite people one by one.

Each meeting has its own chat. The team can discuss the agenda in advance, share materials, and continue the conversation afterward. The meeting chat stays in the project, so participants can go back to it and review decisions at any time.
Files and docs stored in the project give the team access to the latest materials and make information easy to find.
Work with clients and contractors

You can invite a guest to a project, such as a client, contractor, vendor, or partner who does not have a Bitrix24 account in your organization. A guest can chat with the team, work on tasks, and join project meetings. They do not get access to the rest of your company's information.
This lets your team and external participants work in the same space instead of juggling email, messengers, and task tools.

A company that is building a website for a clothing store invites the client's representative to the project. The client can follow progress, join layout discussions, and take part in meetings. The designer attaches a new layout version to the task, and the client leaves feedback in the same place. The team sees the comments right away and does not need to search through old messages for the latest file.
You can set guest access based on their role in the project. For example:
- Let them view only the tasks they participate in
- Give access to all project tasks if the client needs full visibility
- Prevent them from deleting tasks
- Open chat history so a new member can catch up quickly.
In brief
- A task focuses on one result. A project supports a shared goal with several related stages.
- Create a project when several people are involved, the number of tasks grows, and overall progress matters.
- Break the project into clear tasks. Each task should have a result, a responsible person, and a deadline.
- Use the project chat for general questions. Keep details and work results inside the task.
- Create assignments from the project card so they appear in the shared list right away.
- A project keeps tasks, discussions, files, and meetings in one place. Your team always sees current information and spends less time searching and catching up.

titre: Import and export tasks in Bitrix24
sections: Import and export tasks in Bitrix24
Import and export help you move task lists in and out of Bitrix24.

Import lets you upload a ready-made list of tasks from a spreadsheet, another service, or another Bitrix24 account. You do not need to create tasks one by one. Your team keeps deadlines, assignees, and descriptions, and can start work right away.
Export lets you save a task list to a separate file. You can use it to prepare a report or share information with a contractor who does not work in Bitrix24.
In this article:
- When to use task import
- Import tasks into Bitrix24
- When to use task export
- Export tasks from Bitrix24
When to use task import
Import helps you bring a ready-made task list with deadlines, assignees, and descriptions into Bitrix24.

Move data from another service. If your company already manages tasks in another service, you may not want to recreate them one by one in Bitrix24. If the current service already includes task names, descriptions, assignees, and deadlines, you can import that data into Bitrix24 and start working right away.

Start a large project. A manager may prepare tasks in a spreadsheet and assign deadlines and owners in advance. Import helps you move that plan into Bitrix24 at once, so your team does not need to build a long task list manually before work starts.
Import tasks into Bitrix24
By default, all employees can import tasks. A Bitrix24 administrator can limit this permission in the access settings. Configure access permissions in tasks
1. Go to Tasks and projects and select the List view. 2. In the top-right corner, open Settings (⚙️) > Import list > from CSV.
- If you exported tasks from another service or prepared them in a spreadsheet, download and prepare the CSV file.
- If you exported tasks from another Bitrix24 account, the file is ready to upload. How to import tasks into Bitrix24
When to use task export
Export is useful when you need to:
- Save project history to a file
- Prepare a report
- Review team workload

Save project history. When a project is complete, you may want to keep the task list in a separate file. This makes it easy to review what was done, when it was done, and who was responsible. For example, you may need to rebuild the project timeline before starting a new phase several months later.

Prepare a report. A manager may need a task list for a department or project. Export helps you save it to a file and review tasks by deadline, assignee, or status. For example, you can check which tasks the team completed during the month and which ones are still in progress.

Review team workload. After export, you can see who has too many tasks, where overdue items are building up, and which tasks have been in progress the longest. For example, this can help before a team meeting when a manager plans new work and wants to see who is already overloaded.
Export tasks from Bitrix24
Export saves the task list from Bitrix24 to an Excel file. Task chats are not included.
To export tasks:

1. Go to Tasks and projects > Tasks. 2. If needed, click Filter + Search and enter your criteria, or apply a saved filter. For example, if you only need tasks that are currently active, click In progress. Search and filters in Tasks 3. Open Settings (⚙️) > Export to Microsoft Excel.
4. Choose which fields to export:
- Only fields from the list — the file includes only the fields currently shown in the task list
- All fields — the file includes all task list fields in Bitrix24.
5. Click Run. Export starts. The more tasks you have, the longer it takes. 6. Click Download export file to save the spreadsheet to your computer.
In brief
- Task import lets you move a ready-made task list into Bitrix24 from a spreadsheet, another service, or another Bitrix24 account without creating tasks one by one.
- Export is useful when you need to save project history, prepare a report, review team workload, or share data with people who do not work in Bitrix24.

- To import, go to Tasks and projects , select the List view, and open Settings (⚙️) > Import list > from CSV. If the tasks are from another Bitrix24 account, the file is ready to upload. If they are from another service or spreadsheet, prepare the file first.

- To export, go to Tasks and projects > Tasks, filter tasks if needed, then open Settings (⚙️) > Export to Microsoft Excel, choose the fields, and click Run. When export is complete, click Download export file.

titre: Task features that help you get everything done
sections: Task features that help you get everything done

When your team has a lot of tasks, it is easy to lose track of the right file, the next owner, or what is already done. In Bitrix24, tasks are more than a list of assignments. They give you the tools to manage work, collaborate with your team, and finish on time.
Supervisors can track progress, team members understand their roles, and important details do not get lost in chats or emails.
For example, imagine you are launching a new ad campaign. You need to build the concept, write the copy, design the layouts, and launch the ads.

- Without Bitrix24 tasks, the process can quickly become chaotic. The brief gets lost in messages, the designer waits for materials, the copywriter does not know the deadline, and the supervisor spends time asking for updates.

- With Bitrix24 tasks, the process is clear. The supervisor creates a task and links it to the "Campaign Spring 2025" project. The task description includes the goal and deadline. A checklist covers each step: concept, copy, layouts, and launch. Each item has a specific owner. The task also includes all required materials and the media plan. The team can see overall progress, and the supervisor gets a clear view without extra follow-ups.
This is how Bitrix24 turns a simple task into a structured process with clear ownership and a documented result.
In this article, you will learn which task features help teams work efficiently and deliver results.
Deadline: complete tasks on time

A deadline shows when a task must be completed. It helps the assignee set priorities and decide what to work on first. For the supervisor, it shows whether the team is on schedule, which tasks are urgent, where delays may happen, and who may need help. When you compare deadlines with each employee's task load, you get a clear picture of workload and can adjust plans in time.
To keep deadlines clear and realistic, Bitrix24 lets you control who can change them and how:
- Let an employee change the deadline on their own, either freely or with limits. For example, you can set the latest allowed date or the maximum number of changes.
- Turn on the Ask for a reason for change option so the team can see why a deadline moved.

This helps keep the process clear and accountable without constant reminders. The supervisor can see deadline changes and respond quickly. Employees can manage their work and avoid missing fixed deadlines.

For example, a marketing manager creates a task called "Prepare banners for the advertising campaign" with a deadline of October 15. The manager allows one deadline change and requires a reason. The designer moves the deadline by one day because the layout approval was delayed and adds a comment. The supervisor can see the reason right in the task.

In a legal team, there may be a task called "Review the contract" with a deadline of October 10. The supervisor allows the deadline to move only until October 20. This keeps the process under control. Employees can adjust the timeline, but they cannot postpone the task indefinitely.
Files and documents: always use the latest version
A task description does not always include every detail. Files such as layouts, instructions, and contracts help the assignee understand what to do and what the final result should look like.

The new task form includes a separate Files section. All participants share it. Anyone can upload a file, and it appears in the list right away. All materials stay in one place, which makes collaboration easier and removes the need to search through email or messengers.
If you need to discuss something quickly, you can send a file directly in the task chat.
For example:
- A manager attaches a draft contract, and the lawyer reviews it inside the task. All edits and versions stay in one place, so there is no need to send the file by email.
- A designer uploads a banner to the task "Prepare advertising layout." The manager can review the finished file and send it to the client right away.

If you attach a file created in Bitrix24, it is also available in other tools such as Drive and Projects. When the file is updated in Drive, the new version appears in the task automatically, and the same works the other way around. You can also enable shared access and share files with coworkers or external partners.
This helps your team always work with current materials and saves time when searching for files.
Checklists in tasks: do not miss important details
Checklists help you organize a task and track progress. They break a large task into clear steps, show how much is done, and help you avoid missing important details.
You can use checklists in tasks in several ways:

- For step-by-step work, when a task has several stages. For example, a marketer adds a checklist to the task "Prepare a newsletter": gather materials, approve the copy, confirm the layout, and send the newsletter.

- To split a larger task into smaller items when several people are involved or responsibilities need to be clear. You can add sub-items, assign owners, and attach files. For example, in a task for preparing an event, you can add items such as "Invite participants," "Prepare the venue," and "Create a presentation," and assign a responsible person to each step.
This makes it easier for the assignee to plan their work and for the supervisor to see what is done and what is still in progress.
Reminders: never miss a task

Reminders help you complete tasks on time and avoid missing deadlines. You can set them for any participant — the assignee, co-assignee, or observer. Reminders let assignees know when to start a task or finish a stage. For the task creator, reminders help check results at the right moment without constantly following up manually.

For example, a manager sets a reminder three days before the deadline to prepare a proposal for the client, and the supervisor sets one a day before completion to check whether the manager is on track.
Results: document what was accomplished
Results help you capture the outcome of a task and keep everything in one place. The assignee can attach a file, a report, a presentation, or write a short summary of what was done.

To avoid tasks being closed without a real outcome, you can enable the Task status summaries option. Bitrix24 will then remind the assignee to add an outcome and will not allow the task to be completed until a result is recorded. This way, the supervisor can immediately see how the work ended, and the team does not lose the outcome in the chat.
Projects: see the full picture

A project brings together tasks that share a common goal. All assignments and materials are in one place, so participants understand the overall context and can navigate their work faster. Each project can have its own kanban board with custom stages so you can track the workflow easily. The team moves tasks across columns to see what is done, what is in progress, and which tasks need attention.

For example, when launching a new product, tasks for design, marketing, testing, and sales all belong to one project. The supervisor can see the status of each part, and if a delay appears anywhere, it can be spotted and addressed quickly. Create a workgroup or project
In brief
- Task features in Bitrix24 make teamwork clear, help keep the process under control, and ensure everything is completed on time.
- Deadlines help set priorities, track task completion, and adjust plans before it is too late.
- Files and documents are always at hand — current versions are not lost and are available to all participants.
- Checklists help break a task into steps and track the progress of its completion.
- Reminders help complete tasks on time and avoid missing deadlines.
- Results help capture the outcome of a task and keep everything in one place.
- Flows help distribute similar tasks evenly within a team.
- Projects bring related tasks together and give everyone a view of overall progress.

titre: Use subtasks and checklists
sections: Use subtasks and checklists

As your company grows, tasks get bigger and more complex. One goal may no longer fit into a single step or stay under one person's control. If a task is hard to plan, assign, or review, break it into smaller parts.
This helps you:
- Plan large workloads more accurately
- Spot bottlenecks early
- Split responsibility clearly
- See what drives the final result
In Bitrix24, you can break down tasks in two ways — through subtasks and checklists.
In this article:
- When to break down a task
- When to use subtasks
- When to add checklists
When to break down a task
Break down a task when the workload is too large for one task. In that case, it becomes hard to:
- Set realistic deadlines
- Track current progress
- Split work between people
- Catch delays early
Decomposition turns one large goal into a set of clear actions. You can complete, review, and close each action separately.

A task is large and lasts a long time. For example, launching a website involves more than one step. You may need to build a prototype, create the design, prepare the layout, add content, and publish the site. Breaking the work down helps you track each stage and see what is in progress right now, instead of relying on one general status.

One goal includes several stages. For example, preparing a client report may include gathering data, checking figures, formatting a presentation, and approving the final version. If you do not record each stage, it is easy to miss a step or remember it too late.

Different employees or departments work on the task. For example, a company wants to open a new branch. One task cannot cover everything: hiring, onboarding, training, document prep, and approval of the first sales plan.

Without decomposition, a task becomes hard to manage. The workload is too large, the sequence is unclear, and deadlines keep moving. Decomposition adds structure. Each activity gets its own task, assignee, and deadline. Tasks can run in parallel, and the manager can see overall progress without collecting separate updates.
When to use subtasks

Use subtasks when one goal has several independent parts, and each part needs its own result. Each part becomes a separate task with its own assignee and deadline. Subtasks help you see who owns each part, what stage the work is in, and where delays happen.
Use subtasks when:
- Different employees or teams work on the task
- Each part needs a separate measurable result
- Stages take different amounts of time and need different deadlines
- Each part must be reviewed separately from the parent task
For example, organizing a company event may include choosing a venue, approving the menu, ordering decorations, and preparing the program. Each of these can be a subtask under one shared goal.
How to create a subtask:

1. Go to Tasks and Projects > Tasks and open the task form. 2. Click Subtasks and create a new task. If the task already exists, select it from the list. 3. Fill in the required fields: name, description, assignee, and deadlines. 4. Click Create. Create a task
The parent task form shows all subtasks. To open that block quickly, click Subtasks. A subtask form shows only its parent task.
When to add checklists
A checklist works well when one person or a small team handles a task with several small actions that lead to one result.
In this case, creating a separate subtask for every action adds extra complexity. A checklist lets you list all steps and quickly see what is done and what has not started yet.
For example, the task "Prepare a social media post" may include:
- Write the copy
- Choose an image
- Schedule the post
- Check the final display
All of these actions lead to one result: a published post. A checklist is enough.
How to add a checklist in the task form:

1. Click Checklists . 2. Add checklist items and describe what needs to be done. 3. If teammates need to help with specific items, assign co-executors. Select an employee. For example, a designer can prepare the image, a marketer can review the copy, and the main assignee can oversee publication and stay responsible for the final result.
In brief
- As your company grows, tasks get bigger and more complex. If a task is hard to plan, assign, or review, break it into smaller parts.
- Break down a task when it is large, consists of several stages, or involves different employees.
- Subtasks work best when one goal has several independent parts, each with its own result. Each part becomes a separate task with its own assignee and deadline.
- To create a subtask, go to Tasks and Projects > Tasks and open the task form. Add a subtask and fill in the key fields — assignee, deadlines, and description.
- A checklist works well when one person or a small team handles a task with several small actions that lead to one result.
- To add a checklist, open the task form, click Checklists, add items, and assign co-executors for specific actions if needed.

titre: Tasks in Bitrix24: Integration with chats, the Feed, meetings, documents, and boards
sections: Tasks in Bitrix24: Integration with chats, the Feed, meetings, documents, and boards
New assignments often come up in chats, Feed discussions, meetings, or while you work on a document.

In Bitrix24, you do not need to open the Tasks section every time. You can create a task or open a related item right from the tool you are already using. This helps you stay in context, capture decisions faster, and switch between sections less often.
In this article:
- Create a task from a chat
- Create a task from the Feed
- Create a meeting from a task
- Create a task from a board
- Open a task from a document
Create a task from a chat

Assignments often come up in personal and group chats. Someone may ask you to prepare a document, review a layout, or contact a client. If you wait too long, the assignment can get lost in the conversation.

You can create a task from any message in a personal or group chat. You do not need to open the Tasks section and enter everything again. Bitrix24 creates the task where the assignment first appeared and keeps a link to the original message, so you can return to the discussion at any time.
Create tasks from a chat when:
- A clear assignment appears in the conversation
- You want to track it right away without leaving the chat
- You want to keep the link between the task and the message
Examples:

Prepare an estimate . A manager discusses new deal terms with a colleague. In the chat, someone writes: "Prepare three delivery options for the client." The manager creates a task from that message and assigns it right away. There is no need to open the Tasks section, copy the text, or repeat the details.

Fix a bug on the site . A tester posts in the development group chat that the feedback form stopped working after an update. The team lead creates a task directly from the message and assigns it. The team can keep discussing the issue while the task is already in progress.
Create a task from the Feed

Teams use the Feed to share updates, discuss work, and exchange ideas. Specific assignments often come out of these discussions. If no one captures them right away, they can get lost among other posts and comments.
You can create a task from any post or comment in the Feed. The message text goes into the task description, and Bitrix24 keeps a link to the original post. Convert a Feed post into a task
Create tasks from the activity stream when:
- A specific assignment comes up in a discussion and needs tracking right away
- You want to keep the link between the task and its context
- A manager wants to create a task during a discussion without interrupting it
Examples:

Collect ideas to improve customer service . A supervisor posts in the Feed and asks the team for ideas. A manager leaves a useful suggestion in the comments. The supervisor creates a task on the spot and assigns it to an owner. The discussion continues, and the work is already under control.

Update client workflow guidelines . At a general meeting, the team agrees to rewrite the guidelines. Someone posts the summary in the Feed. The supervisor creates a task directly from that post, so the assignment stays connected to the discussion.
Create a meeting from a task
Sometimes a chat discussion is not enough, and task participants need to talk directly. In that case, you do not need to switch to another tool.

For a quick conversation, you can start a call from the task chat. If you need to schedule a time or set up a recurring call, create a meeting from the task chat. Participants are added automatically. FAQ: New tasks in Bitrix24
Create meetings from a task when:
- A question in the chat is easier to resolve by voice
- You need to bring task participants together quickly
- You want to keep meeting results in the task
Examples:

Approve a budget for an ad campaign . A marketer and a CFO cannot agree on the numbers in the chat. The supervisor right-clicks a message in the task chat and creates a meeting. All participants get an invitation, and they resolve the issue by voice the same day. After the call, the supervisor records the results in the task chat.

Prepare a product launch plan . The team has worked on a task for several weeks. The supervisor decides to bring everyone together to align and assign next steps. They create a meeting in the task chat, and participants receive invitations automatically.
Create a task from a board
Teams use boards to collect ideas, build diagrams, and plan projects. Once the work structure is ready, individual stages need to be assigned and tracked.

You can create a task from any object on the board. There is no need to move project stages into the Tasks section manually — they turn into assignments right where the team discussed and planned them.
To create a task, click the three dots (...) next to an element and select Create task .
Create tasks from a board when:
- After a brainstorm, you are ready to move from ideas to execution
- The team has broken a project into stages and is ready to assign responsibility
- You want to keep the link between the project plan and the tasks in progress
Examples:

Launch a new corporate website . The team builds the project structure on a board: design, development, content, and testing. Once the plan is approved, the supervisor creates tasks directly from board objects and assigns owners. The team does not need to re-enter project stages into tasks — work starts right after planning.

Prepare an annual conference . Organizers map out the preparation on a board: find a venue, approve the agenda, invite speakers, launch registration. After the discussion, each stage becomes a separate task. The board remains the big picture of the project, while team members work from their individual tasks.
Open a task from a document

Documents are often opened separately from a task — to review a contract, update instructions, or check a technical specification. Meanwhile, the discussion, deadlines, and responsible people are all in the task.
If a document is used in a task, the document card displays a link to the related task. You do not need to search for it manually — you can open the task directly from the document.
Use the connection between documents and tasks when:
- You need to quickly open the task related to a document
- You want to check deadlines, assignees, or the discussion for a document
- One document is used across multiple workflows
Examples:

Approve a contract with a client . A lawyer opens a contract to review the latest edits. In the document form, they see a link to the approval task and open it right away. The task shows the responsible person, the deadline, and the full discussion history — no need to search manually or ask colleagues for a status update.

Update employee instructions . An editor opens a document and notices that some information is outdated. Through the linked task, they quickly navigate to the discussion, check which comments have already been addressed, and see the deadline for the new version.
In brief
- Tasks in Bitrix24 are connected to other tools — chats, the Feed, meetings, documents, and boards.
- You can create new tasks right where an assignment first appeared — no need to open the Tasks section.
- The link between a task and the original message, discussion, or document helps preserve the work context.
