- If task participants need to talk, you can organize a meeting directly from the task.
- Work stays connected to the tool where it started — agreements are easy to find, and information does not need to be moved manually.

titre: Custom fields: How to use for your company processes
sections: Custom fields: How to use for your company processes
Tasks in Bitrix24 come with standard fields like title, description, assignee, and deadline. But most teams also need to track their own data.
Custom fields fix the information. You can add the exact fields your business needs right in the task form. The same task can support different workflows for different departments.
In this article:
- When to use custom fields
- Field types available in tasks
- How custom fields improve task organization
When to use custom fields
Use custom fields when standard task fields do not give your team enough structure.

Task data needs a clear format. A construction company may need to record a site address. A legal team may need a contract number. If employees choose where to enter this data on their own, task structure quickly becomes inconsistent. Custom fields give everyone the same format.

Different team members need different details. A manager may need to see the project budget. The assignee may need the site address. A supervisor may need the approval status. Custom fields keep all of this in one task form, so each person can find what they need.

You need data for both work and reporting. When tasks include structured data such as department, budget, or request type, supervisors can filter tasks by any of these values. Without custom fields, this information gets buried in the description or is not saved at all.
Field types available in tasks
A Bitrix24 administrator can add custom fields. Open the task form and click Custom fields > Add field . Custom fields for tasks
Bitrix24 offers four field types:
- String
- Number
- Date and time
- Yes/No.
You can also make String , Number , and Date and time fields required or multiple.
String . The most flexible field type. Use it for any text you want to store separately from the description, such as a contract number, product SKU, or site address.

Example: Real estate agents often manage many listings at the same time. If a client calls and asks for a showing in an hour, the agent can open the task and see the address right away in a dedicated field. There is no need to search through messages or ask a coworker.

Number . For values you need to compare, filter, or total. This includes project budgets, equipment counts, and site square footage. A number field works better than a description when you need to use the data later in filters or reports.

Example: In a sales team, each estimate task includes a Client budget field. The manager fills it in after the first call. The sales lead can then filter tasks by budget and focus on the highest-value opportunities.

Date and time . For dates related to the work itself, not the task deadline. These are two different things. The deadline shows when the task must be completed. A custom date field stores a business date, such as when a contract expires, when work is scheduled, or when the next maintenance visit is due.

Example: An engineer gets a task to arrange equipment maintenance. The task deadline is March 10, which means the visit must be confirmed and the documents must be ready by that date. The Maintenance date field shows March 15, which is the actual service date. A supervisor can filter tasks by Maintenance date and review all scheduled visits for the month.

Yes/No . For simple status checks, such as contract signed, brief approved, or report received. These fields help both assignees and supervisors. The assignee can quickly see whether work can begin. The supervisor can filter tasks by status and find items still waiting for approval or signature.

Example: A designer is preparing banners for an ad campaign. Before work starts, the brief must be approved. The Brief approved field is set to Yes . The designer opens the task and knows they can begin right away. There is no need to check chat history or ask a manager. A supervisor can filter tasks by Brief approved and see campaigns still waiting for client confirmation.

Required field . A required field prevents users from creating a task without key information. If a value is critical, do not rely on employees to remember it. Mark the field as required. Bitrix24 will not save the task until the field is filled in.
Examples:

- Prepare an estimate — a manager assigns a task to a sales specialist. Without a deal number and client name, the specialist cannot prepare the documents. The Deal number and Client fields are required, so the task always includes the needed information.
- Prepare court documents — a lawyer receives tasks from different managers. The Case number field is required, so every task includes the details needed to start work right away.
To make a field required, mark the Required option when creating it. Bitrix24 will show a warning until the field is filled in.

Multiple field . It allows storing more than one value of the same type. By default, a field holds one value. If there may be several values of the same type, make the field multiple so employees can add as many values as needed.
Examples:

- Service equipment on site — an engineer visits a server room for scheduled maintenance. All inspected device serial numbers need to be recorded. In a multiple Serial number field, the engineer can add every number without listing them in the description or creating separate fields for each device.

- Prepare a document package for a deal — a lawyer is processing documents for a major client involving several contracts. In a multiple Contract number field, all related contracts can be entered. When documents for a specific contract are needed later, the number is easy to find using a filter.
To make a field multiple, mark the Multiple option when creating it.
How custom fields improve task organization
Once fields are created, a task becomes more than an assignment — it becomes a structured process card. Every team uses the same tasks but fills them with data that fits their own workflows.
For example:
- A construction company stores the site address, cost of work, and act signing status in the task
- A legal team stores the contract number, client tax ID, and contract expiration date
- A service department stores equipment serial numbers and the next maintenance date.

The task structure stays consistent across the whole team. Every employee fills in the same fields in the same place. No one has to decide where to write the contract number or site address — the field is already there, ready to be filled in.
Supervisors can view all data in a clear format and filter tasks by any field — for example, to find all tasks related to a specific contract or to see which sites still have an unsigned act.
In brief
- Custom fields add the data your business needs directly to tasks, such as contract numbers, site addresses, and budgets.
- A Bitrix24 administrator can add fields, and they appear across all tasks immediately.
- Bitrix24 offers four field types: String for text, Number for numeric values, Date and time for business-relevant dates, and Yes/No for statuses.
- A required field prevents a task from being saved without key data, building control into the creation process.
- A multiple field supports several values of the same type, such as multiple sites, serial numbers, or addresses.
- Field data is available in filters and reports, making it easy to search and group tasks.

Search for tasks
Use filters and search tools to find tasks quickly.
Use filters and search tools to find tasks quickly.

- Assisting

Sort tasks By default, tasks are sorted by activity (recent updates appear first). To change sorting, select any column. For example, select Deadline to sort by due date.

titre: Deadline view in Tasks
sections: Deadline view in Tasks
Bitrix24 has several views for working with tasks: List, Deadline, Planner, Calendar, and Gantt. Each of them helps to emphasize certain elements of tasks.
The Deadline view is suitable for employees who need to do everything on time. Tasks are automatically organized into columns depending on the deadline specified in them.
Switch to Deadline view
Select the Deadline view to manage your tasks. This view helps you identify which tasks need immediate attention and which can be postponed.
Go to the Tasks section and select the Deadline view.
1. Go to the Tasks section.
2. Tap the three dots (...) in the top right corner.
3. Select Task view .
4. Choose Deadline .
Deadline view stages
All tasks will be categorized into the following columns:
- Overdue
- Due today
- Due this week
- Due next week
- No deadline
- Due over two weeks
- Completed
Open a task from the list to view or add a comment.
Each stage contains tasks depending on the deadline set in them.
In the top menu, select the desired stage to view all tasks with the corresponding deadline. For example, check which tasks need to be done today in the Due today stage.
Create a task in the Deadline view
Create a new task at a particular stage, and it will automatically have a deadline matching that column.

Click the + Quick task button under the desired stage and enter a task name. To create a detailed task, click the Create button and enter the required information. The task will be moved to the column according to its deadline.
Go to the required stage and tap the + button. Fill in the task fields and tap the blue arrow icon. The task will appear on the corresponding stage.
Move a task to another stage
Change the task stage, and its deadline will be automatically updated.

Tap on the task stage and select the one where you want to move it.
If you move a task to the Due next week or Due over two weeks stage, its deadline will automatically update to the last working day of the week, based on Bitrix24 settings.

titre: Planner view in Tasks

To open Planner:

2. Click the Plus (+) icon on the right.
3. Enter the stage name and select a color.

titre: Kanban: Track tasks in projects effectively
sections: Kanban: Track tasks in projects effectively

titre: Calendar view in Tasks
sections: Calendar view in Tasks
Use the Calendar view to work effectively with task deadlines and plan your workload in different time periods. To access this view, navigate to the Tasks section and switch to the Calendar view.

titre: Gantt chart
sections: Gantt chart

A Gantt chart is a type of bar chart used to visualize a project schedule, including task duration, deadlines, and dependencies. It is useful for planning tasks that need to be completed in a specific order but do not have fixed deadlines.
How to use the Gantt chart
Go to the Tasks and Projects section and open the Gantt view.
The chart lets you visually edit the task schedule using task bars. Each task includes the following dates:
- Start date : represented by the left edge of the task bar.
- End date : represented by the right edge of the task bar.
- Deadline : displayed as a vertical red line.
Drag either side of the blue task bar to change the Start date or End date. To move the entire task schedule, drag the whole task bar across the chart.
You can also set the Start date and End date in the task form under the Time planning section.
Task bars can also display additional details:
- Overdue tasks are partially highlighted in red.
- The vertical red line shows the task deadline.
- A thin dark line inside the task bar shows the period when work was performed on the task.
Hover over a task bar to view task details.
To edit a task, right-click the task bar and choose an action from the menu. You can also double-click the task bar to open the full task form.
To zoom in or out on the chart, use the + and - icons on the left.
How to create task dependencies in the Gantt chart
Task dependencies define the order in which tasks must be completed. They help show which tasks are primary and which depend on others.

To create a dependency, drag a connection line between two tasks. For example, you can create a Finish-to-Start dependency. In this case, when you move the End date of the main task, the Start date of the dependent task changes automatically.
Task dependencies in Gantt chart
In brief
- A Gantt chart is a bar chart used to visualize a project schedule.
- Tasks appear as blue bars on the chart. Each task includes a Start date and End date that define the planned work period.
- You can create dependencies between tasks to maintain the task sequence when changing the Start date or End date of the parent task.

titre: Task dependencies in the Gantt chart
sections: Task dependencies in the Gantt chart
Task dependencies define the relationship between tasks and control the order in which they happen. They show which task comes first and which tasks depend on it.
You can create task dependencies in the Gantt Chart task view.
Create task dependencies

For example, if you need to create a marketing campaign, you may first need to complete the design before you can create the content. Task dependencies help you organize tasks in the correct order and keep deadlines aligned.
To create a dependency:
1. Identify the main task . If you change the dates of the main task, the dependent task updates automatically.
2. Select the dependency type . The dependency type defines how the main task affects the dependent task.
The following dependency types are available:
- Finish to Start (FS) : When you change the End date of the main task, the Start date of the dependent task updates automatically.
- Start to Start (SS) : When you change the Start date of the main task, the Start date of the dependent task updates automatically.
- Finish to Finish (FF) : When you change the End date of the main task, the End date of the dependent task updates automatically.
- Start to Finish (SF) : When you change the Start date of the main task, the End date of the dependent task updates automatically.

3. Connect the tasks . Hover over a task bar to display circles on both sides of the task. Click the Start or End point of one task and drag it to the Start or End point of another task. A dotted line appears while you create the connection.

One task can have dependencies with multiple tasks. When you create a new dependency, the system checks for conflicts with existing dependencies. If the new dependency creates a conflict, the system does not save it and displays the following error message: Circular links are not allowed .
Delete task dependencies
To remove a dependency, hover over the connection arrow, click it, and select Delete .
In brief
- Task dependencies create visual relationships between tasks in a project.
- Dependency types control task order and automatically adjust task dates when you change the Start or End date of the main task.

titre: Task efficiency
sections: Task efficiency
Bitrix24 tracks assigned tasks to measure how many are completed on time and without objections.

The Efficiency indicator helps you evaluate performance for individual employees and teams. When performance is measurable, it is easier to improve. You can also use this metric as part of your KPI framework to support fair decisions about promotions and rewards.
What the efficiency indicator shows
Efficiency is calculated based on tasks where an employee is listed as the responsible person or a participant.
Efficiency = 100 – (Objections / Total in progress) * 100 Efficiency starts at 100% by default.
An employee completed 10 tasks during the month. Two tasks were overdue.
The employee’s efficiency score is 80%. To increase the score, tasks should be completed on time.
Where to view efficiency results
Go to Tasks and Projects and open the Efficiency tab.
The report shows:
- Total in progress — number of active tasks.
- Tasks completed — number of finished tasks.
- Tasks with objections — tasks that were overdue.
Use the filter to select the time period for the calculation.
How efficiency changes
- When you create a new task, the number of tasks in progress increases and efficiency may improve.
- If a task is overdue, the number of objections increases and efficiency decreases.
- If a task is created after the deadline has already passed, it does not affect efficiency.
- Tasks an employee creates for themselves are not included in efficiency calculations. This prevents artificially increasing the score.
Track employee efficiency
Managers can review team performance in the Supervising tab.
Project managers can also evaluate task efficiency within a project.
In brief
- The more tasks completed on time, the higher the efficiency score.
- Efficiency is not calculated when the task creator and responsible person are the same user.
- Managers can review employee efficiency at both team and project levels.

titre: Supervising option: How to track subordinates' tasks
sections: Supervising option: How to track subordinates' tasks
In Bitrix24, the head of the department can monitor how employees manage to complete tasks.
Go to the Tasks and projects section and click the Supervising tab.
The Supervising section is available only to users who are assigned as supervisors in the Bitrix24 company structure .
The page contains a list of subordinates and the number of tasks they work with.
All tasks are divided by the roles of employees in them:
- Responsible — the user is specified in the task as a responsible person.
- Set — the user is specified in the task as a created by person.
- Assisting — the user is specified in the task as a participant.
- Following — the user is specified in the task as an observer.
Use the filter to find an employee. Sort the list by efficiency and departments if you manage several departments.
In brief
- The Supervising option is a summary of tasks that subordinates work with.
- The Supervising section is available only to users who are assigned as supervisors in the Bitrix24 company structure.
- Supervisors of several departments can use the filter to find employees and departments.

titre: Check task upon completion
sections: Check task upon completion

Use the Check task upon completion option when you want to review a task before it closes. After the assignee marks the task as completed, the task is sent to you for approval. You can either approve the result or send the task back for changes.
1. Open the task.
2. Click Edit .
3. Next to the Deadline field, click Options .
4. Select the Check task upon completion checkbox.
5. Save the changes.
After the assignee completes the task, you will receive a notification.
If the result needs updates, return the task for revision. If everything looks good, accept the task as completed.
The task remains uncompleted until you review the result.
Turn on the Require task review on close option in the task settings.
After the assignee completes the task, the task moves to the Pending review status. The task stays open until you review the result.
To review the task:
- Tap Approve to mark the task as completed.
- Tap the X icon to send the task back for revision.

titre: Involvement in tasks
sections: Involvement in tasks
The Involvement in tasks section is designed for easier workload management. It shows a chart of the task schedule, making it easy to see everyone's workload.
To find it, go to the Tasks and Projects section > More > Involvement .
You'll see a chart of tasks. If an employee has tasks that overlap, you can click a small arrow next to their name to see all their tasks.
Use filters above the chart to view only those tasks that you need.
- Task status : Filter by any status, like pending, in progress, pending review, completed, or deferred.
- Department : Choose tasks from your department or any other in your company.
- Employee : View tasks for a specific user or everyone.
- Time range : Indicate the time period for which you want to view the workload.
You can view data for any period: day, week, or month. However, it should not exceed 90 days. If you set a longer period, Bitrix24 will automatically reduce it to 90 days.
If you set the time range for a specific month, the chart will also include tasks that start in that month but finish later.
In brief
- The Involvement in tasks section shows a chart of the task schedule, making it easy to see everyone's workload.
- It only shows tasks that have start and finish dates set in the Time planning section of the task settings.
- You can view data for any period: day, week, or month. However, it should not exceed 90 days.

titre: Reports in tasks: How to collect statistics on employees
sections: Reports in tasks: How to collect statistics on employees
Reports help you track tasks and analyze task data. Use them to measure employee performance and identify areas for improvement.
Go to Tasks and projects > More > Reports .
Reports are divided into two categories:
- Personal : Reports you create manually.
- Standard : Built-in report templates.
Personal reports
To create a report, click Add report .
Fill in the required fields. You can create reports for any employee and any reporting period. Both managers and employees can use these reports to review task statistics.
Task statuses in the report
- New : Tasks created during the selected reporting period.
- Open : Tasks started during the reporting period.
- In progress : Tasks with the Running or Waiting for execution status.
- Closed : Tasks completed during the reporting period.
- Overdue : Tasks that passed the deadline but are still incomplete.
- Evaluation : Tasks with a positive or negative rating.
- Efficiency (%) : The percentage of positively rated tasks compared to the total number of tasks in the report.
Standard reports
This section includes reports for different metrics. Report data updates automatically each time you open a report.
You cannot edit standard report templates. To create your own template based on a standard report, click Copy .
Standard reports in tasks
Import reports
You can import reports in CSV format. Click the import button and upload the file.
In brief
- Reports help you measure and improve employee performance.
- Manually created reports are called Personal reports.
- Built-in report templates are called Standard reports.
- You can import previously created reports in CSV format.

titre: Create reports on tasks

titre: Time tracking in tasks
sections: Time tracking in tasks

In Bitrix24, it's easy to track how much time is spent completing a task. Using the built-in timer, employees can log the periods they work on specific assignments. For example, they can start it in the morning and pause it during a meeting or a lunch break.

All data is automatically saved in the task form. This eliminates the need for participants to track time manually and allows the creator to see how long the team has worked on the task and evaluate each participant's contribution.
- Configure time tracking for a task
- Log time spent working on a task
- View the time tracking history and total time
- Add or edit time manually
Enable time tracking
The creator can enable time tracking when creating or editing a task.
1. Go to the Tasks and Projects section, create a new task, or open an existing one.
2. Click Time tracking .
3. Specify the time required to complete the task. This helps the assignee plan their work and allows you to compare planned versus actual time.
4. Disable the Time tracking for the task option if tracking the duration is unnecessary.
Log time spent working on a task
The assignee and participants can enable time tracking from the task form or the list.
Only one task can be tracked at a time. If you start the timer for a second task, the first one will automatically pause.
From the task form. This is convenient if you need to review the assignment and clarify details with the creator in the task chat before starting. Use the following buttons to track time:
- Start — begin tracking time. The time spent by the team on the task is displayed in the tracker.
- Pause — stop tracking time temporarily.
- Complete — the task will be closed, and time tracking will stop.

From the task list. Start and pause time tracking in the Deadlines, List, or Planner views. This is useful if you're already working on a task and want to start the timer without opening the task form.
To manage the timer, hover over the task form and click to start the task or to pause the timer.
View time tracking history
The time tracking history shows who worked on the task, when, and for how long. You can view the records in the task chat or the task form.
In the task chat , system messages display the history. When a participant starts the timer, a notification appears. When paused, a message shows the time spent on the task during that period.
In the task form , you can see how much time the entire team and each participant spent on the task.
1. Click the tracker — the block displays the total time spent on the task.
2. View the time tracking history — records are displayed chronologically.
3. Click the icons in the Total time block to see how much time each participant worked on the task.
Add or edit time manually
Add time. If you forgot to start the tracker or worked offline, you can manually add time to the task. These records will appear in the history and be included in the total task time.
1. Open the task and click the tracker.
2. Click Add record or Record .
3. Enter the time spent on the task and a comment. For example, describe what you accomplished during that time.
4. Save the changes.
Edit or delete a record. You can adjust the time logged for a task. For example, if you started the timer by mistake or forgot to stop it.
Hover over the record and select the desired action.
In brief
- In Bitrix24, you can track how much time employees spend on specific tasks. All data is automatically saved in the task form.
- The creator can enable time tracking when creating or editing a task.
- To set up time tracking, go to Tasks and Projects , create a new task, or open an existing one. Click Time tracking .
- You can start and pause the timer from the task form or the task list.
- Only one task can be tracked at a time. If you start tracking a second task, the timer for the first one will automatically pause.
- The time tracking history shows who worked on the task, when, and for how long. You can view the history in the task chat or the task form.
- If you forgot to start the tracker or worked offline, you can manually add time to the task. These records will appear in the history and be included in the total task time.
- Participants can edit or delete their records in the time tracking history.

titre: Task status summary
sections: Task status summary

Task status summaries help you capture key details such as agreements, progress, and final outcomes. Use this section to store text updates, files, and links in one place. This keeps information organized and helps the task creator review and approve work faster.

For example, a designer can upload logo drafts and explain which options to review. After approval, they can attach the final file. The task creator can see everything in one place and approve the result.
In this article:
- Require a task status summary to complete a task
- Add a task status summary
- View and edit task status summaries
Require a task status summary to complete a task
You can require a task status summary before a task can be marked complete. This ensures the work is finished and ready for review.
The following users can still complete a task without a summary:
- Account administrator
- Task creator and their supervisor
- Assignee’s and participants' supervisors

When you enable this option, the Task status summary is required section appears in the task. Any participant can add a summary there. Once a summary is added, the assignee can complete the task. Check task upon completion
You can require a task status summary when creating or editing a task.
When creating a task:
1. Open Tasks and Projects > Tasks .
2. Click Create > Detailed form .
3. Enter task details such as title, description, and deadline.
4. Click Task status summaries > Create .
When editing a task:
1. Open the task.
2. Click Task status summaries > Add task status summary .
3. To turn off the requirement, open the Task status summary is required section and select Three dots (...) > Don’t require task status summary .
You can only require a task status summary when editing a task.
1. Open Tasks and select a task.
2. Tap Three dots (...) > Task preferences (⚙️) .
3. Turn on Require task status summary . Turn it off to remove the requirement.
Add a task status summary
Task creators often ask for updates as text or files. Even if a summary is not required, participants can still add one to keep information organized.
You can add a task status summary in the Task status summaries section or from the task chat.
Using the Task status summaries section:
1. Click Task status summaries > Add task status summary .
2. Attach files if needed.
3. Click Send .
If summaries are optional, the required section will not appear. You can still:
1. Click Task status summaries .
2. Click Add task status summary to create more entries. There is no limit.
Using the task chat:
1. Send a message in the task chat.
2. Hover over the message and click Three dots (...) → Add to status summaries .
The system saves the original message. Edits will not change the saved summary.
You can add a task status summary using the Task status summaries button or the chat.
Using Task status summaries:
1. Open the task.
2. Scroll to the details and tap Task status summaries .
3. Add files and send the summary.
Using the chat:
1. Send a message and press and hold it.
2. Tap Task status summaries .
The saved summary does not change if the message is edited later.
View and edit task status summaries
All task status summaries are stored in the task.
- Participants can view all summaries and edit their own.
- The admin can delete any summary.
To edit or delete a summary, click Three dots (...) next to it and select an action.
1. Tap Three dots (...) next to a summary to edit or delete it.
2. Tap Add more to create another summary. There is no limit.
3. Tap Show more results to view all summaries.
In brief
- Task status summaries help you capture key information such as agreements, progress, and outcomes. Use this section to store text updates, files, and links in one place.

- To require a summary when creating a task, open the detailed form and click Task status summaries . The Task status summary is required section will appear. The assignee cannot complete the task without adding a summary.
- To add a summary in this section, click Add task status summary , enter the details, attach files if needed, and click Send .
- To add a summary from the task chat, send a message and select Three dots (...) > Add to status summaries .
- If a summary is not required, participants can still add updates. Click Task status summaries to add entries. To add more, click Add task status summary . There is no limit.
- Click Show more results to view all summaries.
- To edit or delete a summary, click Three dots (...) next to it and select an action.
- You can add, view, edit, and delete task status summaries in both the web version and the mobile app.

titre: Ping messages in tasks
sections: Ping messages in tasks
A ping message is a short notification requesting the status of a task. It can be sent to the assignee and task participants to clarify task progress.

For example, the creator sends a ping to the designer, the task assignee. The designer receives a notification and responds in the task chat, allowing the creator to understand the current stage of work.
In this article:
- Request a task status in the web version and mobile app
- View pings for task participants
Sending a task ping
1. Go to the Tasks and Projects section > Tasks .
2. Select the task.
3. Open the Menu (≡) , and click Ping .
If there are multiple tasks, you can request their statuses using group actions. Select the tasks in the list and click Select action > Ping > Apply .
1. Open the Bitrix24 mobile app and go to the Tasks tab.
2. Press and hold the task to open the menu, then select Ping .
The ping message will appear in the task chat, and the assignee and task participants will receive a notification.
How pings work for task participants
Notifications about ping messages are sent to participants responsible for completing the task.
- Creator — views all ping messages in the task chat. Creators do not receive notifications about their own pings, only about actions taken by other employees in the task.
- Assignees and task participants — receive a notification for each ping and view it as a separate message in the task chat.
- Observers — ping messages are automatically marked as read and do not affect task counters.
In brief
- Pings help request task statuses and record the request in the task form.
- You can send a ping from the task list: in the web version via the task menu, and in the mobile app by long-pressing the task.
- The assignee and task participants receive a notification about the ping and view it as a system message in the task chat.
- For observers, ping messages are automatically marked as read and do not affect task counters.

titre: Delete automation rules in tasks and projects
sections: Delete automation rules in tasks and projects
If you no longer need an automation rule, you can delete it.
Delete automation rules in tasks
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > Tasks .
2. Click Automation rules .
3. Select the automation rule you want to delete.
4. Click the X icon.
5. Save your changes.
Automation rules are available for Projects, Planner mode, and Task Statuses.
Delete automation rules in projects
You can delete automation rules in projects the same way as in tasks.
1. Go to the Projects tab.
2. Open the required project.
3. Click the X icon next to the automation rule.
4. Save your changes.
Only the account administrator or the project owner can delete automation rules in a project.

titre: AI Audio and Video Tasks
sections: AI Audio and Video Tasks

AI Audio and Video Task is a new feature in Bitrix24 that uses artificial intelligence. AI recognizes assignments in voice and video messages. It identifies the assignee, the deadline, formulates checklists, and automatically creates tasks.
Assignments are no longer lost in chats. Everything you say in voice or video messages is captured in tasks, helping the team stay on track.
1. Go to Settings > Bitrix24 Settings .
2. Open CoPilot Settings > Chat with CoPilot .
3. Enable the Auto create tasks from audio messages and video notes option.
With AI, you can create tasks in personal and group chats, your notes, projects, and channels.
1. Open the desired chat, channel, or project.
2. Press and hold the microphone or camera icon to record a message.
3. Release the button to send the message. AI will recognize it as an assignment and automatically create a task.
When creating a task, AI automatically fills in the main fields:
- Title — generated based on the meaning of the voice message.
- Description — contains the transcribed text of the assignment.

- Assignee — determined by context: in one-on-one chats, it’s the person you sent the message to. In group chats, it’s the person mentioned in the message. If AI cannot identify the assignee, the task is assigned to the creator.
- Deadline — taken from the voice message. If no deadline is mentioned, it defaults to 5 business days.
- Checklists and priority — added if you list steps or emphasize urgency and importance.

After the task is created, a notification will appear in the chat, indicating that CoPilot has created it. You can open the task and configure additional tools: specify participants, add files, and more.
In brief
- AI Audio and Video Tasks is a new task creation feature in Bitrix24 that uses artificial intelligence to recognize assignments in voice messages and create tasks automatically.
- You can create tasks in personal and group chats, projects, and channels.
- AI automatically recognizes the content of the voice or video message and fills in the task fields: title, description, assignee, deadline, and priority.
- After the task is created, a notification appears in the chat. You can open the task and configure additional tools: specify participants, add files, and more.

titre: Task templates
sections: Task templates
Task templates let you create tasks with preset settings. These settings can include the description, deadline, assignee, checklist, and more. Set up a template once, then reuse it anytime.

Templates work well for recurring tasks, such as onboarding new employees or preparing monthly reports. You do not need to re-enter details each time. The assignee gets a clear, structured task with all required steps.
In this article:
- Create task templates
- Create a task from a template
- Create a task with subtasks from a template
Create a task template
By default, all employees can create task templates. To restrict this, update the access settings.
Go to Tasks and Projects > More > Templates > Create . This opens the template form.
Enter a name . Enter a short, clear name. Example: Prepare sales report .
Add a description . Add instructions or required details. When users create a task from the template, they can edit the description without changing the template.
Example: In a Prepare monthly report template, describe the process, list required metrics, and define the format. In the task itself, a manager can add the reporting period and a link to the file.
Add an assignee . Select who will complete the task. You can change the assignee when creating a task without editing the template.
Assign this task to all new users . Enable this option to automatically create tasks from this template for every new employee. The new employee becomes the assignee.
Specify the task owner . You can set a task owner in the template. However, when someone creates a task, the task owner becomes the person who created it.
Add other participants . Add participants who work on the task. Add observers who track progress but do not take action.
Set a deadline . Set how long tasks should take. This deadline applies to every task created from the template. You can select a value or enter a custom one.
Example: If you set three days, each task must be completed within three days.

Add more options . You can also add a checklist, files, time tracking, or recurring task settings. These options help define steps, attach materials, track time, and repeat tasks on a schedule. Create a task
Set access permissions . Select who creates tasks from this template and who edits it.
1. In the lower-right corner of the form, click Access permissions .
2. Click Add and choose users or groups: all employees, specific users, a workgroup, or a department.
3. Set an access level:
1. Full access : Edit and delete the template.
2. Read-only access : View the template and create tasks.
4. Click Done .
After you create a template, it appears in the list and is ready to use. You can edit it anytime.
Edit a template
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > More > Templates .
2. Open the template.
3. Update the task settings, such as files or observers.
Changes apply only to new tasks. Existing tasks stay unchanged.
Create a task from a template
Users with access can create tasks from templates in several ways.
From the Tasks and Projects section . Click the arrow next to Create , select Task using template , and choose a template.
From a new task form . In Tasks and Projects , click Create . In the task form, select Detailed form . At the bottom, open the Templates block and choose a template.
From an existing task .
1. Open a task.
2. Click the three dots next to the task name.
3. Select Create using template .
4. Choose a template and click Menu (≡) > Create using template .
From the Templates section .
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > More > Templates .
2. Find a template by name or use the filter.
3. Click Menu (≡) > Create using template .
4. If needed, edit the task settings. This will not change the template.
5. Click Create .
Create a task with subtasks from a template
Add subtask templates to a main template to define the structure in advance.
Example: Annual sales report as the main template and Monthly sales report as a subtask template.
First, create a separate template for the subtask and link it to the main template.
Create a separate subtask template. You can do this in two ways:
- In the template list, find the main template and click Menu (≡) > Add subtask for template .
- In the template form, click the three dots and select Create subtask for template .
Fill in the subtask template. The system links it to the main template automatically. Click Create .
When you create a task from the main template, you can create subtasks automatically or manually.
Create a subtask automatically
1. Open the main template and click Create task .
2. Edit the task if needed.
3. Click Create .
4. Confirm that you want to create subtasks
If the template includes multiple subtask templates, the system creates all of them.
Create a subtask manually
1. In the template list, find the main template and click Plus (+) .
2. Select a subtask template.
3. Click Create task .
4. Edit the task if needed and click Create .
In brief
- Task templates let you create tasks with preset settings.
- To create a template, go to Tasks and Projects > More > Templates > Create .
- Create tasks from templates in several ways: from the main section, task form, template list, or an existing task.
- Add subtask templates to define the task structure in advance.

titre: Bitrix24 Flows: Get started
sections: Bitrix24 Flows: Get started

Bitrix24 introduces Flows , a tool for collecting and managing tasks from different departments. For example, if an employee needs software installed, they can add a task to a Flow. The system then distributes tasks to the responsible team members.
Flows. Jumpstart Guide Create a flow Create and find tasks in Flows Distribute tasks in the Flow
What you can do with Flows
- Collect tasks in one place and assign them automatically or manually
- Monitor employee workload
- Track task completion speed
- Identify bottlenecks and problem areas
Work with Flows
1. Go to Tasks and Projects
2. Open the Flows tab
Create a new Flow . Typically, a department manager creates a Flow. Each Flow shows:
- Task deadlines
- Linked project
- Number of team members
- Tasks at each stage
- Efficiency score
Create a flow
Efficiency is based on the percentage of tasks completed on time. If it drops below the set threshold, the Flow indicator turns red. The threshold is defined in the Flow settings.
Choose task distribution method . Tasks in a Flow are assigned to a team, not an individual. The Flow creator selects how tasks are distributed:
- Automatically
- Manually
Manual distribution . A manager assigns a responsible employee. This person distributes tasks to colleagues and is automatically set as the assignee for new tasks.
Flows in Bitrix24 mobile app
You can view Flows in the Tasks section of the Bitrix24 mobile app.
Mobile Flows show:
- Title and description
- Project
- Task deadlines
- Efficiency
- Administrator
You can enable and create a new Flow only in the web version.
In brief
- Use Flows to collect and distribute tasks across a department
- Find them in Tasks and Projects > Flows
- Any employee can add tasks to a Flow
- Tasks can be distributed automatically or manually
- You can create Flow tasks in both web and mobile apps
- You can only enable and create Flows in the web version

titre: Create a flow
sections: Create a flow
Use Flows to collect department or project tasks and distribute them to performers.
Bitrix24 Flows: Get started Create and find tasks in Flows Distribute tasks in the Flow
1. Go to the Tasks and Projects section.
2. Open the Flows tab.
There are two ways to create a Flow:
- Add a new one
- Select a ready-made template
Click New Flow or select a template.
Go to the Flow settings.
Fill in the information about the Flow
1. Add name and description.
2. Add employees who will be able to set tasks in the Flow.
3. Specify the Planned completion time in hours, days or months. The same deadline will automatically appear in all tasks of the Flow.
Configure Flow
1. Choose how to distribute tasks to employees:

- Use queue: Add employees to the task distribution queue. New tasks are automatically assigned to the next person in the list. After everyone has received a task, the cycle starts over from the first employee. This method works great for teams that need to keep the workload evenly balanced.

- Assign manually: All tasks are assigned to one selected employee, who can reassign them to others if needed. This approach is useful when a coordinator or manager needs to review tasks first and decide who should handle them. For example, in a marketing team, all tasks can go to the project manager first, who then distributes them among the designer, copywriter, and targeting specialist.

- Self-assign tasks: Employees choose tasks themselves when they are ready to start something new. This method works well for teams that prefer flexible task distribution instead of assigning tasks to specific employees. For example, in a Legal Department flow, tasks might be created by any employee in the company. Lawyers then open the task list and choose the next task when they’re available to take on a new request.

- Automation rule-based: Tasks are automatically created and assigned using automation rules or workflows. The assignee is defined in the settings—you can choose a specific employee or use a CRM item field, such as lead creator. Task parameters like project, deadline, and other fields come from the flow settings. For example, when a deal moves to the Contract stage, an automation rule creates a task in the Legal review flow and assigns it to the lawyer responsible for contract checks.
2. Configure additional task options:
- Allow the assignee to change the deadline
- Enable halfway point alert
- Submit task to creator for approval
3. Select a project for the flow.
4. To ensure colleagues create tasks in the flow only using a template, toggle the switch. Choose a template from the list or create a new one.
You can link multiple flows to a single project. If no project is specified, Bitrix24 will create one automatically.
Configure the control
1. Specify an administrator to control the Flow. He or she will receive notifications on tasks and changes settings.
2. Set up notifications for changes in Flow tasks: overload and low efficiency of the team. If efficiency drops, the Flow funnel will turn red.
3. Click Create Flow.
By default, any employee can create a flow. Bitrix24 administrators can limit this right in the task settings. Tasks: Access permissions

To edit, disable, or delete a Flow, click menu and select an action. The Disable option temporarily suspends the Flow and colleagues will not be able to assign tasks to it. You can re-enable the Flow in the future.
In brief
- Use Flows to collect department or project tasks and distribute them to performers.
- There are two ways to create a Flow: add a new one or select a ready-made template.
- Choose how to distribute tasks to employees: automatically by queue, manually, through self-assignment, or based on automation rules.
- The Flow administrator monitors the team's work.

titre: Create and find tasks in Flows
sections: Create and find tasks in Flows
You can create tasks for a specific department or workflow, such as onboarding new employees. The system assigns the task automatically, even if you don’t know who will complete it.
Bitrix24 Flows: Get started Create a flow Distribute tasks in the Flow
Create a task
You can create a task in a Flow in two ways.
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > Flows .
2. Select a Flow and click Create Task .
From other Bitrix24 tools
For example, you can create a task from a chat message:
1. Click Create task and select Flow in the top menu.
2. Enter the task name and the description, set additional settings: reminders, time tracking and others. An assignee, a task deadline and a project are configured automatically. Create a task
3. Click Add task .
Start working on tasks
If the Flow uses the Self-assign tasks option, team members get a notification when a new task is available.
To start a task:
1. Go to the Workgroups section and open the Flow .
2. Click on the Tasks tab and open the desired one.
3. Click Start .
Find a task
You can track tasks you need to start and tasks you created.
Open My Tasks in the Flow list. You will see the number of tasks next to each Flow you are part of. Click Tasks to open the list.
The system applies a filter automatically. It groups and sorts tasks by Flow and status.
In brief
- Flow tasks are assigned automatically, even if you don’t know the assignee.
- Go to Tasks and Projects > Flows > Create task.
- Find your tasks in My Tasks or in the general task list.

titre: Distribute tasks in the Flow
sections: Distribute tasks in the Flow

Use Flows to manage tasks for specific teams and processes. When a supervisor creates a Flow, they choose how tasks are assigned: automatically (queue), manually, via self-assignment, or with automation rules. For manual distribution, assign each task to a specific employee.
Bitrix24 Flows: Get started Create a flow Create and find tasks in Flows
Open a task in a Flow
1. Go to Tasks and Projects > Flows .
2. Select a Flow and open a task in My tasks .
By default, the user who creates tasks becomes the assignee. You can change this.
Change the assignee in one task
1. Open the task.
2. In the Assignee field, click the current user.
3. Remove them and select a new assignee.
Change the assignee in multiple tasks
1. Open Flow tasks and switch to List view .
2. Select the tasks.
3. Click Select action .
4. Choose Change assignee .

6. Click Apply .
List view in Tasks
In brief:
- Use Flows to group tasks by team or workflow.
- Employees assign tasks to a Flow, not directly to each other.

titre: CoPilot in Flows
sections: CoPilot in Flows
Bitrix24 Flows include an AI assistant called CoPilot. It analyzes your flow, finds issues that affect efficiency, and suggests ways to improve the process.
Bitrix24 Flows: Get started

CoPilot provides recommendations when flow efficiency drops below 80%. For example, it may suggest adding more details to a task template or redistributing workload between employees. If efficiency is high, CoPilot highlights what helped your team achieve these results.
To use CoPilot, an administrator must enable the CoPilot in Flows option in the account settings. Bitrix24 Settings: new single section
Click the CoPilot button next to the flow efficiency indicator to open recommendations.
CoPilot shows recommendations only if the flow has at least 10 tasks in any status. If there are fewer tasks, you will see sample recommendations.
You can turn any recommendation into a task or a meeting. Open the message menu and choose an action to start working on the suggestion.
In brief
- CoPilot analyzes flows and suggests improvements.
- Recommendations appear when efficiency is below 80%.
- CoPilot requires at least 10 tasks in the flow.
- You can create tasks or meetings based on recommendations.

titre: Invite a guest: how to add an external user to a task
sections: Invite a guest: how to add an external user to a task

Sometimes you need to collaborate with people outside your company, such as clients, partners, or freelancers. These users are external guests. They can work on tasks without getting access to other company data.
You can invite external guests to Bitrix24 tasks by email. This helps task participants share updates quickly while keeping other tasks private.
Create a task
Describe the task in detail so external guests clearly understand what they need to do.
Create a task
Assign a task role
An external guest can be a responsible person, participant, or observer.
To invite a guest:
1. Open the task.
2. Select a role.
3. Click Add > Invite Guest .
Send an invitation
Enter the guest’s email address, first name, and last name, then click Invite .
After you create the task, the guest receives an email with the task details.
How guests work with tasks
After guests receive the email invitation, they can open the task, follow updates, and leave comments.
Guests receive an email notification every time the task changes.
In brief
- External guests are invited users who do not work in your company.

- Guests can follow task updates and add comments.

titre: Team collaboration with Scrum
sections: Team collaboration with Scrum
Use Scrum in Bitrix24 to organize teamwork and distribute tasks clearly.
Bitrix24 SCRUM Guide
Create a Scrum team and schedule meetings
Go to Tasks and Projects > Scrum and create a Scrum team.
Bitrix24.Scrum
Start by scheduling team meetings. Scrum includes four meeting types:
- Daily Scrum A 15-minute meeting. The team reviews progress toward the sprint goal and adjusts upcoming work.
- Sprint Planning The team selects backlog items to complete during the sprint.
- Sprint Review The team presents completed work and reviews progress toward the product goal.
- Sprint Retrospective A recurring meeting at the end of a sprint. The team discusses what worked well and what to improve.
Select a meeting type and create a new event.
Create tasks in the backlog
Any team member can add tasks to the backlog.
- Click Create and choose a template.
- Or click + Task in the backlog.
Add an epic to group related tasks under a shared goal or context.
1. Click + Epic .
2. Enter a name and description.
3. Assign the epic to tasks in the backlog.
You can also view and manage epics in the Scrum items tab.
Define a Definition of Done (DOD) for tasks. This is a checklist that confirms when a task is complete.
Create a checklist and enable These items are required to be completed . Users must complete all checklist items before they can close the task.
Assign the checklist to the task.
- Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Development Team can view and manage tasks.
- Stakeholders can view tasks but cannot edit them.
Plan and start a sprint
1. Define the sprint goal.
2. Drag tasks from the backlog into the sprint.
3. Enter a sprint name and duration.
Estimate task effort using Story Points . Then start the sprint.
Monitor sprint progress
Track progress in the Active Sprint section.
The Task burndown chart shows how much work the team has completed.
- The vertical axis shows total Story Points .
- The horizontal axis shows days remaining in the sprint.
After several sprints, use the Team velocity tool to estimate how much work your team can complete in future sprints.
In brief
- Go to Tasks and Projects > Scrum and create a Scrum team.
- Schedule Scrum meetings.
- Add tasks to the backlog and assign epics and Definition of Done (DoD) .
- Define a sprint goal, move tasks to the sprint, and estimate with Story Points .
- Start the sprint and track progress in Active Sprint .
- Use the burndown chart and Team velocity to plan future work.

titre: Bitrix24 Scrum: Getting started
sections: Bitrix24 Scrum: Getting started

Scrum in Bitrix24 is a tool for managing projects. You break a large project into short cycles called sprints. Each sprint lasts from 1 to 4 weeks. After each stage, you see the results and determine the next steps.
Scrum is suitable for various teams, such as developers, marketers, project managers, and more.
In this article:
- Use Scrum to improve your work
- Create a Scrum team
- Set the team privacy level
- Add team members
- Edit a Scrum team
Use the main Scrum elements
Scrum helps teams focus on priority tasks, improve communication, and speed up work. Here are the main elements a Scrum team can use:

Sprint is a fixed period for completing tasks, lasting from 1 to 4 weeks. By the end of the sprint, the team delivers a finished result. If a task is too large, break it into parts. One part can be completed in one sprint, and another in the next.
Backlog is a list of tasks to be completed. To start working, move a task from the backlog to the sprint.

Definition of Done refers to pre-agreed criteria that determine when a task is considered complete. For example, the code is written, tested, and documented. Before submitting, the assignee checks these conditions, reducing errors and omissions.
Regular meetings keep the team updated, resolve issues quickly, and prevent problems. Scheduled meetings help maintain focus and ensure progress.
Create a Scrum team
Go to the Tasks and projects section > Scrum tab and click Create .
On the Features tab, choose a theme, specify the team name, set parameters, and add tools.
About the Scrum team:
- Name and description — specify what the team will work on.
- Theme and team icon— choose from the available options or upload your own.
Click Extended parameters to specify details and select tools.
Scrum team parameters:
- Project dates — specify the timeframe for completing the work.
- Sprint length — choose the period for completing the planned workload.
- Assignee — specify who will be the default assignee for tasks: the creator or the Scrum master.
- Tags — group Scrum teams by common themes. Use existing tags or create new ones to filter projects, like #marketing, #development. Tags in tasks and projects
Features . Select the Bitrix24 tools your Scrum team needs, like chat, tasks, Drive, and more. Click Continue .
Set the privacy level
Decide who can see and join the Scrum team. There are three privacy levels:
- Public — the Scrum team is visible to everyone, and any employee can join it.
- Private— the Scrum team is visible to everyone, but joining requires approval.
- Hidden — the Scrum team is not listed, and joining is by invitation only.
Click Continue .
Add members to the Scrum team
To ensure the Scrum team works effectively, assign roles and add team members:
- Product owner — responsible for goals and results. This can be a department head, director, or project manager.
- Scrum master — ensures the team follows Scrum rules.
- Development team — employees who complete Scrum tasks, such as developers, designers, and testers.
- Stakeholders — employees who observe the Scrum team’s work and results. They can provide feedback but cannot edit the Scrum. These may include colleagues from other departments or supervisors.
Click Continue.
Once the Scrum team is created, you can schedule meetings, add tasks to the backlog, and plan sprints. Team work using Scrum method
Edit a Scrum team
You can edit a Scrum team in the project form or the list of Scrum teams. Go to Tasks and projects > Scrum and find the desired team.
In the Scrum team list . Click Menu (≡) next to the desired Scrum team and select Edit .
In the Scrum team form .
1. Open the Scrum team form, click About Scrum .
2. Click Actions > Edit Scrum .
In brief
- Scrum in Bitrix24 is a tool for managing projects using a special methodology: break a large project into short cycles called sprints lasting 1 to 4 weeks.
- The number of Scrum teams depends on your plan.
- To create a Scrum team, go to the Tasks and projects > Scrum > Create .

titre: Automation rules and triggers in Bitrix24 Scrum
sections: Automation rules and triggers in Bitrix24 Scrum

Scrum is a flexible way for teams to work together. In Bitrix24, it helps you split big projects into short cycles called sprints. Each sprint lasts a few weeks, allowing the team to track progress, manage tasks, and quickly adjust to changes.
To save your team time on routine tasks, you can set up automation rules and triggers to complete some work automatically.
Automation rules perform actions when a task reaches a specific stage. For example, when a task moves to the Pending review stage, it can automatically send the task creator a message with a link.

Triggers track changes in tasks, like upcoming deadlines, status updates, or new comments. When a defined action occurs, the trigger moves the task to a different stage. For example, if a task's status switches to In progress , the trigger moves it to the corresponding stage. This helps the team see which tasks are active and which are still pending.
- Add automation rules and triggers
- Configure automation rules and triggers
Add automation rules and triggers
1. Go to Tasks and Projects .
2. Select Scrum .
3. Open the project you need.
4. Switch to the Active sprint tab.
5. Click Automation rules .
6. Click Create or + Add at the stage where you want to add the rule.
All Scrum team members can add automation rules and triggers, except those with the Stakeholder role.
Automation rules and triggers are grouped into several categories:
- For employee: Rules that automate internal team tasks, such as creating or updating tasks, sending notifications via chat or email, managing stages and statuses, and more.
- Custom automation rules: Rules and triggers from the Market, created by Bitrix24 partners to extend standard task management features.
- Triggers: Track deadlines and task changes.
Configure automation rules and triggers
After you add automation rules and triggers, you’ll need to set them up. They all share the same basic settings:
- Execution: Choose whether the rule runs right after the previous one or independently.
- Time: Decide if the action happens immediately or after a set time.
- Condition: Apply the rule or trigger only to certain tasks, like important or overdue ones. Conditions in automation rules
- Allow moving back to previous stage: If enabled, the trigger can move a task to an earlier stage, for example, from the last stage to the first. This option is available for triggers only.

Other settings depend on the specific automation rule or trigger. For example, the Create task rule requires you to select participants, while the Add notification rule requires you to enter the message text.
You can add multiple automation rules and triggers to a single stage, but each one must be configured separately. For example, at the Testing stage, you can set up two automation rules:
- Add notification: When a task reaches this stage, a notification is sent in Bitrix24 to the supervisor to review the work.
- Change stage: If only one day remains before the deadline, the task is moved to the Urgent stage. This helps the team quickly identify priority tasks and take action in time.
In brief

- Scrum is a flexible way for teams to work together. In Bitrix24, it helps you split big projects into short cycles called sprints. Each sprint lasts a few weeks, allowing the team to track progress, manage tasks, and quickly adjust to changes.
- To save your team time on routine tasks, you can set up automation rules and triggers to complete some work automatically.
- Automation rules perform actions when a task reaches a specific stage, such as sending notifications, creating tasks, adding participants, and more.
- Triggers track changes in tasks, like upcoming deadlines, status updates, or new comments. When a defined action occurs, the trigger moves the task to a different stage.
- To configure automation rules, go to Tasks and Projects > Scrum , open the project you need, switch to the Active sprint tab, and click Automation rules .
- All Scrum team members can configure automation rules and triggers, except those with the Stakeholder role.

titre: FAQ: New tasks in Bitrix24
sections: FAQ: New tasks in Bitrix24

New tasks in Bitrix24 are more than just fields and comments. They are a single workspace where everything happens—discussion, action, and results. The task chat is now the central place for communication and process coordination. Your team can make calls, share files, and make decisions without losing context or switching between different tools. New task form
In this article:

How to delete a task chat if you don’t need it
You can’t delete a task chat. It’s built into the task and is used for communication and tracking changes.
However, you can adjust the chat width. Just drag the divider between the panels. Your preferred width will be saved automatically for all tasks.
Where to find old task comments
To view old comments, open the task and click Previous comments in the chat. These comments are read-only.
How to move old comments into the chat
To move information from old comments into the chat, copy the text you need and post it as a new message in the task chat.
How to write a long comment with images in the text
In new tasks, all discussions happen in the chat. You can write long messages, but images can only be attached as separate files—they can’t be embedded directly in the text yet.
To include images with a long comment, try one of these options:
- Split your text into multiple messages and attach images between them.
- Use the Task status summaries section, where images can be embedded directly in the text.
How to find a task in the chat list
Currently, you can’t search for tasks by name or use filters in task chats. These options are under development.
Why task updates don’t appear under Notifications
When a task is updated, notifications appear as follows:
- A new message and counter appear in the task chat.
- The Tasks and projects section shows a counter for new events.
To see all updates, open the task chat list—it contains every task update.
Find a task in the chat list

To find a task in the chat list, go to the Messenger section and select Task chats . Start typing the task name in the search bar above the chat list. A list of results will appear. Select the desired task chat from the results.
Why I can’t delete a file from a task
Only the person who uploaded a file can delete it. If your colleague uploaded the document, only they can remove it.
Why files appear twice in the task description and the Files section
Sometimes the same file shows up in both places. This happens because of the interface update.
Why a document shared in the task chat doesn’t appear in the Files section
Files sent in the task chat are saved only in the chat. Only documents uploaded directly to the task form show up in the Files block.
To have a file in both the chat and the Files section, manually add it to the Files block.
Why mentioning a colleague in the chat doesn’t add them to the task
Mentioning someone in the chat does not automatically add them as a task participant. To include them, manually assign a role in the left section of the task form.
Administrators can see all tasks, while supervisors can see tasks assigned to their subordinates. If a supervisor writes a message in the task chat, the system automatically adds them as an observer.
How to copy a task link
You can copy a task link in two ways:
- From your browser’s address bar.
- From the task form by clicking the Copy link icon.
How to create a recurring task
Recurring tasks are based on templates.
1. Go to Tasks and projects > Templates .
2. Create a new template or open an existing one.
3. Enable the Recurring task option and set up the schedule.
Recurring tasks
How to highlight part of the task description as a quote
Automatic quoting from the task description isn’t available yet. To highlight text, copy the desired fragment and paste it into the chat manually.
How to format text inside a task
In the visual editor, you can highlight text, create lists, and add links.
Select the text, and the formatting panel will appear.
Why the task chat didn’t appear in the chat list
A task chat appears when:
- You create a new task.
- You are added as a participant.
- There’s activity in the task, such as completing a checklist item.
If the chat doesn’t appear, perform any action in the task—it will then be created.
Where to see the task's creation date
Open the task form and hover over the task status. The creation date and time will be displayed.
How to mute the task chat
Task chat sounds follow the task’s notifications. If you turn off notifications for a task, its chat will also be muted.
To mute a task:
1. Open the task.
2. Click the icon next to the task name.
3. Select Mute .
How to enable "Require approval upon completion"
1. Open the task.
2. Click Settings (⚙️) next to the Deadline field.
3. Enable the Require approval upon completion option.
How to prevent the assignee from changing the deadline
1. Open the task.
2. Click Settings (⚙️) next to the Deadline field.
3. Disable the Assignee can change deadline option.
Where to view the task history
You can view a task’s history in two places:
- Task chat
- Task history section in the sidebar
These sections record key actions, such as deadline changes, checklist item completion, or status updates.
How to add results to a task
To specify a task result before completing it, you can do one of the following:
- Use the Task status summary is required block—add a description or attach a report file manually.
- In the task chat—send a message and mark it as a task status summary.
This helps you capture not just the final result but also important intermediate outcomes, like key stages or partial project results.
When tasks are created from voice messages
AI automatically creates a task if a voice message contains an assignment—for example, “Prepare a report on closed deals for the week.” If there’s no assignment, AI simply transcribes the message.
You can disable AI Audio Tasks in Bitrix24 settings. This lets you manually transcribe messages and decide whether to create a task based on the results.
Why I can’t create a task using AI voice commands

AI can create tasks from voice messages and video notes only if the Auto create tasks from audio messages and video notes option is enabled in Bitrix24 settings. If the account administrator has disabled this option, tasks won’t be created.
AI audio and video tasks are available only in the Bitrix24 mobile app. AI Audio and Video Tasks
How to disable automatic task creation from voice messages
Account administrators can turn off automatic AI task creation from audio and video messages. Here's how:
1. Go to Settings > Bitrix24 settings .
2. Open CoPilot preferences > Chat with CoPilot .
3. Disable Auto create tasks from audio messages and video notes .
4. Click Save .

titre: FAQ: Tasks in Bitrix24
sections: FAQ: Tasks in Bitrix24

Bitrix24 tasks help organize team work: assign tasks and manage large projects. Tasks allow tracking employee progress, controlling deadlines, and distributing responsibilities. We gathered frequently asked questions about tasks.
In this article:
- Why not all tasks appear in the report
- What access employees have to task templates on different plans
- Why a recurring task shows an incorrect deadline
- Why the administrator doesn't see all task templates
- Why notifications are disabled for task observers
Why not all tasks appear in the report
The report for the specified period includes tasks that are:
- Created and completed within this period
- Completed within this period
- Created before the period starts and remain in progress
- Created before the period starts and completed after it ends
Reports in tasks: How to collect statistics on employees
What access employees have to task templates on different plans
Extended access permission settings for task templates are available on Professional and Enterprise plans. Other plan users have standard access permissions to task templates:
- All users can create task templates.
- Users can view and manage only the templates they created. This rule applies even if other employees are assigned as the creator and assignee.
Bitrix24 plans Tasks: Access permissions
Why a recurring task shows an incorrect deadline
In recurring tasks, the deadline is calculated from the task creation date. If the template has the "Skip weekends" option enabled, the deadline will consider the working hours set in Bitrix24.
The task deadline does not account for the user's time zone and is calculated based on server time.
Why the administrator doesn't see all task templates
By default, Bitrix24 administrators can only see task templates they created or have access to. To view all templates, enable Admin mode .
Open your profile and click Administrator > Admin mode .
Why notifications are disabled for task observers

Notifications for task observers are muted by default. Observers don't receive updates but see a gray counter for unread comments. This helps avoid unnecessary distractions since observers aren’t directly involved in the task but can check its progress at any time.
To turn on notifications, open the task, click Menu (☰) and select Unmute .

titre: CRM implementation steps
sections: CRM implementation steps

Bitrix24 CRM is a powerful tool, but it requires proper setup to work well. Every business has different goals. A small family business and a large company will use CRM differently. The implementation process helps you adjust Bitrix24 to fit your needs.
Follow these steps to get started.
Configure CRM for your business

Statuses and dropdowns Go to CRM > Settings > CRM Settings > Start point > Statuses and Dropdowns . Set up deal stages, contact sources, and company industries. This is a required step for working with CRM. Statuses and dropdowns in CRM
Products Go to CRM > Inventory > Products . Add your products or services. Organize them into sections to find items faster. Product catalog in CRM
Units and taxes Set units of measurement in CRM > Settings > CRM Settings > Units of Measurement . Set tax types and rates in CRM > Settings > CRM Settings > Taxes . Units of measurement Taxes in CRM

Email templates Go to CRM > Settings > CRM Settings > Email > Email Templates . Create templates for common emails. For example, greetings or signatures. You can also insert dynamic data like customer name, company name, or deal amount. Email templates in CRM
Company details Go to CRM > Settings > CRM Settings > Start point > My Company Details . Add your company information. New invoices and documents will include this data automatically. Company details

Invoice and estimate templates Go to CRM > Settings > CRM Settings > Payment options > Payment systems . Customize invoice and estimate templates for daily use. Invoice (an old version) and estimate templates
Access permissions Go to CRM > Settings > Access permissions > CRM . Define user roles and control who can access specific data. Access Permissions in CRM
Add data to CRM
After setup, start adding your data.

Get started with CRM
Bitrix24 helps you manage the full sales cycle. From the first contact to closing deals and processing payments.
Start by collecting customer data. Then guide leads through each stage until you close the deal.
If you want a simpler process, use the Simple CRM mode to skip leads and work directly with deals. CRM modes
Integrate third-party services
You can connect other tools you use in your business. Bitrix24 supports many integrations through apps. Find and install Bitrix24 Market applications
Setting up Bitrix24 correctly helps your business grow and keeps your processes organized.

titre: Choose a CRM mode
sections: Choose a CRM mode

Bitrix24 offers two CRM modes: Classic CRM (with leads Leads are potential customers. They can come from website inquiries, inbound calls, social media interactions, and more. ) and Simple CRM (without leads). The Simple CRM mode is enabled by default.

Classic CRM allows you to separate potential and existing customers, set up lead forms, and create stages. This mode is suitable for large companies with busy sales departments. Lead analytics help identify customer sources. Leads overview

The Simple CRM mode functions without leads. Any customer request, call, or email immediately becomes a deal and a contact or company. This mode is ideal for small sales teams focused on processing inquiries and recording customer contacts. Deals overview
Select a CRM mode

To choose the suitable mode, you can use the web version or the Bitrix24 mobile app. Only Bitrix24 administrators and employees with permission to change CRM settings can do this. Access Permissions in CRM
1. Go to CRM .
2. Open Leads or Deals .
3. Click Settings (⚙️) .
4. Select CRM mode .
5. Choose the suitable mode.
1. Go to CRM .
2. Open Leads or Deals .
3. Tap the three dots (...) in the top right corner.
4. Select CRM mode .
5. Choose the suitable mode.
Switch CRM modes
You can switch modes anytime. For example, if your customer base grows and you need to categorize them, switch from Simple to Classic CRM.
Switching from Classic to Simple CRM will automatically convert all active leads into deals and customers.
1. Go to CRM .
2. Open Leads or Deals .
3. Click Settings (⚙️) .
4. Select CRM mode .
5. Choose the desired mode.
When switching from Classic to Simple CRM, configure the deal creation mode to determine how active leads are converted.
Create a customer . Decide whether to create a contact or company with each deal. You can select both items.
Choose a deal pipeline . If you have several pipelines, choose which one to create deals in. Sales pipelines

Don't close activities after conversion . If this option is enabled, any activities planned in the lead form will stay open after conversion to a deal, so you can keep working on them in the deal form.
If it's disabled, all activities will automatically be completed during the conversion. Universal activity in CRM
1. Go to CRM .

Move activities to deals . If this option is enabled, any activities planned in the lead form will stay open after conversion to a deal, so you can keep working on them in the deal form.
If it's disabled, all activities will automatically be completed during the conversion.
In brief
- Bitrix24 offers two CRM modes: Classic CRM (with leads) and Simple CRM (without leads). The Simple CRM mode is enabled by default.

- Classic CRM allows you to separate potential and existing customers, set up lead forms, and create stages. This mode is suitable for large companies with busy sales departments. Lead analytics help identify customer sources.

- The Simple CRM mode functions without leads. Any customer request, call, or email immediately becomes a deal and a contact or company. This mode is ideal for small sales teams focused on processing inquiries and recording customer contacts.
