titre: CRM Cleanup
sections: CRM Cleanup

When your Bitrix24 account runs out of space, new leads, deals, contacts, and other items cannot be created. The CRM Cleanup tool helps quickly identify what is taking up space and remove unnecessary data, such as old deals or leads.
- Identify what is taking up space in CRM
- Delete unnecessary items
Identify what is taking up space in CRM
1. Go to the CRM section > More > Settings > CRM Settings .
2. Select Other > Space Usage .
3. Click Start Scan.
The scan may take a few minutes depending on the amount of data. Do not close the page during the scan. Otherwise, not all records will be processed.
After the scan, you will see a table with the results showing which data is taking up space. Use this table to determine what can be deleted, such as old deals with documents or activities.
The Other section includes additional data not related to primary CRM items, such as company details, CRM forms, and other records.

You can customize which columns are displayed in the table. This helps identify which sections take up the most space and prioritize what to clean up first, such as deals with documents or leads with activities and emails.
1. Click Settings (⚙️) in the top-left corner of the table.
2. Select the desired fields.
3. Click Apply .
Delete unnecessary items
The CRM Cleanup tool helps quickly delete unnecessary data, such as old deals or leads. Data backup and recovery
Click the Menu (≡) icon next to the desired item type and select what to delete:
- All items. For example, Delete deals . CRM will completely clear the deal list.
- Activities and history for an item. For example, Delete activities and history for deals . CRM will clear stage transitions, field changes, task actions, comments, and more.
To delete specific items only, set filters by Creation Date and Stage Group. For example, you can delete lost deals from the previous year.
1. Click Filter.
2. Specify the parameters.
3. Click Search.
After cleaning up space, repeat the scan to view updated information.
In brief
- When your Bitrix24 account runs out of space, new leads, deals, contacts, and other items cannot be created.
- The CRM Cleanup tool helps quickly identify what is taking up space and remove unnecessary data.
- Only Bitrix24 administrators and employees with the appropriate permissions can delete CRM items.
- To access the Cleanup tool, go to CRM > More > Settings > CRM Settings > Other > Space Usage.
- The results table shows which data takes up the most space. Use it to determine what to delete first.
- To delete unnecessary data, click Menu (≡) next to the desired item type and select what to delete: all items or activities and history.
- To delete specific items, set filters by Created on and Stage Group. For example, you can delete lost deals from the previous year.

titre: Reassign CRM items from dismissed users
sections: Reassign CRM items from dismissed users

If an employee leaves the company, it becomes necessary to assign the CRM items they handled to other employees. This ensures that the ongoing needs and satisfaction of the customers are met without any disruption or inconvenience.
Change responsible person in leads, deals, contacts, companies, and estimates
To change the responsible person in leads, deals, contacts, companies, or estimates,
1. Go to CRM and open the needed section. In our example, it's Deals . Switch to the List view to proceed.
2. Click on the search bar and add the Responsible person field.

3. If the employee has not been dismissed from your Bitrix24 yet, select them from the general user list. If the employee has already been dismissed, switch to the Dismissed persons tab. It shows dismissed employees who still have CRM items assigned to them.
4. Select an employee and click Search to view the list of CRM items they worked on.

5. Tick all or some of the items in the list, click Select action at the bottom, and select Change responsible person . Enable the For All option to apply the action to all items selected by the filter, including items on other pages.
6. Select an employee to assign the chosen CRM items to, then click Apply .

It is important to change the responsible person even for those deals and leads that have been completed. The new responsible person will receive calls and notifications if there is a need to resume them.
Change responsible person in activities and invoices
When the deals are assigned to another employee, it is necessary to do the same for activities linked to these deals as well.
To change the responsible person in activities,
1. Go to CRM > More > My activities .
2. If the employee has not been dismissed from your Bitrix24 yet, click on the search bar and add the Responsible person field. Select the employee from the general user list.
3. Tick the activities in the list, click Select action at the bottom, and select Assign responsible person .
4. Select an employee to assign the chosen activities to, then click Apply .
Note that the method of changing the responsible person differs in the Invoices section. Open the invoice form and select another employee in the Responsible person field.
If the employee has already been dismissed from your Bitrix24, you'll need to hire them back for a while. To do this,
1. Go to Employees and open the Employees tab.
2. Click on the search bar and apply the default Dismissed filter.
3. Open the employee's profile and click Hire in the actions menu.
4. After that, go to CRM, find their invoices or activities, and change the responsible person in them.
5. Don't forget to dismiss the employee from your Bitrix24 again after it's done. Dismiss users
In brief
- When an employee leaves the company, assign the CRM items they handled to other employees.
- Replace the dismissed responsible person in leads, deals, contacts, companies, estimates, invoices, and activities.
- After the deals are assigned to another employee, do the same for activities linked to these deals as well.

titre: Disable showing CRM calls in calendar

1. Go to CRM .
2. Expand More .
3. Click Settings and select CRM settings .
4. Open the Other tab on the left.

6. Open the Activities tab.
7. Disable the Create calendar events for all calls option.
8. Click Apply at the bottom.
Keep only the events in your calendar that are important for your work.

titre: CRM History
sections: CRM History
The CRM history logs key changes to CRM items, such as exporting contacts or updating field values. Use it to track activity related to clients and deals.
The Bitrix24 administrator can view all changes in CRM history. Other users can only see changes for items they have access to. Access Permissions in CRM
In this article:
- What changes appear in history
- Find a record in history
- Delete a record from history
Go to the CRM section > More > History .
What changes appear in history
By default, the history includes the following changes.
- Actions with CRM items.
- Viewing a CRM item form.
- Exporting a CRM item form.
- Changes to fields such as name, deal stage, responsible person, comment, status, phone, work email, type, source, and completion date.
- Adding or removing links to other CRM items: contact, company, lead, deal, invoice, estimate, or SPA.
Actions in the timeline
- Creatу activities such as tasks, calls, emails, or documents.
- Send emails.
- Delete emails from the timeline.
Actions with products
- Add a product.
- Change product amount or quantity.
- Change the calculation mode of the Amount field.
You can disable specific history events if needed:
1. Go to Settings > CRM Settings .
2. Select Other > Other Settings .
3. Open the History tab, choose the events to track, and click Apply .
Find a record in history
Use list settings and filters to find records faster.
Configure the list
1. Open Settings (⚙️) in the top-left corner.
2. Select the fields you want to display.
3. If you are an administrator, choose:
1. Apply selection to me — only you see the changes.
2. Apply selection to everyone — all employees see the changes.
4. Click Apply .
Click Default to reset the view. All fields except ID will be visible.
Configure filters
Use filters to narrow down results.
- ID — Enter the item ID to see its history.
- To find the ID, open the item (for example, a deal) and check the URL. Example: https://b24-abc.bitrix24.com/crm/deal/details/123/ — here, 123 is the ID.
- CRM item — Select an item from the list if you don’t know the ID.
- Entity — Filter by item type: lead, contact, company, deal, estimate.
- Type — Choose the type of change: custom, changes, email, view, export, delete, linked entities.
- Event type — Select events such as information, phone call, or email sent.
- Description — Search by keyword or phrase.
- Created by — Filter by the employee who made the change.
- Date — Select a specific date or range.
Delete a record from the CRM history
Only an administrator can delete history records.
1. Click Menu (≡) > Delete .
2. Click Continue .
In brief:
- CRM history tracks major changes to CRM items.
- Administrators can see all changes. Other users only see changes they have access to.
- By default, history includes actions with CRM items, products, and timeline events. You can change this in CRM settings.
- Use list settings and filters to find records quickly.
- Only administrators can delete history records.

titre: Create and configure auto numbering templates in CRM
sections: Create and configure auto numbering templates in CRM

Auto numbering templates assign a unique number to each document. Numbers can include digits, dates, prefixes, and other values. This helps you avoid duplicates, find documents faster, and keep records organized.
You can set up separate numbering for documents, invoices, and estimates. Leads and deals use a default numbering format that you can’t change.
In this article:
- Create an auto numbering template
- Configure an auto numbering template
- Edit or delete an auto numbering template
- Check and change the next number
- Fix numbering issues
Create an auto numbering template
You can create a template in CRM settings or from a document template.
In CRM settings
1. Go to CRM > More > Settings > CRM settings > Auto numbering template .
2. Select the item: documents, invoices, or estimates.
3. Click Create auto numbering template .
In a document template
1. Go to CRM > Deals and open any deal.
2. Click Document > Add new template .
3. Select a template and click Edit .
4. Click Create next to Use auto numbering template .
Configure an auto numbering template
Set basic parameters. Give the template a clear name. Then add and arrange the elements you want in the number.
Sequential numbers . A sequential number increases with each new document (1, 2, 3, and so on). Use it when you need a simple numbering system based on the order documents are created.
Sequential number settings
If you choose Sequential numbers in a template, configure these options:
Start sequential numbering with — Set the first number in the sequence (for example, 101).
Increment sequential numbers by — Set how much the number increases each time. For example, if you set it to 3, the sequence goes 101, 104, 107.
Sequential number length — Set the total number of digits. For example, a length of 3 formats numbers as 001, 002.
Padding character — Add a leading character if the number is shorter than the set length. For example, with a length of 2 and padding set to 0, numbers appear as 01, 02, 03.

Automatic numbering template activity period — Choose when numbering resets: continuously, daily, monthly, or yearly. If you reset numbers regularly, include the date ( Current day, month, and year + Sequential number ) to avoid duplicates.
Time zone — By default, the system uses server time. Select your time zone to control when numbering resets and avoid overlaps.
Use continuous numbering across all of my companies — Enable this to share one sequence across all companies. Disable it to keep separate sequences for each company.
Additional elements
You can combine sequential numbers with other elements:
Current day, month, or year — Adds the document creation date. Use this to track when documents were created.
Random number — Adds a random mix of digits and uppercase letters (for example, 4C2FW). Use this when you need less predictable numbers.
Prefix — Adds text or numbers at the beginning (for example, DOC). Use it to identify document types, projects, or departments.
ID — Uses the ID of the related CRM item (such as a deal or lead). This helps link documents to specific records.
My company ID — Adds your company’s ID. Useful if you manage multiple legal entities. Add company details
Client ID — Adds the ID of the selected contact or company. Use it to quickly find documents for a specific client.
Edit or delete an auto numbering template
You can manage auto numbering templates in CRM settings. To edit or delete a template, select it from the list and click Edit or Delete .
In a document template, you can only edit a template:
1. Select the template from the list.
2. Click Configure .
Check and change the next number
If you need to continue numbering from another system or set your own sequence, you can manually update the next document number.
For templates shared across multiple companies:
1. Open the template in edit mode.
2. Click Edit current number .
A panel opens on the right. It shows the next number for each company.
The Numbering template key column displays company IDs:
- Company_ID_ — documents without a linked company.
- Company_ID_1 — documents for the company with ID 1.
To find a company ID, go to CRM > Settings > My company details . Company details
To update the next number:
1. Select a company.
2. Click Edit .
3. Enter a new number in the Next number will be column.
4. Save the changes.
Fix incorrect document numbering
If you see unexpected numbers when creating documents, the numbering setup may be incorrect.
Common reasons
- Use continuous numbering across all of my companies is not enabled.
- You added a company after setting up numbering. This resets the sequence.
- You switched the default seller to another company. This also resets numbering.
- You added a company and then deleted it.
- You enabled Use continuous numbering across all of my companies after creating templates.
How to fix it
Create a new template, set the correct starting number, and enable Use continuous numbering across all of my companies if needed.
In brief
- Auto numbering templates can include numbers, dates, and other values. Customize them for documents, invoices, and estimates.
- You can create and edit templates in CRM settings and document templates.
- Combine different elements to match your company’s needs.
- If numbering breaks, create a new template, set the correct starting number, and enable Use continuous numbering across all of my companies .

titre: Link deals, contacts and companies
sections: Link deals, contacts and companies
A deal is a key step when working with a customer. Every deal starts with communication, whether you’re working with an individual or a company representative.
How deals, contacts, and companies are connected

The standard workflow links one contact to one company and one deal. Use this option when converting a lead by selecting Deal + Contact + Company mode. The system will automatically connect all three items.
This is not the only workflow in CRM. For example, one person can work for multiple companies. In the contact form, you can see links to all companies associated with that person.

Companies usually have multiple employees. You may work with several representatives from the same company at the same time. In this case, the company form shows all employees, and the deal can include multiple contacts.
Convert leads
To link a company and contacts:
1. Open the CRM form. Select a company from the field menu or create a new one.
2. A contact can be linked to more than one company. Click Add participant to add another company.
A deal can include multiple contacts but only one company. When you link a company to a deal, all contacts from that company are automatically added to the deal form.
If you don’t need all contacts, remove the extra ones using the cross icon.
If you select the same company in another deal, only the contact you kept last time will be added.
You can also customize the Client field. Click the gear icon.
In brief
- The standard workflow links one contact to one company and one deal. Use Deal + Contact + Company mode when converting a lead.
- Companies usually have multiple employees, and you can work with several representatives at the same time.
- Open the CRM form. Select a company or create a new one.
- A contact can be linked to multiple companies. Click Add participant to add another company.
- A deal can include multiple contacts but only one company. When you link a company, all its contacts are added automatically.

titre: Delete CRM entities
sections: Delete CRM entities
In Bitrix24, you can delete unnecessary CRM items. This helps to keep the data in CRM up to date, frees up space and makes it easier to find information.
To delete CRM items, employees must have access permissions. They can be configured by CRM administrator or Bitrix24 administrator.
Access Permissions in CRM
Deleted items first go to the recycle bin. They are stored there for 30 days and then automatically deleted. During this time, you can restore items or delete them manually.
CRM Recycle Bin
- from the list,
- from the Kanban,
- from the CRM form,
- from the CRM recycle bin.
Delete from the list
In the list, you can delete a specific CRM item or several items at once.
To delete a specific item, click the Menu icon - Delete .
It is convenient to delete several items in a list at once. To do this:
1. Filter the items you want to delete. For example, by creation date, amount, and other parameters. You can skip this step if the items are easy to find in the list without sorting.
2. Select the items.
3. To select items on all pages at once, check the For All box.
4. Click Delete .
Delete from the Kanban
You can delete one or more items in the Kanban.
1. Switch to the kanban view.
2. Select CRM forms.
3. Click Delete or move the forms to the Delete stage at the bottom of the kanban.
Delete from the form
You can delete an item directly from the CRM form. To do this, click Settings - Delete .
Delete from the CRM recycle bin
Deleted CRM items first go to the recycle bin. They are automatically deleted from it after 30 days. To avoid waiting a month, you can delete them manually, for example, to free up space in CRM.
To manually remove items from the recycle bin:
1. Go to the CRM section - More - Recycle bin.
2. Filter the items you want to delete. You can skip this step if the items are easy to find in the list without sorting.
3. Select the items you want to delete.
4. To select items on all pages at once, check the For All box.
5. Click Delete .
In brief:
- In Bitrix24, you can delete unnecessary CRM items. This helps to keep the data in CRM up to date, frees up space and makes it easier to find information.
- CRM items can be deleted from the list, the Kanban, and an item form.
- You can delete a single item or several items at once.
- Deleted CRM items first go to the recycle bin. They are automatically deleted after 30 days. To avoid waiting a month and free up space in CRM, you can delete them from the recycle bin manually.
- Group actions in CRM
- Search for CRM items using a filter

titre: Recycle bin in CRM
sections: Recycle bin in CRM
The CRM Recycle Bin is a temporary storage for deleted deals, contacts, companies, and other items. It helps to:
- Restore accidentally deleted information
- Free up space by permanently deleting unnecessary records
The account administrator views all deleted items in the CRM Recycle Bin. Other user only see the items they deleted.
Items are stored in the Recycle Bin for 30 days. Then they are automatically deleted at a rate of 100 items per day. If more items are deleted in a day, the storage period will increase.
In this article:
- Send items to the Recycle Bin
- Find items in the Recycle Bin
- Recover or permanently delete an item
Go to the CRM section > More > Recycle Bin .
Send items to the Recycle Bin
The Recycle Bin contains information about the deletion of the following items:
- Lead
- Deal
- Contact
- Company
- Activity
- Invoice
- SPA element
If necessary, you can disable the Recycle Bin for certain CRM items:
1. Go to the More tab > Settings > CRM Settings.
2. Select Other > Other settings .
3. Open to the Recycle Bin tab. Choose which items will go to the Recycle Bin and click Apply .
Find items in the CRM Recycle Bin
To quickly find the necessary items in the Recycle Bin, choose which fields to display in the list and set up filters.
1. Click on the Settings (⚙️) icon.
2. Check the fields you want to add to the list.
3. If you are an administrator, you can enable the Apply for all users option.
4. Click Apply .
The Default button will reset all field view settings to standard.
Configure filters
Filters help you quickly find the necessary data. For example, items deleted this month.
ID. This is the unique identifier of a CRM item. Specify an ID to check if an item is in the Recycle Bin.
Find the item ID
Deletion time. Choose an option from the list.
User. Specify the employee who deleted the item.
Type. Choose the item type: lead, contact, company, deal, activity, invoice, or SPA.
Recover or delete an item from the CRM Recycle Bin
Recover an item
Click Menu (≡) > Recover next to the item.
When the CRM item is recovered, you will see a notification about it.
If an activity is linked to a deleted CRM item, you should first recover the item itself.
Only a Bitrix24 administrator can delete an item from the Recycle Bin.
1. Click Menu (≡) > Delete .
2. Select Continue .
In brief:
- The CRM Recycle Bin is a temporary storage for deleted deals, contacts, companies, and other items.
- Items in the Recycle Bin can be recovered or permanently deleted. Only a Bitrix24 administrator can delete them.
- Items are stored in the Recycle Bin for 30 days. Then they are automatically deleted at a rate of 100 items per day.
- The Bitrix24 administrator views all deleted items in the Recycle Bin. Employees only see the items they deleted.
- You can disable the Recycle Bin for certain items in CRM settings.

titre: Maps in CRM for address visualization
sections: Maps in CRM for address visualization
In Bitrix24, you can use OpenStreetMap and Google Maps to manage deliveries and specify client addresses in CRM.
How it works
Open a CRM entity form and find the Address field. When you start typing an address, you'll see suggestions and a map showing the location.

titre: My CRM data is missing. What can I do?
sections: Step 1. Check the CRM Recycle bin
When you delete a CRM item, it isn't permanently removed; it moves to the CRM Recycle Bin. From there, you can either permanently delete or restore items. CRM Recycle Bin
Step 2. Confirm the data is missing
If someone deletes CRM items, the action is logged in the CRM History section. To verify if items were deleted:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Select History .
4. Click on the filter.
5. In the Type field, select Delete . You'll see who deleted the items and when. CRM History
Also, ensure that filters aren't hiding items. Click the cross (X) in the filter to clear it.
If these steps don't resolve the issue, contact Bitrix24 Support. Our specialists can help recover lost data upon request. How to contact Bitrix24 Support
Step 3. Request data recovery

All Bitrix24 Cloud accounts are backed up daily (both free and commercial plans). This protects your data from technical issues or unexpected events that may happen at our end. These backups are usually stored for one week.
You can request a full Bitrix24 backup restore, which will revert your entire account database to a previous date. Note that all changes made after that date will be lost.
Please note :
- The account administrator must submit the data recovery request.
- Data recovery affects all account users, not just one employee.
- Data recovery is possible for up to one week back.
- All data added after the requested backup date will be lost.
How it works :
1. Send a message to Bitrix Support24 chat.
2. A specialist will inform you about available backups and coordinate a recovery time.
3. Choose and confirm the data restore time.

titre: Cannot access CRM settings. Why?
sections: Cannot access CRM settings. Why?
If you open CRM > Settings > CRM settings and can see only the Email section, it means you don't have permissions to configure CRM settings. Contact your Bitrix24 administrator to request access.
By default, only Bitrix24 administrators can configure CRM settings, but they can easily grant admin permissions to any user. Here's how:
1. Open a user's profile.
2. Click Actions next to the user's photo.
3. Select Assign admin permissions from the drop-down menu.
Assign administrator permissions
Alternatively, an administrator can adjust CRM access permissions to allow users with a specific role to edit settings. Here's how:
1. Go to CRM and expand Settings .
2. Select Access Permissions > CRM .
3. Select a role and click the pencil icon to edit it.
4. Enable the User can edit settings option.
5. Save the changes.
6. Assign this role to a user.
7. Click Save .
Access Permissions in CRM
Once this is done, the user will have access to the CRM settings section.

titre: Access problems after editing the company structure
sections: Access problems after editing the company structure
If you update your company structure—for example, change a department manager or move an employee to another department—you may run into CRM access issues. Company Structure overview

titre: Invite a customer to Telegram chat from mobile CRM
sections: Connect Telegram to Bitrix24 in the mobile app

You can connect Telegram to Bitrix24 from the mobile app. Send a customer an SMS with a link to your Telegram bot, then continue the conversation in chat. Bitrix24 saves the chat history in the related CRM item.
To use Invite to chat , connect a Telegram bot to Bitrix24 first.
Connect Telegram
Only users with access to Open Channels can connect Telegram to Bitrix24.
You need an access token to connect a Telegram bot. You can get the token when you create a new bot or request it for an existing bot.
Telegram connects to the first Open Channel you created. You can choose a different Open Channel in the web version.
To connect Telegram:
1. Open a CRM item.
2. Tap the button at the bottom to view communication channels.
3. Select Connect Telegram .
4. Enter the access token.
5. Tap Continue .
6. Set up the agent queue. Selected users will receive incoming Telegram messages.
7. Save the changes.
After setup, copy the link and send it to your customer. You can also show the customer the generated QR code.
Invite a customer to chat
1. Open a CRM item.
2. In the Details or Timeline tab, tap + in the bottom-right corner.
3. Select Invite to chat .
If the deal has several contacts , select the contact you want to invite to Telegram. Then choose a service to send the SMS.
To send SMS messages, set up an integration with a messaging service first. You can use the built-in Twilio integration or install another SMS app from Bitrix24 Market .
You can check the message status in the deal timeline. When the customer opens the link and starts a chat, you can open the chat from the deal.
You can also go to Chats > Open Channels to open the Telegram chat.
You can use the generated Telegram bot link or QR code on your website, in emails, and in marketing campaigns.

titre: Filters in CRM
sections: Filters in CRM

Use CRM filters to quickly find the items you need. Search by standard or custom fields, linked CRM items, and change history. For example, find deals with no linked leads or deals assigned to a specific employee with an upcoming activity deadline.
In this article:
- Filter leads
- Filter deals
- Filter products
- Filter invoices
- Filter estimates
- Filter items by associations
To filter CRM items, open the section you need, click the search bar, and select the fields to filter by.
Filter leads
- "Lead in progress" stage group. Leads that are still being worked on.
- "Lead converted" stage. Leads that have resulted in deals or contacts.
- "Lead failed" stage group. Leads that are not suitable for further work.
Status group in history:
- "Lead in progress" stage group. Leads that were in progress.
- "Lead converted" stage. Leads that resulted in deals or customers.
- "Lead failed" stage group. Leads that were not suitable for further work.
The Status filter shows the current stage group of the lead, while Status group in history allows you to analyze the stages the lead has gone through since creation.
Closed:
- Yes — leads that have been moved to the final stage.
- No — leads that are still being worked on.
Repeat lead:
- Yes — leads associated with existing customers.
- No — first contact from a potential customer.
Activities:
- Inbound — leads with scheduled activities.
- For today — leads with activities scheduled for today.
- Overdue — leads with activities past their due date.
- No activities — leads with no scheduled activities.
- Pressing — leads with activities nearing their deadline.
In progress — select a specific day, month, or date range to see leads that were being worked on.
Stage — shows leads currently at the selected stage, such as In progress .
Status group in history — shows the stages a lead has gone through, even if it is currently at a different stage.
Status group in history (with stage changes) — considers both actual and possible skipped stages.
Stage changed by — select the employee who moved the lead to a different stage.
Stage change date — shows leads moved to another stage within a specified period.
Filter deals
New deal — deals at the first stage.
Repeat deal — deals with customers who have had successful deals before.
Repeat inquiry — deals with customers previously worked with, but no deal was successful.
In progress — deals that were in progress on a selected day, month, or other time period.
Start date — deals created within a specified period.
End date — deals completed within a specified period.
Stage group:
- "Deal in progress" stage group. Deals currently in progress.
- "Deal won" stage. Successfully completed deals.
- "Deal lost" stage group. Unsuccessfully completed deals.
Stage group in history:
- "Deal in progress" stage group. Deals that were in progress.
- "Deal won" stage. Deals that were successfully completed.
- "Deal lost" stage. Deals that were unsuccessfully completed.
The Stage group filter shows only the current stages of deals, while Stage group in history considers all stages a deal has gone through since creation.
Delivery status — deals with the selected delivery status: Delivered or Awaiting shipping .
Payment status — deals with the selected invoice payment status: Not paid , Sent, not paid, Viewed, not paid, Paid, Canceled , and Refunded .
Payment date — deals with invoices paid on a specific date or within a date range.
Event type — deals with calls or emails.
Event date — deals with calls or emails on a specified date or within a date range.
Deals in test mode — deals being tested by the automation rule test mode. Automation rule test mode
Stage — shows deals currently at the selected stage.
Stage in history — shows the stages a deal has gone through, even if it is currently at a different stage.
Stage in history (with stage changes) — considers both actual and possible skipped stages.
Stage changed by — select the employee who moved the deal to a different stage.
Stage change date — shows deals moved to another stage within a specified period.
Repeat sales script — shows deals created from repeat sales scripts, such as Holiday customer, Monthly customer, or Semi-annual customer. AI-assisted repeat sales in CRM
You can search deals using fields from linked contacts and companies. For example, find all deals where the contact has an email address or filter deals by the company’s industry.
Filter products
Include subsections — allows searching for products in the selected section and its subsections.
Active from — finds products that became available to customers in the online store from a specified date.
Active until — finds products that became unavailable to customers in the online store from a specified date.
Type:
- Simple — product without variants.
- SKU — product with variants.
- Invalid SKU — variants not linked to a specific product.
- Product offer — product variants.
- Service — shows only services.
Availability — shows products available or unavailable for sale.
Warehouse balance — shows products with a specific quantity in stock. Specify a number or range.
Reserved — displays products reserved in the selected quantity. Inventory management settings
Purchase price — products with a specified purchase price. Specify a number or range.
Purchase price currency — products with a purchase price in the selected currency.
SKU — shows all variants of the selected catalog product.
Filter invoices
Pay before — finds invoices expected to be paid by a selected date or within a specified range.
- In progress — invoices awaiting payment.
- Success — paid invoices.
- Failed — unpaid invoices.
- Activities — invoices with scheduled or overdue activities.
- Deals — invoices linked to a selected deal.
- Estimates — invoices linked to a selected estimate.
Filter estimates
Last updated on — finds estimates updated on a selected date or period. All changes, including timeline entries, are considered.
Created by CRM form — select the form on which the estimate was based.
Activities — shows all estimates with scheduled or overdue activities.
In CRM, you can filter data not only by fields of a specific CRM item but also by related CRM items. For example:
- Lead + Activity — find leads with assigned activities.
- Deal + Company — find deals linked to a specific company.
To find leads with assigned activities:
1. Click on the search bar and select Add field .
2. Choose the Lead and Activity options and mark the necessary fields.
Filter items by associations
You can find CRM items based on whether they are linked to other CRM item types. For example, find deals with no linked leads or deals linked to contacts.
The following example shows how to find deals with no linked leads. Follow the same steps for other CRM items.

1. Go to CRM > Deals . 2. Click the Filter and search field at the top. 3. Click Add field . 4. Find and select CRM entity associations . 5. Click Apply . 6. Select a CRM item type and an association condition. 7. To find deals with no linked leads, select Leads: no association exists . 8. Click Search .
In brief
- Use CRM filters to quickly find the data you need. Search by standard and custom fields, linked CRM items, and change history.
- Check if CRM filter search is available on your plan.
- To filter CRM items, open the section you need, click the search bar, and select the fields to filter by.
- You can filter CRM items by their own fields or fields from linked items.
- Use CRM entity associations to find items that are or aren't linked to other CRM items.

titre: AI-assisted repeat sales in CRM
sections: AI-assisted repeat sales in CRM

Repeat sales are planned purchases from customers who interacted with your business before. The Repeat sales tool uses AI to identify customers who are likely to buy again and automatically creates deals for them. CoPilot adds an activity to each deal with personalized recommendations for your sales agents on what to offer and how to lead the conversation.
Go to CRM > Sales > Repeat sales .
In this article:
- AI-assisted repeat sales: How it works
- Set up your CRM for repeat sales
- Enable and configure repeat sales
- Set access permissions for repeat sales
- Find repeat sales deals
- Track repeat sales statistics
AI-assisted repeat sales: How it works
Analyze customers. Every day, AI analyzes the sales history in your CRM to find customers ready to buy again. There are three scripts:

- Monthly customer — These are customers who buy once a month. AI checks the last three months of successful purchases, excluding the current one. For example, if a customer orders coffee for the office each month, AI will remind you at the beginning of the month to offer a new blend or a promotion on a larger quantity.

- Semi-annual customer — These are customers who tend to buy every six months. For example, a company might update its software in June and December. In May and November, AI will send a reminder to offer an updated version or a discount.

- Holiday customer — These are customers who usually buy around the same time each year. AI analyzes the purchase history over the past two years, excluding the current one. For example, a customer might buy equipment every December for Christmas events. AI will remind you to contact them in advance to offer relevant products or services.

Create deals. When AI finds a suitable customer, it automatically creates a deal. The deal form includes an activity with personalized recommendations from CoPilot on what to offer and how to lead the conversation.
If no repeat sales deals appear in CRM, check the following:
- Make sure Repeat sales are enabled in your Bitrix24 settings. Enable and configure repeat sales
- Confirm there are deals in CRM from the past six months.
- Follow our recommendations for working with CRM. Set up your CRM for repeat sales
Analyze sales data. This helps you understand which repeat sales scripts work best and adjust your settings if needed. Track repeat sales statistics
Set up your CRM for repeat sales
Accurate and complete data in your CRM helps the AI-assisted repeat sales tool identify customers ready to buy again and create personalized recommendations.

Complete customer and deal forms in detail. Use standard fields to enter the customer’s name, phone number, and email. You can also create custom fields with clear names to track specific preferences. This gives AI more data to better identify repeat purchase opportunities. Standard fields in CRM Custom fields in CRM
For example, if you sell office furniture, create custom fields like Room type , Furniture style , and Budget . This helps AI decide who and when to offer new collections or discounts.

Set up sales pipelines. Create separate pipelines for each stage or type of sale. Your pipelines should reflect how your team actually works with customers. For example, if you sell air conditioners, you might have one pipeline for sales. If you start offering installation and maintenance, create separate pipelines for those services. Sales pipelines

Use AI to transcribe and analyze calls. Connect telephony and enable AI-powered transcription. AI can analyze conversations to detect customer needs and suggest when to offer new services. Telephony connection options overview AI Speech analytics and Sales scripts in CRM

Keep your product catalog up to date. Add detailed descriptions, pricing, and seasonal features to the catalog to let AI recommend the right products. In deals, you can select products directly from the catalog to quickly create invoices and estimates. Create products and configure product catalog Services in CRM
For example, if your catalog includes Christmas gift sets, AI will recommend them to customers who purchased similar items last December.

Track agreements with customers. Note details and agreements using comments and universal activities in the deal form. This gives AI more context for future follow-ups and personalized offers. Universal activity in CRM
For example, if a comment says a customer plans to upgrade their office equipment in six months, AI will remind you to contact them in advance and offer relevant models or favorable terms.
Enable and configure repeat sales

Enable repeat sales. By default, AI regularly identifies customers who are likely to buy again. However, it doesn't create repeat deals unless this feature is enabled. Only administrators or users with permission to edit deals can turn on deal creation via a special banner in CRM.
Bitrix24 administrators can also manage repeat sales in Bitrix24 settings. Here's how:
1. Click Settings in the left menu.
2. Select Bitrix24 settings .
3. Open the Tools tab.
4. Expand CRM .
5. Enable Repeat sales .
6. Save the changes.

Configure repeat sales. You can activate and adjust standard repeat sales scripts, but custom scripts are not currently supported. Only administrators or users with the necessary permissions can configure them. Set access permissions for repeat sales
To configure scripts:
- Enable — AI will add recommendations to the activity, like what to offer and how to lead the conversation.
- Disable — A default text will appear, which can be edited manually.
- Pipeline for new deals — AI will create repeat deals in this pipeline.
- Stage — Select the stage where the new deal should appear.
- Responsible persons — Choose one or more employees to manage new deals. If you select multiple people, deals will be assigned to them in rotation.
- Default deal title — This is the name that will appear in CRM.
Set access permissions for repeat sales
Administrator can allow users to configure repeat sales scripts and view related statistics.
To set access permissions:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Settings .
4. Select CRM access permissions .
5. Click Repeat sales .
6. Set permissions for the following actions: View settings — allows users to view repeat sales statistics. Edit settings — allows users to configure repeat sales scripts.
7. Click Save .
Role-based access permissions in CRM
Find repeat sales deals
To find all deals automatically created by AI-assisted repeat sales, use the Repeat sales script filter.
1. Go to CRM .
2. Open Deals .
3. Click Filter and search .
4. Click Add field .
5. Select the Repeat sales script field and click Apply .
6. In the field, choose one or more scripts, such as Annual customer and Monthly customer .
7. Click Search .
The CRM will display all deals created from the selected repeat sales scripts.
Track repeat sales statistics
Statistics help you understand how well repeat sales are working. Only Bitrix24 administrators or users with the necessary permissions can view this data.
To view repeat sales statistics:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Open the Deals section.
3. Click Repeat sales .
4. Choose a period: Last 30 days, Quarter, Half year, or Year.
The statistics include the following metrics:
- Number and total value of deals in progress
- Number and total value of won deals
- Conversion by number — the percentage of won deals compared to all deals created by the repeat sales script during the selected period
- Conversion by amount — the total value of won deals compared to the total value of all deals created by the repeat sales script during the selected period
In brief
- AI-assisted repeat sales are a new tool that identifies customers who are ready to buy again and automatically creates deals for them.
- CoPilot adds an activity with personalized recommendations for your sales agents on what to offer and how to lead the conversation.
- Check if AI-assisted repeat sales are available on your plan.
- Go to CRM > Sales > Repeat sales and select which scripts will automatically create repeat deals: Monthly customer, Semi-annual customer, or Holiday customer.

- The more accurate the data in CRM, the better repeat sales work. Complete customer and deal forms in detail, set up sales pipelines, use AI to transcribe calls, keep your product catalog up to date, and note agreements in the CRM item forms.

- By default, AI regularly identifies customers ready for new purchases but doesn't create repeat deals. Bitrix24 administrators or users with permissions to edit deals can enable deal creation via a special banner in CRM.
- To find all deals automatically created by AI-assisted repeat sales, use the Repeat sales script filter.
- Built-in statistics help you understand how well repeat sales are working.

titre: Open slots in CRM
sections: Open slots in CRM
Open slots in CRM are a useful tool for client-facing employees. Share a link to your open slots with clients, allowing them to pick their preferred date and time for meetings.
How to configure available slots
1. Open a deal form and select Slots in the timeline on the right.

2. Select the preferred days and hours for open slots. For example, you can align with your company's business hours: from Monday to Friday, from 10 am to 7 pm. Also, indicate the duration of each time slot for customer meetings.
If there are several linked contacts, select the one to whom you want to send a link. To do this, click the gear button (⚙️) and choose a contact under Recipient .
How to invite colleagues to a meeting with a client

Click Add (+) and select employees from the list to invite them to a meeting with your client. Shared slots take your colleagues' availability into account, so the client can pick the time when all the attendees are available.
How to share open slots with clients
Once you set up the open slots, click Send link . Bitrix24 generates a link to your open slots and sends it via SMS to the linked contact.

Or, you can choose Copy link and send it to the customer in any convenient way. The generated link is active for 7 days, and the customer can use it again during this period to schedule another meeting.
To see how the recipients will view your open slots, insert the copied link in a browser.
The meeting appears as an event in your calendar and as an activity in the deal. Edit the event to change its default name, specify the location, or add a colleague as an attendee.
There is no way to edit the date and time of the meeting, but you can decline it. Click the three dots (...) button and select Cancel meeting . The contact will be notified about that.
All the contact's actions are recorded in the deal timeline. Therefore, you can see when exactly they opened the link and created a meeting.
To hold a meeting online, you can use the Video Conferencing feature. Video Conferencing in Bitrix24
In brief
- Open slots in CRM serve as a tool for scheduling meetings with clients.
- Send a link to your open slots to your client from the deal form.
- Find and manage the scheduled appointments in your calendar.
- Configure slot duration and availability to offer to your clients.

titre: FAQ: CRM
sections: FAQ: CRM

CRM is a tool for managing customer relationships. It stores contacts, deals, communication history, and purchase records. CRM helps you stay connected with customers and boost sales. This article provides answers to frequently asked questions about setting up and using CRM.
- CRM item form settings
- Working with CRM items
- Data import and export
- Access permissions
- Working with activities
- Reports and analytics
- Products and currencies
Can I change the set of fields in the CRM item form?
You can customize lead, deal, or other CRM item forms to suit your business needs:
- Hide standard fields you don’t need. These fields cannot be deleted. For example, hide the Second name field if you often work with international customers. Standard fields in CRM
- Add custom fields. For instance, add fields for address, delivery terms, or order number to a deal. Custom fields in CRM
Hide a field in a CRM item form.
1. Click Settings (⚙️) next to the field you want to hide.
2. Select Hide .
3. To restore the field, click Select field and choose the one you need.
Create a field in a CRM item form.
1. Open the CRM item form.
2. Click Create field and select its type.
3. Enter the field name and enable the required parameters.
How can I restrict access to specific fields in the CRM item form?
You can restrict the visibility of custom fields only.
1. Click Settings (⚙️) next to the field.
2. Select Configure .
3. Check the box next to Make this field visible to selected users only .
4. Choose which employees or departments can see the field.
Limit custom fields visibility in CRM
Why were custom fields from one CRM item copied to another?
Issue: Custom fields from one CRM item were copied to another. For example, fields from a deal appeared in an invoice form.
Reason: Custom fields are transferred during workflow imports. If a workflow is exported from deals and then imported into invoices, the custom fields are copied over as part of the process.
Solution: If you don't need these fields, delete them manually. Here's how:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Settings .
4. Select CRM settings .
5. Open the Form and report settings section.
6. Click Custom fields .
7. Choose the CRM item and click Field .
8. Click Menu (≡) > Delete next to the field. Note that deleting a field will also remove its data.
How many deals and customers can I add to CRM?

In Bitrix24 CRM, you can add an unlimited number of contacts, companies, deals, and leads. However, there are limitations on filter-based searches and the maximum number of leads, deals, contacts, and companies for CRM analytics reports. Bitrix24 plans and pricing
Can I merge duplicates in CRM?

In Bitrix24 CRM, you can merge duplicate leads, contacts, and companies using automatic duplicate control or manually. Deals can only be merged manually. Automatic duplicate merging in CRM Merge duplicates in CRM
Can I disable automation rule and workflow events in the timeline?
The system always shows automation rule events in the timeline, and they can’t be disabled. However, you can turn off workflow events in the workflow template settings.
1. Go to Automation .
2. Click Workflows .
3. Select Workflows in CRM .
4. Click Templates next to the required CRM item.
5. Select the workflow.
6. Click Template parameters .
7. Disable the Show workflow events in the timeline option.
8. Save the changes.
Workflow events in CRM item form
Can I import data into Bitrix24 in XML format?
Bitrix24 supports data import only in CSV format. If your file is in XML format, convert it to CSV. Import to Bitrix24 CRM Import contact and company details Product import
Why are some contacts not exported?
Ensure the Included in export option is enabled in the contact form. You can enable it for a specific contact or using group actions for multiple contacts. Export CRM data Group actions in CRM
Can I import and export CRM activities?
This option is not currently available. Export CRM data Import to Bitrix24 CRM
Why is the Export option missing in CRM?
The Export option in CRM might not be available for the following reasons:
Plan limitation. Exporting contacts isn’t included in all plans. Bitrix24 plans and pricing
Insufficient access permissions. The user doesn’t have export permissions for CRM items. To grant export permissions:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Settings .
4. Select CRM access permissions .
5. Choose the CRM item, such as Contacts , and grant export permissions.
Role-based access permissions in CRM
Incorrect view mode. Items can only be exported when using the List view.
How to import deals linked to a contact?
To import deals linked to a contact, follow these steps:

1. Import contacts. Go to CRM > Customers > Contacts > Settings (⚙️) > Import custom CSV and download the import file. Fill out the file by entering the contact’s first and last name in separate columns. Import to Bitrix24 CRM
2. Import deals. Go to CRM > Deals > Settings (⚙️) > Import Deals and download the import file. Fill out the file by entering the contact’s first and last name in one column.
After importing, contacts will automatically link to the deals.
What do the values in square brackets mean when exporting fields of the "Bind to CRM items" type?
When exporting items with a field of the Bind to CRM items type, the export file includes a code in square brackets next to each value. This code indicates the type of CRM item the link refers to:
- [С] — contact
- [CO] — company
- [L] — lead
- [SI] — invoice
- [D] — deal
- [T...] — SPA item, converted to hexadecimal. For example, if the SPA ID is 170, its hexadecimal value is AA. In the export file, this item will appear as [Taa].
Custom fields in CRM
Why can’t an employee complete or delete an activity in a CRM item?
Issue: The employee can edit the deal but can’t complete or delete a linked activity.

Reason: Activities in CRM can be linked to multiple items, like a deal and a contact. To complete or delete the activity, the employee must have permission to edit all linked items. If they don’t have access to even one of them, they won’t be able to complete or delete the activity.
Solution: There are two options:

- Adjust the employee’s access permissions to allow them to edit all items linked to the activity. For example, if the activity is linked to a contact, give permission to edit contacts. Role-based access permissions in CRM
- Contact the Bitrix24 or CRM administrator, who has full access and can complete or delete any activity.
Why is the CRM section missing from the left menu?
Issue: The CRM section is not visible in the left Bitrix24 menu.
Possible reasons:
- The CRM section is hidden in the left menu.
- CRM is disabled in Bitrix24 settings.
- The user doesn’t have permission to access CRM.
Solutions:
Make the CRM section visible. Click Show all in the left menu to see hidden items, then move CRM to the main part of the menu. Left menu in Bitrix24
Enable the CRM section. Go to Settings > Bitrix24 settings > Tools and enable CRM. Only account administrators can do this.

Adjust CRM access permissions. Only account administrators or employees with the User can edit preferences permission in CRM can do this. Go to CRM > More > Settings > CRM access permissions and configure permissions for the required role. Role-based access permissions in CRM
Why aren't the Call and Meeting activities showing in the CRM item form?
The activity types Call and Meeting are outdated. Instead, you can use universal activities. Universal activity in CRM
A universal activity is a convenient form for managing any client-related tasks.
In the activity form, you can:
- Set the meeting location with the customer.
- Link the activity to a specific customer.
- Synchronize the activity with your calendar.
- Add colleagues.
- Reserve a meeting room.
- Organize activities using color coding.
How to set a default calendar for creating activities in the CRM item form?
This option isn't available yet. By default, the company calendar is used when creating an activity in CRM.
To use a different calendar by default, you can hide the company calendar in the settings.
1. Go to Calendar .
2. Click Calendars .
3. Open the three-dot menu (...).
4. Select Remove from list .
Can I make the "Add to calendar" option automatically selected when creating an activity?
This option isn't available yet. To show activities in the calendar, you’ll need to select it manually when creating them. Universal activity in CRM
What is the reporting period in CRM reports?
The reporting period is the time range for building analytical reports in CRM. It helps you track the items that employees worked on during this time. Reporting period in CRM
A deal is considered as belonging to the reporting period if:
- It is added, edited, or closed during this time.
- It was closed earlier, but a new activity, such as a call or email, has been added.
- It is still in progress and hasn't been closed yet.
What are deals on hold in CRM analytics reports?
Deals on hold have no activities within the reporting period, such as stage changes, completed activities (calls, emails, or meetings), or created invoices. My reports: Deals
Why can’t I add a product from the catalog to a deal?
You can’t select a product from the catalog in a deal if it’s inactive. Add products to the catalog
To change the product’s activity status:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click Inventory .
3. Select Product catalog .
4. Find and select the product you need.
5. In the product form, check these fields: Active from : Enter a past date. Active until : Enter a future date or leave it blank.
6. Save your changes.
Once updated, the product will be available for selection in deals.
Can I use different currencies in CRM?
You can work with different currencies in CRM, which is convenient for dealing with international customers. You can:
- Select a base currency for deals.
- Add other currencies and set their exchange rates.
- Choose a currency for reports and invoices.
To add and configure a currency:
1. Go to CRM .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Settings .
4. Select CRM settings .
5. In the Start point section, select Currency .
You’ll see a list of currencies, with one set as the base currency. Currencies in CRM

titre: Bitrix24 Inventory Management
sections: Bitrix24 Inventory Management
Inventory Management in Bitrix24 helps you track products across warehouses. You can record stock receipts, sales orders, transfers, and write-offs in one place.
Every inventory operation is saved in the system. Your team can update inventory online, and you can monitor stock movement and warehouse activity in real time.
Enable Inventory Management
1. Open the CRM section.
2. Click Inventory .
3. Select Inventory management .
A panel will open on the right side of the page. Choose a costing method and click Enable Inventory Management at the bottom to proceed.
Inventory management: costing methods and gross profit report
Start working with Inventory Management
If you are new to Bitrix24 or do not have products in the catalog yet, add products manually or create stock adjustments.
Start working with Inventory Management
If you already use products in Bitrix24, reset the current stock balances before you enable Inventory Management.
Inventory Management: balances reset
If you manage inventory in another system, you can migrate your data with apps from Bitrix24 Market.
Inventory management: migrate data from other systems
How Inventory Management works
Inventory Management includes four sections:
1. Inventory
2. Sales orders
3. Transfers
4. Write-offs
Use these sections to create documents and manage warehouse operations.
Learn more:
- Inventory Management: stock adjustment
- Inventory Management: stock receipt
- Inventory Management: sales orders
- Inventory Management: stock transfer
- Inventory Management: write-offs
- Migrate stock with Zoho Inventory app

titre: Inventory management: Getting started
sections: Inventory management: Getting started
Inventory management helps you track products in your warehouse. It records receipts, sales, transfers, and write-offs. Stock data updates in real time.
With inventory management, you can:
- See current stock levels. Data updates after every operation.
- Reserve products for a specific customer while a deal is still in progress.
- Find losses faster by spotting discrepancies and checking their causes.
- Track gross margin for each product, including cost and gross profit.
Add products to the catalog
The catalog is a single list of products and services for CRM and your online store. You can use catalog products in your online store or website.
1. Go to CRM > Inventory > Product catalog. 2. Click Create.
For each product, you can add a price, SKU, barcode, dimensions, photo, and variants such as size or color. Add product to the catalog

If you have a large catalog, organize products into sections and subsections so managers can find items faster in deals. If you have many products, import them in bulk instead of adding them one by one. Product catalog Product import
Enable Inventory management
After you add products to the catalog, enable Inventory management. The first time you open this section, Bitrix24 asks you to choose a working mode and a costing method.
1. Go to CRM or Sites and Stores and open Inventory > Inventory management. 2. Select a costing method — how product cost is calculated at the time of sale:
- FIFO: items acquired first are sold first which determines the cost of an item.
- Average: the item cost is calculated as an average cost of the same items in the warehouse.
To change the costing method after enabling inventory management, you need to disable and re-enable it. Costing methods and gross profit report
3. Click Enable Inventory management. 4. Confirm the stock reset — before enabling inventory management, Bitrix24 resets current stock levels to zero. Document drafts are saved.
Enter opening stock balances
To make inventory management reflect your actual stock, record how many products you already have. Create a stock receipt document to do this.
If you already have products in Bitrix24 with non-zero stock levels, reset them before you start. Otherwise the data will be incorrect. Reset balances
If your data is stored in another system, you can transfer it to Bitrix24. Migrate data from other systems to Bitrix24 Inventory management
After you enable inventory management, the Receipts section opens and prompts you to add the first stock receipt. Create a stock adjustment
1. Click Create. 2. In the document, enter the products, quantity, purchase price, and warehouse. 3. Click Save and post.
After posting the document, the products appear in the warehouse and become available for deals in CRM.
In the Inventory management section, tap Plus (+). Select the document type Stock adjustment.
Tap Add products and enter the products, quantity, warehouse, and purchase price. Tap Create, then Process.
Configure access permissions
Access permissions define what each employee can do. Set them up in advance so employees work only with the data they need and do not make accidental changes.
Go to CRM > More > Settings > Inventory access permissions.
If the default roles do not fit your needs, create custom roles. Configure access permissions to Inventory Management Allocate access permissions for Inventory management
Work with documents

After you add products, enter stock balances, and set up permissions, you can start daily inventory tracking. All product operations are recorded through documents. The Inventory management section has five document types, each recording a specific operation:
- Stock receipt — records products that arrived at the warehouse not from a supplier: opening balances or surpluses found during inventory.
- Receipt — records products received from a supplier. Stock levels increase.
- Sales — records a sale to a customer. When a deal closes in CRM, a sales document is created automatically and stock levels decrease.
- Transfer — records a product transfer between warehouses.
- Write-off — records product losses unrelated to sales: defects, damage, or shortages.

For each document, you can create a printable form — an invoice or act — and print it, email it to a customer, or share a link. Create a stock receipt Work with sales orders Transfers Write-offs Print Inventory management documents
Go to the Inventory management section. All Inventory documents appear here. Use the tabs at the top to open the document type you need: Inventory, Sales order, Transfer, or Write-off.
Work with products in CRM
Products from the catalog are available right inside deals. Managers can check stock levels and reserve products without leaving the deal.
Reserve a product. When a manager adds a product to a deal, they can reserve it for a specific customer. A reserved product lowers the available stock, so another manager cannot sell it by mistake.

By default, a reservation lasts three days, but you can change this period. The reservation ends automatically when the deal is closed or when the product is removed from the deal. Reserve products in deals Find deals with reserved products
1. Go to CRM > Deals and open the deal you need. 2. Open the Products tab. 3. Add a product, select a warehouse, and enter the quantity in the Reserve field.

1. Go to CRM > Deals and open the deal you need. 2. Open the Products tab and tap Plus (+). 3. Tap Find or create a product and select the product you need. 4. Tap the product name. 5. In the Stock and reservation section, enter the quantity in the Reserve field and tap Done.

Process a sales order when closing a deal. When a deal moves to the final stage, Bitrix24 automatically creates a sales order and deducts the products from the warehouse. If there is not enough stock, you cannot close the deal until you fix the issue.
To close a deal with a sales order, move it to the final stage. Bitrix24 will check stock availability and create the sales order automatically. Inventory management documents in deals
In brief
- Inventory management helps you track stock levels, plan purchases, and avoid selling products that are out of stock.
- When you enable inventory management, select the mode.
- Right after you enable it, set the costing method: average cost or FIFO.
- Add products to the catalog and create a stock adjustment to record actual stock levels.
- Set up access permissions for employees who work with the warehouse.
- Use the right document type to record receipts, sales, transfers, and write-offs. You can also generate and print a form for each document type.
- Products from the catalog are available directly in CRM deals. Managers can reserve them for a specific customer, and Bitrix24 creates a sales order automatically when the deal is closed.

titre: Conditions for enabling Bitrix24 Inventory Management
sections: Conditions for enabling Bitrix24 Inventory Management
We updated the conditions for enabling Bitrix24 Inventory Management. These changes affect CRM modes and help ensure stable performance.
For current users
If you use the Deals and orders mode and want to enable Inventory Management, you first need to switch the CRM mode to Deals .
To change the mode:
1. Open CRM .
2. Go to Settings > Order handling mode .
3. Select Deals .
The Deals and orders mode is no longer supported in Bitrix24. After you switch to Deals , you cannot switch back.
If you already use Inventory Management with the Deals and orders mode enabled, Inventory Management will continue to work. However:
- You will not be able to use the new booking modes.
- You will only have access to the old settings.
If you already use the Stock control option, it will continue to work without changes. However, if you disable this option, you cannot enable it again.
- Migrate stock with QuickBooks Inventory

titre: Inventory management settings
sections: Inventory management settings
On the settings page, you can configure various Inventory management parameters:
- Select a reservation mode for products in deals
- Change the costing method
- Enable subscription for out-of-stock products, configure tax settings, and make out-of-stock items available for purchase
- Configure Inventory management mode
Go to CRM or Sites and stores > Inventory > Inventory management > Settings > Common parameters .
Reservation options . Select a reservation mode and how many days the product will be reserved. There are three modes:

- Manual : Employees manually enter the number of products and the reservation period in a deal. If a customer changes their order, employees must update the reservation manually. This mode is useful if you do not need to reserve each product. For example, you might have many microwaves but only a few fridges in a warehouse, so you only reserve fridges.
- When adding products to deal : Products are automatically reserved when added to a deal. Reservations update automatically if the product quantity changes.
- Upon payment : Products are reserved at the moment of payment, even if entered manually. This ensures products are only reserved after payment is received.

Auto sale unshipped items when completing deal : This option is always enabled and helps manage warehouse stock. For example, if an employee completes a deal but the product has not yet been shipped, the system automatically creates a sales order. If stock is low, the system will warn the employee to choose a different warehouse to complete the deal. Reserve products in deals

Costing method . The method is initially configured when enabling Inventory management. In this block, you can view the selected costing method used for selling products. To change it, disable and then re-enable Inventory management. Costing methods and gross profit report
Product options . In this section, you can configure three parameters:

- Enable subscription for out-of-stock products : Customers can sign up to get notified when an item is back in stock. You can see how many customers have subscribed, helping you estimate demand. Product subscription

- Set "Tax Included" option for all new products and SKU's : Enable this option, and the system will automatically add tax to the cost of all new products and SKUs. This saves employees from having to specify tax for each product. You can set the rate in the Default tax rate field. Taxes in CRM

- Make out-of-stock items available for purchase : Enable this option to allow customers to see and order products even if they are not in stock. Employees can send a payment link even if the product is out of stock.
Inventory management mode . In this block, you can disable Inventory management. Disable Inventory management
In brief
- Open CRM or Sites and stores > Inventory > Inventory management > Settings > Common parameters .
- Select a reservation mode and set the reservation period.
- To change the costing method, restart Inventory management.
- Configure product options: subscriptions, tax, and availability.
- You can disable Inventory management in the Inventory management mode section.

titre: Vendors in the Inventory management
sections: Vendors in the Inventory management

Vendors are companies or individuals that supply products. In Inventory Management, you can store all vendor details in one place, including contact information, addresses, and company details. This makes it easier to find vendor contacts, communicate with them, and track deliveries.
- View the Inventory Management documents section
- Create and edit stock receipt documents
- View, add, and edit contacts, companies, and vendors.
In this article:
- Add a vendor to a stock receipt
- Find the vendor list
Add a vendor to a stock receipt

A stock receipt shows which products arrived and which vendor supplied them. When you fill out the document, you can choose an existing vendor or create a new one. In Inventory Management, vendors are based on contacts and companies. Their details are stored in CRM item forms.

1. Go to CRM > Inventory > Inventory Management . 2. In the Inventory tab, click Create . The stock receipt form will open. 3. In the form, open the General tab and find the Vendor field. You can select an existing company or contact, or create a new one. The same way as the Client field in CRM. Client field in CRM item form
Select an existing vendor. If the vendor already exists, start typing the company name or contact name in the Vendor field and select the right option from the list.
Create a new vendor.

1. Enter the company name or the representative's name. 2. Click Create new contact or Create new company . 3. Fill in the phone number, email, address, and company details. 4. If the vendor has several representatives, such as a director and an accountant, click Add participant and enter the additional contacts. 5. Complete the remaining fields in the stock receipt and save your changes. Create a stock receipt
Find the vendor list
You can find the vendor list in both CRM and Inventory management. There, you can open a vendor record, view details, or add a new vendor.
CRM. Go to CRM > Customers > Vendors > Companies or Contacts .
Inventory management. Go to CRM > Inventory > Inventory management > Customers > Vendors > Companies or Contacts .
Click Create in the Companies or Contacts section to add a new vendor. Fill out the form with the name, phone number, and other details. Companies Contacts
Click a contact or company to open the record and view the vendor's details. From there, you can make a call, send an email, or schedule an activity.

For example, if a delivery is delayed, a manager can send an email from the record, confirm the reason for the delay, agree on a new delivery date, and then create a call reminder. Calls, emails, activities, and other events appear in the Timeline. This helps you review the full communication history or hand off the work to another employee. CRM item form: features and settings Timeline in CRM item form
In brief
- Vendors are companies or individuals that supply products. In Inventory Management, you can store all vendor details, including contact information, addresses, and company details.
- Vendors are based on contacts and companies, and their details are stored in CRM item forms.
- You can add a vendor directly in a stock receipt. Choose an existing vendor or create a new one on the spot.
- You can find the vendor list in CRM > Clients > Vendors or in the Inventory Management (documents) section.
- From a vendor record, you can call, send an email, or schedule an activity. The full communication history is stored in the Timeline.

titre: Reset balances
sections: Reset balances

Inventory management in Bitrix24 helps you track products in your warehouse. It records all product operations, including receipts, sales, transfers, and write-offs. It also shows current stock levels in real time.

If your Bitrix24 account already had products with stock quantities before you turned on Inventory management, Bitrix24 will ask you to reset those quantities to zero. You must complete this step before you can enable Inventory management.

This reset prevents incorrect data from carrying over. For example, you may have sold products through CRM without warehouse documents or you may have entered values manually in the Available stock field in the catalog. In both cases, Bitrix24 cannot determine the actual quantity in stock. After the reset, all stock quantities are set to zero, but the products stay in the catalog.
In this article:
- Reset stock to zero
- Enter actual stock quantities
Reset stock to zero
The reset happens automatically during the final step of enabling Inventory management.

1. Go to CRM > Inventory > Inventory management . 2. Select the operating mode and click Select . 3. Choose the costing method and click Enable Inventory management . Costing methods and gross profit report 3. In the Stock will be reset to zero dialog, click Continue . Bitrix24 resets stock quantities to zero and saves document drafts.
After that, inventory management is enabled, and all product stock quantities are set to zero.
Enter actual stock quantities
To make inventory management show accurate product quantities, create a stock adjustment document.
After you enable inventory management, the Inventory section opens with a prompt to add your first stock adjustment.
1. Click Create . 2. In the document, enter the products, quantity, purchase price, and warehouse. 3. Click Save and process .
After you process the document, the products appear in the warehouse with current stock quantities. They also become available for use in CRM. Create a stock adjustment
In brief
- Resetting stock to zero is required. You cannot enable inventory management without it.
- The reset happens automatically when you enable inventory management. Products stay in the catalog, but their stock quantities are set to zero.
- After you enable inventory management, enter your actual stock quantities in a stock adjustment document so inventory management shows accurate data.

titre: Import data from other Inventory management services into Bitrix24
sections: Import data from other Inventory management services into Bitrix24
Inventory management in Bitrix24 helps you track products in your warehouse. It records receipts, sales, transfers, and write-offs, and updates data in real time.

If you already use inventory management in another service, you can move your data to Bitrix24. Your product catalog imports automatically, so you do not need to recreate it or fill out product cards by hand.
In this article:
- Prerequisites for data migration
- How migration apps work
- Migrate data to Bitrix24
Prerequisites for data migration
To transfer data from another service, install an app from Bitrix24 Market. Apps are available for migrations from MoySklad, Zoho Inventory, and QuickBooks Inventory.
These apps work only when inventory management is enabled in Bitrix24. You can find inventory management in two sections: CRM and Sites and Stores .
If inventory management is not enabled:

1. Go to CRM or Sites and Stores > Inventory > Inventory Management . 2. In the Inventory management in Bitrix24 window, click Select . 3. Choose a costing method: average cost or FIFO. Calculate product total cost by average cost method Calculate product cost using FIFO 4. Click Enable inventory management . 5. After you enable it, click Migrate . Bitrix24 Market will open.
If inventory management is already enabled:
1. Go to CRM or Sites and Stores > Inventory Management . 2. In inventory management, click More > Data migration . Bitrix24 Market will open.
How migration apps work
Choose the app for the inventory service you are moving from. Each app has its own supported data and limits.
Zoho Inventory. Data transferred from Zoho Inventory:
- Product name, description, status, unit of measure, creation date, and last modified date
- Product dimensions and weight
- Composition, including whether the product consists of multiple individual products
- Quantity tracking status
- Currency and purchase price
- Stock balance and reserved quantity
What to know:
- You can start migration only if the base currency in Bitrix24 matches the store currency in Zoho Inventory. Add and customize currencies in CRM
- The app imports only products that have the Sales Information block filled out, such as base price per unit and tax rate.
- It transfers products from all Zoho Inventory warehouses into one Bitrix24 warehouse.
- It imports only the main product image.
- It imports only whether tax is included in the price. Other tax details do not transfer.

- Units of measure do not transfer automatically. Before you start the import, add the same units of measure to Bitrix24 that you use in Zoho Inventory. The names must match exactly. For example, if Zoho Inventory uses Pieces , Bitrix24 must also use Pieces . Add units of measurement in CRM
- After import, the app creates a stock adjustment document with only the products that are currently in stock.
QuickBooks Inventory. Data transferred from QuickBooks:
- Products and services
- Categories
What to know:
- The app does not import product bundles or images.
- After import, it creates a stock adjustment document with only the products that are currently in stock.
Migrate data to Bitrix24 Inventory management

1. In Bitrix24 Market, select the app. 2. Click Install . 3. Accept the Terms of use and click Install . 4. Click Open app or wait for it to open automatically. 5. Enter your login and password and click Save . 6. Click Start migration . Migration time depends on the number of products. The process runs in the background, so you can close the page and return later to check the status.
When the import is complete, products will be added to the catalog and a posted stock adjustment document will appear in inventory management.
If the product limit on your Bitrix24 plan is reached during migration, the import will stop. In that case, enable demo mode for your Bitrix24 plan. Free 15-day trial
In brief
- If you use Inventory management in another service, you can automatically transfer your product catalog to Bitrix24.
