You can also contact Bitrix24 partners for help with site settings and configuration. Bitrix24 Partners

titre: Unlink a domain from a site or online store
sections: Unlink a domain from a site or online store
Unlink a domain if you plan to:
- Connect it to another site
- Delete the site but keep the domain
Open site settings:
1. Go to Sites and Stores .
2. Select the site and click the three dots > Configure site .
3. Click the pencil icon in the Site address field.
Open the Bitrix24 subdomain section and replace your current domain with any available one.
Delete or modify resource entries. Resource records can conflict with new settings and break forwarding.
- If you have not decided where to use the domain, delete the resource records. The domain will be unavailable until you add new records.
- If you plan to use the domain in another Bitrix24 zone or on an external site, update the resource records.
If you are not deleting the site or online store, republish it:
1. Set the status to Unpublished .
2. Click Publish .
In brief:
- Unlink the domain if you want to use it on another site, change the Bitrix24 zone, or keep it after deleting a site.
- Go to Sites and Stores and open Configure site .
- Click the pencil icon in the Site address field.
- In the Bitrix24 subdomain section, replace your domain.
- Delete resource records if you are not sure where to use the domain.
- Update resource records if you plan to use the domain elsewhere.
- Leave resource records as is if you connect the domain within the same Bitrix24 zone.
- Republish the site if you keep it.

titre: Connect Google Analytics to Bitrix24
sections: Connect Google Analytics to Bitrix24

Google Analytics is a set of tools that helps you collect site statistics, visitor data, and marketing performance data. It tracks events on your site, such as page views, form submissions, and file downloads.
Connecting Google Analytics is available on Bitrix24 plans and pricing .
How analytics data is collected
Google Analytics automatically collects data from a site that has a tracking code installed. You can view and analyze this data in your account dashboard.
Connect Universal Analytics and Google Analytics 4
Open the Google Analytics website and create an account.
Enter an account name and go to the next step.
Enter a property name. Then select a time zone and currency.
By default, Google creates a Google Analytics 4 property. To create a Universal Analytics property, open Advanced options and turn on the option to create a Universal Analytics property.
Enter your website address. Then choose one of these options: create both property types or create a Universal Analytics property only.
Add your business information and click Create .
To view your properties, go to Admin and open the property list.

You will see two properties: UA — use this one to get the Universal Analytics tracking ID and GA4 — use this one to get the Google Analytics 4 ID. Google creates a separate ID for each analytics type.
To get the tracking code, click Data Streams . Select a stream and open its settings.
Copy the stream ID.
Paste the ID into your site settings. Save the changes and republish the site.
If you connect Google Analytics in the site settings, Bitrix24 collects data from all pages. To collect data from one page only, add the stream ID in that page's settings.
Connect Google Analytics 4 when Universal Analytics is already set up
Go to Admin. Open GA4 Setup Assistant and choose what you want to do: create a new property or connect an existing Google Analytics 4 property.

titre: Place Google Tag Manager container on your site
sections: Place Google Tag Manager container on your site
Google Tag Manager is a free tool that lets you add and manage marketing and analytics tags on your website without editing the site code.
To use Google Tag Manager with sites created in Bitrix24.Sites, add your container ID in the site settings.
Add a Google Tag Manager container ID
1. Go to Google Tag Manager and click Start for free .
2. Click Create Account .
3. Fill out the account form.
4. Copy the container ID (for example, GTM-XXXXXXX).
5. Open your site or page settings in Bitrix24.Sites .
6. Paste the container ID into the Google Tag Manager field.
7. Save your changes.

titre: Add your website to Google
sections: Add your website to Google
When your website is ready, the next step is to help people find it. Most users discover websites through search engines like Google.
Use Google Search Console to add your site to Google’s index.
Why use Google Search Console
Google Search Console helps you manage how your site appears in search results. You can:
- Make sure Google can access your content.
- Submit new pages for indexing and remove outdated ones.
- Improve how your pages appear in search results.
- Keep your site running without affecting search performance.
- Detect and fix malware or spam issues.
Set up Google Search Console
Open the Google Search Console and click Start now .
Select URL prefix , enter your website URL, for example, https://b24-4tzc7y.bitrix24.site and click Continue .
Verify that you own the website.
You can choose one of these methods:
- HTML tag - add a meta tag to your site's home page.
- Domain name provider - sign in to your domain name provider.
- Google Analytics - use your Google Analytics account.
- Google Tag Manager - use your Google Tag Manager account.
In this example, we will use the first method - add a meta tag to our site's home page.
Select the HTML tag option and copy the meta tag.
Go to your Bitrix24 Sites page and select Configure site in the site action menu.
Enable the Google Search Console option in the Ownership verification section and paste the meta tag to the field. Click Save .
Then open the home page and select Page settings in the action menu.
Enable the Get the page indexed by search engines option in the Add to search engine index section. Click Save .
Publish your website.
Check whether the meta tag appeared in the code of the page. Open your website, right-click View page source . Use the search function to find the meta tag.
Go to the Google Search Console and click Verify .
Done! Your ownership has been verified, and your site is indexed by Google.
Google Search Console tools are now available for your website.

titre: Add your website to Bing
sections: Add your website to Bing
Submit your website or online store to Bing Webmaster Tools to help potential customers find your business. Bing Webmaster Tools .
Here are some features of Bing Webmaster:
- Crawling and indexing your website
- Website statistics
- Crawl issues report
- Robots.txt and sitemap.xml validator
- Keyword search tool
- SEO reports
- Malware and phishing re-evaluation
- And many more useful tools
There are two ways to add your website to Bing: by using the Bing Webmaster Tools or Google Search Console .
1. Bing Webmaster Tools
Sign in to the Bing Webmaster Tools with any of the proposed options (Microsoft Account, Google Account, Facebook Account) > specify your website address > click Add .
Then you need to verify that you are the owner of the website. Let's select the second option - HTML Meta Tag . Copy the meta tag.
Open Page settings of the homepage of your website > click More > Custom HTML > paste the copied meta tag. Don't forget to enable the Add to search engine index option.
Save the changes and publish the page to apply them.
Check whether the meta tag appeared in the code of the page. Open your website > right-click > View page source . Use the search function to find the meta tag.
Go back to the Bing Webmaster Tools and click Verify .
Bing Webmaster tools are at your disposal, and your website is submitted to the Bing search engine.
2. Google Search Console

If you are the Bitrix24 Free plan subscriber and have your own domain , you can use the Add CNAME record to DNS option in the Bing Webmaster Tools to verify the website ownership. If you are the Bitrix24 Free plan subscriber and don't have your own domain (your website address ends with .bitrix24.site ), you won't be able to paste the meta tag to the Custom HTML field (as the Custom HTML option is available to the commercial plans subscribers only).
But don't worry! You can import your website if it's already verified in the Google Search Console. Just add your website to Google first, and then add it to Bing.
Go to the Bing Webmaster Tools > click Import .
Click Continue . You'll be asked to sign in to the Google Seach Console .
Select a website from the list of sites already verified in the Google Search Console and click Import .
Bing Webmaster tools are at your disposal, and your website is submitted to the Bing search engine.

titre: Sitemap - sitemap.xml
sections: Sitemap - sitemap.xml
A sitemap helps search engines find and index your website pages.
A sitemap is a file named sitemap.xml. It lists your page URLs and includes basic details, such as the last updated date. This helps search engines crawl your site more efficiently.
Create sitemap
In Bitrix24.Sites, the sitemap.xml file is created automatically.
To add pages to the sitemap:
- Select the website and click View pages .
- Open a page > Actions > Page settings .
- Click More , scroll down, enable Sitemap , and click Save .
Bitrix24 updates the last modified date each time you publish a page.
To include all pages, turn on the Sitemap option for each page.
Check the sitemap.xml file
your_website_address/sitemap.xml

titre: Bitrix24 Sites Terms of Use
sections: Bitrix24 Sites Terms of Use
Bitrix24 Sites helps you create websites and landing pages quickly. Because your site is published online, you must follow applicable laws and basic compliance rules.
Follow applicable laws
Use only content you have the legal right to publish. Do not post information that is restricted or prohibited under the laws of your country.
Laws related to intellectual property, advertising, marketing, and privacy vary by jurisdiction. Make sure your website complies with all relevant regulations.
You are responsible for your content
Alaio Inc. does not create, edit, or publish content on your website. The company does not review or verify the legality of the information posted on sites built with Bitrix24 Sites.
If violations are detected, Alaio Inc. reserves the right to disable the website without prior notice.
Copyright and legal compliance
You confirm that the content published on your website:
- does not violate copyright or intellectual property rights
- does not disclose confidential or private information
- does not harm a person’s reputation, dignity, or rights
- is obtained and used legally
Consult a legal professional
If you are unsure whether certain content complies with the law, consult a qualified attorney before publishing it.
Report violations
Bitrix24 does not monitor websites created with Bitrix24 Sites. If you believe a site violates these rules, submit a report using the Abuse form.
For full details, see the Bitrix24 Terms of Service.
Remember: you are fully responsible for the content published on your website.

titre: CoPilot in Bitrix24 Sites
sections: CoPilot in Bitrix24 Sites
CoPilot, your AI assistant, is now available in Bitrix24 Sites. Use it to create content faster and manage site text more easily.
Without CoPilot, you need to:
- Assign someone to write all site content manually
- Spend time creating and editing text for every page
With CoPilot, you can:
- Generate and improve text
- Get ideas and recommendations
- Fix grammar mistakes and typos
Get started with CoPilot
Go to Sites and Stores and open your site in edit mode. You can also create a new site. Learn how to create a site in Bitrix24
To use CoPilot, click any text block on the page and select CoPilot from the toolbar.
Create and edit text with CoPilot
CoPilot includes built-in pre-prompts to help you work with content faster. Pre-prompts are ready-made requests that generate specific results without needing to write detailed instructions yourself.
The pre-prompts are grouped by task.
Analyze text
Use this group to improve existing content.
For example, if you receive text from a copywriter, CoPilot can:
- Simplify unclear wording
- Shorten long paragraphs
- Keep the main ideas while making the text easier to read
Modify text
Use this group to edit and refine content.
CoPilot can:
- Shorten or expand text
- Add or remove details
- Check spelling and punctuation
- Improve wording and structure
- Translate content into another language
Write for me
Use this group to generate new content from scratch.
Add a short description of what you need, and CoPilot can create:
- Articles
- News posts
- Press releases
- Job descriptions
Write your own prompts
You can also create custom prompts for CoPilot.
Describe the result you want as clearly as possible. The more details you provide, the more accurate the generated text will be.
For example, you can ask CoPilot to create a promotional offer for a beauty salon and include details about services, discounts, and tone of voice.
In brief
- CoPilot is an AI assistant available in Bitrix24 Sites.
- Use CoPilot to generate, edit, and improve site content.
- Built-in pre-prompts help you complete common writing tasks faster.
- CoPilot can check grammar, rewrite text, expand or shorten content, and translate text.
- You can also write your own prompts for more specific results.

titre: Publication of new sites on free plans
sections: Publication of new sites on free plans
Previously published sites and pages will remain active and continue to work.
- Limits do not apply to previously created published or unpublished sites. You can edit and publish these sites and their pages.
- You can create and edit new sites and their pages, but you cannot publish them.
On commercial plans, everything remains unchanged.

titre: New interface for site design
sections: New interface for site design
We updated the color picker for sites and online stores. You can now choose any color for text and backgrounds, adjust opacity, and set background images for blocks.
Customize block colors
On your site page, click Design and select the block you want to edit.
A panel opens on the left. In this panel, you can:
- Choose a preset color . The color applies to the block right away.
- Browse more color combinations . Click More to see additional options.
- Select a custom color or enter a color code . Click the color code to open the palette.
How to set a color code
Click the color code.
Enter a HEX value and click Select .
- Use the site’s primary color . This is the color you selected when you created the site.
- Adjust color opacity . Click Opacity and choose a value.
To restore the original color, click Revert to default color .
Set a background color
Open the Color fill tab to set a background color.
These settings match the text color options, with one difference: you can create gradients in the Gradients tab.
You can:
- Choose linear or radial gradients.
- Swap colors.
- Rotate the gradient.
Change the background image
Open the Image tab in the panel.
Click Upload to add an image, or drag and drop a file into the upload area.
To add a color overlay on top of the image, use the Color overlay tab.

titre: FAQ: Bitrix24 Sites
sections: FAQ: Bitrix24 Sites
This article answers common questions about Bitrix24 Sites.
How do I use Bitrix24 Sites?
Bitrix24 lets you create your own website. Websites include widgets and CRM forms by default. All submitted data goes directly to the CRM. Create your site in Bitrix24
How do I connect my own domain to a Bitrix24 site?
You can connect a custom domain in the site settings. Connect your site to your own domain
Can I add a countdown timer to a page?
Yes. Use the Event countdown block to add a timer for promotions, events, or special offers.
Can I configure SEO settings for my site?
Yes. Bitrix24 Sites include several SEO options:
- Add meta tags for each page
- Include pages in sitemap.xml
- Connect Google Analytics
- Connect Google Tag Manager
- Prevent search engines from indexing a page when needed
How do I delete a site in Bitrix24?
1. Go to Sites and Stores .
2. Open the menu next to the site.
3. Select Delete .
The site moves to the recycle bin and stays there for 30 days. Unpublish and delete sites
You can also unpublish a site to make it unavailable to visitors. You can publish it again later.
Why are blocks missing or not visible on the site?
Check whether the blocks are connected to third-party apps. In the editor, these blocks have a blue exclamation mark icon in the right-side menu.
Review the installed apps for your sites, including template and block sets. Some apps may no longer work because the trial period has expired.
How do I undo unpublished changes to a site?
On the site settings page, use the Undo and Redo buttons to manage recent changes.
You can undo changes within 24 hours.

titre: Place an order in the Bitrix24 online store
sections: Place an order in the Bitrix24 online store

In the Bitrix24 online store, customers can browse the product catalog, choose products, and place an order. During checkout, they select a payment method, choose a delivery option, and enter their personal details. Each order automatically creates a deal in CRM, where a sales representative can review the order details and start processing it.
In this article:
- Place an order as a customer
- Process an order in CRM
Place an order as a customer
A customer can start checkout in two ways:
- Add a product directly to the cart
- Compare several products first, then choose one
Add a product directly to the cart. This option works best when the customer already knows what they want to buy.
1. Hover over a product.
2. Set the quantity with the Plus (+) and Minus (-) buttons.
3. Click Buy . The product is added to the cart, which opens automatically.
4. Click Checkout .
Compare several products. This option works best when the customer wants to review multiple items before making a choice.
1. Hover over a product and select the Compare checkbox to add it to the comparison list.
2. After adding the products you need, open the comparison page in one of these ways:
1. Click Compare products in the pop-up after adding a product.
2. Click Go to comparison page in the Comparison list block in the upper-left corner.
3. On the comparison page, compare all product characteristics or only the differences. You can also choose which characteristics to compare, view product images, and remove products from the list.
4. After choosing a product, click Buy below its name. The product is added to the cart, and the cart opens automatically.
5. Click Checkout .
Checkout has several steps. Click Next to continue or Back to return to the previous step.
1. Shopping cart. The customer reviews the selected products and prices and can apply a discount coupon.
Once checkout starts, the customer cannot change product quantities or remove products. To make changes, they need to go back to the cart, update it, and start checkout again.
2. Payer type. The customer selects who is paying for the order — individual or legal entity. The form fields depend on this choice.

3. Delivery. The customer selects a delivery method. The available options depend on the delivery services connected to the online store. By default, courier delivery and pickup are available. The delivery cost is added to the order total automatically. Delivery services

4. Pickup. If the customer selects pickup, they can choose a warehouse or pickup location. Click Change next to Pickup , then select a location on the map or from the list. If only one warehouse or pickup location is available, it appears automatically.

5. Payment. The customer selects a payment method. The available options depend on the payment systems connected to the online store. By default, two options are available: cash on delivery and a printable invoice. Payment systems for online stores

6. Customer. The customer enters their contact details. The required fields depend on the payer type. An individual enters their name, email, phone number, and delivery address. A legal entity enters the company name, contact person, email, delivery address, and other company details.
After completing all steps, the customer agrees to the processing of their personal data and clicks Checkout to place the order.

After the first order, the customer gets access to a personal section. This is a self-service account where they can manage their details and orders, including tracking order status on the Current orders tab. Online store: Personal account
If the customer has placed an order before and is signed in to their personal section, their details are filled in automatically during checkout.
Process an order in CRM
When a customer places an order in the online store, Bitrix24 automatically creates a deal in CRM with the customer and order details. Work in Store without orders
1. Open CRM > Deals . Online store deals appear in the New stage. Click a deal to open its form.
2. In the Payment and delivery field, review and update the payment and delivery statuses.
3. Depending on the payer type, Bitrix24 creates a contact or company for the customer. It appears in the Client field.
Client field in CRM item form
In brief
- In the Bitrix24 online store, customers can browse the product catalog, choose products, and place an order.
- To place an order, the customer selects a payer type — individual or legal entity, chooses a delivery and payment method, and enters their contact details.
- For each order, Bitrix24 automatically creates a deal in CRM with the customer and order details.

titre: Online store: Personal account
sections: Online store: Personal account

The personal section is where buyers manage their profile and orders in your online store. They can update their information and handle orders without contacting support. For example, they can check order status, top up their account balance, change a delivery address, and review purchase history.
In this article:
- Access the personal section
- Personal section pages
How buyers access the personal section

To access the personal section, a buyer must place an order in the store. During checkout, the buyer enters an email address. That email receives a confirmation message with login details and a link to create a password. Place an order on the website
To sign in to the personal section, click Log in in the lower-left corner of the site. Enter the email address in the Login field and the password created from the email link.
Personal section pages
The personal section includes these pages:
- Current orders
- Personal account
- Personal information
- Order history
- Order profiles
- Shopping cart
- Subscription
Current orders. On this page, buyers can:
- Check order and delivery status
- Change the payment method and pay for an order
- View order details, reorder, or cancel an order

Personal account . A personal account is the buyer's store balance. On this page, buyers can add funds by entering an amount and choosing a payment method. The balance is charged when an order is paid and refunded if a paid order is canceled.
Create a personal account for a buyer in the store
A Bitrix24 administrator or an employee with section configuration access permissions can create a personal account. Inventory access permissions

1. Go to Sites and stores > More > Settings > Customers > Accounts . 2. Click Add a new account to create a new account. 3. In the User field, click +Add , select the buyer from the list or start typing their name in the search field. 4. Click Save . The account is now created. The buyer can top it up in the personal section and use it to pay for orders.
Personal information. On this page, buyers can view and edit their personal details, including full name, email, and password. They can also see the date of the last update and the last sign-in.
Order history. This page shows completed and canceled orders.
Order profiles. This page stores information about people connected to store orders. One account can have several profiles. For example, a buyer may place orders for different recipients.
On this page, buyers can edit profile details such as profile name, buyer name, email, phone number, and address. To delete a profile, click the X icon.
Shopping cart. On this page, buyers can view selected products and continue to checkout.
Subscriptions. This page shows products the buyer has subscribed to. For example, they can subscribe to get notified when a specific size is back in stock. Product subscriptions
When you hover over a product, these actions are available:
- Details — open the product details page
- Unsubscribe — cancel the product subscription
In brief
- The personal section is where buyers manage their profile and orders.
- The personal section is available only in the Classic online store. Clothing template.
- Buyers get access to the personal section after placing their first order.
- In the personal section, buyers can check order status, top up their balance, edit personal information and profiles, view order history, and manage product subscriptions.
- A buyer can have a personal account to add funds and pay for orders.
- A Bitrix24 administrator or an employee with section configuration access permissions can create a personal account.

titre: Configure order and delivery statuses in Bitrix24
sections: Configure order and delivery statuses in Bitrix24

Statuses show the path an order takes in your online store, from placement to delivery. You can customize this flow to match your team's process. For example, you can add an Order confirmation status. This helps managers see each step an order must go through and reduces manual follow-up.
In this article:
- Find status settings
- Configure order statuses
- Configure delivery statuses
Find status settings
Go to Sites and stores > More > Settings > Advanced settings > Statuses . Then choose the section you need: Order statuses or Delivery statuses .
Configure order statuses
By default, an order moves through three stages:
- Initial — with one status: Accepted, awaiting payment .
- Intermediate — with two statuses: Paid, preparing for shipment and Shipped .
- Final — with two statuses for successful and unsuccessful outcomes: Completed and Canceled .
You can add statuses only in two stages: intermediate and final for unsuccessful orders. For all other statuses, you can only change the name and color.
Example: add an intermediate status called Order confirmation . A manager can use it to contact the customer and confirm the order details.

1. Click + Add status under the intermediate statuses section. 2. Enter the name. 3. Click the fill icon to the right of the status name and choose a color from the palette. Color helps you quickly identify statuses in the order form. 4. Click the three-line icon (≡) to the left of the status name and drag the status to the right place in the list. 5. Click Save — the new status will appear in the order form.
Configure delivery statuses
By default, delivery has no intermediate statuses. It includes only two stages:
- Initial — with the status Awaiting processing .
- Final — with two statuses for successful and unsuccessful outcomes: Dispatched and Canceled .

You configure delivery statuses the same way as order statuses. You can add statuses only in two stages: intermediate and final for unsuccessful deliveries. For all other statuses, you can only change the name and color.
Example: add an intermediate status called Ready for dispatch . A warehouse employee can use it to mark an item as packed and ready to ship, so the manager does not need to check the status manually.
1. Click + Add status between the initial and final stages. 2. Enter the name. 3. Click the fill icon to the right of the status name and choose a color from the palette. 4. Click Save .
In brief
- Statuses show the path an order takes in your online store.
- You can configure order and delivery statuses in Sites and stores > More > Settings > Advanced settings > Statuses .
- The flow includes three stages: initial, intermediate, and final for successful or unsuccessful outcomes.
- You can add statuses only in the intermediate stage and in the final stage for unsuccessful orders.
- This setting is only available in Unlimited deals + Orders mode.

titre: Create an order in CRM
sections: Important

The Deals + Orders mode is no longer available for new Bitrix24 accounts. If your account already uses Deals + Orders , it will continue to work as usual. If you switch to Deals , you cannot switch back to Deals + Orders .
The instructions below apply only to accounts that still use Deals + Orders mode. For more details, see the article Work in Store without orders .
Work with orders in CRM
Orders are a key part of any online store. In Bitrix24 CRM, you can create, process, and complete orders in one place.
To view all orders, go to CRM > Orders . The list shows current orders and basic details for each one.
To create a new order, click New order .
Configure order details
First, select the order source and payer type.
Based on your selection, Bitrix24 automatically creates a new contact or company if needed.
Add products
Open the Products tab to add items to the order.
You can:
- Create a new product
- Select an existing product from the catalog
After adding products, Bitrix24 automatically calculates the order total, including:
- Product cost
- Taxes
- Shipping fees
- Weight
- Other charges
If you add or remove products, the total updates automatically.
Specify customer information
Open General > Order properties to add customer details.
You can:
- Create new properties
- Link existing properties to the order
By default, Bitrix24 creates a new contact or company automatically when needed.
Set up payment
Choose a payment method for the order.
By default, the following options are available:
If the customer has already paid, change the payment status to Paid .
Configure shipment
Select a shipping method in the Shipment section.
By default, two options are available:
- Delivery service
- Local pickup
Shipping cost is calculated automatically based on the selected method.
Save the order
Click Save to finish. The order will appear in your online store order list.

titre: Create and configure product catalog
sections: Create and configure product catalog

Bitrix24 uses a single product catalog for both CRM and online stores. When you create a page in your online store, you can add products from this catalog. In CRM, you can add products to an invoice or estimate when working with customers.
Open the product catalog:
- CRM → Inventory → Product catalog
- Sites and Stores → Inventory → Product catalog
Before adding products, create sections and set up custom product properties.
Create product sections
1. Click Create > Section .
2. Enter the name and description.
3. Save the changes.
You can also create subsections. Select a parent section and link subsections to it. Fill in the fields and save.
Add product properties
The catalog includes standard properties such as product name, brand, and unit of measurement.
To create custom properties:
1. Go to Sites and Stores .
2. Open Settings .
3. Click Product catalog .
4. Select Product properties .
5. Click Create .
Main tab
Fill in these fields:
- Type — defines the data format (list, number, file, and others).
- Symbolic code — use Latin characters, numbers, and underscores only.
- Name — property name.
- Sort order — controls where the property appears in the online store.
- Active — enable to show the field in the product form.
- Multiple — allows selecting multiple values.
- Required — makes the field mandatory.
- Searchable — enables search by this field in the catalog and online store.
- Show in online store — displays the field in the store, product form, and catalog.
More tab
Configure additional options:
- Show in product catalog filters — displays the field in store filters.
- Show in smart filter — choose how values appear (checkboxes, radio buttons, or dropdown).
- Show expanded — shows values in expanded form to customers.
- Show hint in smart filter — displays a hint icon next to the field.
Save the changes. The property will be available in the product form.
You can also add product properties in CRM.
Product properties
Create a product
On the Product catalog page:
1. Click Create > Product .
2. Fill in the required fields.
3. Add a description, set the price, and assign the product to a section.
Add products to the catalog in CRM
You can also add product variants. Product variants are different versions of the same product, such as different colors of a T-shirt.
If you have a product list in CSV format, you can import it into Bitrix24.
Working with product variants Product import Access permissions to import and export products
Configure the product catalog
1. Click the Settings icon.
2. Select the fields you want to display.
3. Click Apply .
Enable Apply for everyone to use the same view for all employees.
You can also edit multiple items directly in the list:
1. Select items.
2. Click Edit .
3. Update the data and save.
Summary
- Bitrix24 uses a single product catalog for CRM and online stores.
- Create sections and custom product properties before adding products.
- To add a product, click Create , fill in the fields, set the price, and assign it to a section.

titre: Catalog settings
sections: Catalog settings
In Catalog settings , you can choose how unavailable products appear, decide whether prices include tax, set up a user agreement, and configure other catalog options.
To open catalog settings:
1. Go to Sites and stores .
2. Open the Online stores tab.
3. Open the three-dot menu ( ... ) next to your store.
4. Select Settings .
5. In the left menu, select Catalog settings .
Catalog settings
First, select the product category to show on the page in the Catalog folder field.
Create products and configure product catalog
Then configure the settings in four sections:
- Product and view
- Price and discount
- Analytics
- User agreement
Product and view
Unavailable products : Choose how to show products that are out of stock.
A product with SKUs, or variants, is available if at least one SKU is available.
Unavailable SKUs : Choose how to show SKUs that are out of stock.
Notification : Turn on back-in-stock notifications. Product subscription
Quantity : Allow customers to choose how many items to buy, or require them to buy one item at a time.
Product comparison : Turn on product comparison. Place an order on the website
Shopping cart alignment : Choose where the shopping cart appears on your website.
Price and discount
Price type : Select the price type to show in the catalog.
If you do not select a price type, the Buy and Add to Cart buttons will not be available.
Show quantity range prices : Turn on this option to show all price types.
Show price for quantity : Enter the quantity used to show the price.
Tax rate : Specify whether VAT is included in the product price.
Old price : Turn on this option to show the previous price.
Discount percent : Turn on this option to show the discount value in the catalog.
Analytics
Send data : Turn on this option to send e-commerce data to Google.
Leave the other fields unchanged.
User agreement
Require user agreement : Turn on this option and select the consent that customers must accept when they place an order.

titre: Setting up SEO parameters for the product catalog
sections: Setting up SEO parameters for the product catalog
SEO helps your website appear higher in search engine results.

When you configure SEO parameters, search engines can better understand and rank your website content. Higher rankings help more customers find your products and make purchases. In Bitrix24, you can configure SEO settings for the entire product catalog, catalog sections, images, and individual products.
Set up SEO parameters for the product catalog
To configure SEO settings for the entire product catalog:
1. Go to CRM > Inventory > Product catalog .
2. Click the gear icon.
3. Select Catalog SEO settings .
In this example, we’ll use an online clothing store. Start by adding meta tag templates for catalog sections and products.
Meta tags are HTML elements that give search engines information about a webpage. Search engines like Google and Amazon use meta tags to rank search results.
You can enter meta tags manually or generate them automatically from catalog fields.
META TITLE and Section title
The META TITLE and Section title templates define:
- the title shown in the browser tab
- the section heading on the page
META KEYWORDS and META DESCRIPTION
Use the META KEYWORDS and META DESCRIPTION templates to add keywords and descriptions for catalog sections.
When users search for phrases that match these keywords, search engines can show the section in search results with the related description.
To verify the changes, open the page HTML in your browser and check the updated meta tags.
Configure image SEO settings
You can also configure SEO settings for full-size images.
Available parameters include:
- ALT template : Displays alternative text if the image cannot load. For example, this can happen because of a slow connection or browser settings.
- TITLE template : Shows additional information when users hover over the image.
- File name template : Creates readable file names for images.
Clear the cache
In the Manage section, enable the Clear cache option to apply changes immediately.
Configure SEO settings for a specific product
After you save the catalog settings, Bitrix24 applies them to all products.
To change SEO parameters for a specific product:
1. Open the product form.
2. Click the gear icon.
3. Select SEO settings .
Well-configured SEO parameters can improve your website ranking in search engines. This helps customers find your products faster and can increase sales.

titre: Simple product variants
sections: Simple product variants

You can manage product variants at any time. Add or remove variants, or create new properties like color or size. In Bitrix24, products are created with variants by default. Each variant has a unique ID.
Edit products
If a product does not have variants, you cannot add new properties to it.
To fix this, create a new product or copy an existing one. Before copying, delete the mnemonic code. If you don’t, the system will show an error and the copy will fail.
To add a new variant:
1. Open the product form.
2. Click Add SKU .
3. Enter the variant details.
To edit, deactivate, or delete a variant, open the action menu and select the needed option.
In brief:
- You can add or remove product variants and properties at any time.
- Products without variants do not support new properties.
- Create or copy a product to work with variants. Remove the mnemonic code before copying.
- To add a variant, open the product and click Add SKU .
- Use the action menu to edit, deactivate, or delete variants.

titre: Change the online store catalog title
sections: Change the online store catalog title

When a customer opens your online store product catalog, the browser tab shows a default title, such as Catalog . Search engines use this title to understand what the page is about. You can change it to improve how the page appears in search results. For example, a sneaker catalog could use the title Original Sneakers at Low Prices .
In this article:
- Change the title in the product catalog
- Change the title in the store page settings
Change the title in the product catalog
To change the title, edit the section SEO settings. Use this option when you want to set a title for a specific section or subsection, such as Laptops , Smartphones , or Accessories .

1–3. Go to Sites and stores > Inventory > Product catalog . 4–5. Click Menu (≡) next to the section or subsection name and select Edit . 6–7. Open the SEO tab. Use the META TITLE template field to set the browser tab title. Setting up SEO parameters for the product catalog
You can change the title in two ways.
Enter the title manually. Enter a title in the META TITLE template field and save your changes. Use this option when you need a unique title for a specific section.
Fill the title automatically from the section name. Use this option when the browser tab title should match the section name.

Click the three dots (...) to the right of the META TITLE template field and select Section fields > Current section name . The formula {=this.Name} will appear in the field and insert the section name automatically. Save your changes.
Change the title in the store page settings

In the store page settings, you can set the title that appears in the browser tab. Use this option when you want to change the title for the entire catalog page, for example, to something like Online Store Product Catalog .
If you set a title both in the product catalog and in the page settings, the catalog title takes priority.

1–3. Go to Sites and stores > Online stores . Hover over the store and click View pages . 4–6. Open the Catalog folder. Find the Catalog page and click Actions > Page settings . 7–9. In the Page settings section, click the arrow next to More . Select the Edit meta tags checkbox and enter the title in the Title, title tag field. 10. Save your changes. The browser tab will show the title from the Title (TITLE tag) field. Webpage title
In brief
- When a customer opens a product catalog in your online store, the browser tab shows a default title, such as Catalog .
- You can change this title to improve how the page appears in search results. You can do this in the product catalog or in the store page settings.

- To change the title for a specific catalog section or subsection, go to Sites and stores > Inventory > Product catalog . Click Menu (≡) next to the section and select Edit . Open the SEO tab and enter a title in the META TITLE template field, or fill it automatically from the section name by selecting Section fields > Current section name .

- To change the title for the entire catalog page, go to Sites and stores > Online stores > View pages . Open the Catalog folder, configure the Catalog page, and enter a value in the Title (TITLE tag) field.
- If both titles are set, the title from the product catalog overrides the title from the page settings.

titre: Product subscriptions
sections: Product subscriptions

Product subscriptions help you keep potential buyers when a product is out of stock. On the product page, customers see the Notify when back in stock button. They enter their email address and get a notification when the product becomes available again. This helps you avoid lost sales and understand real demand for a product.
Product subscriptions are not available in the CRM + Online Store template.
In this article:
- Enable product subscriptions
- Find the subscription list
Enable product subscriptions
To let customers subscribe to out-of-stock products, update settings in two places: Inventory management and products and Catalog settings .
Step 1. Update settings in Inventory management and products

1. Go to Sites and stores > More > Settings > Advanced settings > Inventory management and products . 2. Turn on Enable subscription for out-of-stock products . 3. Turn off Make out-of-stock items available for purchase . Otherwise, customers will be able to place an order, and the Notify when back in stock button will not appear. Inventory management settings 4. Click Save .
Step 2. Update Catalog settings
1. Go to Sites and stores > Stores . 2. Select the store you need and click Three dots (...) > Settings . 3. Turn on Enable back-in-stock notifications . 4. Save your changes. Catalog settings
Step 3. Check that the Notify when back in stock button appears on the site

1. Go to Sites and stores > Stores . 2. Click Open next to the store address. 3. Open any out-of-stock product. On the product details page, you will see the Notify when back in stock button. Create a detailed product page 4. If a customer is signed in to their account on the store site and clicks Notify when back in stock , they will see a confirmation message. If they are not signed in, a window will open and ask for their email address.
When the product is back in stock, the customer gets an email. After they place an order, the subscription is removed automatically.
Find the subscription list
Go to Sites and stores > More > Settings > Customers > Product subscriptions .
This section shows the subscription date, customer email, product name, and other details. You can also filter the list by values such as subscription date and product ID.
In brief
- Product subscriptions let customers get notified when out-of-stock products become available again.
- Bitrix24 administrators and employees with permission to edit site content settings and out-of-stock product sale settings can enable subscriptions.
- To enable subscriptions, update settings in two places: Inventory management and products and Catalog settings .
- In Inventory management and products , turn on Enable subscription for out-of-stock products and turn off Make out-of-stock items available for purchase .
- In Catalog settings , turn on Enable back-in-stock notifications .
- The Notify when back in stock button appears on the product details page for out-of-stock items.
- When the product is back in stock, the customer gets an email. After they place an order, the subscription is removed automatically.
- You can find the subscription list at Sites and stores > More > Settings > Customers > Product subscriptions .

titre: Configure order and delivery statuses
sections: Configure order and delivery statuses
An important part of setting up an online store is defining the stages an order goes through.
Configure order statuses
Go to Sites and Stores > Stores > Settings > Advanced Settings > Statuses > Order Statuses .
By default, Bitrix24 includes a standard set of statuses.
Each order pipeline must include:
- One initial status
- One final successful status
- One final unsuccessful status
You can add as many intermediate statuses as your business process requires.
To create a new status:
1. Click Add Status .
2. Enter a name for the status.
3. Select a color.
4. Save the changes.
To reorder statuses, drag a status to the required position in the list and save the changes.
The new status becomes available for all orders.
Configure delivery statuses
Go to Sites and Stores > Stores > Settings > Advanced Settings > Statuses > Delivery Statuses .
Delivery statuses are configured the same way as order statuses.
By default, delivery includes:
- One initial status
- One final successful status
- One final unsuccessful status
There are no intermediate delivery statuses by default.

titre: Delivery services
sections: Delivery services

Delivery is usually the last step in a deal. To avoid issues during checkout, set up your Online Store delivery services in advance. By default, the store includes two delivery options: Local pickup and Delivery service . You can also create custom delivery services so customers can choose the option that works best for them.
Go to Sites and Stores > Payment systems and Delivery > Delivery services .
In this section, you can view all available delivery services. To create a new one, click Add > Custom delivery service .
In the General parameters tab, enter the delivery service name and description. Customers will see this information during checkout.
Next, open the Handler settings tab and specify the delivery time and cost.
In the Restrictions tab, you can limit the delivery service by different conditions. For example, you can make express delivery available only in certain locations.
In the Extra services tab, you can add optional services. For example, you can offer door-to-door delivery.
When you finish the setup, click Save .
The new delivery service will appear in the shopping cart. Customers will be able to select it together with any extra services you added.

titre: Payment systems for online stores
sections: Payment systems for online stores

After creating a product catalog, set up your payment systems. By default, Bitrix24 includes Internal account, Cash, and PayPal as payment options. You can also integrate other payment systems if needed.
To view and manage your payment systems:
1. Go to Sites and stores .
2. Click More .
3. Expand Payment systems and Delivery .
4. Select Payment systems .
To add a new payment system:
1. Click New payment system .
2. Choose a handler. You can select from the following payment systems:
1. Cash: The customer pays the courier in cash upon delivery.
2. Payment forward (cash on delivery): The customer pays for the order at the post office when the package arrives.
3. PayPal: The customer pays online via PayPal. You'll need a PayPal Business Account to use this option. Register a PayPal Business Account
3. The handler name and payment system fields are completed automatically. Add a description if needed.
4. Click Apply . The Restrictions tab will appear, where you can set limits by payer type, price, delivery method, and more.
5. Click Save .
Depending on the selected payment system, you might need to enter specific handler data. Connect payment systems in Sales Center
The new payment system will now appear in your online store’s checkout process.
In brief
- Bitrix24 includes default payment systems: Internal account, Cash, and PayPal.
- You can add other payment systems and set restrictions by payer type, price, or delivery option.
- New payment systems appear automatically in your store’s checkout.

titre: Online Store: Triggers
sections: What are triggers?
Triggers help automate your online store workflows. They track customer actions, such as:
- Paying for an order
- Submitting a CRM form
- Making or receiving a call
When a trigger detects an action, it automatically moves the order to the appropriate stage.
Each trigger runs based on specific conditions. You can also enable Allow switching to previous status to let a trigger move an order back to an earlier stage.
Available triggers
Runs when you change the person responsible for the order.
Runs when you send or receive an email related to the order, or when a customer views an email.
Runs when a customer clicks a specific link in an email. Add the same link in the trigger settings (for example, a quote or order page link).
Runs when you receive or miss a call from the contact or company linked to the order. You can choose which communication channel to track.
Runs when the customer linked to the order submits a selected CRM form.
Runs when the customer completes a payment. Payment details appear in the order timeline.
Runs when you approve a shipment or add a tracking number in the Shipment section of the order.
Runs when you mark the order as Shipped .
Runs when the order is canceled.
Runs when an external system sends a webhook request for the order.
Runs when visit tracking starts.
Runs when a known customer returns to your website.
Runs when a customer sends a message in the selected open channel. You can track the first message or every message.
Runs when you create a document from a template in the order.
Runs when a customer opens a document generated from the order template.

titre: Online Store: Automation rules for employees
sections: Online Store: Automation rules for employees
Automation rules and triggers help you automate order processing, notify customers about order updates, and assign tasks to your team.
Types of automation
Automation tools are divided into three groups:
- Automation rules for employees – update order details, run workflows, create tasks, and notify team members.
- Automation rules for client communications – send emails, SMS messages, or automated calls.
- Triggers – update the order status automatically.
Set up automation rules
1. Go to Online Store → Orders .
2. Click Automation rules .
3. Select Configure automation rules .
How automation rules work
An automation rule runs when an order enters the stage where the rule is set.
- When the order moves to a new stage, rules from the previous stage stop running.
- Use Run after previous rule to control the order of actions.
Enable this option when you need actions to run one after another. For example, create an order number and then send it to the customer.
If you disable this option, all rules in the stage run at the same time.
Available automation rules
Adds an activity to the order. You can view it in the order form.
Adds a message to the order history.
Adds a comment to the order timeline.
Posts a message to the activity feed.
Marks all shipments in the order as approved for delivery.
Marks the order as Paid, Shipped, or Canceled.
Assigns a new owner to the order.
Updates the order stage.
Sends a notification to an employee. You can configure the sender in Notification , but not in Control .
Creates a document from a selected template.
Adds a new item to a selected list.
Deletes the CRM record if the order is not paid.
Retrieves data from a contact, company, or employee profile.
Updates order fields or related details.
Updates an item in a selected list.
Updates shipment fields in the order.
Sends a message to an employee. For customer messages, use rules in Client communications .
Creates a code based on defined rules.
Use it in later steps when Run after previous rule is enabled.
Retrieves data from a selected list.
Starts a selected workflow.
Creates a call or meeting activity.
Updates the shipment status.
Creates a task.
Pauses the process until a customer action or a set time. Then notifies the responsible employee.

titre: Online Store: Automation rules for client communications
sections: Online Store: Automation rules for client communications
Automation rules help you manage orders, keep customers informed, and automate communication.
Types of automation
Automation tools include three groups:
They are divided into three groups:
- Automation rules for employees – update order data, run workflows, create tasks, and notify team members.
- Client communications automation rules – send emails, SMS messages, or automated calls.
- Triggers – update order status automatically.
Set up automation rules
1. Go to Online Store → Orders .
2. Click Automation rules .
3. Select Configure automation rules .
How automation rules work
A rule runs when an order enters the stage where the rule is set.
- When the order moves to a new stage, rules from the previous stage stop running.
- Use Run after previous rule to control the order of actions.
Enable this option to run actions one after another. For example, generate an order number and then send it to the customer.
If you disable it, all rules in the stage run at the same time.
Available automation rules
Use this rule to call a customer automatically. You must connect telephony first.
Settings:
- Origination number — the number used for the outgoing call.
- — choose what the customer hears:
- Text — the system reads your message.
- Audio file — plays an .mp3 file.
For text calls, set the language, voice, speed, and volume. You can insert dynamic values, such as the customer name or order number.
For audio calls, provide a public link to an .mp3 file.
Use this rule to send text messages to customers. Configure an SMS provider first (for example, Twilio ).
Key points:
- Message length should not exceed 200 characters.
- Pricing and limits depend on your provider.
Settings:
- Phone number type — select which number to use.
- If not available, the rule will not run.
- Auto select uses the first number in the contact or company record.
- Provider — select your SMS provider.
Use this rule to send emails from a connected mailbox .
Settings:
- From - select the mailbox.
- Auto select uses the last used mailbox.
- Subject and text - enter your email content.
- You can insert CRM or order fields.
- Client address type - select which email address to use.
- If not available, the rule will not run.
- Auto select uses the first available address.
Sends a message through the last channel the customer used to contact you.
Hidden message (whisper mode) Enable this option to send an internal message. The customer will not see it, but your team will.

titre: Automation rules and triggers in CRM: Employee monitoring and control
sections: Automation rules and triggers in CRM: Employee monitoring and control
Automation rules and triggers in CRM help you automate routine work.
Automation rules can send emails or chat messages, create tasks, and generate documents.

Triggers respond to customer actions or changes in CRM. For example, they can react when a customer opens an email, pays an invoice, or updates a field. When a trigger fires, it can move the CRM item to a new stage.
Automation rules in CRM Triggers in CRM
Go to CRM , select an entity, and click Automation .
Automation rules and triggers are grouped by purpose, such as client communication, employee notifications, or document processing.
This article covers the Employee monitoring and control group. These rules help supervisors track employee work, assign tasks, and get alerts when deadlines are missed.
Notify supervisor
Sends a notification when tasks are overdue or rules are violated. For example, if an employee does not contact a customer or move a deal to the next stage on time.
Time : Run immediately or after a delay.
Condition : Add CRM data (like responsible person or deal amount) to the message.
Recipients : By default, the employee’s supervisor receives the notification.
Add history entry
Adds a note to the CRM history so supervisors can track progress.
Time : Run immediately or after a delay.
Condition : Define the text. You can include CRM data such as deal amount, client name, or responsible employee.
Created by : Choose which user appears as the author of the entry.
You can view entries in the History tab of the CRM item or in the CRM History section.
Create task
Creates a task when a CRM item reaches a specific stage.
Example: At the Project Preparation stage, assign a task to designers.
Task name : Include CRM data like deal name or customer name.
Task description : Add details such as order info or customer requirements.
Responsible : Select the employee who will perform the task.
Deadline : Set when the task is due. Enable Respect working hours specified in the Bitrix24 settings , or adjust the time settings if needed.
More : Add participants, link the task to a workgroup, enable time tracking, and more. Create a task
Once set up, the task is created automatically when the item reaches the stage.
Watch for task status (trigger)
Moves a CRM item to another stage when a linked task reaches a specific status.
Example: When a task is complete, move the deal to Project Presentation to Client .
Trigger name : Rename it if you use multiple triggers.
Status : Select the task status that activates the trigger.
Task fields : Add filters, such as tasks with specific keywords.
Change stage as : Choose the user who appears as the one who changed the stage.
Allow moving back to previous status : Let the trigger return the item to a previous stage if needed.
End task
Automatically completes tasks created by other automation rules.
Example: At the Successful Deal stage, close all related tasks.
Complete tasks created in pipeline : Select a pipeline (for deals).
End tasks created while in stage : Choose the stage where tasks were created.
To select multiple stages, hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac).
Plan activity
Creates an activity, such as a call, meeting, or document task, when a CRM item reaches a stage. Universal activity in CRM
Example: At the Create papers stage, schedule a call to discuss contract terms.
Name : Set the activity name.
Description : Add instructions. You can insert CRM field values.
Activity deadline : Set the date and time. Time settings in automation rules
Responsible person : Assign the activity owner.
Choose color : Use colors to organize activities in the calendar.
More actions : Select one or more options:
- Add to calendar : Show the activity in the calendar.
- Select customer : If the item includes multiple clients, choose one or all of them for the activity. This helps the responsible user contact the correct client.
- Invite users : Add colleagues to the activity.
- Enter address : Specify an address for an off-site meeting.
- Select location : Book a meeting room in the office.
- Attach link : Add a link to a Bitrix24 video call. You can insert values from CRM fields.
- Attach file : Add a document or any other file.
Auto complete activity when entity moves to a different stage : Automatically close the activity when the CRM item moves to another stage. Turn this off if you want manual completion.
When the deal reaches the selected stage, the activity appears in both the CRM item form and the user’s calendar.

titre: Online store in Bitrix24: Getting started
sections: Online store in Bitrix24: Getting started
Bitrix24 online store is a ready-to-use solution for online sales. You can launch it quickly and start accepting orders without any programming skills or additional services.
Bitrix24 provides everything you need:
- Ready-made templates designed for different sales scenarios, whether you’re selling through messengers, social networks, or running a store with a large catalog.
- Built-in product catalog with photos, descriptions, prices, and inventory tracking, so customers can easily view products and place orders.
- Flexible payment and delivery settings , allowing you to connect multiple payment systems and delivery methods.
- Free domain name , which is useful for testing your store and starting initial sales. Later, you can connect your own domain to match your brand.
- Full CRM integration , ensuring that products and inventory update automatically and all orders go directly into your Bitrix24.
In this article:
- Use an online store to grow your business
- Create and configure a product catalog
- Configure your online store
- Manage access permissions
- Connect payment systems and delivery services
- Change the domain and add your store to search engines
Use an online store to grow your business
Bitrix24 online store creates new opportunities for businesses of any size, from small workshops to large retail chains. It makes sales easier and helps you attract more customers.
- Reduce costs — sell online without paying for rent or in-store staff.
- Keep a customer database — all orders and contacts are saved in the CRM, so employees can track interaction history and continue working with customers.
- Expand your audience — sell not only in your city but also across the country or internationally.
- Sell 24/7 — customers can place orders anytime it’s convenient for them.
- Support any assortment — sell products, services, subscriptions, online courses, tickets, and more.
- Automate sales — orders are sent to your Bitrix24, and customers automatically receive notifications. This saves employees time and reduces errors.
Create and configure a product catalog

Bitrix24 offers a single product catalog for both CRM and online stores. You can create it manually or upload a ready-made file if you have a large product range. Create and configure product catalog Product import

Add photos, descriptions, prices, and product properties such as color or size. Organize products into sections and subsections for easier navigation. Once the catalog is linked to your online store, customers can quickly find what they need. To show only available items, set up inventory management. Bitrix24 Inventory Management
Configure your online store

In Bitrix24, you can create an online store using a ready-made system template or one from the Market. Each template includes everything you need, such as a product catalog, shopping cart, checkout page, and more.

To customize the store for your business, edit the template blocks, design, and catalog settings, like product display, pricing, and cart placement. Create an online store in Bitrix24 Add custom CSS to website and online store Site and page settings
Manage access permissions

Control employee access to the entire Stores section or to specific online stores. Use standard roles or create custom ones. Specify which actions employees can perform to prevent errors, protect data, and ensure clear task distribution within your team.

For example, you might allow a manager to edit content and publish the store, so they can update the catalog and share information about new promotions. An administrator has full access to set up the store and manage promotions. Site access permissions
Connect payment systems and delivery services
Make checkout easy for customers by offering a variety of payment and delivery options.

By default, customers can pay using their internal account or cash. Delivery options include courier delivery or self-pickup. You can also add other methods, such as card payments, instant payment systems, or third-party delivery services. This lets customers select their preferred option and encourages repeat purchases. Personal area in the online store Payment systems for Online store Delivery services
Change the domain and add the store to search engines

By default, every Bitrix24 online store is assigned a free address on the *.bitrix24.shop subdomain, allowing you to start selling and testing your store at no extra cost. Later, you can connect your own domain to build customer trust and make the store part of your brand. Connect your site or store to your own domain

To attract more customers, add your store to search engines and set up SEO. This increases its visibility to new audiences and allows you to track analytics and ad campaigns. Setting up SEO parameters for the product catalog Add your website to Google
In brief
- Bitrix24 online store is a ready-to-use solution for online sales. You can launch it quickly and start accepting orders without coding or extra services.
- Bitrix24 offers a single product catalog for both CRM and online stores. You can create it manually or upload a ready-made file if you have a large product range.

- Add photos, descriptions, prices, and product properties such as color or size. Organize products into sections and subsections for easier navigation. Once the catalog is linked to your online store, customers can quickly find what they need.
- To create an online store, choose a ready-made template, edit blocks, and configure the design and catalog.
- Control access to the store using standard or custom roles to prevent errors and ensure clear task distribution within your team.
- Make checkout easy by connecting payment systems and delivery services, so customers can choose how to pay and receive their orders.
- If needed, change the domain and add your store to search engines to increase visibility and reach more customers.

titre: Work in Store without orders
sections: Work in Store without orders
In the Online Store, you can use the Without Orders mode. This mode lets you manage sales through deals instead of orders.
Why use deals instead of orders
Working with deals has several benefits:
- It’s a familiar and simple workflow.
- All data is stored in one place. You can quickly find customer details and track the sales process.
- You can use automation tools such as business processes, apps, and pipelines.
It works well for companies that don’t have a dedicated order management team or don’t rely on e-commerce as their main business.
Important
The Deals+Orders mode is no longer available for new Bitrix24 users.
If you already use Deals+Orders , it will continue to work as is.
If you switch to Deals , you can’t switch back to Deals+Orders .
In the deal timeline, you can track:
- Payments
- Deliveries
- Customer communication (SMS, email, chat)
Enable or disable work without orders
1. Go to CRM > Deals .
2. Click the gear icon and select Order handling mode .
3. Choose one of the options:
1. Deals
2. Deals + Orders

titre: Create an online store in Bitrix24
sections: Create an online store in Bitrix24

You can launch an online store in Bitrix24 without programming skills. The ready-made templates include everything you need for sales, like a product catalog, shopping cart, checkout page, and more. You can customize the blocks and design of the store to suit your business needs. The online store is integrated with the CRM—products and inventory are updated automatically, and orders are sent directly to your Bitrix24.
In this article:
- Create an online store
- Customize blocks and design
- Add and configure the product catalog
- Publish the online store
Create an online store
1. Go to the Sites and Stores section > Online Stores > click Create .
2. A template catalog will open where you can choose the one that suits your needs.
3. Click Create Online Store .
Standard templates
- CRM + Online Store . Optimized for mobile devices. Suitable for sales through messengers and social networks.
- Classic online store. Clothing . A fully loaded template that can be easily customized for your business. Ideal for stores with a large number of products.
- Classic online store. Handmade items . A minimalist template for stores with a small number of products.
- Products on Sale . Designed for promoting a single product.
Templates from the Bitrix24 Market
1. Click Download template from Market .
2. Select one of the tags and choose a template from the list.
3. Alternatively, search for a template using keywords. Enter them in the search bar and select the desired template from the list.
Install an online store
1. Read the template description and click Install .
2. Review the Bitrix24 Market terms of use and check all required boxes. Click Install .
3. Click Open application .
4. Click Complete installation .
5. To preview the store, click Demo . It will open in a new browser tab.
6. Click Install .
7. Select the uploaded template and click Create Store .
Customize blocks and design
After creating the store, it will open in the editor. Here, you can add and modify blocks, customize the design, adjust the layout, and configure the product catalog.
Add additional blocks
Add the necessary blocks:
1. Click the Add block button where you want to place it.
2. Select a template from the list.
Customize a block
Hover over the block you want to edit—a list of available actions will appear:
- Edit . Change the block settings and content, like the title and captions for elements.
- Design . Change the block style settings and configure its visibility on desktops, tablets, and smartphones.
- Superblock . Add or remove block elements, like titles, icons, images, videos, and more.
- Additional actions for the block : move, delete, hide, copy, and more.
To undo or redo an action, use the buttons at the top of the screen.
Create and configure your Bitrix24 site CoPilot: AI assistant to create websites
Add and configure the product catalog
To allow customers to purchase products, link the CRM catalog to the store.
Add a product catalog to the Online store
1. Click Online store features > Settings (⚙️) .

2. Open the Catalog settings tab.Click the icon next to the folder name and select the catalog section with all the products you plan to sell in the store. Items inside can be listed together or grouped into subsections. New products should be added to this catalog.
3. Fill in the remaining fields and click Save .
Catalog settings
Products from the catalog will appear in the Product list block without being divided into subsections.
Customize the product list block
Click Edit to configure the block. Fill in the fields and save the changes.
Go to the Bitrix24 product catalog to manage products—create new ones or edit existing ones.
Set SEO tags and page title. Check the box if you want to apply the catalog's SEO settings to the store. Setting up SEO parameters for the product catalog
Section ID. Leave the default value to ensure the product catalog displays correctly in the store.
Sorting. Specify the field to sort products by and the order: ascending or descending.
Buttons. Choose the action for the button under the product: add to cart or purchase—proceed to checkout. Edit the button labels and add a message for out-of-stock items.
Configure catalog navigation
If the product catalog has subsections, add links to them in the store menu.
1. Open the Header page.
2. Click on a menu item to edit it.
3. Change the name.
4. Configure the click action: select Open product page from the dropdown menu.
5. Click the icon and choose the desired catalog item or section.
6. Save the changes.
7. To manage menu items, hover over an item and click ➕ to duplicate it, or the bin icon to delete it.
Publish the Online store

By default, Auto-publish mode is enabled. Stores are published after the first edit. When you edit the store, changes are applied automatically. If the edit does not appear, click Publish store —the change will appear in the store.

If auto-publish is disabled, click Preview —the store will open in a new tab, and edits will only be visible to you. To check how the store will look on different devices, click the icons at the top of the screen.
Click Publish store to make the changes available to customers. Auto publish and preview options and site navigation
In brief
- Bitrix24 helps you launch an online store using a ready-made template. It includes everything you need for sales, like a product catalog, shopping cart, and checkout page.
- You can customize the blocks and design of the store to suit your business needs.
- The online store is integrated with the CRM—products and inventory are updated automatically, and orders are sent directly to your Bitrix24.
- To create a store, go to the Sites and Stores section > Online Stores > click Create .Choose a standard template or upload one from the Bitrix24 Market.
- Customize the blocks, store design, and product catalog.
- To synchronize product inventory between the CRM and the store, you need to set up Inventory management.
- For sites and stores, Auto-publish mode is enabled by default—changes are applied to the store automatically. If the edit does not appear, click Publish store —the change will appear in the store.
- If auto-publish is disabled, click Preview —the site will open in a new tab, and edits will only be visible to you. Click Publish store to make the changes available to customers.

titre: FAQ: Online store
sections: FAQ: Online store

Bitrix24 online store is a ready-to-use solution for online sales. You can launch it quickly and start accepting orders without any programming skills or additional services. This article answers frequently asked questions about working with online stores in Bitrix24.
- How to show multiple variants of a product to customers
