You can dismiss an employee with active integrations ( webhooks A webhook is a piece of code that tracks changes on one website and sends that data to another. ) the same way as any other employee: from the employee list or from their profile.
When you dismiss an employee with active integrations, Bitrix24 shows a dialog box. You can choose to disable the integrations or keep them active.
To dismiss an employee with active webhooks:
1. Go to the employee list.
2. Next to the employee's name, click Menu (≡) > Dismiss .
3. Choose one of these options:
1. Keep integrations and dismiss
2. Disable integrations and dismiss
Disable integrations and dismiss. The employee is dismissed like any other user, and the integrations stop working. Dismiss an employee
Keep integrations and dismiss. If you keep the integrations active, Bitrix24 transfers them to a system user, and the integrations continue to work. System user in Bitrix24

The system user is a service account that Bitrix24 automatically creates when you dismiss an employee who has active integrations. The system user gets the permissions required for the webhooks to keep working.
Access to Bitrix24 data through webhooks remains available. Anyone with the webhook link can still use it.
To view the list of employees with active integrations:
1. Go to the Developer resources section.
2. Click Integrations .
If another employee edits an integration (webhook) that is assigned to the system user, Bitrix24 reassigns the integration to that employee. After that, the system user no longer manages it.
View tasks and activities of a dismissed employee
Even after termination, you can view:
- Your conversations with a dismissed employee
- Tasks they participated in
- Meetings they attended
- Files they created
- Feed posts
- Groups they were part of

To access this information, open the employee's profile. By default, terminated employees may be hidden. To display them in the list, the Bitrix24 administrator must enable the Show terminated employees in the employee list option.
1. Click the icon next to Bitrix24 or your company name and select Settings .
2. Go to the Employees > Invitations tab.
3. Enable the Show terminated employees in the employee list option. Save changes.
1. Go to the Employees section and click Menu (≡) > View profile .
2. Select the required section, such as Drive or Tasks. To access the chat, click Conversation history .
Rehire a dismissed employee
1. Go to the Employees section.
2. Click the Menu (≡) icon and select Hire .
To rehire an employee from the personal profile, click Dismissed > Hire .
In brief
- If employees no longer work at your company, you can terminate their access to Bitrix24. They will lose access, but all their tasks, conversations, and files will remain.
- Dismissed employees can be found in the user list.
- Only a Bitrix24 administrator or a user with the access permission can terminate an employee.
- You can dismiss an employee from their personal profile or the employee list.
- If an employee has active integrations, such as webhooks, you can choose to disable them or keep them active under a system user.
- If you didn’t transfer the employee’s responsibilities before termination, you can do it afterward by assigning a new responsible person for tasks, CRM items, files, and other data.
- After termination, you can view your conversations, tasks, meetings, files, and more related to the employee in their personal profile.
- By default, dismissed employees may be hidden in the list. To display them, the administrator should enable the Show dismissed employees option.
- You can rehire a dismissed employee in the employee list or the personal profile.

titre: Change or dismiss the main administrator in Bitrix24
sections: Change or dismiss the main administrator in Bitrix24
The primary administrator is the employee who created your Bitrix24 account. System notifications are sent to their email address, including plan renewals, Feed updates, and webinar invitations.
If this employee leaves the company or no longer manages Bitrix24, transfer their rights to another user. Only another administrator can perform this action.

The primary administrator has the same permissions as other administrators, with one key difference: only this user can approve the transfer of ownership and confirm their own removal. This prevents unauthorized changes to the account owner.
Transferring rights and removing the primary administrator follow the same steps. The difference is that after removal, the employee can no longer sign in to Bitrix24.
In this article:
- Send a request
- Confirm the transfer of rights
Send a request
To get primary administrator rights, send a request to the current primary administrator.
1. Open the primary administrator’s profile. Click Administrator > Revoke administrator permissions. 2. Confirm the action and click Yes, send.
When the administrator responds, you will receive a message from the Admin bot in chat.
Confirm the transfer
The primary administrator receives a message from the Admin bot with the request details.
To approve the transfer:
1. Click Transfer previleges.
2. Enter Transfer in the confirmation field.
3. Click Confirm.
After confirmation, primary administrator rights are assigned to the new user.
If the transfer is declined
If the primary administrator declines the request, contact them to understand why. Explain the reason for the transfer and send a new request if needed.
If there is only one administrator
- On paid plans (except Basic), the primary administrator must first assign another administrator. That user can then request the transfer. Assign admin permissions

- On the Basic plan, the administrator must manually grant admin rights to another employee. After the transfer, the original administrator becomes a regular user. The new administrator can then remove them and take over the role.
In brief
- The primary administrator is the account owner who created the Bitrix24 account.
- They have full admin rights and are the only user who can approve ownership transfer or confirm their own removal.
- To transfer ownership, send a request to the current primary administrator.
- The administrator can approve or decline the request. If declined, follow up and resend if needed.

titre: Reassign tasks from a dismissed employee
sections: Reassign tasks from a dismissed employee

In Bitrix24, you can reassign tasks from a dismissed employee to another user. For example, if a manager leaves in the middle of a project, you can transfer the tasks to a colleague to keep work moving and avoid losing important assignments.
1. Open the dismissed employee's profile and go to the Tasks tab.
2. Check the filters in the search bar to make sure the right tasks appear. For example, use the In progress filter to show only active tasks.

3. Select the tasks where you want to change the assignee. To reassign all tasks from the dismissed employee, select the For all checkbox. This action applies to all tasks in the current filter, including tasks on other pages.
4. Click Select action .
5. Choose Change assignee . If you need to reassign tasks where the dismissed employee was the creator, choose Change creator .
6. Click the empty field and select an employee from the list, or start typing the name > Apply > Run .
After Bitrix24 processes the request, the new employee appears in the Assignee column.
In brief
- In Bitrix24, you can reassign tasks from a dismissed employee to another user.
- Only a Bitrix24 administrator can reassign tasks from dismissed employees.
- Open the profile and select Tasks .
- You can also change the creator.

titre: Transfer a dismissed user's email address
sections: Transfer a dismissed user's email address
In Bitrix24, you can assign a former employee's email address to a new user. The steps depend on how the former employee used the email address:
- If the email was only a contact address, an administrator can update it in the former employee's profile.
- If the email was used to sign in to Bitrix24, the account owner must update it in their Bitrix24 Network profile.
In this article:
- Check how an email address is used
- Update a contact email address
- Update an email address used for sign-in
Check how an email address is used
To see how an employee uses an email address, open their profile and click Security in the top-right corner. Only Bitrix24 administrators can access this section.
For example, you want to assign transfer@example.com to a new employee.
If the Security section shows a different email address, transfer@example.com is only a contact email address.
If the Security section shows transfer@example.com , the employee uses this address to sign in to Bitrix24.
Update a contact email address
To remove an email address from a former employee's account:
1–2. Go to Employees > Dismissed employees . 3. Open the former employee's profile. 4. Change the contact email address — in our example, this is example@internet.com . 5. Save your changes.
You can now assign transfer@example.com to a new user. For example, invite the new employee to Bitrix24 with this email address.
Update an email address used for sign-in
If the employee has already been dismissed. The former employee must update their email address in their Bitrix24 Network profile.

1. Open the Bitrix24 Network profile . 2. Click Change next to the email address. 3. Enter a different email address that isn't already used in Bitrix24. In our example, this is example@internet.com . You'll receive a message at this address to confirm the email change. Change Bitrix24 login or password 4. Save your changes.
After that, an administrator can update the email address in the former employee's profile and assign the old address to a new user.
If the employee hasn't been dismissed. The employee can update their email address in their personal profile.

1. Click your profile photo in the top-right corner. 2. Select Change account . 3. Click Change next to the email address. 4. Enter a new email address that isn't already used in Bitrix24. In our example, this is example@internet.com . You'll receive a message at this address to confirm the email change. Change Bitrix24 login or password 5. Save your changes.
In brief
- You can assign a former employee's email address to a new Bitrix24 user.
- The steps depend on whether the email was used as a contact address or to sign in to Bitrix24.
- To check how an email address is used, open the employee's profile and click Security . Only administrators can do this.
- If the email is only a contact address, an administrator can update it in the former employee's profile.
- If the email is used to sign in, the account owner must update it in their Bitrix24 Network profile.

titre: Extranet users in Bitrix24
sections: Extranet users in Bitrix24

Extranet users, also called external users, are authorized users with limited access to your Bitrix24 account. You can invite suppliers, distributors, contractors, and other partners to the Extranet to keep communication in one place.

External users can discuss work, share files, and collaborate with employees in extranet workgroups and projects. They cannot access your private company data. Extranet users also count toward the user limit in your Bitrix24 plan.
Inviting users to Extranet from a workgroup or project
To add a new external user to an extranet workgroup:
1. Open the About workgroup menu and select Members .
2. Click Invite .
3. Click Add employee and select Invite employee or external user .
You can identify extranet users by these signs:
- Their first and last names appear in yellow.
- A globe icon appears next to their name in tasks and comments.
- Their profile includes the Extranet label.
External users can complete their profiles in the same way as regular intranet users. Profile page
Extranet users are visible only to Bitrix24 administrators and employees in the same workgroup.
Tools available to extranet users
Here are the sections available to external users.
Feed
Extranet users can view the workgroup feed and messages addressed to them. They can also create posts, tasks, and polls. However, they cannot access appreciations or calendar events in the Feed.
Files (My Drive)

Extranet users can access personal files and folders, including shared files on the workgroup drive. They can manage access permissions for their files and folders and share them with other employees. They can also create public links to share files with people outside Bitrix24.
Workgroups
External users can see the list of workgroups and projects they belong to. You can limit access to specific tools and sections by editing workgroup settings.
Tasks

In this section, extranet users can see the tasks they are working on. They can create and assign tasks to employees in their contact list. When you create tasks in an extranet workgroup, only workgroup members can participate in them.
And for the rest, extranet users are allowed to work with tasks in the same way as regular intranet users. Working with tasks
External users cannot see observers in a task if they are not in the same external workgroup.
Contacts
External users can see people who belong to the same external workgroup.
Conversations
External users can send posts and messages to people in their contact list or to the entire extranet workgroup.
External workgroup
In this example, the workgroup is called Designers . Since the external user belongs to this workgroup, it appears in the left menu.
Chat and calls
To access this section, external users can open any chat from the right-side panel. They can chat and start calls with members of the same external workgroup.
Bitrix24 Network profile

This section is fully available to external users. Bitrix24 Network profile Mobile app External users have the same content and permissions as in the web version. Bitrix24 Messenger app The app includes the same features as the web version. Turning an extranet user into a company employee To move an extranet user to the intranet: Open the user profile. Click Extranet . Select Hire as an employee from the actions menu.
Mobile app
External users have the same content and permissions as in the web version.
Bitrix24 Messenger app
The app includes the same features as the web version.
Turning an extranet user into a company employee
To move an extranet user to the intranet:
1. Open the user profile.
2. Click Extranet .
3. Select Hire as an employee from the actions menu.

titre: Synchronize users' contacts with iOS Contacts app
sections: Synchronize users' contacts with iOS Contacts app
Use CardDAV to sync contacts on iOS devices. This protocol lets you access and share contact data stored on a server.
First, set up a CardDAV account on your device and connect it to your Bitrix24 account. Your contacts will sync automatically with the iOS Contacts app.
In Bitrix24, go to Employees > Settings (⚙️) > Synchronize with CardDAV .
Follow these steps to set up CardDAV on your device.
1. Open Settings on your iPhone.
2. Go to Contacts > Accounts > Add Account .
3. Tap Other , then select Add CardDAV Account .
4. Enter your Bitrix24 account address, login, and password. If you use two-step verification, enter the password from your profile: Application passwords > Contacts .
5. Tap Next to finish setup.
1. Open the Bitrix24 mobile app and go to More .
2. Tap Settings > Synchronize .
3. Select Synchronize contacts and allow the configuration profile to download.
4. On your device, go to Settings > Profile Downloaded > Install .
Edit or turn off the account
1. Open Settings .
2. Go to Contacts > Accounts .
3. Select your Bitrix24 account.
4. Make changes or turn off the account toggle.
Remove the account
1. Open Settings .
2. Go to General > VPN & Device Management .
3. Select your Bitrix24 configuration profile.
4. Tap Remove Profile .

titre: Synchronize contacts with Microsoft Outlook
sections: Synchronize contacts with Microsoft Outlook
Sync contacts between Bitrix24 and Outlook to have up-to-date data in both systems.
To configure synchronization:
1. Go to the Employees section.
2. Select the Employees tab.
3. Click Settings (⚙️) on the right.
4. Select Synchronize with Microsoft Outlook in the menu.

Click Advanced to customize the folder in the Outlook pop-up window. You can change the folder name and determine whether the contacts list will be available on all devices with the current account or not.
When settings are complete, click OK , then click Yes .
Synchronization is complete. Now contacts from Bitrix24 are available in Outlook.

titre: Synchronize Bitrix24 user details with Android device
sections: Synchronize Bitrix24 user details with Android device
Synchronize your company contacts with Android phones. You can sync contacts manually or enable automatic synchronization.
Enable synchronization
1. Open your phone settings.
2. Go to Accounts .
3. Tap Add account .
Section names may vary depending on your phone model.
Select Bitrix24 from the list and enter your login details. Then tap Save .
After you add the account, you can sync your Calendar and Contacts . Open the account settings and enable the options you need.
Set up automatic synchronization
To enable automatic synchronization, choose how often your phone should sync data. Your contacts will update automatically in the background.
Disable synchronization
To stop synchronization, remove the connected account from your phone.

titre: Select сontacts in Bitrix24 for synchronization with your phone
sections: Select сontacts in Bitrix24 for synchronization with your phone

You can sync colleague and client contacts from Bitrix24 to your phone's address book. After that, they appear in the Contacts section on your device, so you do not need to open Bitrix24 to find them. This is helpful if you often call clients or coworkers from your phone.
1. Click your photo to open the employee widget. 2. Click Security . 3. Open the Syncronize section. 4. Choose which contacts you want to sync.
Sync by default is the contact group that syncs automatically if your device does not specify which contacts it needs during transfer. This can happen on some Mac devices.
You can choose one of these options: System Users, Extranet Users, CRM Contacts, CRM Companies. You can also turn on specific groups individually below.

System Users . Sync employee contacts from your company structure. Select the checkbox and choose one or more departments. Contacts from employees in the selected subdepartments will also appear on the device. To select multiple departments, hold Ctrl on Windows or Command on Mac.
Extranet Users . Guests and external users invited to Extranet groups. Select the checkbox next to Enable to sync their contacts.

CRM Contacts . Sync contacts from CRM. Select the checkbox to enable sync. Then set the maximum number of contacts to transfer to the device. In the Filter field, choose: Mine — only contacts assigned to you, or All — all CRM contacts.

CRM Companies . Sync company contacts from CRM. Select the checkbox to enable sync. Then set the maximum number of contacts to transfer to the device. In the Filter field, choose: Mine — only contacts from companies assigned to you, or All — contacts from all CRM companies.
When you finish configuring all settings, click Save.
After you save your changes, the contacts appear in your device's address book automatically. To update the contact list later, return to this page and select or clear the checkboxes.

titre: FAQ: Employees
sections: FAQ: Employees
The Employees section helps you track working hours, manage schedules, and review reports. Below are answers to common questions.
- Why is the "Start workday" button missing?
- What is the difference between reports in the Work reports and Working time sections?
- Why can't an employee end their workday?
- How to grant permissions for adding absences to the schedule for all employees?
- Why are there multiple entries for one day in working time or a "Expired" status displayed?
Why is the "Clock in" button missing?
Issue The Clock in button does not appear in the employee widget.
Possible reasons
- Working time tracking is not enabled for the employee.
- The employee does not have permission to use the Working time tracking feature.
Solution Make sure working time tracking is enabled and permissions are set correctly.
Enable working time tracking
1. Go to Employees > Time and reports > Worktime . 2. Click the clock icon next to the employee’s name. 3. Choose one of the following:
- Inherit department settings — use existing department settings.
- Enabled — turn on tracking for this employee only.
4. Save your changes.
Check permissions
1. Go to Employees . 2. Open Time and reports > Access permissions . 3. Click Add access permission . 4. Select a user or department. 5. Assign a role:
- Employee — can manage their own workday and reports.
- Department supervisor — can manage their own data and their team’s data.
6. Save your changes.
What is the difference between Worktime reports and Work reports?
Bitrix24 provides two types of reports:
Worktime report
- Available in the employee widget under Work report .
- Employees list tasks completed during the day.
- The Daily plan tab shows scheduled tasks and meetings.
- Reports are tied to a specific date.
Work reports section
- Located in Employees > Time and reports > Work reports .
- Covers a selected period (day, week, or month).
- Automatically compiles data from daily reports.
- Managers can review and leave feedback.
Why can’t an employee end their workday?
Issue An employee cannot end their workday and sees an error.
Common causes
- Overlapping shifts in the schedule.
- The schedule does not match the actual start time.
- The employee is assigned to multiple schedules.
Solution
1. Go to Employees > Time and reports > Work schedules . 2. Check:
- No overlapping shifts.
- Schedule matches actual working hours.
- The employee is not assigned to conflicting schedules.
3. If needed, add the employee to Exceptions in other schedules.
To add an employee to exceptions:
1. Select the schedule the employee is assigned to, for example, Fixed Schedule . 2. Click Exceptions > Select . 3. Add the necessary employees to the list and save the changes. Work schedule types
How can employees add absences to the schedule?
In Bitrix24 Cloud, only administrators can add absences directly. Employees can use these options:
Calendar
- Create a calendar event.
- In Availability , select Absent (Add to absence schedule) .
Workflows
1. Go to Feed > More > Workflows . 2. Start a workflow (for example, Leave Approval ). 3. After approval, the absence appears in the schedule.
In the Bitrix24 On-Premise version, absences can be added to the schedule by administrators and users included in the HR Department group.
Why are there multiple entries or an “Expired” status in work time?
Issue You see multiple entries for one day or an Expired status.
Common causes
- The schedule changed after the workday started.
- The employee is assigned to multiple schedules or overlapping shifts.
- The actual start time does not match the schedule.
What happens
- The system closes the original entry and marks it as Expired .
- A new entry starts based on the updated schedule.
Solution
Adjust work time
1. Go to Employees > Time and reports > Worktime . 2. Open the Expired entry and click Edit . 3. Update the time or date. 4. Add a comment and save.
Check schedule settings
1. Go to Employees > Time and reports > Work schedules . 2. Select the schedule. 3. Update settings if needed. 4. Save changes.

titre: Time and reports
sections: Time and reports
Time is a key resource. Use it effectively to keep your team productive. Bitrix24 includes a dedicated set of tools to track and manage working time.
In this article:
- Worktime
- Work reports
- Work schedules
- Meetings and briefings
- Absence chart
Worktime

Use Worktime to track the start and end of the workday, breaks, and absences. You can also plan daily tasks, track how long they take to complete and generate reports on employee working hours at any time.
Worktime Worktime tracking in Bitrix24
Work reports
Set up reminders for work reports and choose how often employees submit them: daily, weekly, or monthly.

Employees add details about completed tasks. The system automatically includes related events in the report. Supervisors review reports, leave comments, and assign grades. This helps managers evaluate performance and make adjustments when needed.
Work reports Complete and confirm a work report
Work schedules
Use work schedules to manage employee working hours. This helps you spot delays or missed hours.
You can also create custom schedules for different departments based on their needs.
Work schedules Work schedule types
Meetings and briefings
Plan meetings in advance. Add agenda items, assign responsible employees, and create tasks. This helps you stay organized, avoid missed topics, and track progress after the meeting.
Create a new meeting Hold a meeting
Absence chart
The absence chart shows all types of absences, including business trips, sick leave, maternity leave, and vacation. Use it to plan workloads and distribute tasks across your team.
Absence chart Add absence to the chart

titre: Worktime tracking in Bitrix24
sections: In brief
Web version . Click your profile photo, then click Clock in . At the end of the day, click Clock out . Use the widget options to change the clock-in or clock-out times.
Mobile app . Go to Menu and tap Clock in in the Working day widget. At the end of the workday, tap Clock out .
In detail
Worktime tracking helps you monitor how many hours an employee has worked, which is useful for calculating salaries.
You can clock in and out or take a break in the Workday widget.
Clock in .
1. Click your profile photo in the top right corner.
2. In the employee widget, click Clock in .
The clock-in and clock-out times are automatically included in the report. Worktime
Break . Pause time tracking (1) if you take a break and click Continue when you return.
Clock out . Click Clock out (2) at the end of the working day.
Click the pencil icon (3) to edit the clock-in or clock-out times if needed.
Go to Menu and tap Clock in in the Working day widget.
To pause time tracking, tap the Pause button. Tap Resume when you return from a break. At the end of the day, tap Clock out .
Supervisors can set up automatic end-of-day times in the schedule settings. Work time control and limits
Tap the widget and select Working day . In this menu, you can:
- Clock in and clock out
- Fill out a work report
- Change the working day
- Start using other time
- End using other time
No widget
Error : The employee does not see the Workday widget.
Solution :
1. Ensure the Worktime and reports option is enabled in Bitrix24 Settings. Bitrix24 Settings
2. Check if time tracking is enabled for the employee under Company > Time and Reports > Worktime . By default, all departments inherit the head department setting.

3. Verify the employee's role in access permissions. To display the widget, select the Department employee or supervisor role. Or add another one with the same settings. Access permissions to Work schedules and Worktime records
Error during the working day
Error : "You didn't clock out" message appears.
Solution :
1. Supervisors or administrators should check for overlapping shifts if the employee works on a shift schedule.
2. Ensure the work schedule settings match the employee's working hours. For example, an employee with a schedule from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. should not start the working day at 5:00 a.m.
3. Check which schedules apply to the employee. If there are multiple, add the employee to Exceptions to avoid conflicts. Work schedule types

titre: Worktime
sections: Worktime
Track employee working hours and daily reports in one place. Use this page to monitor performance and review activity across your team.
In this article:
- Track working hours
- Use filters
- Monitor employee's working day
- Configure daily reports
- Configure additional settings
Track working hours
Go to Employees > Time and reports > Worktime .
Access depends on your role:
- Administrators can view all employees’ workdays.
- Supervisors can view only their team’s workdays.
- Employees can view only their own workdays.
If an employee has two entries for the same day, they were added to a new work schedule. In this case, they will see the You didn't close the previous day error.
Work schedules Work schedules access permissions
Use filters
Use filters to view a specific reporting period or selected dates.
Supervisors and administrators can:
- View and edit time records for all employees.
- Customize filter fields to find data faster.
Worktime tracking in Bitrix24
Unapproved days are not included in work hour statistics.
Monitor employee's working day
Select an employee and click a day in the calendar.
You will see:
- Total work time
- Breaks
- Daily reports
If an employee forgot to start or end the workday, a supervisor can update the time manually.
Configure daily reports
1. Click the clock icon next to the employee.
2. Choose a setting in the Daily report field.
3. Save your changes.
Available options:
- Required – the report form appears at the end of the workday and must be completed.
- Not required – the form appears, but completion is optional.
- Don't show report show – the form does not appear.
Additional settings
Click the gear icon to open Worktime settings.
Available options:
- Statistics – adds a summary table with employee work data.
- Clock-ins and clock-outs – shows start and end times in the calendar.
- Time zone – sets the time zone for displayed data.
- Work schedules – lets administrators view, edit, and create schedules.
Work schedule types
- Export to Microsoft Excel – exports worktime data for the selected period.
In brief
- Track working hours and daily reports in Employees > Time and reports > Worktime .
- Administrators and supervisors can view and edit employee records.
- Use filters to focus on specific dates or employees.
- Click a calendar day to see detailed work activity.
- Set up daily reports using the clock icon.
- Adjust settings to control how worktime data is displayed and exported.

titre: Worktime and reports option
sections: Worktime and reports option
Bitrix24 administrators can disable time management for the entire company, specific departments, or individual employees.
Disable time management for the entire company
1. Open the account settings.
2. Go to Tools .
3. Expand the Company section.
4. Disable the Worktime and reports option.
5. Click Save .
Disable time management for specific employees or departments
1. Go to Employees > Time and reports > Worktime .
2. Click the clock icon next to an employee or department.
3. Enable or disable the Working time management option.
Some employees may also see the Inherit department settings option. When this option is enabled, the employee uses the same time management settings as their department.

titre: Daily plan
sections: Daily plan
Plan your workday in Bitrix24. Schedule meetings, create tasks, build to-do lists, and stay on top of current work.
Add tasks for the day:
1. Click your profile photo.
2. Select Daily plan and report .
3. In the Today's tasks tab, click Select from list .
You can also create a new task. Enter a task name in the field and click Plus (+) .
The task appears in the list. Click the task name to open it, view details, and make changes.
Create a task
You can also plan an event:
1. Enter an event title and click Plus (+) .
2. Select Out of office to add the event to your calendar and the Absence Chart .
Add event to calendar
Add completed tasks to your work report so you do not miss anything. Bitrix24 automatically collects all daily reports into a weekly report.
Work reports
In brief
- Add tasks from the work time panel or create new ones. Tasks appear in a list where you can view and edit them.
- Start the time tracker. The flag icon shows how many tasks are still incomplete.
- Add events by entering a title and clicking Plus (+) . Mark events as Out of office to add them to your calendar and the Absence Chart.
- Fill in the work report to track completed tasks. Daily reports are included in the weekly report automatically.

titre: Work reports
sections: Work reports

Supervisors should clearly understand how employees are performing and if they're meeting their goals. Meanwhile, employees need to know how their work is evaluated and if they're completing tasks correctly.
Work reports are a useful tool for this. They allow supervisors to review performance and make changes if needed, while providing employees with helpful feedback.
Configure work reports
1. Go to the Employees section.
2. Expand Time and reports .
3. Select Work reports .
4. Click the Settings button in the top right corner.
5. Click the gear (⚙️) next to an employee or department name.
6. Select the report period: day, week, or month. You can also select a specific day of the week and time for the report form to appear.
7. Save your settings.

If you need to adjust the reporting period for a specific employee, you can do so even if you've set a standard for the entire department. For example, if a new employee needs to submit daily reports while others do so weekly, click the gear (⚙️) next to their name and set Day as the reporting period. This will apply individual settings for that employee.
At the specified time, Bitrix24 will remind employees to complete their work reports. Supervisors will then review, comment, and score them. Complete and confirm a work report
You can only submit a work report once per period. Existing reports cannot be modified or resubmitted for the same period.
Manage work reports

Use filters at the top of the section to quickly find the reports you need. You can filter by reporting period, department, or employee. Check the Statistics box to see Rate of reports with scores and Rate of positive scores for each user.
Reports are color-coded based on the supervisor's evaluation:
- Green : The report is rated positively.
- Red : The report is rated negatively.
- Orange : The report is confirmed without a score.
- Gray : The report is not confirmed.
In brief
- Work reports in Bitrix24 help supervisors track employee performance and goal achievement while providing employees with valuable feedback.
- Administrators and certain roles can configure report settings and manage reports using filters. Regular employees can only see their reports and statistics.
- If you need to adjust the reporting period for a specific employee, you can do so even if you've set a standard for the entire department.
- Reports are color-coded based on evaluations, helping everyone quickly assess performance.

titre: Complete and confirm a work report
sections: Complete and confirm a work report
The Work Reports tool helps you manage employee performance, track tasks, and review progress.
Work reports
Fill out a report
At the end of a day, week, or month, the report form opens automatically.
The report includes these fields:
- Report - include everything that was done during the specified reporting period.
- Plan - make plans for the next reporting period.
- Files - attach files to the report.
- Tasks - include tasks that you have done.
- Events - are added automatically to your work report if you have confirmed participation.
When you submit the report, your supervisor gets a notification. You will also get a notification after they review it.
If you did not send the report
If you skip a report, you will see a notification on the Work reports page.
Confirm a work report
After employees submit reports, the supervisor reviews them, adds comments, and evaluates the results.
The employee receives a Feed notification when the report is confirmed.

titre: Work schedules
sections: Work schedules
Add work schedules to manage and track employees' working hours. With this feature, you can set clock-in and clock-out times, weekly workdays, and break durations.
For example, imagine you own a restaurant. You can use work schedules to align staff shifts with customer flow, assigning more employees on busy Fridays and fewer on slower Mondays.
This approach helps balance workloads, improve customer service during peak hours, and reduce costs by cutting back on staff during quiet periods.
Configure work schedules
1. Go to the Employees section.
2. Open the Time and reports tab.
3. Select Work schedules .
4. Click Add schedule in the top right corner.
5. Choose the type of work schedule: fixed, flexible, or shifts. Work schedule types
6. Adjust the working hours, reporting period, and other settings. Working time control
7. Save your changes.
Once saved, the new schedule will appear in the list on this page.
Examples of work schedules
Depending on your company's workflow, you can set up different types of work schedules. For example, a furniture manufacturer might use the following:
- Fixed schedule : Production employees work set hours, such as 8 AM to 5 PM every day. This benefits both employees and the company with consistent working hours and a known workshop schedule.
- Shift schedule : The support team operates 24/7, so employees work day and night shifts. This ensures customers always have someone available to answer questions or resolve issues.

- Flexible schedule : The creative department focuses on developing new furniture ideas. A flexible schedule gives employees freedom in how they organize their work, which supports creativity and innovation.
In brief
- Create fixed, flexible, or shift-based schedules in Bitrix24.
- Set working hours, workdays, and breaks to fit your company’s needs.
- Balance workloads across teams, improve customer service during peak times, and reduce costs during slower periods.

titre: Work schedule types
sections: Work schedule types
Employees in different departments often follow different work schedules. Set up schedules to track and manage employee work time more effectively.
Go to the Employees section > Time and reports tab > Work schedules .
Bitrix24 supports three schedule types:
- Fixed
- Flexible
- Shifts
Fixed schedule
Use a fixed schedule to strictly control working hours and track violations. This option works well if pay depends on actual hours worked.
To set it up:
1. Select Fixed as the schedule type.
2. Enter a schedule name or keep the default.
3. Choose a reporting period: week, two weeks, month, or quarter.
4. Select employees or departments. To exclude specific employees, add them to exceptions .
5. Set working days, hours, and break duration. The total time is calculated automatically.
6. Define weekends and holidays. Use the gear icon to select a country or add custom days off.
7. Configure additional work time rules if needed.
Working time control and restrictions
Flexible schedule
A flexible schedule lets employees clock in and out at any time. A workday can exceed 24 hours.
To set it up:
1. Select Flexible as the schedule type.
2. Enter a schedule name or keep the default.
3. Choose a reporting period.
4. Select employees. Add exceptions if needed.
5. Choose which devices employees can use to clock in and out in the Allow clock-in and clock-out section.
Shifts schedule
Use a shifts schedule to assign employees to rotating shifts. Each shift defines when the workday starts and ends.
To set it up:
1. Select Shifts as the schedule type.
2. Enter a schedule name or keep the default.
3. Choose a reporting period.
4. Select employees or departments. Add exceptions if needed.
5. Set the Maximum early shift start (offset) .
6. In Work hours , click Add shift and define working hours and breaks.
7. Save the schedule and assign shifts.
Shift colors
Green marks upcoming shifts.
Red means the employee missed the shift.
Yellow means the employee clocked in before the shift started. A supervisor must approve the change. Otherwise, this time is not counted.
In brief:
- Create work schedules to manage employee time.
- Go to the Employees section > Time and reports tab > Work schedules .
- Choose from fixed, flexible, or shift-based schedules depending on your needs.

titre: Working time control
sections: Working time control
Tracking employee work hours is essential for many companies. With Bitrix24, you can easily create work schedules for your team and manage their working hours using simple, built-in tools.
Check if work schedules are available on your plan. Bitrix24 plans and pricing
To create a work schedule:
1. Go to the Employees section.
2. Click Time and reports .
3. Select Work schedules .
4. Click Add schedule .
5. Configure the settings.
Choose a schedule type, set a reporting period, and select the employees for this schedule. Work schedule types
Work hours . Select the working days, hours, and break duration.
Working time control . Select which events to control:
- Clock-in and clock-out
- Clock-in only
Track schedule violations . Select which types of schedule violations you want to track:
- Clock-in and clock-out: Set required times for clocking in and out. If an employee violates these times, notifications will be sent to the selected recipients.
- Working hours per day: If an employee works fewer hours than specified, the selected users will be notified.
- Maximum length of time to shift clock-in and clock-out times: Set how much employees can edit their clock-in and clock-out times. Edits beyond this limit will trigger a violation notification.
- Maximum underworked hours for reporting period: Define how many total hours an employee can underwork during the selected period. Exceeding this limit will trigger a violation notification.
Notifications about violations can also be sent to an employee’s supervisor. To use this option, make sure your company structure is configured. Company structure
A Shifts schedule includes additional options for tracking violations:
- Maximum length of time to shift clock-in and clock-out times: Set how much employees can edit their clock-in and clock-out times. Edits beyond this limit will trigger a violation notification.
- Shift start: Specify how late an employee can start their shift.
- Missed a shift: A notification is sent if the employee doesn't start their shift at all.
Restrictions . Choose the devices employees can use to manage their work time:
- Web browser
- Mobile app
- Both options

Important: Adjust a work schedule before an employee clocks in. If you make changes during the workday, the Worktime section will show two entries: one for the time worked before the change and another marked as Expired .
In that case, the employee will need to clock out and provide a reason. If the recorded time is incorrect, the administrator can edit it in the Worktime tab.
In brief
- Create work schedules and control employee working hours in Bitrix24.
- Track schedule violations and notify supervisors automatically.
- Choose which devices employees can use to record work time.
- Update schedules before employees clock in to ensure accurate records.

titre: Access permissions for Work schedules and Worktime records
sections: Access permissions for Work schedules and Worktime records
Set access permissions for work schedules and work time records. Choose which sections employees can view or edit.
Go to the Employees section > Time and reports tab > Access permissions .

By default, there are two user groups: administrators and regular users. Each group has preset permissions and standard roles. You can also create new roles and assign them to employees and departments.
Assign roles to users
Follow these steps:
1. Click Add access permission .
2. Select a user, department, or project/workgroup member.
3. Assign a role and click Save.
Add a new role
1. Click Add under the list of standard roles.
2. Enter a role name and set the required permissions.
The following access permissions are available:
- View all work schedules — view existing work schedules.
- Edit all work schedules — create and edit work schedules.
- View all shift schedules — view employee shift schedules.
- Edit all shift schedules — plan and edit employee shifts.
- View all worktime records — view all work time records.
- View my and subordinates' records — view work time records for your department.
- Edit all worktime records — edit any work time record.
- Edit my and subordinates' records — edit work time records for your department.
If you enable User can edit settings, users with this role can manage access permission settings.

titre: Create a new meeting
sections: Create a new meeting
Bitrix24 includes a built-in tool for meetings and briefings. Use it to discuss work with your team, capture decisions, and track follow-up tasks.
How to create a meeting
Go to Employees > Time and reports > Meetings and briefings .
If you don’t see the Meetings and briefings tab
If your plan includes this feature but the tab is missing, the tool may be disabled in your account settings.
To enable it:
1. Open the account settings.
2. Go to the Tools tab.
3. Expand the Company section.
4. Enable Meetings and briefings .
5. Click Save .
To create a meeting, click New meeting .
Enter the meeting topic, date, time, and duration. Then add attendees and select an administrative assistant who will take notes during the meeting. You can also specify the meeting location.
Add a description and attach any necessary files. You can also link the meeting to a workgroup or project.
In the Agenda section, add the topics you want to discuss. You can import topics from another meeting or from a task. For each agenda item, you can:
- Assign a responsible person
- Create a task
- Set a deadline
If the meeting is linked to a project, all related tasks are automatically added to that project.
When everything is ready, click Create meeting .
All attendees will receive a notification with the meeting invitation.

titre: Hold a meeting
sections: Hold a meeting

Meetings and briefings in Bitrix24 help teams run department meetings, company-wide meetings, and quick briefings. You can use this tool to schedule meetings, reserve meeting rooms, track agenda items, and save meeting notes.
How to start a meeting
Go to Employees > Time and reports > Meetings and briefings .
The page displays all scheduled, active, and completed meetings.
Use the filters on the right to find a meeting. You can search by:
- Meeting name
- Owner
- Status
- Attendee
- Project
Before the meeting starts, open the action menu to:
- Copy the meeting
- Edit the meeting
- Delete the meeting
To open a meeting, click its name or select the corresponding action.
On the right side of the page, you can view meeting details, including:
- Attendees
- Date and time
- Status
- Linked project
When all attendees are ready, click Start meeting .
The meeting status changes to In progress .
During the meeting, you can:
- Add agenda items
- Edit or delete topics
- Add topics from other meetings or tasks
- Create tasks and assign them to team members
- Add notes in the Minutes section
Finish a meeting
To end the meeting, open the Agenda tab and click the red button.
Completed meetings appear in gray in the meeting list.
Note that only owners can edit or start meetings.

titre: Absence chart
sections: Absence chart

Absence management shows when employees are unavailable due to vacation, sick leave, business trips, or other reasons. Use this information to plan projects and balance workloads. For example, when an employee schedules vacation time, their manager can see it on the chart in advance and assign urgent tasks to other team members.
Go to Employees > Time and Reports > Absence management .

All employees can view the absence chart. In Bitrix24 Cloud, only administrators can add absences from the chart. In Bitrix24 On-Premise, administrators and members of the HR Department workgroup can add absences. Employees can add absences only through the calendar or a workflow. How to add an absence to the chart

Choose a chart view. Use the Day, Week , and Month options in the upper-right corner. The Month view does not show absences shorter than one day, such as a few hours of time off. Select Day to view these events.
View absence details. Hover over an event to view its name and dates without opening it. Click an event to open its details, edit it, or delete the record.
Filter absences by type. Click Absence types in the upper-left corner and select the types you want to see, such as annual vacation only. The chart hides all other absence types.
Choose a subdepartment. By default, the chart shows employees from all company departments. To view absences for a specific department, select it in the Subdepartment field.
In brief
- Absence management shows when employees are on vacation, sick leave, business trips, or away for other reasons.
- Open the chart in Employees > Time and Reports > Absence management .
- All employees can view the chart.
- In Bitrix24 Cloud, administrators can add absences from the chart. In Bitrix24 On-Premise, members of the HR Department workgroup can also add absences.
- You can view absences by day, week, or month. You can also filter them by type and subdepartment.

titre: Add absences to the chart
sections: Add absences to the chart
Keep track of employee absences with the Absence chart. Choose the most convenient way to record absences:
- Add absences manually to the chart
- Add absences through the Calendar section
- Add absences using the Leave Approval workflow
Add absences manually to the chart
Only Bitrix24 administrators can add an entry directly to the chart.
To add a new absence entry:
1. Go to the Employees section.
2. Expand the Time and reports tab.
3. Select Absence chart .
4. Click the Add Entry button in the top right corner.
Next, fill out the new entry form:
1. Pick the absent person from the list of employees.
2. Select the type of absence from the drop-down list.
3. Enter details in the Reason for absence and Time of absence fields.
4. Click Add .
If you need to schedule more than one absence in a day, click Set time to specify the exact timing.
That’s it! You can now add more absences or close the form.
Once added, the event will appear in the Absence chart. Click it to view more details or access options to edit or delete it.
Add absences through the Calendar section
Any employee can register an absence using a special option in the calendar event. Follow these steps:
1. Go to Calendar .
2. Click Create to add an event.
3. Open the More section in the new event form.
4. Under Availability , select Away (add to absence chart) .
Create a calendar event
These absences appear in gray in the Absence chart because they come from personal calendars.
Add absences using the Leave Approval workflow
You can also add an absence using the standard Leave Approval workflow:
1. Go to Feed .
2. Click More in the new message form.
3. Select Workflow .
4. Find the Leave Approval workflow and click Start .
5. Click Next to proceed.
6. Specify the dates and absence type, then click Start again.
After approval, the absence appears in the chart automatically.
In brief
- The Absence chart helps you keep track of employee absences.
- Add absences in three ways: manually to the chart, through the Calendar section, or using the Leave Approval workflow.
- Once added, absences appear in the chart, where you can view, edit, or delete them.

titre: New workflow builder in Bitrix24
sections: New workflow builder in Bitrix24

The Bitrix24 workflow builder has been fully redesigned. The interface and logic are updated. You now get a single workspace where you can view the entire workflow at once. You can manage long and complex workflows without switching between tabs.

A single workflow can include actions from different Bitrix24 tools. For example, it can create a task, update a deal stage, and send a customer notification. This helps you build end-to-end workflows across multiple departments.
Below is an overview of the new builder and how to use it.
Updated interface
The new workflow builder is more visual and easier to use. You can build the entire workflow in one window and access all actions directly on the screen.
To open the builder:
1. Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflow templates .
2. Click Add to create a new workflow or open an existing one.
3. The visual editor opens.
The editor has three main areas:

Workspace .This is where you build the workflow. It contains action blocks called nodes. Each node performs a specific task, such as sending a notification, creating a task, or updating a status. You define the sequence and connections between nodes to build the workflow logic.
You can zoom in or out to view the entire workflow. This is useful for large or complex processes.
Action menu . The left panel shows available nodes. These are grouped by tools and use cases, for example:
- Sales and CRM: deals, leads, contacts.
- Customer communication: calls, emails, messages.
- Internal communication: chats, workgroups, notifications.
- AI scripts: automation using AI for analysis and responses.
Use the search bar to quickly find a node. Click the Magnifying glass icon and enter the action name.
To get more space, click Menu (≡).
Control panel . The top panel includes tools for managing the workflow template. You can:
- Rename the workflow for easier identification in the list
- Ensure changes are saved
- Apply all new settings and changes to the template
The builder saves changes automatically, but to run the updated script, you need to publish the template. Autosave and publishing
Canvas management. The bottom-right corner contains tools for working with large, branching processes. Here you can:
- Turn on template autoformatting
- Add comments to nodes, dependencies between them, or specific canvas areas
- Move around the canvas with the Hand tool
- View the entire template on the minimap and quickly navigate to any area
- Adjust the zoom level with the Minus (–) and Plus (+) buttons or enter a specific percentage
Nodes in workflows
Nodes are the building blocks of a workflow. Each node performs a specific action, such as sending a notification, updating a status, or creating a CRM record.
Working with actions has become easier:
Multiple actions in one block. You can add several actions to a single node. For example, create a task and set its status to In progress.
Parallel branches . You can run multiple actions at the same time. For example, send a contract for approval and legal review simultaneously.
Triggers . Trigger nodes track events and start actions automatically. For example, when a deal field changes, the workflow can send a notification or create a task.
AI nodes . AI nodes can analyze data and perform actions automatically. For example, if a message says “I want to take a vacation,” the system can start a vacation workflow.
Working with nodes
To build a workflow, select and configure nodes.
Select a node . Drag a node from the action menu to the workspace. To edit it, double-click the node or click Three dots (...) > Open.
Configure a node . Each node has settings that define how it works. You can set:
- Action: what the node does
- Condition: when the action runs
- Exit points: what happens next based on the result

This allows you to set different node logic for various situations within a single process. For example, in a task-related node, you can configure the "Create a task for the accountant to prepare documents" action. It will only be performed under certain conditions. If the "Purchase type" field in the purchase request is filled or the request is at the required stage. Then, two exit points are configured:
- If the condition is met and the task is created, the workflow moves to the branch for purchase processing.
- If the condition is not met, the workflow moves to the branch for data verification.
This way, one node responds to different events and performs the necessary steps in each script.
Autosave and publishing
The builder saves all changes automatically. You can leave the page and return later—your draft remains unchanged. Only you can see the draft until you publish it.
To apply changes, publish the workflow. New runs will use the updated version, while active workflows continue with the previous settings.
In brief
- The workflow builder is now a single workspace with a full workflow view.
- Nodes are more flexible. You can add multiple actions and create parallel branches.
- Trigger nodes automate actions based on events.
- AI nodes can analyze data and run actions automatically.
- Changes are saved automatically. Publish the workflow to apply updates.
- Only Bitrix24 administrators can use the new editor.

titre: Nodes in the new AI workflow builder
sections: Nodes in the new AI workflow builder

A node is a block on an AI workflow diagram. Each node handles one step: it tracks an event, performs an action in Bitrix24, or checks a condition. Nodes connect to each other through links, forming the logic of the entire workflow.

In the new builder, a node checks conditions, performs the needed action, and routes the workflow into different branches through exit points. For example, in the Deal node, you can set up different actions for large and regular deals and route the result into different branches.
In this article:
- How does an AI workflow work?
- Add a node to a diagram
- Open node settings
- Configure a node rule: actions, object, conditions, and outputs
- How data passes between nodes
How does an AI workflow work?
A workflow in the builder consists of nodes, flows, ports, and the links between them. You’ll need these concepts to read and configure any diagram.
An AI workflow template is a diagram that describes when a workflow starts, what actions it performs, and where it sends the result. You can run a workflow from the same template multiple times.
A node is a separate block on the canvas. A node tracks an event, performs an action in Bitrix24, or checks a condition.
A flow is a sequence of connected nodes that starts with a trigger. A single template can contain several flows.
A port is a connection point on a node. A node receives the flow and data through an input port, and sends the result onward through an output port.

A data channel is an input port of a universal node with its own set of settings. A simple action node has one input and one output, so channels aren’t singled out for it. A universal node has several inputs, and each one is a separate channel with its own settings. Channels are labeled with system names: G1, G2, and so on.
A link is a line between the ports of two nodes. It defines the direction of the workflow and how data passes along it.
A workgroup is a set of conditions and actions within a node rule. A node checks groups one by one and runs the actions of the first workgroup whose check passes.
Add a node to a diagram

1. Open Automation > Workflows> Workflow templates > Add . An empty canvas opens — the editor’s workspace. 2. On the left is the node library. Nodes are grouped by scenario: sales and CRM, client document workflows, internal communications, HR processes, task management, and others. 3. To find a node quickly, use the search bar. 4. Drag a node from the library onto the canvas — it appears on the diagram with input and output ports.
The builder has four node types:
- Trigger nodes track an event and start a flow. A trigger has no input port: it is the start of the flow. For example, the Deal created trigger.
- Simple action nodes perform one predefined action: send a notification, pause the workflow, and so on. They usually have one input and one output. For example, the Notify user node.

- Universal nodes represent Bitrix24 objects: a deal, lead, contact, company, task, SPA, and others. Inside this type of node, you choose an action on the object, set up several inputs, and route the result into different outputs. For example, the Deal node.
- Specialized nodes perform supporting operations: check a condition, repeat steps in a loop, store data, or process it through AI. For example, the Condition node.
A node’s color shows its subject area:
- Green — client communications, for example the Send email node
- Blue — product objects: deals, tasks, SPAs, for example the Deal node
- Yellow — employees and internal communications, for example the Notify user node
- Purple — AI scenarios
- Teal — storage
- Gray — technical elements: conditions, loops, iterators.
To see the exact action, check the node’s name and description in the right-hand panel.
Open node settings
Click a node on the canvas to open the right-hand panel with its settings. The panel has three sections: the General tab, the Settings tab, and the Data button.

Check the node’s overall setup on the General tab. Here you see the full picture of the node’s setup: the custom name and description, available and generated data, and a list of inputs with a short summary of the configured rules. This is a convenient way to check the whole node without opening each rule separately.

Enter a name in the Custom name field and describe what the node does in the Description field — this way you won’t get confused if the diagram has several similar blocks. For example, instead of two identical Deal labels, name them after their task: Move deal to approval and Assign supervisor as responsible .
Build the node rule on the Settings tab. This is where you build the node rule — what the node does with the data coming into the channel. We’ll cover how this works in the next section.

If a node has several channels, switch to the one you need in the dropdown list at the top of the tab. Each channel is configured separately, so a node can process data differently depending on which flow it came from. Before changing settings, check that the correct channel is open: edits to G1 won’t affect G2.

For example, two triggers connect to the Deal node: Deal created goes to channel G1, and Deal field changed goes to channel G2. In the G1 settings, you can check the fields of a new deal and immediately assign a responsible person, while in G2, you can respond only to a change in the amount and notify the supervisor. Both triggers lead to the same node, but each channel has its own conditions and actions, independent of each other.
Open the available data panel. The Data button opens a panel with the values available to the selected node. How data passes between nodes
Configure a node rule
A channel rule consists of four stages, and which ones you need depends on the node type:
- Base action — runs always, if the node has one
- Object — needed only if the node lacks data and must look up an item separately
- Condition groups — needed only if the workflow must branch depending on the data
- Output — needed to pass the result to the next node.
Base settings define what the node always does, regardless of condition workgroup. Simple action nodes already have their action set — for example, the Notify user node sends a notification.

In the Base settings card, fill in only the required fields, marked with an asterisk: for example, Notification sender and Notification recipient — you can populate both from data that came from the previous node instead of entering them manually.

For a universal node, first choose an action in the base settings: what to do with the object — for example, create an item, change fields, or change the stage. After you choose an action, its fields appear — fill in the required ones, or the node won’t save.

You can add base settings only once per channel — this action doesn’t depend on conditions; it runs every time the node receives data, before the condition groups are checked. If you need more complex logic — different actions depending on which data arrived — use the Action card inside condition groups instead of the base settings.

You need an object if the item isn’t in the incoming data. Click the Object button at the top of the tab if the node needs to look up an item on its own because it isn’t in the incoming data. For example, a trigger passes data about an employee but doesn’t pass the specific deal to work with.
Specify the CRM item type — deal, lead, company, SPA, and so on — and the condition the node will use to find it: field, operator, and value.

For example, to find deals where the stage equals Approval and the amount is greater than $1,000, specify two conditions and combine them with AND — only deals that match both conditions at once will trigger. If you combine the conditions with OR , any deal that matches at least one will trigger.
If the needed item already arrived at the node from a previous step, you don’t need to add an object — go straight to the conditions.

Condition groups route the workflow into branches. Click Condition to create a rule workgroup. A workgroup combines the condition that triggers it with the actions to run. To add a condition, click If inside the workgroup — a card appears where you specify the field, operator, and value to check.

For example, to make the workgroup trigger only for deals from ads, specify the field Source , the operator equals , and the value Ads . If you need more than one condition, combine them with AND — only items that match all conditions at once will trigger — or with OR — an item that matches at least one will trigger.
Give the workgroup a clear name, for example New clients — this way you can read the rule on the General tab without opening each workgroup separately.

Click Action inside a workgroup to add an operation that runs only if the workgroup’s conditions are met. For example, in the Deals from ads workgroup, add the Create task action — it creates a task for the manager to contact the client. A workgroup can contain several actions — the node runs them in the order you added them.

If a rule has several groups, the node checks them one by one, from top to bottom. As soon as a workgroup’s conditions are met, the node runs its actions and doesn’t check the remaining groups. So place groups with narrower conditions first, and put the group with the general condition at the very end.

If you need an action for cases when an item doesn’t match any workgroup, you don’t need to create a separate workgroup for it. Click the Action button on the tab’s top panel — an action card without a condition is added. It runs if none of the groups above matched.
If no such form exists and the item doesn’t match any of the groups, the node doesn’t perform the activities from the rule.

The exit passes the result forward. Add an Exit form at the end of the workgroup and connect it on the canvas to the input port of the next node. For universal nodes, exits are labeled E1, E2, and so on.

If you select an exit in the settings but don’t draw a connection on the canvas, the flow ends there — the next node won’t receive data. Before publishing, check that each exit you need is connected to the correct next node.
How does data move between nodes?

A node doesn’t need to enter the same data again at each step — it takes data from the previous nodes in the chain. For example, if the Deal created trigger received the client’s phone number and name, the next node doesn’t need to look up this data again — it pulls it from the data panel.

A node receives an object in two ways: through a connection from the previous step, where the ID and other data arrive automatically, or through an Object form, if the node looks up the item itself. If there’s no connection between nodes, data from the previous step won’t reach the next one — use the Object form or check the connections on the canvas.

Separately from these two methods, a node has access to the process’s global data — for example, constants set in the template. This data doesn’t depend on connections between specific nodes and is always visible in the data panel.
To see what data is available to a node, open the Data button in the right panel.

The panel supports two modes: Schema — a tree-like list of sources, nodes, and fields, and Table — a flat list of fields, convenient for quick searches. Next to each field, you’ll see the value type: string, number, date, user, file, and others.

To insert a value into a setting field, open the data panel, find the field you need, and drag it into a field that supports insertion — marked with a curly brace {} icon. Not all fields support insertion: a condition operator or an exit number is selected from a fixed list.
As the chain progresses, data accumulates — a node uses data from the previous step and from earlier related nodes.
Common mistakes when setting up a node

Mixing up channels. If a node has multiple inputs, check which channel is open on the Settings tab before changing any settings. Edits in G1 don’t cancel or duplicate the settings in G2 — you need to make changes separately for each one.
What to do: before each change, check the channel number in the dropdown list against what you see on the node’s input diagram.
Using an object instead of a condition — or vice versa. Object finds the item the node will work with. Condition decides whether to continue down a branch.

What to do: first figure out whether the node actually needs an item that isn’t already in the incoming data — if so, add an object. If the item already exists and you just need to select a branch, add a condition.
Exit not connected to a node. An exit that’s configured but not connected on the canvas ends the branch — the next node won’t receive the flow.
What to do: after configuring the exit in the right panel, go back to the canvas and check that a line runs from each required exit to the next node.

Groups placed in the wrong order. The builder checks groups from top to bottom and stops at the first one where the conditions are met. If a general condition comes before a specific one, the builder never reaches the specific one.
What to do: arrange groups from the narrowest conditions to the broadest — place the general option with no conditions, if you need one, last.
Forgetting to publish the template. Changes save to the draft automatically, but they don’t take effect until you click Publish .
What to do: after each round of edits, check the status in the top panel — if it shows Not published , click Publish before closing the editor.
In brief
- A node is a building block of an AI workflow: it tracks an event, performs an activity in Bitrix24, or checks a condition.
- A node’s rule consists of basic settings — what always runs — and groups with conditions, activities, and an exit, which trigger only under certain conditions.
- An object finds the item the node will work with, while a condition decides which branch to run next — these are different tools.
- Data passes between nodes through connections and accumulates as the chain progresses — you can insert it using the Data panel.
- Changes save to the draft automatically, but they take effect only after you publish the template.

titre: Set up a workflow with the universal Deal node
sections: Set up a workflow with the universal Deal node
The new AI workflow builder creates scenarios from ready-made nodes. Some nodes respond to events, while others check data or perform actions based on specified rules.

Let’s look at an example of how nodes work together. We’ll set up a workflow for new deals: for large deals, we’ll add the supervisor as an observer and send the client an SMS. For regular deals, we’ll schedule an activity for the employee and send the client an email.
This article covers a specific workflow. For general information:
- To learn what nodes are and how to configure them, see Nodes in the new AI workflow builder .
- To learn how the new workflow builder works, see New workflow builder in Bitrix24 .
In this article:
- Add a trigger and the universal node
- Set up a group for large deals
- Set up a group for regular deals
- Add client notifications
- Publish the template
Step 1. Add a trigger and the universal node

Every flow starts with a trigger that tracks an event and passes data through the workflow. In this case, the flow starts when a new deal is created in the CRM, so the first node in the template is a trigger for this event.
Add a trigger. Find the trigger in the node library and drag it onto the template canvas. The canvas is empty when you create a template.
1. Go to Automation .
2. Click Workflows .
3. Select Workflow templates .
4. Click Add to create a new template. An empty editor canvas opens.
5. In the node library on the left, find the Deal added trigger and drag it onto the canvas.
6. Click the node to open its settings.

7. On the General tab, enter a custom name, such as New deal from the Sales pipeline , and describe why you need this trigger. The exact name will be useful later. If you add a second trigger or another Deal node to the template, for example, to work with a different pipeline, labels will help you tell the blocks apart.
8. Go to the Rules tab for the same trigger.
9. In the Sales pipeline field, specify the pipeline the deals should come from, such as Sales .
10. Click Save .

Add the Deal node. The trigger only reports the event; it does not check or change deal data. To sort deals by amount and perform actions, use the universal Deal node. It receives data from the trigger and divides the process into two scenarios based on configured rules.
1. Find the universal Deal node in the library and place it to the right of the trigger.

2. Connect the trigger output to input G1 of the Deal node. Without this connection, the node will not receive data. Only a connection turns two separate blocks into a working flow. Through G1, the node receives all fields from the created deal, including the amount, responsible person, and source. You can use these fields in later conditions and actions.
3. Click the Deal node to open its settings.
4. On the General tab, enter a name, such as Process a new deal .
5. Click the pencil icon next to the G1 input rule to open its settings.
Step 2. Set up a group for large deals

Next, configure the node logic—the rule it uses to check each incoming deal. Start with the branch for large deals: first define the condition that identifies a large deal, then specify what the node should do when the condition is met.
Add a condition. The condition determines which deals belong to this rule group. The node compares a deal field value with the value you specify and decides whether to perform the following actions.
1. On the Rules tab, make sure input G1 is selected.
2. Click + If to create the first rule group.
3. In the If card, select the field the node will use to distinguish large deals from regular deals: Amount .
4. Set the operator to More or equal .
5. Enter the deal amount at which a deal is considered large. For example, enter 50000 . Set your own threshold based on your company’s average deal size.
6. Name the group High-value deal . This name appears in the brief rule list on the General tab, helping you identify each group without opening it.
Add actions. A condition determines whether a group runs, but it does not change data or perform operations on its own. Actions inside the group determine what happens to a large deal.

In this example, two actions run in sequence. First, the supervisor is notified about the large deal. Then, the employee receives an activity to contact the client. You can change these actions to fit your task.
1. Click + Action .
2. Click the Action field.
3. Select Change observers .
4. Enter a custom name for the action. For example, explain why the action runs. In the Apply action to observers field, leave add selected.

5. In the Observers field, enter a value using a constant with the User field type, or select an employee from the trigger data. This lets the appropriate person, such as the supervisor, view and monitor the deal even when another employee runs the process.
6. Click + Action again to add a second operation. It will run after the first one.
7. Click the Action field.
8. Select Plan activity so the employee does not miss the deal.
9. Enter the activity name and description, and set a deadline.
10. Next to the Responsible person field, click Three dots (...) .
11. In the list, select the Responsible person field from the deal data. The activity is then automatically assigned to the employee responsible for the new deal.
12. Set the activity color and complete the remaining fields, including event duration, client selection, colleague invitations, and more.
13. Configure reminders and automatic activity completion when the stage changes, according to your company’s activity rules.

You can use a general phrase in the activity description or another field, or tailor it to each deal. To do this, insert deal field values using the Data panel. For example, you can populate the activity description, SMS text, or email text this way.
1. Click Show data in the upper-right corner of the Rules panel. A tree of all fields available to the node opens.
2. Find the field you need, such as Created on , and click the copy icon next to it, or drag the value directly into the text.
3. Paste the copied code into the required text field.

Set up the output. The node performs the actions in the group, but the branch for large deals remains incomplete until you specify where to send the result next. The output determines the next step in the workflow, such as notifying the client or performing another action.
Output E1 is created automatically with the first condition group. Select it from the list.
1. Click + Output .
2. In the Value field, click the drop-down list.
3. Select output E1.
Step 3. Set up a group for regular deals

The branch for large deals is ready, but the node does not yet process the remaining deals. They need a separate group with its own condition, action, and output. Configure it the same way, using different values.
Add a condition. The second group should include all deals that do not meet the first condition—that is, deals with amounts below $50,000.
1. Click + If again to create a second group. It appears in the rule list below the first group.
2. Name the group Standard deal .
3. In the condition, specify:
1. The Amount field
2. The Less operator
3. The value 50000
Add an action. As with the first group, the action determines what happens to a deal that meets the condition.

In this example, regular deals have only one action: schedule an activity for the employee. The supervisor does not receive a notification. You can also add other actions. For example, notify a department chat or send an email to the responsible person. Choose the actions that best fit your workflow.
1. Click + Action .
2. Click the Action field and select Plan activity . Enter the activity name and description, and set a deadline.
3. Set the responsible person, activity color, and duration. Select the responsible person from the deal data instead of entering it manually.
4. Complete the remaining fields, including the link, location, reminders, and automatic completion.

Set up the output. As with the first group, you need an output to pass the result through the workflow. For regular deals, use a separate branch with its own value. No output is created automatically for the second and later groups, so create one manually.
1. Click + Output .
2. Click the Value field.
3. Select Add output .
4. Select E2 so regular deals follow a separate branch and do not overlap with large deals.
5. Click Save .
On the General tab, both groups appear in the brief list, making it easy to review the entire logic at once.
Step 4. Add client notifications
