The Deal node divides the process into two branches, but neither branch continues because outputs E1 and E2 are not connected. Add a separate node to each output to send a notification to the client.
In this example, the two branches use different channels: SMS for large deals and email for standard deals. This is only one possible setup.
Large deals usually require a faster response, and clients are more likely to see an SMS quickly. An email is sufficient for standard deals because clients can read it without urgency.
Set up SMS for the large deal. Connect this node to output E1 so the message is sent only through the large-deal branch.
1. Find the Send SMS node in the library and drag it onto the canvas.
2. Connect output E1 of the Deal node to this node’s input.
3. Click the node to open its settings.
4. On the General tab, rename it, for example, Customer notification (high-value deal) , and describe its purpose. This will help you distinguish it if you add another SMS node later.
5. Open the Rules tab.
6. Enter the message text.
7. Select the client’s phone number type, such as Work Phone .
8. Select the provider.
9. Leave the recipient type as Client so the message goes to the deal’s client rather than an employee.
10. In the Employee field, select the responsible person from the deal data.
11. Click Save .
Set up the email for regular deals. Connect this node to output E2 so the email is sent only along the regular deals branch.
1. Find the Send email node and drag it onto the canvas.
2. Connect it to output E2.
3. Click the node to open its settings.
4. Rename it, for example, Client notification (standard deal) , and describe its purpose.
5. Open the Rules tab.
6. Complete the From field: select the email address to use for sending notifications.
7. Enter the email subject and body.

8. To insert deal data into the email, click Show data , find the required field, and add it to the email body. Copy it using the copy icon or drag it directly into the text. The value is filled in automatically from the deal data.
9. Check the remaining settings: text type, client address type, placement, and so on.
10. Click Save .
Step 5. Publish the template
The configured workflow remains in draft and does not apply to actual deals until you publish the template.
Click Publish in the upper-right corner of the editor.
After publication, the workflow runs for new deals in the selected pipeline.
Final diagram: the trigger passes data to the Deal node, which checks the amount and splits the flow into two outputs. Each output leads to a separate client notification.
In brief
- The trigger starts the flow and passes data to the next node. Connect its output to input G1 of the Deal node.
- The workgroup condition checks a deal field, in this example, the amount, and determines which activities to run and where to route the result.
- The node checks condition groups in order, from top to bottom, and stops at the first match. Place specific conditions above general ones.
- Each workgroup ends with an output. Without it, the next node does not receive data even if the condition matches.
- Insert values from deal data using the Data panel instead of entering them manually, so the activity or email automatically adjusts to the specific deal.

titre: Workflow templates: Team management
sections: Workflow templates: Team management

Reports, sick leave, and work time tracking need regular attention. The Team management group handles these routine tasks for you. It starts scenarios at the right time and completes actions automatically.

The workgroup includes triggers and actions. Triggers watch for events and start a scenario when something happens. Actions run inside a scenario that has already started and complete specific tasks. A trigger always comes first. Actions follow it.
In this article:
- Sick leave added
- User clocked in
- Report sent to your supervisor
- Work report is due
- Get work report
- Update work report
- Report sent to your supervisor
- Open Channel first message response is overdue
- Save daily report
- Get daily report
- Save daily plan
Sick leave added
This trigger starts when someone adds a sick leave entry to the absence chart. It launches the needed actions automatically, so nothing depends on someone noticing the update manually.
Example: A sales manager goes on sick leave. As soon as the HR manager adds the entry to the chart, the scenario redistributes tasks and notifies the team:
- The supervisor gets a notification.
- The backup employee gets a task.
- Colleagues get a message about the client reassignment.
User clocked in
This trigger starts when an employee begins their workday. It starts daily processes automatically.

Example: A supervisor wants a summary of overdue team tasks every morning. When employees start their workday, Bitrix24 collects the data and sends the summary to a chat. The supervisor does not need to check tasks separately.
Report sent to your supervisor
This trigger starts a process when an employee sends a report to the supervisor for a specific period. It helps you track reports, so the supervisor can review them on time.
Example: A manager sends a weekly report to the supervisor. Bitrix24 records the submission date and creates a task for the supervisor to review the report before the end of the day.
Work report is due
This trigger reads the scheduled report time from the work report settings and starts the scenario. Bitrix24 then collects, processes, and adds the data to the report automatically.

Example: The work report settings specify Friday at 4:00 PM. At that time, the trigger starts the scenario. Data about tasks and meetings is collected, processed by AI, and added to the report automatically.
Get work report

This action gets an employee's report for a selected period and passes it to the next step in the scenario. This helps you collect employee data automatically instead of requesting each report manually.

Example: A supervisor needs monthly reports from all employees to review department efficiency. The action gets each employee's report for the selected period and sends it to the next analysis step. The supervisor then gets a summary without reading every report one by one.
Update work report
This action adds data from earlier steps in the scenario to an employee's report for the selected period.

Example: Earlier steps collected and processed data about an employee's tasks and meetings for the month, such as closed deals, overdue tasks, and notes for the supervisor. The Update work report action writes this data to the report.
Report sent to your supervisor
This action sends a notification about overdue tasks. It helps leaders spot issues quickly and respond right away.

Example: Each morning, the action checks employee tasks. If someone has overdue tasks, the supervisor gets a message that shows who missed tasks, how many there are, and how overdue they are. The supervisor can then update deadlines or check task status right away.
Open Channel first message response is overdue
This trigger starts if a manager takes too long to respond to a client's first chat message. It helps prevent lost clients caused by slow response times.

Example: A client writes in the chat, but the manager does not reply within the set time. The trigger detects this and starts the scenario. The supervisor gets a notification, and the chat is reassigned to another manager.
Save daily report

This action saves an employee's report for the day. You can choose the report type in the action settings: daily, weekly, or monthly. Place this action at the end of the scenario, after all data has been collected and the result is ready to save.
Example: At the end of the workday, the scenario collects data about an employee's tasks. The action saves it as a daily report, so the supervisor can see the results without additional requests.
Get daily report
This action gets and passes the text of an employee's daily report. This can be a report created with AI, generated automatically, or written by the employee.

Example: At the end of the workday, the scenario collects reports from all sales department managers. The action gets each employee's report and passes it to the next step. The supervisor gets a notification with the day's results without requesting reports manually.
Save daily plan
This action saves an employee's plan for the current day.
Example: Each morning, the scenario collects data about an employee's tasks and meetings. The action saves it as a daily plan, so the employee does not need to spend time creating one.
In brief
- The Team management group automates report tracking, task monitoring, and team notifications without manual effort.
- The workgroup includes ten nodes: four triggers and four actions.
- Triggers start scenarios based on events: sick leave added to the chart, workday started, report sent, and scheduled report time reached.
- Actions process data inside the scenario: they get employee reports, build user lists for AI reports, fill out reports, and send notifications to management.
- Nodes work together: a trigger starts the process, and actions run sequentially after it.

titre: Workflow templates: Customer documents
sections: Workflow templates: Customer documents

The Customer documents node group includes nodes that track document signing. For example, when the required party signs a document, the node automatically starts the next step. You do not need to check the signing status or continue the process manually.
In this article:
- Track signing by your side
- Track signing by the other party
- Track signing by all parties
Track signing by your side
The First party signature provided trigger starts the process after someone on your side signs the document.

For example, a client contract may go through several approval stages. When the director signs the contract on behalf of the company, Bitrix24 automatically notifies the lawyer. Responsibility for the next step then moves to the lawyer.
Track signing by the other party
The Second party signature provided trigger starts the process after the other party, such as a client or contractor, signs the document.

For example, a company may have a contract workflow in place. When the client signs the contract, Bitrix24 automatically moves the deal to the next stage and assigns the manager a task to issue an invoice. The process continues without manual action.
Track signing by all parties
The Document signed by all parties trigger starts the process after all participants sign the document.

For example, a manager, a lawyer, and a client may all need to sign a contract. After everyone signs, the supervisor automatically receives a notification. This means the contract is now in effect and the team can move to the next stage.
In brief
- The Customer documents node group node group includes triggers that automate document signing. The workflow responds to signing events automatically.
- The First party signature provided trigger starts the process when someone on the company side signs the document.
- The Second party signature provided trigger starts the process when the client or contractor signs the document.
- The Document signed by all parties trigger starts the process when all participants have signed.

titre: Workflow templates: Internal communications
sections: Workflow templates: Internal communications

The Internal communications node group includes actions and triggers that help you automate team communication. You can use these nodes to send messages to employees, create chats and projects, publish Feed posts, and work with Chat bots.
In this article:
- Select employee
- Create group chat
- Add members to group chat
- Send message to group chat
- Add chat bot to group chat
- Chat bot settings
- Send a chat bot message
- Chat bot received a message
- Send a direct message to employee
- Create new project
- Feed post
- User notification
Select employee
This node finds an employee based on the criteria you set and passes their data to the next steps in the workflow.

Example: A company uses an onboarding workflow for new hires. When a new employee is added to Bitrix24, this node finds the head of the employee's subdepartment and passes that data to the next step. Bitrix24 then adds the manager to the chat with the new employee and sends a welcome message.
Create group chat
This node creates a group chat and adds the selected employees.

Example: When a deal moves to the Document preparation stage, Bitrix24 updates the deal data and creates a group chat with the manager, lawyer, and accountant. They can start discussing the contract right away.
Add members to group chat
This node adds selected employees to an existing group chat.

Example: A company uses a separate group chat for each deal where the lawyer and accountant work together. When all parties sign the contract, Bitrix24 adds the manager to the chat automatically. The manager can join the discussion right away and review the chat history.
Send message to group chat
This node sends a message with your text to a group chat on behalf of a selected employee.

Example: When a report deadline is coming up, Bitrix24 sends a reminder to the subdepartment chat with the due date and a list of employees who have not submitted their reports yet. The manager does not need to send the reminder manually each time.
Add chat bot to group chat
This node adds the workflow Chat bot to the selected group chat.
Example: When all parties sign a contract, Bitrix24 adds the bot to the deal chat automatically. The bot can then send reminders about the next steps and upcoming deadlines.
Chat bot settings
This node creates a new Chat bot in a workflow or updates an existing one. You can set the bot name, title, and avatar.

Example: A company launches an onboarding process. This node creates a Chat bot named Onboarding Assistant. The workflow then adds the bot to the new employee's chat, and the bot sends a welcome message with the first-week schedule.
Send a chat bot message
This node sends a message to an employee on behalf of a selected Chat bot. The employee receives the message in their personal chat with the bot.
Example: A company uses a bot to help employees complete e-Learning courses. When three days remain before the deadline, the bot sends each employee a reminder with a link to the course.
Chat bot received a message
This trigger starts a workflow when an employee sends a message to the Chat bot. This lets the system reply automatically without a live agent.

Example: A company has a corporate knowledge base. When an employee sends a question to the bot, such as how to submit a travel request, the trigger starts the workflow. An AI agent finds the right article and sends the link back.
Send a direct message to employee
This node sends a message to an employee in their personal chat.

Example: A company uses a workflow to process orders. When an order status changes to Paid , Bitrix24 sends the manager a personal chat message automatically. The manager sees the payment right away and can move to the next step with the client.
Create new project
This node creates a project in Bitrix24 and adds the selected members.

Example: When a new order is added to CRM, Bitrix24 creates a project automatically and adds the required employees. The next node sends the order details to the project chat so the team can start work.
Feed post
This node creates a post in the Bitrix24 Feed for selected employees or the entire company.

Example: A company manages corporate events through a Bitrix24 Smart Process. When the manager moves a request to the Confirmed stage, Bitrix24 publishes an announcement in the Feed automatically. All employees see the date and details right away.
User notification
This node sends a notification to an employee through the Bitrix24 web messenger. This is a system notification format. It appears in the notification center, not in a personal chat.

Example: A company processes expense requests through Smart Processes. When a request status changes to Awaiting Approval , Bitrix24 sends the manager a notification automatically. The manager can open the request right away and make a decision.
In brief
- The Internal communications node group includes actions and triggers that help you automate team communication.
- The workflow sends messages to employees, creates chats and projects, publishes Feed posts, and works with Chat bots.
- Chat nodes let you create a new group chat, add members or a bot to it, and send a message to the whole team or a specific employee.
- Chat bot nodes let you create a bot, configure it, add it to a chat, and send messages on its behalf.
- The Chat bot received a message trigger starts the workflow when an employee sends the bot a message.

titre: Workflow templates: e-Signature for HR
sections: Workflow templates: e-Signature for HR

In Bitrix24, you can automate document signing with employees. The e-Signature for HR node group in the BI Builder workflow starts the required actions automatically. This happens when a document moves to approval or signing, when filling begins, or when all signatures are collected.
Triggers and activities help you tailor automation to your company's needs. You can add a node for each event or step that does not require employee involvement.

The e-Signature for HR nodes include four triggers and one activity. Triggers start a process when a specific event happens, such as when a document moves to signing. The activity completes a specific step in the process. For example, it can send a document to an employee for signing.
In this article:
- Track document approval
- Track document filling
- Track document move to signing
- Track signing completion
- Sign a document with an employee
Track document approval
The Document is send for approval trigger starts a process when a document moves to approval. You can automatically notify the people or prepare the next step.
Track document filling
The Document field completing started trigger starts a process when document filling begins. You can involve the right employees early in the document workflow.

For example, a legal department intern opens an employment contract to enter an employee's personal data. Bitrix24 notifies the chief legal officer that work with personal data has started and should be reviewed for accuracy.
Track document move to signing
The Document submitted trigger starts a process when a document moves to signing by an employee or company representative. This helps you monitor every stage of the signing process.
For example, when the company director signs the weekend work policy and the document is sent to employees, Bitrix24 creates a task for the HR manager to track which employees have signed it.
Track signing completion
The Document was signed trigger starts a process when all employees have signed a document or declined to sign it.

For example, when all employees finish working with the document, Bitrix24 notifies the HR manager. If everyone signed, the process is complete. If someone declined, the HR manager gets a task to find out why.
Sign a document with an employee

The Document signed by all parties trigger sends a document template from the company to an employee for signing. The document is sent automatically at the right time, so there is no need to send it manually at each stage.
For example, when an employee fills out and submits a consent form for personal data processing, Bitrix24 automatically sends the employment contract for signing.
In brief
- The e-Signature for HR node group includes four triggers and one activity to automate HR document workflows.
- The Document is send for approval trigger starts a process when a document moves to approval.
- The Document field completing started trigger starts a process when document filling begins.
- The Document submitted trigger starts a process when a document is sent to an employee or company representative for signing.
- The Document was signed trigger starts a process when all employees have signed the document or declined to sign it.
- The Document signed by all parties trigger automatically sends a document template to an employee for signing.

titre: Workflow templates: Payments
sections: Workflow templates: Payments

The Payment for Goods and Services group includes activities and triggers that help you automate customer billing. Activities create invoices and payment links. Triggers react to changes in orders and invoices and start automation at the right time.

These nodes reduce manual work with invoices. Activities can create an invoice and payment link automatically. Triggers can track whether a customer has paid and then start the next step, such as moving a deal to a new stage or assigning a task to an employee. Managers do not need to create documents by hand or keep checking payment status.
In this article:
- Create a payment link
- Process an automatic payment
- Invoice
- Track invoice payment
- Track order payment
- Track order cancellation
- Order created
- Invoice created
- Order field changed
- Invoice field changed
- Manual start from invoice
Create a payment link

This activity creates an online payment link and passes it to other nodes in the workflow, such as Send email . The customer can open the link, review the selected products or services, and pay right away.

Example: A deal moves to the Awaiting payment stage. The node creates a payment link and passes it to the Send email node, so the customer gets the link by email. Then the Notify employee node reminds the manager to follow up on the payment.
Process an automatic payment
This activity charges the customer's card automatically if they agreed to automatic payments when placing an order in the online store.

Example: A customer places an order in an online food delivery store and saves a card for automatic payments. When the order moves to the Awaiting payment stage, the activity charges the card automatically. Then the Send SMS node tells the customer that the payment was successful. The company gets paid without any manager involvement.
Invoice
This is a general-purpose node for working with invoices. In the settings, choose the action you want to perform:
- Create an invoice
- Schedule an activity
- Edit an invoice
- Change the linked company
- Change the linked contact
- Change followers
- Change the person responsible
- Update company details
- Change stage
- Create a document
- Add comment
- Add a product line item
- Remove product line items
- Delete an invoice.

Create an invoice — create a new invoice during the workflow. Example: A deal moves to the Approval stage. Bitrix24 automatically creates an invoice based on the deal data, including products, amount, and company details. The manager does not need to fill in anything manually.

Schedule an activity — create a call, meeting, or email linked to the invoice. Example: An invoice was sent to the customer, but payment has not arrived after two days. The workflow automatically creates a Call client activity for the manager. The employee sees the reminder in the calendar and follows up on payment status.

Edit an invoice — update invoice fields such as amount, due date, or other values. Example: The total amount in a deal changes. The workflow automatically updates the amount in the linked invoice, so the customer gets a document with the current amount.

Change the linked company — link the invoice to a different company. Example: It turns out the invoice should be issued to the parent company instead of a branch. The workflow updates the linked company in the invoice, and the correct company details appear in the document automatically.

Change the linked contact — link the invoice to a different contact. Example: A different employee on the customer side is now handling the deal. The workflow updates the linked contact in the invoice, so notifications go to the right person.

Change followers — add or remove employees who follow the invoice. Example: The invoice amount is higher than a set threshold. The workflow automatically adds the supervisor as a follower so they can monitor payment for a large deal.

Change the person responsible — assign a different employee as the person responsible for the invoice. Example: The manager handling the deal goes on leave. The workflow automatically reassigns the invoice to a colleague, so work with the customer continues without interruption.

Update company details — update banking or legal information in the invoice. Example: The company changes its bank account. The workflow automatically applies the new company details to invoices created after that date.

Change stage — move the invoice to a new stage. Example: The customer pays the invoice at a terminal. The workflow automatically moves the invoice to the Paid stage. The manager does not need to update it manually.

Create a document — create a document for the invoice from a template. Example: An invoice moves to the Approved stage. The workflow automatically creates a document from the template and attaches it to the invoice, so the manager can send it to the customer right away.

Add comment — add a note to the invoice. Example: Payment does not arrive on time. The workflow adds a comment to the invoice with the date and reason for the delay, so the full history stays in one place.

Add a product line item — add a product or service to the invoice. Example: An extra service is added to an order after the invoice is already created. The workflow automatically adds it to the list of product line items, so the manager does not need to redo the document manually.

Remove product line items — remove a product or service from the invoice. Example: The customer cancels one of the items in the order. The workflow automatically removes it from the invoice and the total is recalculated.

Delete an invoice — remove a document that is no longer needed. Example: A manager created an invoice by mistake, or the customer cancelled the deal. The workflow automatically deletes the unnecessary invoice so it does not clutter the list or confuse employees.
Track invoice payment
This trigger starts the workflow when an invoice status changes to Paid .

Example: A customer pays an invoice for a service. The trigger fires and the deal moves to the Product assembly stage. The warehouse employee can see that payment went through and starts preparing the shipment.

When a customer pays an invoice for a room rental, the trigger records the payment and starts the workflow: the action moves the deal to the Booking confirmed stage. The next action in the chain assigns the manager a task to send the customer a payment confirmation and details.
Track order payment
This trigger starts the workflow when a customer pays for an order at a terminal.
Example: A customer pays for a product at the checkout. The trigger fires and automatically moves the deal to the Item pickup stage. The manager does not need to switch the stage manually.

Or, after a terminal payment, the customer needs to receive a receipt. The trigger fires and the Send SMS node sends the customer a link to an electronic receipt. The customer gets the document right after payment.
Track order cancellation
This trigger starts the workflow after an order is cancelled.

Example: A customer cancels an order in the online store. The trigger fires and the Notify employee action sends the manager a task to contact the customer and find out the reason. The manager responds in time and does not lose the customer.
If a customer places an order but does not pay on time, the order is automatically cancelled. The trigger fires and the Send email node notifies the customer about the cancellation.
Invoice created
This trigger starts the workflow when a new invoice is created in CRM.

Example: A manager creates an invoice for a customer. The trigger fires and the Send email node automatically sends the customer the invoice with payment details. The manager does not need to send the invoice manually.

Or, a new invoice needs to be approved by a supervisor. The trigger fires and the Notify employee node sends the supervisor a task to review and confirm the invoice. The approval process starts without any reminders.
Invoice field changed
This trigger starts the workflow when the value of a selected field in an invoice changes.

Example: An accountant updates the amount in an invoice. The trigger fires and the Send email node automatically sends the customer the updated invoice. The customer gets the current document without any reminders.
Or, the due date in an invoice changes. The trigger fires and the Send SMS node notifies the customer about the new due date. The manager does not need to call each customer manually.
Manual start from invoice
This trigger fires when a manager manually starts a workflow from an invoice card.

Example: A manager starts the invoice sending process for a customer. The Manual start from invoice trigger fires and launches a parallel workflow — the Notify management node sends a reminder to check payment status in three days.

Or, a manager starts the invoice approval process. The trigger fires and in parallel launches a workflow that creates a task for the accountant to prepare company details. Both workflows run at the same time without any extra steps from the manager.
In brief
- The Payment for Goods and Services group includes activities and triggers for automating customer billing.
- The Create a payment link node generates a payment link and passes it to other nodes, for example to send the customer a link by email or in a chat.
- The Process an automatic payment node charges the customer's card automatically if they agreed to it when placing the order.
- The Invoice node creates and updates invoices, assigns responsible employees, and updates data without manager involvement.
- The Track invoice payment and Track order payment triggers start

titre: Workflow templates: Task management
sections: Workflow templates: Task management
The Task management and Task distribution groups include activities and triggers for working with tasks inside a workflow.
- Task management . Use these nodes for basic task actions. You can create tasks, update task fields, assign responsible users, and get task data.

- Task distribution . Use these nodes to work with flows. They distribute tasks among participants based on set rules. The workflow reacts to events like status changes or overdue tasks and balances the workload automatically.
In this article:
- Task node
- Task information
- Track a task status from CRM
- Overdue task
Task node
This node creates and manages tasks in a workflow. Open the node. In the Rules section, click Add rule . Select Activity as the rule type. Then choose an action:
- Create task
- Get task information
- Modify task
- Change status
- Change assignee
- Delete task
Create task — create a task for an employee.
Example: A company uses an onboarding workflow for new hires. HR, a supervisor, and IT each need to complete part of the process.

When the Accept new employee workflow starts, Bitrix24 creates tasks for all participants automatically. HR gets a task to prepare documents and send the offer. The supervisor gets a task to interview and approve the candidate. IT gets a task to prepare the workstation and set access rights. Tasks appear on time, and no step is missed.
Get task information . Get task data and pass it to the next workflow steps.
Example: Managers create tasks to prepare client contracts. The workflow needs to add task data to documents automatically.
In the Prepare client contract workflow, Bitrix24 takes the task creation date and inserts it into the document. The employee does not need to enter the data manually.
Modify task . Change task fields such as the deadline, description, or other parameters. Before setup, select the task that started the workflow or a task from a linked deal.
Example: Employees work on tasks related to client documents. If a task is not completed on time, the supervisor needs to step in right away.
The workflow includes the Overdue task trigger. When the task deadline passes, Bitrix24 adds the supervisor as a follower automatically. The supervisor gets a notification and can respond right away.
Change status . Move a task to the required status. This activity works with a selected task, such as the task that started the workflow or a task linked to the process.

Example: A CRM manager works with deals for different clients. Large clients need an extra review. A supervisor must check a task before documents are sent or work begins. Other clients do not need this review.

The workflow includes the Track a task status from CRM trigger. When a task moves to Under review , Bitrix24 checks the linked deal. If the deal is not for a large client, the workflow moves the task to Completed automatically. This keeps regular tasks from getting stuck in review and saves time.
Change assignee . Assign a different responsible user to a task. This activity works with a selected task, such as the task that started the workflow or a task from linked process data.
Example: Tasks are linked to deals. Each deal has a task for document preparation. If the deal amount is above a set threshold, a more experienced employee must handle the task.
The workflow checks the deal amount, finds the linked task, and reassigns it to the senior manager automatically. This helps make sure important tasks go to the right person right away.
Delete a task . Remove a task that is no longer needed. This activity works with a selected task, either the task that started the workflow or a task returned by other activities.
Example: In CRM, tasks help track client work stages. Some tasks are only technical steps, such as checking data or preparing a document.

The workflow includes the Track a task status from CRM trigger. When a task moves to Completed , Bitrix24 deletes it if it is no longer needed. This keeps the task list clean and focused on active work.
Overdue task

This trigger starts a workflow when a task status changes to Overdue . It helps respond to delays on time: you can notify the supervisor or start additional actions. The workflow starts on its own without manual deadline tracking. Examples:

- In a deal, a manager creates a task for an accountant to prepare a client invoice. If the task becomes overdue, Bitrix24 starts the workflow — it sends a notification to the supervisor or creates a new task marked Urgent .
- A company has a task to prepare a commercial proposal. If the task deadline passes, Bitrix24 starts the workflow: it notifies the supervisor and reassigns the task to the senior manager.
In brief
- Workflows are built from nodes — ready-made action blocks.
- The Task node creates, updates, and deletes tasks inside a workflow, assigns responsible users, and changes statuses.
- The Overdue task trigger starts a workflow when a task is overdue and automatically notifies the supervisor or launches additional actions.

titre: Workflow templates: Customer base
sections: Workflow templates: Customer base
The Client base management node group helps automate work with contacts and companies. It reacts to new clients automatically and helps keep duplicate inquiries out of your CRM.
In this article:
- Contact created
- Company created
- Add customer to Exceptions
- Company
Contact created
This trigger starts the workflow when a contact is created.
Examples:
- A client submits a request on your website, and CRM creates a new contact. The trigger starts, and the Notify employee node alerts the manager about the new client so they can respond right away.

- A sales manager meets a company representative at a trade show and adds their contact to CRM. The trigger starts, and the Send email node automatically creates and sends a quote based on the data from the contact form. The client gets a personalized offer, and the manager saves time.
Company added
This trigger starts the workflow when a company is created.
Examples:
- A manager creates a record for a new partner company. The trigger starts, and the Send email activity sends a welcome email with a service presentation.

- A manager finishes negotiations and creates a new company record. The trigger starts, and the Create task activity automatically assigns a task to send a quote within two days. This helps the manager stay on top of the new client.
Add customer to Exceptions
This activity adds a client's phone number or email address to the stop list. CRM will no longer automatically create leads or deals from that contact.
You can use this node in workflows for any CRM item, including leads, deals, contacts, and others.

Example: A manager closes a deal with the Spam status because the client is not a good fit. When the deal moves to the selected stage, the node automatically adds the contact to the stop list. If another request comes from that phone number or email address, CRM will not create a new lead.
Company

This is a universal node for working with companies in CRM. To configure it, open the node, go to the Main tab, and click the Rules field. In the settings, select the action type and choose what to do with the company:
- Create a company
- Schedule an activity
- Update the company
- Update followers
- Update the responsible person
- Update company details
- Create a document
- Add comment
- Delete the company

Create a company — Creates a new company record during the workflow. Example: A deal moves to the Contract signed stage. The workflow automatically creates a company record based on the deal data. The manager does not need to fill it in manually.

Schedule an activity — Creates a call, meeting, or email activity linked to the company. Example: Negotiations are complete, but no decision has been made yet. The workflow automatically schedules a call back activity for the responsible manager. The employee sees the reminder and does not miss the follow-up.

Update the company — Updates data in the company record. Example: A company moves to a new city. The workflow automatically updates the address in the record. The manager does not need to edit it manually.

Update followers — Adds or removes employees who follow the company. Example: A deal amount goes over a set threshold. The workflow automatically adds a supervisor as a follower so they can track work with an important client.

Update the responsible person — Assigns a different employee as responsible for the company. Example: The manager working with a client goes on vacation. The workflow automatically reassigns the company to another employee so the work continues without interruption.

Update company details — Updates the company's bank or legal details. Example: A company changes its bank account. The workflow automatically updates the company details in the record. New documents use the current information.

Create a document — Generates a document from a template and attaches it to the company record. Example: A deal moves to the Contract signed stage. The workflow automatically creates a contract from a template. The manager can send it to the client right away.

Add comment — Adds a comment to the company record. Example: A manager finishes negotiations and records the agreed terms. The workflow adds a comment with the summary so all history stays in one place.

Delete the company — Deletes the company record. Related deals, contacts, and tasks are not deleted. They simply lose the link to that company. Example: A company record turns out to be a duplicate. The workflow automatically deletes it when the selected condition is met. The manager does not need to clean up the database manually.
In brief
- The Client base management node group automates work with contacts and companies in CRM.
- The Contact created and Company created triggers start the workflow as soon as a new client appears in the database.
- The Add customer to Exceptions activity prevents duplicate leads and deals from being created from a client's phone number or email address.
- The Company node supports many actions, from creating and updating a company record to generating documents and deleting the record.

titre: Workflow templates: Automated solution
sections: Workflow templates: Automated solution

Automated solutions are workspaces in Bitrix24 for smart process automations that are not linked to CRM. You can use them to automate work in any department, such as HR, accounting, IT, and more. Each automated solution includes smart processes with their own forms, stages, and settings. Automated solutions: automate work of company departments
The Automated solutions trigger group lets you start workflows manually from an item or automatically when a new form is created or a field value changes.
In this article:
- Automated solution created
- Automated solution field changed
- Manual start from automated solution
Automated solution created
This trigger starts a workflow when a new item is created in a smart process inside an automated solution.

A transport company buys a new vehicle. An employee creates a form with the vehicle details, and the trigger starts the workflow. Bitrix24 automatically creates tasks for vehicle registration and insurance. This helps the company prepare the required documents faster and put the vehicle into service right away.
Automated solution field changed
This trigger starts a workflow when a field value changes in an item form. It reacts to a specific change, so you do not need to track updates manually.

A company uses an automated solution for hiring. A recruiter uploads a completed test assignment to a candidate form. The trigger detects the field change and starts the workflow. Bitrix24 automatically sends the manager a notification with a link to the item for review. The assignment does not get lost, and the hiring process moves faster.
Manual start from an automated solution
This trigger lets you start a workflow from an item form. The employee clicks the Workflow automation in CRM button and selects the required scenario.

A support specialist cannot resolve a client issue alone. They open the request form and start the workflow manually. Bitrix24 automatically adds a senior specialist as an observer and sends a notification that help is needed.
In brief
- The Automated solutions trigger group lets you respond automatically to events in smart processes or start scenarios manually from an item form.
- The Automated solution created trigger starts a workflow when a new item is added to a smart process.
- The Automated solution field changed trigger reacts to a change in a specific field in a form and starts a workflow automatically.
- The Manual start from an automated solution trigger lets you start a workflow from an item form. The employee clicks the Workflow automation in CRM button and selects the needed scenario.

titre: Workflows templates: Delivery
sections: Workflows templates: Delivery

The Delivery trigger group includes triggers that track order events from shipment to delivery. You can use them to start an automation when the delivery or shipment status changes, when a tracking number is added, or when the customer receives the order. Online store in Bitrix24: Getting started
In this article:
- Track delivery status updated
- Shipment ID was specified
- Shipment status updated
- Product was shipped
- Order received by customer
Track delivery status updated
This trigger starts an automation when the delivery status changes in the order form.
Examples:

- The order status changes to "In transit." The trigger starts an automation and sends the customer an SMS with the tracking number. The customer can track the order, and the manager does not need to send the message manually.

- The order status changes to "Delivery delayed." The trigger creates an activity in the deal form so the manager can contact the customer and explain the issue. This helps the manager respond on time and avoid missing problem orders.
Shipment ID was specified
This trigger starts an automation after a tracking number is added to the deal form.
Examples:
- The manager enters a tracking number in the deal form. The trigger records it and sends the customer an email with a tracking link. The customer gets the tracking number right away.
- A tracking number is added to the order and the delivery is on the way. The trigger notifies the responsible manager. This helps the manager track shipments without checking every deal manually.
Shipment status updated
This trigger starts an automation whenever the shipment status changes in the deal form.
Examples:

- The status changes to "Handed to courier." The trigger automatically moves the deal to the "Shipped" stage. The manager sees the current status in CRM and does not need to update the stage manually.

- The status changes to "Return." The trigger creates an activity so the manager can contact the customer and find out the reason. This helps the manager learn about the return right away instead of from a customer call.
Product was shipped
This trigger starts an automation as soon as the product leaves the warehouse.
Examples:

- The warehouse ships an order. The trigger automatically sends the customer a notification that the order has been handed over for delivery. The customer stays informed, and the manager does not need to reach out manually.

- The order is shipped, but payment has not been received yet. The trigger creates an activity in the deal form so the manager can confirm payment before delivery. This helps the manager keep track of these orders.
Order received by customer
This trigger starts an automation when the delivery status in the deal form changes to "Delivered".
Examples:
- The customer receives the order. The trigger automatically sends an email asking for a review. The manager does not need to send the message manually.
- The customer receives the order. The trigger automatically moves the deal to the "Completed" stage. The manager does not need to update the stage manually.
In brief
- The Delivery group includes triggers that track events throughout the delivery process. In CRM, all orders are stored as deals.
- The "Delivery status updated" trigger starts an automation whenever the order status changes, such as when the order is in transit or delayed.
- The "Shipment ID was specified" trigger starts when a tracking number is added to the deal card.
- The "Shipment status updated" trigger responds to any shipment status change, such as when the order is handed to a courier or returned.
- The "Product was shipped" trigger starts once, when the product leaves the warehouse.
- The "Order received by customer" trigger starts when the delivery status changes to "Delivered."

titre: The Workflow control node group
sections: The Workflow control node group

The Workflow control group includes activities and triggers that control workflow logic and flow. You can use these nodes to start a process on a schedule, set conditions for activities, and merge parallel branches. This helps you build different automation scenarios, from simple flows to complex loops and branching logic.
In this article:
- Get user data
- Merge
- Condition
- Condition block
- Schedule-based launch
- Start smart script
- Run workflow
- Iterator
- Pause
- Interrupt process
- Set workflow result
- Loop
Get user data
This node lets you set up constants and configure the form layout where users enter them. Employees and supervisors can enter starting process data without opening the workflow builder.
For example, in the AI agent for knowledge base Q&A process, this node creates a launch form with constants such as the agent name, role, communication rules, knowledge base, and chat.
Merge
This node merges two parallel process branches. The process continues only after both branches are complete.
For example, in the Contract signing process, a document goes to two parties for signing. This node merges the branches, and the process continues only after both parties sign the document.
Condition
This node checks a condition and sends the process down the true or false branch based on the result.

For example, in the Contract approval process, a document goes to a lawyer for review. If the document passes review, the node sends it to the supervisor for approval. If it does not, the node sends it back for revision.
Schedule-based launch
This trigger starts a process on a set schedule. You can choose the start time and frequency: every hour, day, week, month, or year.

For example, this trigger can start the Weekly report process every Friday. When it runs, the process gathers meeting and task data for employees in subdepartments, and the supervisor gets a short weekly summary.
Start smart script
This node starts a smart script inside a process. A smart script is a sequence of automation rules that handles routine CRM actions. Smart scripts in CRM

For example, if a deal amount is higher than a set threshold, the node starts a smart script for large clients. The script can schedule a meeting, create a contract, and send a notification to the supervisor.
Run workflow
This node starts another workflow at a specific stage of the current process. In the settings, you can turn on waiting. In that case, the current process continues only after the other workflow ends.
For example, when a deal moves to the Document preparation stage, the node starts the Document approval workflow. After approval is complete, the main process continues.
Iterator
This node runs an activity for each value in a multi-value variable.
For example, at the end of the Project management process, the system starts collecting feedback. The node gets a variable with the list of project members and creates a task for each one.
Pause
This node delays the next activity in a process for a set period or until a specific date.
For example, the node can pause a process until the day of a client meeting. On that morning, the process resumes and the manager gets a reminder with the key details.
Terminate process
This node stops a workflow. After that, the process cannot continue from the same step. You need to start it again.
For example, in the Contract approval process, the supervisor approves the document. The manager then gets a notification, and the node ends the workflow.
Set workflow result
This node lets you define the workflow result:
- Process completion for a selected employee
- A document, field, or file.

For example, in the Proposal preparation process, the supervisor approves the proposal and the node saves the file as the workflow result. The file then appears in the list of completed processes, and the manager can open it right away.
In brief
- The Workflow control group includes activities and triggers that control workflow logic and flow.
- The Get user data node lets you set up constants and configure the form layout where users enter them.
- The Merge flow node merges two parallel process branches.
- The Condition node checks a condition and sends the process down the true or false branch based on the result.
- The Schedule-based launch trigger starts a process on a set schedule.
- The Start smart script node starts a smart script inside a process.
- The Run workflow node starts another workflow at a specific stage of the current process.
- The Iterator node runs an activity for each value in a multi-value variable.
- The Pause node delays the next activity in a process.
- The Interrupt process node stops a workflow.
- The Set workflow result node lets you define the workflow result.

titre: Workflow templates: Storage node group
sections: Workflow templates: Storage node group
The Storage group includes actions for working with data storages in your processes. Use these actions to create storages, save data, read data, and delete data when needed.

Storages help you keep data inside a process. For example, you can save results from AI agents or track changes to the responsible person in deals. This data is global, so you do not need to create a separate storage for each branch or process.
In this article:
- Create storage
- Write data
- Read data
- Delete data
Create storage
This action creates a storage, which is a table for saving data in a process.

For example, when you launch an AI agent to answer knowledge base questions, this action creates a table with system data, such as who started the agent and which chat it works in. The agent uses this data to know where to send replies.
Write data
This action adds data to a storage. You can create a new record, add data to an existing record, or replace it.

For example, when the responsible person changes in a deal, this action adds a record to the storage. You can then use this data to create a monthly summary that shows which employees worked on the deal and how much time they spent.
Read data
This action gets data from a storage and sends it to the next steps in the process.

For example, in the AI agent for employee testing process, this action gets data about when employees took a test and how many correct answers they gave. The next action uses this data, and the supervisor gets a summary in chat.
Delete data
This action deletes data from a storage. You can delete selected records by filter or remove all data at once.

For example, an AI agent for onboarding helps new employees learn internal policies and checks their knowledge. The test results are saved in a storage. After an employee finishes the probation period, this action deletes their results from the storage.
In brief
- The Storage group includes actions for working with data storages in processes.
- Create a storage, which is a table for saving data.
- Write data adds data to a storage.
- Read data gets data from a storage and sends it to the next steps of the process.
- Delete data removes data from a storage by filter or deletes all data.
- Storages are available across all branches and processes.

titre: Workflow templates: Marketing and Lead generation
sections: Workflow templates: Marketing and Lead generation
In the new Workflow Builder, every workflow is made up of nodes. Nodes are ready-to-use blocks for specific actions.
Some nodes start the workflow. These are called triggers. Other nodes perform actions, such as creating a lead, generating a QR code, or sending a notification.

A trigger is always the first step in a workflow. It watches for an event and starts the workflow when that event happens. For example, a client submits a form on your website or returns to the site after a long break. After the trigger runs, the workflow moves to the action nodes.

The Marketing and Lead Generation groups include nodes for working with potential customers automatically. You can use them to track website activity, create and update CRM leads, and generate QR codes for marketing tasks. Each node can work in its own scenario and does not depend on the others.
In this article:
- Lead
- CRM form completed
- Customer revisited the website
- Create a QR code
Lead
Use this node to work with leads inside a workflow.
Open the node. In the Rules section, click Add rule . Select the Action rule type. Then choose one of these actions:
- Create a lead
- Schedule an activity
- Update a lead
- Update a linked company
- Update a linked contact
Create a lead . This action creates a new lead in CRM and fills it with data from the workflow.
Example:
A real estate agency runs ads and places a form on its website.
The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger. When a potential buyer submits the form, Bitrix24 starts the workflow and creates a lead with the client's name, phone number, and request.
The manager opens the lead and sees all client data right away. There is no need to copy information from the form to CRM by hand, and no request gets lost.
Schedule an activity . This action adds an activity to the lead timeline, such as a call, meeting, or email.
Example:

An electronics ecommerce store works with clients who showed interest in a product but did not make a purchase. A manager sent one client a list of laptops and a quote, but the client opened the email and did not reply.

The workflow uses the Track client return to site trigger. When the client visits the website again, Bitrix24 starts the workflow and adds a call activity to the lead timeline. The manager sees the activity and calls at the right time.
Update a lead . This action updates lead fields such as status, responsible person, stage, or other details.
Example:
A construction company collects requests for renovation estimates. A client sent a request a month ago, the manager sent the estimate, and then the client stopped responding.

The workflow uses the Track client return to site trigger. When the client returns to the website and opens the portfolio page, Bitrix24 finds the lead and automatically moves it from the Estimate sent stage to the Renewed interest stage. If you set up a condition in the workflow, Bitrix24 can also assign the lead to a senior manager who works with warm leads.
The senior manager gets a notification and calls the client while the client is still on the site.
Update a linked company . This action updates the company linked to the lead.
Example:

A client submits a request and enters a department name. The lead is created, but the wrong company is linked. Later, the client submits another form and provides the correct legal company name for the contract.
The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger. When the client submits the second form, Bitrix24 finds the lead and updates the linked company.
The manager opens the lead and sees the current data. There is no need to search for the company and fix it manually.
Update a linked contact . This action updates the contact linked to the lead.
Example:
A law firm works with returning clients. A former client submits a form again, but this time uses a new work phone number and email address after changing jobs.
The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger. When the form is submitted, Bitrix24 finds the existing contact and updates the phone number and email address.
The manager opens the record and sees the current data. There is no need to compare old and new requests or update anything by hand.
CRM form completed

This trigger starts the workflow after a client submits a CRM form, such as a request, registration, or question. You do not need to track new requests manually. The workflow starts automatically as soon as the form is submitted.
Examples:

- A store adds a fitting appointment form to its website. As soon as a client submits the form, Bitrix24 starts the workflow. The Track CRM form submission trigger runs, and the Lead node creates a lead with the client's data. The manager opens the lead and sees who booked and for what time.

- A company hosts a webinar and collects registrations through a form. When a participant submits the form, Bitrix24 starts the workflow. The trigger records the event, and the Lead node creates a lead with the participant's data. The manager sees the new request in CRM and contacts the participant.
Customer revisited the website

This trigger starts the workflow when a client visits the website again. It helps you respond to client interest at the right time. The workflow starts automatically, without any manual visit tracking.
Examples:

- A company that sells industrial equipment works with long sales cycles — a client may evaluate options for several weeks. A manager sent the client a quote, but the client went silent and did not answer calls. Two weeks later, the client returned to the website and started browsing equipment pages.

The workflow uses the Track client return to site trigger. Bitrix24 sees that the client is back on the site and immediately sends the manager a notification. The manager calls and reaches the client at the moment the client is actively reviewing the offer. The chance of closing the deal increases sharply.

- A fitness club works with clients whose memberships have expired. When a former client visits the website and opens the pricing page, Bitrix24 sees the visit and starts the workflow. It automatically sends the client an email with a personal offer — 20% off a membership purchased within three days. The client receives the offer at exactly the right moment, when they have shown interest themselves.
Create a QR code

This node creates a QR code inside a workflow and passes its data to the next steps — for sending to a client, inserting into a document, or publishing on a website. The node generates several formats: a short link to a page, links for BB-code or HTML insertion, a print-ready version, and others. You can use this data in other nodes in the workflow — for example, to send a link to a client.
Examples:

- A company hosts a closed presentation for key partners. Bitrix24 creates a QR code for entry to the event. A partner scans the code and clicks the confirmation button. Bitrix24 sees that the partner has arrived and sends a notification to the responsible manager. The manager knows the partner is already there and goes to greet them in person. No important guest goes unnoticed.

- A company participates in an industry exhibition and wants to collect visitor contacts right at the booth. The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger, which runs when a visitor scans the code and submits the form. The visitor scans the code with their phone, opens the form, and leaves their contact details. The manager does not need to collect business cards and enter data manually — all requests go directly into CRM.
In brief

- The CRM form completed and Track client return to site triggers are starting points. They monitor client behavior on the website and start the workflow automatically, without any manager involvement.
- The Lead node performs actions with leads inside the workflow: creates new leads, updates existing ones, schedules activities, and updates linked data.
- The Create a QR code node generates a code and passes links to the next steps in the workflow — for sending to a client, inserting into a document, or publishing on a website.
- Each node can be used in its own scenario and does not depend on the others.

titre: Workflow templates: CRM
sections: Workflow templates: CRM
In the new workflow builder, a trigger is the first step in any process. It watches for an event and starts a chain of actions when that event happens.

Triggers in the CRM group help you react to CRM changes at the right time. For example, when a manager updates a deal stage, Bitrix24 can automatically create a task for a lawyer. When the responsible person changes, the new manager can get a notification right away. If an automatic trigger does not fit your case, you can start the process manually from the item form.
In this article:
- Field change triggers
- Responsible person changed trigger
- Manual start triggers
Field change triggers

Triggers in this workgroup watch for changes in CRM forms and start a process when a specific field is updated. You do not need to check each form manually. The trigger runs as soon as the data changes.
Deal updated. This trigger starts a process when a selected field in the deal form changes, such as stage, amount, responsible person, or another field.

Example: A company sells software with a long approval cycle. When a manager moves a deal to the Contract pending signature stage, a lawyer needs to review the contract. The process uses the Deal updated trigger to watch the Stage field. As soon as the value changes, a Task node creates a task for the lawyer, and a User notification node sends a notification with a link to the deal.
The contract goes to review right away, without calls or reminders from the manager.
Contact updated. This trigger starts a process when a selected field in the contact form changes, such as phone number, email, job title, or another field.

Example: A law firm sends clients a newsletter with legal updates and contract renewal reminders. When a client provides a new email address and the manager updates the Email field in the contact form, the Contact updated trigger runs. A User notification node tells the manager that the email has changed and reminds them to update the mailing list.
The manager sees the notification immediately and updates the mailing list without delay.
Company updated. This trigger starts a process when a selected field in the company form changes, such as industry, number of employees, address, or another field.

Example: An insurance company works with corporate clients and sets package pricing based on headcount. When a client grows from 50 to 100 employees and the manager updates the Number of employees field in the company form, the Company updated trigger runs. A User notification node alerts the manager, and a Task node creates a task to review the terms and contact the client.
The manager learns about the change right away and can offer updated terms on time.
Lead updated. This trigger starts a process when a selected field in the lead form changes, such as source, stage, budget, or another field.

Example: A real estate agency collects leads from several platforms. When a manager asks a client how they heard about the agency and sets the Source field to Referral , the Lead updated trigger runs. A User notification node reminds the manager to find out who made the referral and save it in CRM. A Lead node moves the lead to the Qualification stage.
Referral data is always captured, so the agency knows who brings in new clients.
Estimate updated. This trigger starts a process when a selected field in the estimate form changes, such as status, amount, expiration date, or another field.

Example: A company sends estimates to clients. When a manager sets the estimate status to Declined , the Estimate updated trigger runs. A Notify management board node alerts the supervisor, and a Task node creates a task for the manager to find out why the estimate was declined.
The supervisor sees the declined estimate right away and can step in.
SPA updated. This trigger starts a process when a selected field in an SPA form changes.
An SPA is a custom CRM item type that a company creates for its own needs, such as purchase requests, contracts, claims, and more. The available fields depend on how the SPA is set up.

Example: A manufacturing company manages a Purchase request SPA in Bitrix24. When the CFO approves a request and changes the Approval status field to Approved , the SPA updated trigger runs. A Task node creates a task for the purchasing manager, and a User notification node sends them a notification.
The purchasing manager gets the task as soon as the request status changes to Approved .
Track responsible person change trigger
This trigger starts a process when the responsible person changes in a CRM item.

Example: In a large company's sales department, managers sometimes go on vacation or transfer to another department. When a supervisor changes the responsible person in a deal, the Track responsible person change trigger runs. A User notification node sends the new manager a notification with a link to the deal, and an Add participants to group chat node adds them to the client chat.
The new manager immediately sees the conversation history and knows what stage the deal is at.
Manual start triggers
Manual start triggers let you start a business process directly from an item form, without waiting for an event.
The Sales and CRM workgroup includes several manual start triggers:
- Manual start from deal
- Manual start from contact
- Manual start from company
- Manual start from lead
- Manual start from estimate
- Manual start from SPA
- Manual start from order
- Manual start from invoice .
The logic is the same for all triggers: a manager starts the process manually when needed. Here are some examples:

- A client wrote in chat and asked to send closing documents for the deal. Nothing changed in the form, so an automatic trigger would not run. The manager opens the deal form and starts the process manually: a Task node creates a task for the accountant to prepare the documents, and a User notification node informs them.
- A client asked to receive an estimate. The manager opens the estimate form and starts the process manually: a Send email node composes the email and sends it to the client.
In brief
- Field change triggers watch specific fields in CRM forms and start a process as soon as a field is updated.
- The Responsible person changed trigger runs when the responsible person changes and helps hand off work without losing context.
- Manual start triggers let you start a process from a form at any time, when an automatic trigger does not fit or you need to act right now.
- For each item type — deal, contact, company, lead, estimate, SPA, order, and invoice — there is a dedicated manual start trigger.

titre: Work with CRM workflow templates
sections: Work with CRM workflow templates
The Sales and CRM workgroup nodes work with CRM items such as leads, deals, companies, contacts, estimates, invoices, and SPAs.

With these nodes, a workflow can create and update CRM records, schedule activities, pass data between linked items, and, for some nodes, assign responsible users and followers. This removes manual work. Managers do not need to move data between forms, update statuses, or set reminders on their own.

In the new workflow builder, these nodes are called actions. They run after a trigger node starts the workflow. For example, a workflow can start after a CRM form submission on a website or after a user launches it manually from a form.
In this article:
- Lead node
- Deal node
- Company node
- Contact node
- Estimate node
- Invoice node
- SPA node
- Add CRM event node
To learn about trigger nodes that start a workflow when CRM fields change or when a workflow is launched manually from a form, see.
Lead node
This node works with leads in a workflow. Available actions:
- Create lead — creates a new lead and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity and links it to the lead. For example, a call, a meeting, or document preparation.
- Update lead — updates lead fields such as status, source, or priority.
- Update linked company — updates the linked company. For example, the company name, details, or industry.
- Update linked contact — updates the linked contact. For example, the phone number, job title, or email address.
Examples:

- A store adds a request form to its website. The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger. When a client submits the form, the Schedule activity action runs. Bitrix24 adds an activity to the lead Timeline right away: call the client within one hour. Managers no longer need to create an activity manually for every new request.

- The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger. When a client submits the form, the Update lead action runs. Bitrix24 sets the Source field to Website and the priority to High . The manager can open the lead and see where the client came from without filling in the fields manually.
Deal node
This node works with deals in a workflow. Available actions:
- Create deal — creates a new deal and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity for the deal. For example, a call, a meeting, or document preparation.
- Update deal — updates deal fields, such as the stage.
- Change responsible — assigns a new responsible user to the deal.
- Update followers — adds, replaces, or removes followers in the deal.
Examples:

- In this company, deals at the Negotiation stage are handled by a senior manager who discusses terms in detail and works with the client directly. The workflow uses the Deal field changed trigger. When a deal moves to the Negotiation stage, the Change responsible action runs. Bitrix24 reassigns the deal to the senior manager.

- A client pays an invoice linked to a deal. The workflow uses the Track invoice payment trigger. The Update deal action runs. Bitrix24 moves the deal to the Paid stage. Managers do not need to find the deal manually and move it through the pipeline after payment.
Company node
This node works with companies in a workflow. Available actions:
- Create company — creates a new company record and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity linked to the company, such as a call, a meeting, or sending documents.
- Update company — updates company fields such as details, client status, or industry.
- Update followers — adds, replaces, or removes followers in the company record.
- Change responsible — assigns a new responsible user to the company.
Examples:

- A company works with a client on a trial basis. The workflow uses the Track invoice payment trigger. When the client pays an invoice for the first time, the Update company action runs. Bitrix24 changes the company status from Trial period to Active client . Employees can see right away that the relationship has moved to a paid stage, without checking payments manually.

- A client company increases its purchase volume and moves to the key accounts segment. The sales supervisor starts the workflow manually from the company form. The workflow uses the Manual launch from company trigger. The Change responsible and Update followers actions run. Bitrix24 assigns the key account manager as the responsible user and adds the previous manager as a follower so they can share context and support the transition.
Contact node
This node works with contacts in a workflow. Available actions:
- Create contact — creates a new contact record and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity linked to the contact, such as a call, a meeting, or sending an email.
- Update contact — updates contact fields such as phone number, email address, job title, interaction status, and other data.
- Update linked company — updates the fields of the company linked to the contact.
- Update followers — adds, replaces, or removes followers in the contact record.
Examples:

- A client submits a request form on the website. The workflow uses the Track CRM form submission trigger. The Schedule activity action runs. Bitrix24 adds an activity to the contact Timeline: call the client back within one hour. The manager can see right away who to call and does not miss the new contact.

- A client calls the company after a long break in communication. The workflow uses the Track incoming call trigger. When the call ends, the Schedule activity action runs. Bitrix24 creates an activity in the contact record: prepare an updated proposal and follow up with the client the next day. The manager does not need to record agreements manually or set a reminder after the call.
Estimate node
This node works with estimates in a workflow. Available actions:
- Create estimate — creates a new estimate record and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity linked to the estimate, such as a call, a meeting, or sending documents.
- Update estimate — updates estimate fields such as status, responsible user, comments, and other data.
- Update linked company — updates the fields of the company linked to the estimate.
- Update linked contact — updates the fields of the contact linked to the estimate.
Examples:

- During negotiations, a client expressed interest in a service and asked for an estimate with the terms of cooperation. The manager starts the workflow manually from the deal form. The workflow uses the Manual launch from deal trigger. The Create estimate action runs. Bitrix24 creates an estimate and fills it with deal data. After that, the Send email to client action runs. Bitrix24 immediately sends the client an email with a link to the estimate. The manager does not need to transfer client, product, and pricing information manually or write to the client separately: the estimate is created and sent for approval in a single workflow run.

- The manager discussed the terms with the client by phone, and the client agreed to the proposed conditions. The manager starts the workflow manually from the estimate form. The workflow uses the Manual launch from estimate trigger. The Update estimate action runs. Bitrix24 changes the estimate status to Approved . The manager can see in the form that the terms are confirmed and can move on to preparing the invoice.
Invoice node
This node works with invoices in a workflow. Available actions:
- Create invoice — creates a new invoice record and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity linked to the invoice.
- Update invoice — updates invoice fields such as status, comment, responsible user, and other data.
- Update linked company — updates the fields of the company linked to the invoice.
- Update linked contact — updates the fields of the contact linked to the invoice.
Examples:

- A company agreed on terms with a client and sent a contract for signing. The workflow uses the Track signing by the second party trigger. When the client signs the contract, the Create invoice action runs. Bitrix24 generates an invoice. Managers do not need to create an invoice manually after every signed contract.

- An accountant starts the workflow manually from an overdue invoice that the client never paid. The workflow uses the Manual launch from invoice trigger. The Update invoice action runs. Bitrix24 changes the invoice status to Canceled . The accountant can see in the form that the invoice is closed as unpaid.
SPA node
This node works with SPA items in a workflow.
An SPA is a separate type of CRM record created when standard CRM items are not enough — for example, for contracts, purchases, or equipment requests. Available actions:
- Create SPA item — creates a new SPA item and fills it with workflow data.
- Schedule activity — creates an activity linked to the SPA record.
- Update SPA item — finds an item using field filters and updates its values.
- Update linked item — replaces or removes the link between the SPA item and a CRM item, such as a deal.
- Update linked company — updates the fields of the company linked to the SPA item.
Examples:

- A company manages contracts in a separate SPA called Contracts . A manager agrees on terms with a client and creates a new contract record, then starts the workflow manually from that record. The workflow uses the Manual launch from SPA trigger. The Schedule activity action runs. Bitrix24 adds an activity to the contract Timeline for the lawyer: check the details, prepare the text, and send it for approval. The lawyer can see right away what needs to be done, and the manager does not need to write to them separately in chat.

- A company tracks contracts in a separate SPA. When a client company's old contract expires and a new one is signed, an employee starts the workflow manually from the company form. The workflow uses the Manual launch from company trigger. The Update SPA item action runs with a filter for that company and the Active status. Bitrix24 finds the contract and changes its status to Expired . The employee does not need to search for the contract manually among other SPA records.
Add CRM event node

This node adds a record to the Timeline of the CRM item where the workflow is running. This is useful when a workflow automatically performs an action — for example, changes the responsible user or the stage — and you need to record not just the change itself, but also the context: why it happened.

For example, in a company, deals at the Negotiation stage are handled by a senior manager. The workflow uses the Deal field changed trigger.
