When a deal moves to this stage, the Log CRM event action runs. Bitrix24 adds a record to the Timeline: "Deal transferred to senior manager for negotiations." The supervisor can see not just the fact that the responsible user changed, but also the context — why it happened.
In brief

- Seven nodes work with CRM items — leads, deals, contacts, companies, estimates, invoices, and SPAs. With these nodes, a workflow creates and updates CRM items, assigns responsible users and followers, and schedules activities.
- The Lead node creates and updates leads, schedules activities, and updates linked companies and contacts.
- The Deal node creates and updates deals, schedules activities, and changes the responsible user and followers.
- The Company node creates and updates companies, schedules activities, and changes the responsible user and followers.
- The Contact node creates and updates contacts, schedules activities, and updates the linked company and followers.
- The Estimate node creates and updates estimates, schedules activities, and updates linked companies and contacts.
- The Invoice node creates and updates invoices, schedules activities, and updates linked companies and contacts.
- The SPA node creates and updates SPA items, schedules activities, and updates linked items and companies.
- The Add CRM event node adds a record to the Timeline of a CRM item.

titre: Workflow templates: Customer communications
sections: Workflow templates: Customer communications
The Communications node group includes activities and triggers that help you manage incoming and outgoing communication in a workflow.
Activities send messages and place calls to customers. They help the workflow contact a customer automatically at the right time.
Triggers watch for communication events. They start the workflow when a customer or employee takes a specific action, such as opening an email, sending a chat message, or answering a call.
In this article:
- Send email
- Send a message to Open Channel
- Make a call
- Send SMS
- Make AI-assisted call
- Incoming email received
- Inbound call received
- Outbound call
- Email message viewed
- URL was clicked
- Open Channel first message received
- Customer conversation recorded
- New message received
- Open Channel first message received is overdue
- Email was sent to customer
- Missed call received
- Agent accepted Open Channel chat
Send an email

This activity sends an email to a customer from a workflow. For example, you can send an estimate, invoice, order tracking number, or other documents. The email is sent automatically, with no action needed from the manager.

Example: After an order is paid, the company sends a confirmation email automatically. The email includes the order number, item list, delivery dates, and support contact details. When the Track order payment trigger detects the payment, the workflow runs the Send an email activity and sends a prepared message with order data. The manager does not need to follow up manually.
Send a message to Open Channel
This activity sends a message to a customer through an open channel, such as a website chat or messenger.

Example: A customer sends a message in chat. When the Track the first client chat message trigger detects the request, the workflow runs the Send an open channel message activity. It automatically sends a reply that confirms the request was received and that a manager will respond soon. The customer gets an instant response, and the manager does not need to send routine replies.
Make a call
This activity starts a voice bot that calls the customer at a set time or when a condition is met. To use this activity, connect Bitrix24 telephony first. Telephony connection options overview

Example: A customer schedules an appointment. When it is time to confirm the visit, the workflow starts a call. The bot contacts the customer and checks whether they will attend. The manager does not need to make the call manually.
Send an SMS
This activity sends an SMS to a customer at the right time. For example, it can send an order confirmation or a delivery tracking number.

Example: A customer pays for an order. The Track order payment trigger starts the Send an SMS activity. The customer receives a confirmation message with the order number, and the manager does not need to send anything manually.
Make AI-assisted call
This activity starts an AI call. A voice bot calls the customer and follows a script that you define.

Example: When the Track delivery status change trigger detects the Delivered status, the workflow starts an AI call. The bot tells the customer that the order has arrived and asks for a convenient pickup time. The manager does not need to call manually.
Incoming email received
This trigger starts the workflow when a customer email arrives. You do not need to monitor email manually because the workflow can respond automatically.

Example: A customer sends an email with a question. The trigger starts the workflow and automatically creates an activity in the customer record with the note Reply to email. The manager sees the reminder and does not miss the request.
Inbound call received
This trigger starts the workflow after a customer calls.

Example: A customer calls the manager. After the call ends, the workflow automatically moves the deal to the In progress stage. The request is already logged, so the manager does not need to update the stage manually.
Outbound call
This trigger starts the workflow after a manager calls a customer.

Example: A manager calls a customer from the CRM while the deal is in the New stage. After the call ends, the workflow automatically moves the deal to the In progress stage. The call itself shows that work with the customer has started, so the manager does not need to update the stage manually.
Email message viewed
This trigger starts the workflow after a customer opens an email.

Example: A manager sends an estimate to a customer. When the customer opens the email, the workflow automatically creates an activity for the manager called Call the customer back, scheduled for two days later. This gives the customer time to review the estimate and helps the manager follow up at the right time.
URL was clicked
This trigger starts the workflow when a customer clicks a link in an email.

Example: A manager sends an email with a link to a contract. When the customer clicks the link, the workflow automatically moves the deal to the Contract sent for client signature stage. The manager can then see all deals at this stage and know who to follow up with if the contract has not been signed.
Open Channel first message received
This trigger starts the workflow after a customer sends their first message in the website chat through a Bitrix24 open channel. Create and configure Open Channels

Example: A new website visitor sends their first chat message. The workflow automatically sends a notification to the responsible manager: New chat request, please respond to the customer. The manager responds in time and does not miss the first message.
Customer conversation recorded
This trigger starts the workflow after a manager records a conversation with a customer using the visit tracker.

Example: A manager holds a meeting with a customer and records the conversation. After the recording is saved, the workflow automatically creates an activity for the manager's supervisor in the CRM record — to listen to the recording and evaluate the meeting quality. Quality control starts without any additional reminders.
New message received
This trigger starts the workflow when a customer sends a chat message that contains specific words or phrases defined in the node settings.

Example: A customer types the word complaint or refund in the chat. The trigger detects the keyword and starts the workflow, which automatically notifies the supervisor about the problematic request. Important messages are not missed.
Open Channel first message received is overdue
This trigger starts the workflow if a manager does not respond to a customer's first message within a set time. The time limit is defined in the node settings.

Example: A customer sends a chat message, but the manager does not respond within 15 minutes. The workflow automatically notifies the supervisor and reassigns the chat to another available employee. The customer receives a response on time.
Email was sent to customer
This trigger starts the workflow after a manager sends an email to a customer.

Example: A manager sends a contract to a customer for review. After the email is sent, the workflow automatically creates an activity — follow up with the customer in three days if no reply has been received. The manager sees the reminder and follows up on time.
Missed call received
This trigger starts the workflow after an incoming call from a customer goes unanswered.

Example: A customer calls outside of business hours and cannot reach anyone. The trigger detects the missed call and automatically creates an activity for the responsible manager — call the customer back. The manager sees the task and contacts the customer during the next working hours.
Agent accepted Open Channel chat
This trigger starts the workflow at the moment an employee begins a conversation with a customer.

Example: A manager accepts a chat from a customer. At that moment, the workflow automatically moves the deal to the In progress stage. The manager does not need to update the stage manually — the workflow detects the start of the conversation and updates the deal automatically.

titre: Workflow templates: Other
sections: Workflow templates: Other
The Other operations node group includes actions for Drive, absence management, Calendar, and codes.
You can use these nodes to:
- Keep Drive organized. For example, upload files, create folders, and delete items you no longer need.
- Add events to the Calendar and the absence chart.
- Generate discount coupons and QR codes for customers.
In this article:
- Add absence chart event
- Get Drive file or folder details
- Upload to Drive
- Upload new version to Drive
- Outbound Webhook
- Copy or move in Drive
- Generate code
- Calendar event
- Create QR code
- Create folder in Drive
- Delete Drive object
Add absence chart event
This node adds different event types to the absence chart, such as vacation, business trips, sick leave, time off, and more.

For example, in a Vacation approval workflow, a manager approves the request first, and then an accountant processes it. After that, the node adds an event to the chart with the employee name, the Annual vacation type, and the start and end dates.
Get Drive file or folder details
This node gets detailed information about a Drive item, such as a file or folder. You can retrieve the ID, name, size, view link, and other details.

For example, in a Contract approval workflow, a lawyer uploads a contract file to Drive. The node then gets the file name and view link. The workflow sends the manager a notification with a link to the document.
Upload to Drive
This node uploads a file to the selected Drive storage: a user Drive, workgroup Drive, shared Drive, or folder.

For example, in a Purchase approval workflow, a manager uploads a vendor invoice to a task. The node automatically saves the file to an accounting folder in Drive, where the team can find it later during reconciliation or an audit.
Upload new version to Drive
This node uploads a new version of a file to Drive. The new file replaces the previous version.

For example, in a Contract signing workflow, a lawyer uploads a scanned contract to Drive and sends it for signature. When both parties sign the document, the node replaces the original file with the signed scan.
Outbound Webhook
This node sends data to external systems through a webhook.
For example, in a Purchase approval workflow, a manager approves the request, and the node sends order data to an external warehouse system. The required quantity is then reserved automatically.
Copy or move in Drive
This node copies or moves Drive items, including files and folders. You can copy or move an item to a user Drive, workgroup Drive, shared Drive, or folder.
For example, in a Contract signing workflow, after both parties sign the document, the node moves the file from the In progress folder to the Archive folder.
Generate code
This node generates a code with the length and format you choose. The code can include numbers, special characters, lowercase letters, and uppercase letters.
For example, when a customer messages an Open Channel chatbot, the node generates a discount coupon code. The workflow then sends a reply with an offer to use the coupon.
Calendar event
This node adds an event to a calendar, such as a workgroup calendar, company calendar, or personal calendar.

For example, in an Annual planning workflow, department heads upload and align development plans with the director one by one. When the last plan is approved, the node creates a Year planning discussion meeting in the company calendar.
Create QR code
This node creates QR codes for marketing tasks. You can pass the QR code to the next workflow step as a page link, an HTML image, or another format.
For example, a customer fills out a form to register for an event, and the node generates a personal QR code for entry. The workflow then sends the customer an email with the QR code as an image.
Create folder in Drive
This node creates a folder in the selected Drive: a user Drive, workgroup Drive, shared Drive, or another folder.
For example, in a Project management workflow, the node automatically creates a folder in the project Drive where team members can upload materials.
Delete Drive object
This node deletes a Drive item, such as a file or folder.
For example, in an Onboarding and orientation workflow, a folder with assignments is created in a new employee's Drive. When the employee completes the probation period, the node deletes the folder.
In brief
- The Other operations node group includes actions for Drive, absence management, Calendar, and codes.
- The Add absence chart event node adds vacation, business trips, sick leave, time off, and other events to the absence chart.
- The Get Drive file or folder details node gets detailed information about a file or folder in Drive.
- The Upload to Drive node uploads a file to Drive storage.
- The Upload new version to Drive node uploads a new version of a file to Drive.
- The Outbound Webhook node sends data to external systems through a webhook.
- The Copy or move in Drive node copies or moves files and folders in Drive.
- The Generate code node generates a code with the length and format you choose.
- The Calendar event node adds an event to a calendar.
- The Create QR code node creates QR codes for marketing tasks.
- The Create folder in Drive node creates a folder in the selected Drive.
- The Delete Drive object node deletes files and folders from Drive.

titre: Workflow templates: Project management

titre: Workflow templates: Feedback
sections: Workflow templates: Feedback

In the new workflow builder, each workflow is made up of nodes. Nodes are ready-to-use blocks for actions. Some nodes start a workflow. These nodes are called triggers. Other nodes perform actions, such as creating a task or sending a notification.

A trigger is always the first step. It watches for an event and starts the workflow when that event happens. The Feedback group includes this type of trigger. It tracks when a customer submits a form to leave a review, suggestion, or complaint.
This article explains how to use the Feedback form submitted trigger.

The trigger starts a workflow when a customer submits a CRM form with the Feedback scenario. This scenario is designed for reviews, suggestions, and complaints. You do not need to check for new feedback manually. The workflow starts automatically as soon as the form is submitted.
Unlike the Track CRM form submission trigger, which starts a workflow for any CRM form, this trigger runs only for forms with the Feedback scenario.
Examples:

- An online store collects customer reviews through a form on its website after an order is delivered. The form includes a Rating field with a value from 1 to 5. When a customer submits the form, Bitrix24 starts the workflow and the Feedback form submitted trigger runs. If the rating is 3 or lower, the condition is met and the Task node creates a task for the customer success manager. The manager can contact the customer and resolve the issue. This helps the team react right away instead of discovering the problem later.

- A fitness club chain uses the same type of form to collect feedback after each visit. The form also includes a Rating field from 1 to 5. If a customer gives a high rating, such as 4 or 5, Bitrix24 starts the workflow. The trigger records the form submission, and the Send email node automatically sends a thank-you message. The customer gets a response right away, and employees do not need to reply to each positive review manually.
In brief
- The Feedback form submitted trigger starts a workflow when a customer submits a CRM form with the Feedback scenario. You do not need to review new submissions manually.
- This trigger runs only for forms with the Feedback scenario, unlike the Track CRM form submission trigger, which works with any CRM form.
- You can set up the next steps in action nodes after the trigger. For example, you can create a task for a low rating or send a thank-you message for a high rating.

titre: Time settings in automation rules
sections: Time settings in automation rules
Bitrix24 automation rules include settings that control when a rule runs and which items it applies to. Conditions in automation rules
We added new time settings for automation rules. Now you can:
- Set the exact time for the automation rule work
- Fill in the time in deal and task fields with the automation rules
- Configure the time range in the automation rule condition
Set the exact time for the automation rule work
Use the Time field to choose when an automation rule should run.
Available options:
- After the event
- Before the event
- Exact time
If an item moves to a stage after the scheduled time, the automation rule runs immediately.
Automation rules can perform an action with a delay of several minutes if several automation rules are running at the same time.
How to fill time in element fields with an automation rule
Some automation rules update fields automatically. For example, the Create task automation rule can set a task deadline. You can now specify both the date and the exact time.

For example, you can create the Plan activity automation rule for deals. The rule creates an activity for a manager to prepare an estimate. The deadline is set to two days after the client meeting at 12:00.
Specify the exact time in the Time field.
The selected time appears in the deal timeline.
Configure a time range in automation rule conditions
You can add a time range to a condition to run an automation rule only for specific items.

For example, you can create the Send SMS to customer automation rule for deals. If a deal is created outside working hours, from 8:00 PM to 8:00 AM, the rule sends a message that the customer will be contacted the next day.
To configure this condition:
1. Click Add condition .
2. Select Deal > Time created .
3. Select In range .
4. Enter the required time range.
If the range covers two calendar days, add two separate ranges.
In brief
- You can set an exact time for an automation rule action, for example, 10:00 AM one day before an event or tomorrow at 12:00 PM.
- Automation rules can fill fields with both date and time values.
- You can add time ranges to automation rule conditions, for example, to run a rule only for deals created between 12:00 AM and 8:00 AM.

titre: Variables and constants in automation rules
sections: Variables and constants in automation rules
Variables and Constants in CRM greatly simplify calculations in fields and work scenarios, such as profit calculation.

Constants are values that do not change or change rarely. It can be a tax rate, a specific date, an employee's role, and so on. For example, you can create a "Chief Accountant" constant and assign this role to a specific employee. If the chief accountant is changed, you should change the value of the constant and select another employee. All automation rules that use this constant will automatically use the new value.

Variables are values that can change during the work process. For example, a variable could be the percentage from the deal that managers receive. Depending on the amount of the deal, the managers will receive different percentages.
Create variables and constants
Go to the Automation rules page.
Select Variables or Constants on the top panel.
Edit variable and Math operations
You will see a table with a list of items. If necessary, you can select fields to be displayed. Click on the settings icon.
Constants and variables are created in the same way. Let's consider the settings on the example of a variable.
Click Create and fill in the field values in the slider.
- Name - it is displayed in the list. You can quickly find the desired variable by name.
- Type - select the type of variable from the list: number, string, bind to user, etc.
- Multiple - select how many values a variable can have: one or more.
- Value - it depends on the type of the variable. If the type is "Number", specify a specific number.

- Visibility - select where you can use the variable. Everywhere - in CRM entities, smart processes, workflows, tasks. CRM - in any CRM entities. Specific CRM entity - the variable will be available only in the selected CRM entity, for example only in deals.
- Description - specify the purpose of the variable.
When you have filled in all the fields, click Save.
How to use variables and constants
Constants and variables can be used in automation rules.
Example of using constants and variables in automation rules

For example, we have a warehouse in Boston. After the client makes an order in our online store, we send an email with the information about the approximate delivery time. The order picking at the warehouse never takes more than 1 day. However, the order delivery period is different: within the city, the delivery is done within 1 day, but it can take up to 3 days to deliver an order across the region.
Thus, we can specify the order picking as a constant , and the order delivery as a variable . Their default value will be 1 day.
In the Picking and shipping stage we add the following automation rules:

We use both Perform math operations automation rules to calculate the number of days required to deliver an order in the city and region. The calculated value will be saved to the Order shipping variable.
If the delivery is done within the city, we add 1 day to the order-picking period.
In the same way, we add 3 days in case of the delivery across the region.
Then we can use the Order shipping variable in the text of an email in the Send email to customer automation rule.
The variable will be replaced by the calculated number of days, and our client will be aware of the approximate delivery time.
In brief:
- You can use constants and variables in automation rules to store data.
- Constants are values that do not change or change rarely. It can be a tax rate, a specific date, an employee's role, and so on.
- Variables are values that can change during the work process.
- Values of constants and variables can be used in mathematical operations.
- The constant value can only be changed manually by editing the item. A variable can also be changed by the Variable change automation rule.
Read also:
- Automation rules in CRM
- Triggers in CRM
- Conditions in automation rules

titre: Conditions in automation rules
sections: Conditions in automation rules
A condition defines when an automation rule runs and which CRM items it applies to. For example, you can send emails only during business hours if the deal amount is over $5,000.
In each rule, you can configure:
- Execution way
- Run time
- Launch conditions
Execution way
Choose how rules run within the same stage.
Wait . The rule runs after the rules above it. Use this for step-by-step processes. Example: one rule creates an invoice, then the next sends it to the client.
In parallel : The rule runs independently from others in the same stage. Example: one rule sends a message to the client, while another creates a chat to discuss the deal.
Run time
Set when the rule runs: immediately or at a specific time.
Current time . The rule runs as soon as the CRM item reaches the stage. Example: send an SMS right after a deal is created.
After . The rule runs after a delay (minutes, hours, or days). Example: email the client one hour after a meeting.
Before . The rule runs before a specific event. Example: send a reminder one day before payment is due.
Exact time . The rule runs at a specific date and time. Example: send an email at 12:00 PM on the event day.
In the Time field, select the option you need.
You can also limit rules to business hours. This helps ensure employees don’t miss important events.
Respect working hours specified in the Bitrix24 settings . The rule runs only during company business hours. It accounts for weekends, holidays, and working schedules. Business hours

Respect responsible person's working hours . The rule does not run if the assigned employee has not started their workday, is on vacation, or is on a break. Automation rules: "Respect the responsible person working hours" option
Launch conditions
Use conditions to run rules only for specific items. Conditions can be simple or combined.
Simple condition . A single condition. Example: run the rule only for repeat deals.
Compound condition . Multiple conditions combined with AND/OR.
AND condition . The rule runs only if all conditions are true. Example: send an SMS with a promo code if the customer made a purchase and the amount is over $5,000.
OR condition . The rule runs if at least one condition is true. Example: send an SMS if the client lives in Boston or New York.
AND + OR condition . You can combine both. The system checks AND conditions first.
Example: (A and B) or (A and C)
- If (A and B) is true, the rule runs.
- If (A and B) is false, the system checks (A and C). If true, the rule runs.
- If both are false, the rule does not run.
In this setup, condition A must be true in all cases.
Example: send an SMS if the customer made a purchase and lives in Boston, or made a purchase and lives in New York.
Available condition types
You can apply conditions to different fields and values.
Not empty
Runs if the field has a value.
Add the Amount field to the condition. If the field is filled in the deal form, the rule schedules an activity. If the field is empty, the rule does not run.
Empty
Runs if the field has no value.
Add the Amount field to the condition. If the field is empty in the deal form, the rule assigns an activity to the responsible person.
Equal to
Runs if the field value matches the condition.
Add the City field and set the value to Boston. If the contact form shows Boston, the rule sends a message with special offers.
Not equal to
Runs if the field value does not match the condition.
Add the City field and set the value to New York. If the contact form shows any other city, the rule sends an email.
Is in
Runs if the field value matches a value from the condition, a variable, a constant, or another field.
Add the Comment field. Select the Key plans variable as the value. If the deal comment includes a plan from this variable, the rule reassigns the deal. Variables and constants in automation rules
Example: the Key plans variable includes Professional, Professional Plus, and Enterprise. If the comment contains “Enterprise”, the deal is assigned to a senior specialist.
Is not part of
Runs if the field value is not included in the condition, variable, constant, or another field.
Add the Comment field. Select the Key plans variable as the value. If the comment does not include any of these plans, the rule reassigns the deal.
Example: if the comment contains “Demo”, the deal is assigned to a regular specialist.
Includes
Runs if the field contains specific text.
Add the Comment field and set the value to Discount . If the comment includes “Discount”, the rule emails the client.
Doesn't include
Runs if the field does not contain specific text.
Add the Name field and set the value to test . If the deal name does not include “test”, the rule runs. This helps exclude test deals.
More than
Runs if the value is greater than the condition.
Add the Amount field and set the value to 5000. If the deal amount is over $5,000, the rule changes the responsible person. If it is $5,000 or less, the rule does not run.
Less than
Runs if the value is less than the condition.
Add the Amount field and set the value to 5000. If the deal amount is under $5,000, the rule sends a delivery message.
Not less than
Runs if the value is greater than or equal to the condition.
Add the Amount field and set the value to 5000. If the amount is $5,000 or more, the rule changes the responsible person.
Not more than
Runs if the value is less than or equal to the condition.
Add the Amount field and set the value to 5000. If the amount is $5,000 or less, the rule sends a delivery message.
In range
Runs if the value falls within a set range.
Add the Created on field and set the range from 12:00 PM to 3:00 PM. If the deal was created at 12:30 PM, the rule sends a message.
Supported field types:
- Number
- Integer
- Date
- Date/time
In brief
- Conditions define when automation rules run and which items they apply to.
- Each rule includes execution way, run time, and launch conditions.
- Choose whether rules run in sequence or in parallel.
- Set rules to run immediately or at a specific time.
- Use conditions to target specific items.
- Conditions can be simple or combined with AND/OR logic.

titre: Copy and move automation rules
sections: Copy and move automation rules
If you create a new deal pipeline and implement similar processes there, you don't need to set up automation from scratch. Just move or copy existing automation rules there.
The following scenarios are available for copying and moving rules:
- Between stages of the same pipeline
- Between different pipelines
- Between CRM entities that have automation rules

For example, you have an automation rule that sends payment status notifications to the sales department employees. If you find it useful for accounting or delivery department employees too, simply copy this rule for new recipients.
However, there are some limits to consider:
- Actions can only be performed within CRM.
- Only one automation rule stage can be copied or moved at once.
- You cannot copy or move automation rules if there are unsaved changes.
Go to the Sales automation page and use the actions described below for one or multiple automation rules. Sales automation page in CRM
Individual actions
To move an automation rule to another stage, drag and drop it to the desired column.
To copy an automation rule, click Actions and select Copy . The new automation rule will appear at the same stage.
Group actions
To apply actions to several automation rules,
1. Click Group actions under the desired stage.
2. Tick the needed automation rules or click Select all in stage .
3. Choose the Copy or Move action.
A panel will slide in on the right of the page. Select where to copy or move automation rules, then click Run .
In the top-right corner, you will see how many rules have been copied or moved. Click Cancel , and the rules will be back to their previous places.
No additional settings are required to use the automation rules. After moving or copying them, they will be ready to run.
In brief
- Move or copy automation rules between stages, pipelines, and CRM entity types.
- To change the stage of an automation rule, drag it to the desired column. To copy it, click Actions and select Copy .
- Using group actions, you can copy and move multiple automation rules at once.
- Click Cancel to restore the automation rules to their previous settings.

titre: Disable automation rules and workflow actions
sections: Quick answer
To disable an automation rule:
1. Go to CRM > Automation rules .
2. On the Sales automation page, select a rule.
3. Click Actions > Disable .
To enable the rule again, open the Actions menu and select Enable .
To disable multiple rules:
1. Click Group actions below the automation rule form.
2. Select the rules you want to disable.
3. Choose Disable from the top panel.
Disable an automation rule
1. Go to the CRM section.
2. Open Automation rules .
3. On the Sales automation page, select a rule.
4. Click Actions > Disable .
The rule is now disabled. To turn it back on, use the Actions menu.
Disable multiple automation rules
1. Open Group actions below the automation rule form.
2. Select the rules you want to disable.
3. Choose the action from the top panel.
Disable a workflow action
1. Open the workflow.
2. Select the action you want to disable.
3. Click the settings icon.
4. Open the action menu in the top-right corner.
5. Select Disable .
6. Click Save .
The disabled action appears grayed out.
If you disable a main action, all dependent actions are also disabled. You can enable any action again using the same steps.

titre: Four levels of automation in Bitrix24
sections: Four levels of automation in Bitrix24
Bitrix24 allows you to automate workflows and operations on every level of your company's hierarchy.
Personal
Use CoPilot to generate content, summarize work, automate small routines, and stay productive effortlessly.
CoPilot in Feed
Take advantage of CoPilot for quicker post and comment writing. Open the Feed section and start CoPilot. Then specify your request and get the result in a few seconds.
We have divided the pre-prompts in Feed into several groups:
- Analyze text: Use CoPilot to extract the main points, find the pros and cons, and explain unclear phrases.
- Modify text: CoPilot can shorten or expand your text, simplify it, correct typos, or add emoji.
- Change tone of text: CoPilot is beneficial in making your text more polite or formal.
- Create text: Enter some basic details, and CoPilot will prepare a text according to a chosen format (post, news, greeting, article, or job description).
CoPilot in Tasks
Specify some basic information about your task, then let CoPilot add more details and determine the steps to take.

The main advantage of using CoPilot in tasks is the option of making checklists in one click. There's no need to distribute information manually and worry about missing anything. Provide some essential data and allow CoPilot to create a checklist for the task.
CoPilot in Chat
CoPilot chat conveniently opens in a separate section. There are no pre-prompts, just enter your query concerning any task.

To access the CoPilot chat, click the special icon in the right sidebar. CoPilot saves the chat history and remembers the context of your question in each chat. You can return to the chats you started earlier to proceed.

It is important to clearly define the desired output for CoPilot in your prompt. This way, CoPilot will generate accurate and relevant results. Just be specific: the more details you provide, the better.
CoPilot in Bitrix24 Mail

CoPilot is an AI assistant built into Bitrix24 Mail. It helps you work with emails faster. Use it to summarize email threads, write replies, continue drafts, fix grammar and spelling, or translate text into another language.
Without CoPilot, you may need to:
- Spend time writing emails from scratch
- Carefully word replies, such as polite declines or formal responses
CoPilot helps simplify these tasks. You can use it to:
- Summarize email conversations
- Write or continue email drafts
- Generate client responses
- Improve and edit text
Team
Automate project handovers, status updates, CRM workflows, and call processing to keep teams synced and responsive.
AI Speech analytics and Sales scripts in CRM
Bitrix24 now offers new CoPilot features in CRM: AI Speech analytics and Sales scripts. With CoPilot, you can analyze your agents' customer calls, compare them to scripts, and get improvement tips.

CRM has ready-made sales scripts for various situations, such as talking to new customers, handling complaints, presenting new products, and more. You can use these scripts or create your own to quickly train your agents and improve service quality.
CoPilot helps supervisors by:
- Creating sales scripts
- Analyzing agent calls to find areas for improving customer communication
- Tracking each employee's performance without listening to calls or asking for reports
CoPilot supports agents by:
- Improving customer communication quality through feedback on each call
- Providing specific recommendations to improve customer communication skills
CoPilot in Sites
CoPilot is an AI assistant that generates websites based on a given theme. Describe the main parameters, and it will select the design, images, and text.
CoPilot can help:
- Create a website without programming skills. For example, quickly launch a landing page for a promotion or new business.
CoPilot Follow-Up
CoPilot Follow-Up can help your team have productive meetings. Discuss the agenda, summarize key points, record the results, and keep everything on schedule.
AI Audio and Video Tasks

Turn your voice or video messages into tasks instantly. AI analyzes your message in real-time, identifying the assignee and the deadline, formulating checklists, and automatically creating tasks. Assignments are no longer lost in chats. Everything you say in voice or video messages is captured in tasks, helping the team stay on track.
To create tasks automatically, turn on this option in your Bitrix24 settings.
Department
Enhance departmental efficiency with AI-driven call transcription, follow-up actions, and automated multi-step workflows.
Flows

Flows is a tool for collecting and managing tasks from different departments. For example, if an employee needs software installed, they can add a task to a Flow. The system then distributes tasks to the responsible team members.
What you can do with Flows
- Collect tasks in one place and assign them automatically or manually
- Monitor employee workload
- Track task completion speed
- Identify bottlenecks and problem areas
Flows. Jumpstart Guide Create a flow Create and find tasks in Flows Distribute tasks in the Flow
Sales automation in CRM
Bitrix24 CRM includes a full set of tools to automate and manage customer workflows. You can assign orders to employees, send personalized emails and SMS, generate documents, and more.
To use sales automation in CRM, you need to:
- Add and configure automation rules and triggers
- Set up variables and constants
- Test and validate your automation setup
Automation rules in CRM Triggers in CRM
Task automation

You can automate task workflows using automation rules and triggers. Automation rules handle routine actions such as sending notifications, creating tasks, or adding participants. They run when a task reaches a specific stage.
Set up triggers in tasks Task templates
Company
Standardize and automate organization-wide processes – from HR requests to approvals, contracts, and more.
Robotic Process Automation (RPA)

RPA (Robotic Process Automation) is a tool that automates routine tasks, such as approving leave requests, business trips, invoices, and contracts, or creating tasks and handling other routine actions.

It’s easier to set up than standard workflows and doesn’t require any technical skills—any employee can create a workflow using ready-made assignment templates. This helps your team work faster and make fewer errors.
Create a workflow in RPA Configure stages Add an assignment Add a workflow item
Automated solutions

Smart Process Automation (SPA) lets you build custom workflows. You can create CRM entities with custom fields, kanban stages, permissions, and more. You can also use SPA outside of CRM to automate work for any team, such as HR or accounting. Create a dedicated workspace and set up the tools and settings you need.
Create an automated solution with SPA Configure automated solutions

titre: Delete automation rules and triggers
sections: Delete automation rules and triggers
When using automation tools in CRM, you may need to delete and replace unnecessary rules and triggers with new ones.

To do this, go to CRM and select the desired item type. If you need automation rules for deals, choose the appropriate pipeline, as rules are configured separately for each one. Then, click the automation rule icon.
Select the automation rule or trigger you want to delete and click the cross icon (X) in the top right corner of the block.
To delete multiple automation rules and triggers:

titre: Sales automation in CRM
sections: Sales automation in CRM
Bitrix24 CRM includes a full set of tools to automate and manage customer workflows. You can assign orders to employees, send personalized emails and SMS, generate documents, and more.
On the Sales automation page, you can:
- Add and configure automation rules and triggers
- Set up variables and constants
- Test and validate your automation setup
Before you start, make sure Sales automation is available on your plan.
Open the Sales automation page
1. Go to CRM .
2. Select an item, such as leads or deals.
3. Open the Automation rules tab.
Automation rules and triggers
Use this tab to configure automation for each stage.
- Automation rules run actions when an item reaches a stage. For example, send emails, create documents, or assign tasks.
- Triggers track customer actions and CRM changes, such as email clicks, calls, or payments. When triggered, they move the item to another stage.
Automation rules in CRM Triggers in CRM
Select a pipeline For deals, you can configure automation separately for each pipeline.
Search rules and triggers Use the search bar to quickly find items by name.
Edit in Workflow Designer Use this tool to add advanced actions not available in the standard interface, such as loops or repeated checks.
In Workflow Designer, you can edit both a single rule and a chain of rules at one stage. Workflow designer

Group actions . Use this option to apply changes to multiple or all rules and triggers at a stage. For example, you can transfer all automation rules from deals to leads. Group actions for automation rules
Variables and constants
Use these tabs to store values for conditions, fields, and calculations.
- Constants Fixed values that rarely change, such as a tax rate or a specific role. Example: assign a “Chief Accountant” role to a specific employee.
- Variables Values that change during the process. Example: a commission percentage that varies based on deal amount. Automation rules can use this value to calculate payments.
Automation rule test mode
Use test mode to check how your automation works.
- Run tests with demo or real deals
- Review each step of the automation
- Fix errors as needed
Test results are saved in the Test logs section.
In brief
- Bitrix24 CRM helps automate customer workflows and routine actions.
- Use the Sales automation page to manage rules, triggers, variables, and tests.
- Configure automation for each stage of your CRM items.
- Store reusable values in variables and constants.
- Use test mode to verify and troubleshoot automation.

titre: Helper automation rules
sections: Helper automation rules
Automation rules are divided into basic and helper types. Helper automation rules do not perform an action and require a basic automation rule after them to output the information.

For example, when organizing an event, you decide to send QR codes instead of tickets to your customers. Use the Create QR code and Send SMS to customer automation rules. The first one generates a code, but to actually send it to customers you need to use the second one. This can save a lot of time for your employees.
Type Helper in the search bar to find all helper automation rules.
Here's the list of available helper automation rules:
- Get details values
- Get payment information
- Get product item information
- Get task information
- Get list item information
- Get CRM item information
- Get SPA item information
- Get employee information
- Create QR code
- Create payment link
- Generate code
Use case
Suppose you have an online store and want to email a customer with product information. To get this data, add the Get product item information automation rule.
In the Product ID field, add the Products value from the deal. Then you will get the correct information.
Next, add the Send email to customer automation rule and configure it.
1. Click the three dots (...) next to the input area.
2. Select Automation rules and expand the Get product item information section.
3. Choose the needed fields, like Product name and Price .
The inserted fields will display as code values. Once the automation rule starts, these values will be replaced in the email text and sent to the client.
In brief
- Automation rules are divided into basic and helper types. Helper automation rules don't perform an action and require a basic automation rule after them to output the information.
- Type Helper in the search bar to find all helper automation rules.
- Use helper automation rules to get the needed data and apply it in customer interactions.

titre: Automation rules in CRM
sections: Automation rules in CRM

Automation rules are tools that simplify customer interactions and help automate routine tasks. When a CRM item reaches a certain stage, automation rules can send emails and SMS messages, generate documents, and more.
You can set up automation rules in:
- Leads
- Deals
- Estimates
- Invoices
- SPAs
Add an automation rule
1. Go to CRM .
2. Select the item type, like Leads or Deals.
3. Open the Automation rules section.
4. Click Create .
5. Choose the stage where you want an automation rule to appear.
6. Click the Filter icon.
7. Select Bitrix24 Automation rules to show only automation rules. They're grouped by the task they solve, like customer communication, repeat sales, employee alerts, and more.
8. Click Add next to the rule. To add multiple rules at once, hold the Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) key and select the ones you need.
Configure an automation rule
After adding an automation rule, you'll need to configure it. If you've added multiple rules, they'll be highlighted in yellow. Configure each rule individually.
All automation rules have a common set of settings:
- Execution: Choose whether the automation rule should start after the previous ones or run independently.
- Run: Decide whether the automation rule should perform the action immediately or at a specific time.
- Condition: Set a condition for the automation rule to apply only to certain items. For example, only if the deal amount exceeds $50,000. Conditions in automation rules
You can insert a CRM item status into the text fields of an automation rule.
1. Click the three dots (...) .
2. Open the Status group.
3. Select the parameter you need:
- Status name: where the item came from. For example, Chat with client or CoPilot .
- Status value: the item's current state. For example, Unread or Fields filled in .

This is helpful when automation rules create new items or send notifications. For example, a rule can copy a deal, and the copy's name will automatically include Chat with client: Unread . This lets the manager see the context right in the project Kanban view without opening the form.
Also, each automation rule has unique parameters. For example, the Add product item rule asks you to enter the product ID, price, and quantity. Automation rules: Products
Once you've configured the automation rules, click Save in the rule settings window, then save changes on the Sales automation page.
Check automation rule performance
To see if an automation rule has started for a specific CRM item, open the item form, go to the Automation tab, and check its status.
Each status has a different background color and icon.
- The automation rule worked successfully : green background and check mark .
- The automation rule didn't work as there was an error : green background and attention icon . Hover over the icon to see the reason behind the issue.
- The automation rule didn't work as there was a pause : white background and spinning circle icon . The rule will start after a set time, like after the previous rule.
- The automation rule didn't work at all : white background with no icon. Go to the rule settings and check its conditions and execution parameters.
To ensure all settings are correct, use the Automation rule test mode . It helps you check how the automation rules work and fix possible errors. Automation rule test mode
Edit or delete an automation rule
1. Go to the required CRM section, such as Leads or Deals.
2. Open the Automation rules tab.
3. Choose an action to perform.
Delete (x) : Remove the automation rule if it's no longer needed.
Edit : Modify the automation rule settings. For example, add a new condition or change a field value.
Copy : Duplicate the automation rule with its settings. This is useful if you want to use the same rule at another stage or make minor changes. Copy and move automation rules
Disable : Temporarily turn off the automation rule if it's not needed for a while. You can re‑enable it at any time.
Stop : Use this option to interrupt a chain of automation rules at a certain stage for a specific CRM item. Stop automation rules at a certain stage
Once you've made all changes to the automation rules, click Save .
In brief
- Automation rules are tools that simplify customer interactions and help automate routine tasks.
- When a CRM item reaches a certain stage, automation rules can send emails and SMS messages, generate documents, and more.
- Automation rules in CRM are available in leads, deals, estimates, invoices, and SPAs.
- Automation rules are grouped by the task they solve, such as customer communication, repeat sales, employee alerts, and more.
- To add an automation rule, go to CRM, select the needed item, and open the Automation rules section.
- All automation rules have some common parameters, such as the execution way, run time, and conditions. Other parameters are specific for each automation rule.
- Check if an automation rule has started for a specific CRM item using the Automation tab.

titre: Triggers in CRM
sections: Triggers in CRM

Triggers are tools that simplify customer interactions and automate routine tasks. They track customer actions and changes in CRM, like email link clicks, incoming calls, invoice payments, and more. When a specific action occurs, the trigger moves a CRM item to its designated stage.
You can set up triggers in:
- Leads
- Deals
- Estimates
- Invoices
- SPAs
Add a trigger
1. Go to CRM .
2. Select the item type, like Leads or Deals.
3. Open the Automation rules section.
4. Click Create .
5. Choose the stage where you want a trigger to appear.
6. Click the Filter icon.
7. Select Bitrix24 Triggers to show only triggers. They're grouped by the task they solve, like customer communication, paperwork, and more.
8. Click Add next to the trigger. To add multiple triggers at once, hold the Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) key and select the ones you need.
Configure a trigger
After adding a trigger, you'll need to configure it. If you've added multiple triggers, they'll be highlighted in yellow. Configure each trigger individually.
All triggers have standard settings:
- Condition: Set a condition for the trigger to work only for certain items. For example, only for repeat deals.
- Trigger name: Change the default name if you need to set up multiple triggers. This helps quickly find the required trigger on the Sales automation page.

- By default, the trigger updates the stage on behalf of the employee responsible for the CRM item. You can select a different user, and the stage change will be shown under that user's name in the CRM item timeline and history.
- Allow moving back to previous stage: Decide whether you want the trigger to move the item to a previous stage. For example, move a deal from the last stage to the first.
Other settings are unique for each trigger. For example, in the Track field value change trigger, you need to select which fields in the CRM form to monitor for changes.
Once set up, click Save in the settings window, then save changes on the Sales automation page.
Modify or delete a trigger
1. Go to the required CRM section, such as Leads or Deals.
2. Open the Automation rules tab.
3. Choose an action to perform.
Delete (x) : Remove the trigger if it's no longer needed.
Edit : Modify the trigger settings. For example, add a new condition or change the responsible person.
Copy : Duplicate the trigger with its settings. This is useful if you want to use the same trigger at another stage.
Once you've made all changes to the triggers, click Save .
In brief

- Triggers track customer actions and changes in CRM, like email link clicks, incoming calls, invoice payments, and more. When a specific action occurs, the trigger moves a CRM item to its designated stage.
- In CRM, triggers are available in leads, deals, estimates, invoices, and SPAs.
- Triggers are grouped by the tasks they solve: customer communication, paperwork, and more.
- To add a trigger, go to CRM, select the needed item, and open the Automation rules section.

- All triggers come with standard settings, such as the execution conditions, name, responsible for stage change, and option to move to the previous stage. Each trigger also has its own unique settings.

titre: Edit variable and Math operations

We added two new automation rules: Edit variable and Math operations . Use them to automate actions with variables and constants.
Variables and constants in automation rules
Edit variable

Math operations
