Add automation rules and triggers
Submit document for signing

This rule generates a document from a template in the e-Signature section and sends it to the company representative and the client for signing. The CRM item form shows the sending status. The manager can check when the document was sent and which one was delivered.
What is e-Signature
Set up the "Submit document for signing" rule
Example: set up the rule for deals.

Full name of the signatory on behalf of the company . Enter the full name of the employee who signs the document. You can type it manually or insert a constant, variable, or CRM field value. Click Three dots (...) and select a value. Variables and constants in automation rules
Document template . Select a template or add one in the e-Signature section. Create and send an electronic document for signing
Create document
When a CRM item reaches a selected stage, this rule generates a document from a template, such as an invoice, estimate, or contract.
Set up the "Create document" rule
Example: set up the rule for deals.
Template . Select the template used to generate the document.
Wait for PDF conversion to complete . Enable this option to run the next rule only after the document is ready as a PDF.
With signature and stamp . Add the company signature and seal to the document. Add company details
Create public link . Generate a link for the client to view and download the document.
My company and company details . Select the company and define its details.
Document fields . Add extra fields and set their values, such as document title or legal address. Click Add and choose a field.
Modify details
This rule updates existing contact or company details linked to a CRM item.
Set up the "Modify details" rule

Get details values

titre: Stop automation rules at a certain stage
sections: Stop automation rules at a certain stage

In Bitrix24, you can stop automation rules at a certain stage of a CRM item or task. This is useful if you need to interrupt a series of rules set to run later, like in a few hours or days. The changes will only affect the specific item you modify.
To stop automation rules:
1. Open the CRM item or task form.
2. Go to the Automation tab.
3. Click Stop automation rules at the bottom of the desired stage.
This will stop all the postponed rules, such as those planned for the next day.
Read also :
- Copy and move automation rules
- Disable automation rules and workflow actions

titre: RPA in Bitrix24: Automate your routine tasks
sections: RPA in Bitrix24: Automate your routine tasks

RPA (Robotic Process Automation) is a tool that automates routine tasks, such as approving leave requests, business trips, invoices, and contracts, or creating tasks and handling other routine actions.

It’s easier to set up than standard workflows and doesn’t require any technical skills—any employee can create a workflow using ready-made assignment templates. This helps your team work faster and make fewer errors.
The number of processes you can automate with RPA depends on your plan. Bitrix24 pricing page
- Create a workflow in RPA
- Configure stages
- Add an assignment
- Add a workflow item
Create a workflow in RPA
1. Go to the Automation section.
2. Click RPA .
3. Select RPA list .
4. Click New workflow .
Fill out the form:
- Name: Enter a clear workflow name for the RPA list.
- When created, move items to the next stage after created: Disable this option if you need to move items between stages manually.
- Workflow start: Choose which employees can start the workflow.
- Fields to fill in upon start: Add custom fields for the workflow item form. For example, for leave approvals, these could be Name, Start date, End date, and Leave type . Custom fields in RPA
- Access permissions: Choose who can edit the workflow. Access permissions to RPA
- Workflow image: Select a suitable icon.
Save the changes.
Configure stages

Stages show the progress of a workflow from start to finish. For example, in a leave approval workflow, the stages might be: Request → Approved by supervisor → Approved by chief accountant → Leave approved. This helps employees and supervisors see the current status and make decisions faster.
You can add, edit, or delete stages at any time. To do this, open the workflow and click Settings (⚙️) > Stage settings . RPA: Stages and assignments
Add an assignment
An assignment is a task that needs to be completed at a specific stage of a workflow, such as reviewing a document or approving leave. There are four assignment templates:
- Approve or decline: Use this for workflows that require a decision. For example, a manager can approve or decline a business trip request and provide a reason.
- Request information: Use this when you need more details to move a process forward. For example, an accountant might request receipts or supporting documents for an expense report.
- Review information: Use this to confirm that a participant has received a document or notification.
- Move to stage: Use this to move an item to the next stage without changes. For example, an administrative assistant might check a form for completeness and then forward it for manager approval.
You can configure specific assignments for each stage:
1. Click Add assignment .
2. Select an assignment template and configure it.
RPA: Assignments
Click the Automation rules button to:
- View all assignments set up for each stage
- See which automation rules start them
- Add new rules beyond the built-in assignment templates
Automation rules and triggers in Bitrix24
Add a workflow item
An item is a form that moves through the stages of the workflow. For example, in a leave approval workflow, the item represents a request from a specific employee.
1. Click Add .
2. Fill in the item form fields.
3. To edit a field, click Settings (⚙️) next to its name.
4. If needed, select fields from the list or create new ones.
5. Save the changes.
RPA offers two view modes:
- List: Ideal for detailed analysis, sorting, and deleting multiple items at once.
- Kanban: Shows the stage of each item, making it easy to track progress and manage workloads.
In brief

- RPA (Robotic Process Automation) is a tool that automates routine tasks, such as approving leave requests, business trips, invoices, and contracts, or creating tasks and handling other routine actions.
- The number of processes you can automate with RPA depends on your plan.
- To automate a routine task with RPA, you need to create a workflow, configure stages, and add assignments. After that, employees can add items and move them through the stages.
- To create a new workflow, go to Automation > RPA > RPA list.

titre: RPA: Configure fields in Kanban view
sections: RPA: Configure fields in Kanban view
Workflows you create in the RPA section have the Kanban view to easily add and manage assignments. You can set which fields to show when creating new items and in view mode.
Customize quick create form fields
Decide which fields to display when adding a new workflow item. You can only choose custom fields for this form. Custom fields in RPA
1. Click Plus (+) under the first stage.
2. Click Select field .
3. Select Customize quick create form fields .
4. Check the fields you want to appear when adding an item.
5. Click Save .
Next time you add a workflow item, you'll see the updated fields in the form.
Customize view form fields
Select the fields you want to see in the Kanban view. You can display custom fields and system data, such as ID , Created on , or Created by .
1. Click Plus (+) under the first stage.
2. Click Select field .
3. Select Customize view form fields .
4. Check the fields you want to appear in view mode.
5. Click Save .
All forms on the Kanban board will now show the updated fields.

titre: Custom fields in RPA
sections: Custom fields in RPA
Unlike CRM items, RPA has no preset fields. Create custom ones to store the information needed for workflow assignments.

You can use custom fields either when starting a workflow or while it's running. To use them at the start, add the fields when creating the workflow. To use them later, add the fields in the Field settings section.
In this article:
- Types of custom fields in RPA
- Create custom fields in RPA
- Edit or delete custom fields in RPA
Types of custom fields in RPA
There are several types of custom fields in RPA. They are used for storing different types of data. You can choose the type when creating a field.
- String : Enter any information (text, numbers, or dates).
- Integer : Enter whole numbers.
- Number : Enter any number.
- True/False : Select True or False (e.g., whether a meeting is required or not).
- Date/Time : Specify date and time (e.g., meeting date and time).
- Money : Specify amount and currency.
- Link : Enter URLs (e.g., client's website).
- Address : Select an address on the map (e.g., client's address).
- List : Select one or multiple values from a pre-installed set.
- File : Upload files (e.g., contracts or call recordings).
- Bind to employee : Select a company employee.
- Bind To CRM Items : Select a specific CRM item (e.g., lead, deal, contact, company).
- Bind To CRM Dictionaries : Select a value from the statuses and dropdowns in CRM (e.g., deal stage, contact type, company industry).
- Link to information block section : Select a section from the information block (e.g., company department).
- Bind To Information Block Elements : Select a specific element from the information block (e.g., workflow element).
Create custom fields in RPA
Create a field to fill in upon start. When creating or editing a workflow in the RPA section:
1. Click Create field in the Fields to fill in upon start section.
2. Select the field type from the drop-down list.

3. Specify the field name and enable the necessary parameters. They may vary depending on the field type. Required : Users cannot save the assignment until they fill in this field. Multiple : Allow users to enter multiple values in the field.
4. Click Save , and this field will appear when starting the workflow.
Create a field in the field settings. This method is perfect for fields that are not needed at the start and require additional settings.
1. Go to the Automation section.
2. Expand RPA .
3. Select RPA list .
4. Click Actions next to the workflow you need.
5. Select Field settings .
6. Click Create in the top right corner.
Configure the field parameters. They may differ depending on the field type. Consider the List type as an example:
Common settings. These settings are the same for all data types.
- Data type : Choose the type of data stored in the field. Types of custom fields in RPA
- Field ID : It is generated automatically and can be used to set up integrations with external systems.
- Name : It is displayed in the assignment form and the list of fields.
- Sort : Determines the order of the field in the list. Lower numbers place the field higher.
- Multiple : Allows users to enter multiple values in the field.
- Required : Users cannot save the assignment form without filling in this field.
- Show in filter : Enables filtering assignments by this field's value. If disabled, the field won't appear in the filter.
- Searchable : Enables entering the field value in the search bar and finding all assignments with this value.
List values. These settings are available only for fields of the List type. Specify each value on a separate line.
You can also set the default value that automatically appears in the field. Users can leave or replace this value.
All languages. Specify the field name in all languages used by employees.
Additional settings. These settings may vary depending on the field type.
- Control : Affects how the list of values appears in the assignment form.
- List control height : Specify how many list values are displayed in the selection window. To see other values, scroll down the list.
- Use caption when value is empty : Displays a caption if no value is selected from the list.
- Show empty value in required fields : Enable this option to keep the required field empty until you fill it in. Disable it to automatically insert the first value from the list into the field.
Save the changes, and the field will appear in the workflow.
Edit or delete custom fields in RPA
1. Go to the Automation section.
2. Expand RPA .
3. Select RPA list .
4. Click Actions next to the workflow you need.
5. Select Field settings .
6. Click on the field name to open its settings and apply the needed changes.
You can edit any field parameter, except for Data type , Field ID , and Multiple .
To delete a field, click Delete in the bottom right corner.
When you delete a field, all the data bound to it will also be deleted.
In brief
- Create custom fields to store the information required for workflow assignments. You can do this when creating a workflow or later in the Field settings section.
- Choose the field type and set its parameters: required, multiple, etc.
- After creation, you can edit any field parameter, except for Data type , Field ID , and Multiple .
- When you delete a field, all the data bound to it will also be deleted.

titre: RPA: Stages and assignments
sections: RPA: Stages and assignments

Every workflow in the RPA section has a Kanban view, and each item on it should go from the first to the last stage to complete the workflow. This article explains how to customize stages and create assignments for employees at each of them.
Stages in Kanban
The stages in the workflow work in the same way as the stages in CRM. To complete the workflow, move an item from the first stage to the last.
To configure stages, click the gear (⚙️) in Kanban view and select Stage settings .
By default, there are several stages. Use them or create new ones.
- Initial stage: Starts the workflow. You can rename it but not delete it.
- Additional stages: Used for tasks, such as reviewing documents or approving requests. You can create more stages by clicking + Add stage .
- Final stages: Indicate successful or failed workflow completion. The final successful stage can't be deleted.
Use these action icons to edit or delete stages:
Pencil: Rename the stage. Fill: Change the stage color. Circle back: Reset stage settings to default. Cross: Remove the stage.
Once done, save the changes.
To configure a specific stage rather than the whole Kanban, hover the mouse over it, click on the pencil, and select the desired action.
Assignments
Assignments are tasks employees must complete at specific stages in a workflow, like reviewing information or approving a leave request.
There are four assignment types:
- Approve or decline
- Request information
- Review information
- Move to stage
To create an assignment:
1. Click Add assignment under the stage name.
2. Select the template, for example, Approve or decline .
3. Configure settings in the General and Show fields tabs.
General tab
Assignment : Enter the name and description of the assignment for the responsible person.
Responsible persons : Select who will perform the assignment. It can be a specific employee, several in a certain order, or anyone from the list. Decide how to distribute the assignments:
1. User queue . Add employees in the Responsible persons field. Several options are available:
- Any of listed: Anyone from the selected employees can complete the task.
- Any [number of employees]: Specify how many users are needed to complete the task.
- All in queue: All selected users must complete the task one after another.
- All: All selected users must complete the task without a specific order.
2. Employee supervisors . Responsible users are chosen automatically based on the company structure. The approval follows the chain of supervisors up to the top or to the Final approver .
Extra options:

Final approver : Available if you pick Employee supervisors as responsible persons. Select users who will have the final say. If at least one final approver is in the chain, the approval stops after their decision.
Skip absent users : Decide whether the system should consider the absence chart data when assigning a responsible person. Absence chart
Backup users : Specify users who will participate in approval if all users at the current stage are not available.
Buttons : Choose the name and color of the buttons and the stage to move the item to after the responsible employee completes the task.
Show fields tab
Select the fields the responsible employee will see in the item form.
Save the settings. When you add a new item, the system will create a task and assign it to the appropriate employee based on these settings.
In brief
- Use the Kanban view to manage workflows by moving items from the first to the last stage.
- Customize initial, additional, and final stages using action icons.
- Create assignments at each stage and decide whether to assign them manually to user queues or automatically to employee supervisors.
- Configure assignment settings and select visible fields for responsible employees.

titre: Access permissions to RPA
sections: Access permissions to RPA
Set up RPA access permissions to prevent data loss and accidental changes to RPA workflows.
Workflows and stages
Create workflows. Any user can create new workflows in RPA. Create a workflow in RPA

titre: Automated solutions: automate work of company departments
sections: Automated solutions: automate work of company departments
Smart Process Automation (SPA) lets you build custom workflows. You can create CRM entities with custom fields, kanban stages, permissions, and more. Smart Process Automation in CRM
You can also use SPA outside of CRM to automate work for any team, such as HR or Accounting. Create a dedicated workspace and set up the tools and settings you need.
To access SPAs outside CRM, open the Automated solutions section.
How it works
Automated solutions live in a separate section. They are not tied to CRM.
Each solution can include one or more SPAs. Every SPA has its own:
- Forms
- Pipelines
- Kanban stages
- Automation rules

What you can do
Create an automated solution for any department. Set permissions so only the right employees can access it.
For example, HR can manage:
- Recruiting
- Hiring
- Onboarding
- Offboarding
You can also connect solutions with automation rules. For example, HR can send requests to IT automatically.
Create an automated solution
Follow these steps:
1. Create a solution
Click Create above the list. Enter a name and save.
2. Add or link an SPA
Open the Smart Process Automation tab in the solution settings. Create a new SPA or move an existing one from CRM or another solution. Create SPA for automated solutions
3. Set up forms and kanban stages
Add fields to the SPA form. For example, create a candidate form for HR.
Create kanban stages and move items through them as work progresses. Configure automated solutions
4. Set permissions

- Automated solutions are a separate area for SPA. Use them to automate work for any department.
- Each solution includes SPAs with forms, pipelines, stages, and rules.
- Only employees with permission can access this section from the main menu.

titre: Create an automated solution with SPA
sections: Create an automated solution with SPA
Automated solutions let you use SPAs outside of CRM. This is useful when a team does not work in CRM but still needs structured workflows. Automated solutions: automate the work of any department
Before you start
- Only admins and users with permission to edit CRM settings can create automated solutions.
- You can create automated solutions and SPAs only in the web version.
- You can work with SPA items in both the web version and the mobile app. Automated solutions in Bitrix24 mobile app
Create an automated solution
1. Go to Automation > Automated solutions .
2. Click Create .
3. Open the Settings tab.
4. Enter a name.
5. Click Save .
Create and link an SPA
Each automated solution can include one or more SPAs. Each SPA can belong to only one solution.
To create a new SPA:
1. Open the SPA tab.
2. Click Create .
3. Choose a preset:
1. Essentials only
2. All options selected
3. Empty SPA
You can customize any preset.
We’ll use the Empty SPA preset to walk through these sections:
- SPA components
- SPA form layout
- CRM bindings
- Bindings to other tools
SPA components
Choose which tools to use. These tools work the same way as in CRM.
Enter name : Displays in lists and forms.
Use custom pipelines and sales funnels in SPA : Create multiple pipelines and move items between them. Sales pipelines Sales tunnels
Use custom stages and kanban in SPA : Manage items visually on a board. Kanban view in CRM
Use automation rules and triggers in SPA : Automate tasks, notifications, and assignments. Create automation rules and triggers
Use workflow designer in SPA : Run workflows when items are created or updated. "Autorun: when added" option in workflow templates
Make new pipelines public : Make pipelines visible to all users or restrict access. Access Permissions in CRM
SPA form layout
Select the fields you need:
- Company details : Your company information. Use these details in documents.
- Source : Shows how the customer found your company.
- Customer : Use this if the SPA links to CRM contacts or companies.
- Start date , End date : The creation date and planned end date. The system sets the end date to 7 days after creation.
- Observers : Users who can view the item and start a chat for discussion. Standard fields in CRM
Additional options
Enable the features you need:
- Bind to catalog products . Add products to the form. Changes in work with products in leads and deals
- Use Recycle Bin . Move deleted items to the CRM Recycle Bin instead of deleting them permanently. CRM Recycle Bin
- Use counters . Track and plan pending activities. How counters work in CRM
CRM bindings
Use this section to define how the SPA connects to CRM entities.
Bind to this SPA : Enable this option to link items from another process. Then select the items you want to connect.
Add linked items list to details form : Adds a tab with this SPA to the linked entity form.
Link this SPA to other CRM entities : Enable this option to connect the SPA to other CRM items, such as leads or deals. Then select the required items.
Add linked items list to details form : Adds a tab with the linked items to the SPA form.
Bind to other tools
You can connect the SPA to:
- CRM items
- Calendar events
- Tasks and task templates
For example, when you create a calendar event, you can link it to a specific SPA item.
Save and continue
Click Save after you finish setup.
The automated solution is created. You can open it from the main menu.
Customize each SPA to match your workflow:
- Adjust the item form.
- Set up kanban stages.
- Configure other features.
Configure automated solutions
To edit an automated solution:
1. Find the solution in the list.
2. Open the menu (☰).
3. Click Edit .
In brief
- Create automated solutions in Automation > Automated solutions > Automated solutions .
- Add an SPA to the solution. You can create a new one or migrate an existing one from CRM or another solution.
- Each solution can include multiple SPAs.
- Each SPA can belong to only one automated solution.
- Choose which tools to use in the SPA, such as pipelines, kanban, and automation. These tools work the same way as in CRM.
- Select the system fields for the form and enable additional options like counters.
- Link the SPA to CRM items, calendar events, tasks, and task templates.

titre: Configure automated solutions
sections: Configure automated solutions
After you create a Smart Process Automation (SPA) and add it to your automated solution, configure it based on your workflow. If your solution includes multiple SPAs, configure each one separately.
This article covers how to set up:
- SPA item form
- Kanban and List views
- SPA access permissions
Example: a recruitment SPA that tracks candidates from application to hiring. It stores candidate data, manages vacancies, and uses automation to generate job offers and assign HR tasks.
Configure the SPA item form
Set up the item form so employees can quickly find and enter information. In this example, the form includes candidate details and the related vacancy.
To create or edit fields:
1. Open the Kanban or List view.
2. Click the gear icon (⚙️).
3. Select Field settings .
On this page, you can:
- View all custom fields in the SPA
- Create new fields
- Edit existing fields
Each SPA has its own fields. If you use multiple SPAs, create fields for each one separately.
To create a field:
1. Choose a field type.
2. Enter a name.
3. Set additional options.
Custom fields of invoices and smart processes
To add fields to the item form:
1. Open any item form.
2. Click Select field .
3. Select the fields you want to display.
4. Click Select to save.
CRM item form settings
Arrange fields in a logical order. Group related fields into sections to improve readability.
Example: Create separate sections for candidate details and job information.
Configure the Kanban and List views
You can work with SPA items in two views: Kanban and List . Switch between tabs in the interface to configure each view.
Create stages Set up custom stages to define how items move through the process. Stages help you track progress and workload.
Set up the automation Add automation rules and triggers to stages to create tasks, send notifications, copy items to another SPA, and more.
Create automation rules and triggers
Configure the view form Choose which fields to show in the Kanban view by editing the view form. This helps you focus on key information. Each employee can customize this view individually.
1. Click the gear icon (⚙️) in the top right.
2. Open Kanban settings .
3. Select Configure view form fields .
4. Choose the fields to display.
5. Save changes.
Configure the quick create form Control which fields appear when creating a new item in Kanban.
1. Click the gear icon (⚙️).
2. Open Kanban settings .
3. Select Configure create form fields .
4. Choose the required fields.
5. Save changes.
Choose which columns to display in the List view and adjust the layout.
1. Click the gear icon (⚙️) in the top left corner.
2. Select the fields you want to show.
3. Click Apply .
To reorder columns, drag a column header to a new position.
To export items:
1. Click the gear icon (⚙️) in the top right corner.
2. Select CSV Export or Microsoft Excel Export .
Configure SPA access permissions
Control who can access and manage the SPA.
1. Go to CRM > Settings > Access permissions > CRM .
2. Select a role.
3. Define the actions available for that role.
If your SPA uses pipelines or funnels, set permissions for them in the pipeline settings.
In brief
- After you add an SPA to your automated solution, configure it to match your workflow. Configure each SPA separately if you use more than one.
- Set up the item form with clear fields and sections so users can enter and find information easily.
- Use Kanban stages to manage item progress. Configure view and quick create forms for better usability.
- Add automation rules to streamline tasks and communication.
- Set access permissions in CRM to control who can view and manage the SPA.

titre: Access permissions for automated solutions
sections: Access permissions for automated solutions

Automated solutions are a separate section for SPA, designed to automate the work of any department of your company. Bitrix24 now lets you manage access permissions specifically for this section. Create SPA for automated solutions
Create roles with different permissions for departments and employees. For example, the HR department might have full access to the Hiring automated solution, while other users may only view items.

By default, only Bitrix24 administrators can configure access permissions and assign them to other users. You can choose to set permissions for all SPAs linked to an automation solution or just for specific ones.
You can configure access permissions for:
- Automated solutions
- All SPAs within an automated solution
- Each SPA individually
To set access permissions for automated solutions:
1. Go to Automation .
2. Click Automated solutions .
3. Select an automated solution from the list.
4. Open any linked SPA.
5. Go to the Access permissions section.
6. Select Automated solutions and choose who can create and configure them.
Edit automated solutions : Users can create automated solutions and link SPAs to them. Edit settings : Users can configure access permissions to automated solutions.
To set access permissions for all SPAs linked to an automation solution:
1. Go to Automation .
2. Click Automated solutions .
3. Select an automated solution from the list.
4. Open any linked SPA.
5. Go to the Access permissions section. A list of all SPAs and pipelines will appear.
To set access permissions for a specific SPA:
1. Go to Automation .
2. Click Automated solutions .
3. Select an automated solution from the list.
4. Open the required SPA linked to the automated solution.
5. Select a pipeline to configure access. If there are multiple pipelines in the SPA, configure permissions for each one separately.
6. Click the Settings (⚙️) icon.
7. Select Access permissions .
Configure roles
A role is a set of access permissions given to a user. You can create and customize the roles you need.
Create or clone roles and decide whether to show them in the table. Click the three dots (...) next to Roles and select an action.
Create a role . Select Add new role and give it a name.
Clone a role . This is handy if you need a new role with minor changes.
1. Click Clone role .
2. Select the role you want to clone.
3. All permission settings will be copied to the new role.

Show or hide roles . Keep only the necessary roles visible and hide the others. This is useful for comparing or editing multiple roles. Click Show/hide roles and check the ones you need from the list.
Set up a role . Click the three dots (...) next to the role name and select an action:
- Select all permissions: Gives full access to SPAs for the selected role.
- Unselect all permissions: Denies access to all SPAs.
- Rename: Change the role name.
- Clone: Create a copy of the selected role.
- Delete: Remove the role and all its settings.
Set up permissions
For each role, you can configure access permissions for actions with SPA items. For example, allow users to view all items, but to edit only their own.
Actions with SPA items.
- Read: Allows users to view SPA items.
- Add: Allows users to create SPA items. They won't see the items after creating them unless they have the Read permission.
- Edit: Allows users to modify SPA items.
- Delete: Allows users to delete SPA items.
- Export: Allows users to download SPA items from Bitrix24. Export CRM data
- Import: Allows users to upload SPA items to Bitrix24. Import to Bitrix24 CRM

- Allow custom view form: Allows users to customize the SPA item form. Without this permission, they can only use the item form layout configured by an administrator. CRM item form features and settings
- Automation rules: Allows users to set up, edit, or view automation rules. This permission will appear if automation rules are enabled in the SPA settings. Automation rules in CRM
- Amount on kanban stages: Hides or shows the total amount at the kanban stages. This permission will appear if the kanban is enabled in the SPA settings.
- Move to stage: Specify whether users can move SPA items to any stage or only specific ones.

- History: View records in History for SPAs linked to the automated solution. If this permission is enabled, the History section appears in the automated solution menu, and the History tab appears in the item form. If this permission is disabled, both are hidden.
- User can edit preferences: Gives users full access to change access permissions for automated solutions.
Access levels . Select an access level for each action with SPA items:
- Access: Gives full access or denies access to the selected action, like modifying all SPA items.
- User's items: Allows users to access the items where they are responsible.
- User department's items: Allows users to access the items of their department's employees.
- User dept. subdepartment's items: Allows users to access the items of employees in all subdepartments of their department.
- All items marked as "Available to everyone": Includes all previous permissions and access to the items with the Available to everyone option enabled.
- All items: Allows users to access all SPA items.

- Inherit: Can only be configured for stages. SPA item stages inherit the permissions set for the item itself. For example, if you choose All items to read items, users with this role will view all items at all stages. If needed, you can set up separate permissions for each stage.
Assign employees to roles

Click the Plus (+) icon under the role name and choose a user, department, or workgroup to assign it to. For example, allow supervisors to edit and delete SPA items while letting other employees only view them.

If a user has multiple roles with different access levels, the role with more permissions will apply. For example, if one role restricts viewing SPA items while another allows it, employees will be able to view these items.

To check overlapping access permissions, choose an employee from the field next to the search bar. A slider will show their assigned roles. This helps you review their permissions and adjust settings if needed.
Use the search
To quickly set up permissions for a specific item or find the desired action, use the search bar.
SPA items . Enter the SPA item or pipeline name. All permissions you can set up for them will appear.
SPA item stages . To set up permissions for a specific stage, enter its name. For example, you can find all the items having the In progress stage.
Actions with SPA items . Use the search to display a specific permission like Read for all SPA items.
In brief
- Bitrix24 now lets you manage access permissions specifically for automated solutions. Decide who can add, edit, and delete SPA items.
- You can create or clone roles and choose whether to show them in the table.
- A new role is created without any default permissions, allowing you to customize it as needed.
- For each role, you can configure access permissions for actions with SPA items. For example, allow a user to view all SPA items, but change only their own.

- If a user has multiple roles with different access levels, the role with more permissions will apply. For example, if one role restricts viewing SPA items while another allows it, employees will be able to view these items.

titre: Start workflows in Feed
sections: Start workflows in Feed
Workflows are sets of actions that help you manage daily tasks. Use them to approve invoices, assign tasks to employees, or process leave requests.
You can start workflows from the Feed or from the Automation section.
The updated start page shows key details for each workflow:
- Name . Use the name to find a workflow. Click the question mark to view its description.
- Action . Shows how quickly the workflow is usually completed.
- Last run . Start a workflow directly from the list.

- In progress . Shows active workflows. Use it to review workload and execution time. Click the number next to a workflow to see who started it and who is working on it. The list shows the last 20 workflows.
- Last updated by . Shows who last edited the workflow template.
Pin frequently used workflows to the top of the list. Select a workflow and click Start .
A page opens with tips for completing the workflow and the average completion time.
Click Next , fill in the required fields, and click Start .
Start a workflow with constants
Workflows can include constants. These are fixed values that rarely change.
For example, a Leave Approval workflow may include constants such as Final approver and Processor. Set these values in the workflow template parameters. Business processes templates parameters
You cannot start a workflow with constants until an administrator sets these values.
If a user without admin permissions tries to start such a workflow, they will see this message: "Workflow can be started after the administrator has specified the constants."
Contact your Bitrix24 administrator to add the required constant values.
In brief
- Workflows help you manage daily tasks such as approvals, assignments, and leave requests.
- The updated interface makes it easier to start and manage workflows. It also shows recommendations and average completion time.
- Workflows with constants require an administrator to configure them before you can start the process.

titre: Configure workflows in Feed
sections: Configure workflows in Feed
In Bitrix24, you can run workflows directly from the Feed. For example, you can request leave or submit an expense report. You can also create new workflows or edit existing ones.
Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows in Feed . By default, you will see five workflows:
- Leave Approval
- Business Trip
- General Requests
- Purchase Request
- Expense Report
1. Create a workflow form
Click Create new and enter the workflow details.
- Settings : Add basic info and set the sort order. Turn on auto-lock to prevent multiple users from editing at the same time.
- Titles : Rename elements and sections. For example, change Add element to Add leave request .
- Access : Set permissions for employees who will use the workflow.
2. Add workflow fields
Each workflow includes fields that users must complete before starting it.
Open the workflow form and go to Settings (⚙️) > Customize workflow fields . Click Add field and configure it.
- Select a field type and define its settings. For example, the Money field requires an amount and currency.
- Enable Show in new item form and Show in item edit form so users can fill in the field.
- Use Read-only to prevent editing if needed.
- Enable Show field when creating a list item link if required.
3. Configure the workflow
Open the workflow form and go to Settings (⚙️) > Configure workflows . Add a business process:
- Status-driven : A continuous process with different statuses and permissions (for example, document approval).
- Sequential : A simple step-by-step process (for example, leave approval).
Edit a workflow
Open the workflow form and click Settings (⚙️) . Choose an option:
- Configure workflow preferences : Update workflow settings.
- Configure fields : Edit fields users fill out.
- Configure workflows : Change the process template.
To allow users to run the workflow from the Feed, enable Show in Feed .
Check the Show in Feed box so that employees can start the workflow in Feed. How to start a workflow
Delete a workflow
1. Open the workflow form.
2. Go to Settings (⚙️) > Configure workflow .
3. Click Settings (⚙️) > Delete workflow .
In brief
- You can run workflows directly from the Feed.
- Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows in Feed to manage them.
- To create a workflow, set up a form, add fields, and configure the process.
- You can edit or delete workflows at any time.

titre: Workflows: group actions in Bitrix24 mobile app
sections: Workflows: group actions in Bitrix24 mobile app
You can complete tasks across multiple workflows at once in the Bitrix24 mobile app. You no longer need to approve each workflow separately.
Select workflows
Open the Workflows section and select items from the list. To select all workflows, tap the dots icon and choose Select all .
Workflows with one task type . If you select the workflows to be approved, you can complete tasks in all workflows at once. For example, you can approve all business trips.
Workflows with the same task type
If all selected workflows have the same task, you can complete the action for all of them at once. Example: approve all business trips in one step.
Workflows with different task types
Tap Start . The first workflow opens. Review the details and complete the task.
After you complete a task, the app shows other workflows with the same task type. Choose how to proceed:
- Apply to all — complete the task in all workflows at once.
- Open one by one — complete each workflow separately.
- Show similar workflows — open a list of similar workflows. Select the ones you need and complete tasks in bulk.
Auto-fill field values
If a workflow requires you to enter data in a field, the value can be reused in other similar workflows.
Enter the value, approve the workflow, and apply the action to other workflows. If you need different values, open each workflow and fill in the fields individually.
In brief:
- Complete tasks across multiple workflows at once in the mobile app.
- Open Workflows and select items from the list. Use Select all to choose everything.
- For workflows with the same task type, complete all tasks in one action.
- For different task types, choose bulk action or process workflows one by one.
- Field values can be auto-filled across similar workflows.

titre: Workflows: new interface and features
sections: Workflows: new interface and features

Workflows automate routine tasks. Use them to approve documents, communicate with customers, and manage sales. For example, you can set up automatic invoice approval, send order status updates, or create tasks for employees.
Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows .
Fields for controlling workflows
The list shows key details for each workflow: last activity date, approvers, status, and execution time.
Activity . Shows the date and time of the last update. It also includes two types of counters:
- Red — complete an assignment
- Green — read a comment
Example: an employee starts a Business trip workflow and leaves a comment. The responsible person sees both counters: red and green.
The Workflow section shows the total number of both counters.
Participants . Shows all participants and the total time they spent.
Execution time for each step is rounded using standard rules. Only one time unit is shown: seconds, minutes, hours, days, or months.
Examples:
- The process lasted 11 minutes and 15 seconds — the column shows 11 minutes.
- The process lasted 57 seconds— this is one unit of time, so the column shows 57 seconds.
Status . Shows action buttons to continue the workflow. If the workflow is denied, postponed, or completed, the status appears here.
Time . Shows the total workflow time and access to the journal.
Only one time unit is shown: seconds, minutes, hours, days, or months. The time is rounded upwards only. For example, the process lasted one hour and one minute — the column shows two hours.
The journal logs all actions, participants, and performance.
Efficiency indicators:
- No statistics — no similar workflows have been completed yet
- Good — completed faster than average
- Requires attention — matches the average or exceeds it by up to three days
- Too slow — exceeds the average by more than four days
The average time becomes more accurate as more workflows are completed. Bitrix24 calculates this automatically across the company.
The journal calculates execution time from start to finish and rounds it down. This value may differ from the total time shown in the workflow list.
Complete assignments in a workflow
Assignments are tasks inside a workflow. They can be sequential or parallel.
Example: when organizing an event, you first approve the concept and then the program. At the same time, tasks like choosing a venue and approving marketing materials can run in parallel.
Sequential assignments . Complete these in order from the workflow form:
1. Open the workflow.
2. Review the assignment.
3. Complete it.
4. Move to the next step.
Parallel assignments . You can complete these from the workflow form or the journal.
To start a specific assignment:
1. Open the journal.
2. Select the assignment.
3. Click Start .
If order does not matter, complete them from the workflow form like sequential tasks.
In brief
- Workflows automate routine tasks such as approvals, communication, and sales processes.
- The workflow list shows key details: last activity, approvers, status, and execution time.
- Bitrix24 calculates the average execution time automatically across all workflows.
- Complete assignments in the workflow form. To start a specific parallel task, open the journal, select it, and click Start .

titre: Delete workflows in Feed
sections: Delete workflows in Feed
Each workflow in Feed appears as a form where you configure actions and templates. These forms include all workflows that employees can run in Feed.
This article is for administrators and employees with full access based on permission settings.
For more details about workflows in other tools, see:
- Business processes on Bitrix24 Drive
- Example of using workflows in CRM
To manage workflows in Feed, go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows in Feed . From here, you can delete workflows you no longer need.
Example: Delete the Leave Request workflow
1. Open the workflow form.
2. Click Settings (⚙️) .
3. Select Change workflow preferences .
4. Click Settings (⚙️) again.
5. Select Delete workflow .
6. Click Yes, delete to confirm.
Manually created workflows are deleted permanently. Standard workflows can be restored.
Restore a standard workflow
Bitrix24 includes five standard workflow templates:
- Leave Approval
- Business Trip
- General Requests
- Purchase Request
- Expense Report
If you delete one of these workflows, you can restore it:
1. Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows in Feed .
2. Click Workflow directory .
3. Select the workflow you want to restore.
4. Click Install .
After you restore a workflow, it appears in the list again. Only the preset template is restored. Previously run workflows based on that template are not restored.
In brief
- Only administrators and employees with full access can delete workflows.
- To delete a workflow, go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows in Feed . Open the workflow form and click Settings (⚙️) > Configure workflow parameters > Settings (⚙️) > Delete workflow .
- You can restore only standard workflows with preset templates. Previously run workflows cannot be restored.

titre: Optimize workflow execution time
sections: Optimize workflow execution time
Start and manage workflows in the Bitrix24 mobile app. Check how long approvals take and reduce delays.
This article explains how time indicators work and how to optimize your workflows.
Start a workflow
1. Open the mobile app.
2. Go to Menu .
3. Open the Workflows tab.
4. Tap the Plus (+) icon.
You will see a list of available workflows.
5. Select a workflow and tap Continue .
Example: Leave approval
1. Read the instructions and tap Continue .
2. Fill in the required fields.
3. Tap Start .
Your request will appear in the Workflows tab. You can track its progress there.
Reduce workflow execution time
If a workflow takes too long, review its structure and steps.
Common issues to check:
- No backup during absence . If someone is unavailable or overloaded, tasks can stall. Reassign tasks or involve additional team members.
- Unclear starting point . If users don’t know what to do first, the workflow slows down. Add clear instructions to each field.
- Delayed approvals . Approvers may miss requests. Add reminder notifications to keep things moving.
Use the Workflow Designer to update templates and automate task assignments.
Edit a workflow
To review and edit a certain workflow,
1. Go to Automation .
2. Open the Workflows tab.
3. Select Workflows in Feed .
4. Choose a workflow.
5. Click the gear icon ( ⚙️ ).
6. Select Configure workflows .
7. Open the required workflow template.
The Workflow Designer will open. Update the workflow settings as needed.
All workflow setup consultations and support are provided exclusively by Bitrix24 partners .
In brief
- Workflows are available in the mobile app.
- Check execution time to understand approval delays.
- Use the Workflow Designer to reduce approval time.

titre: Workflow events in CRM item form
sections: Workflow events in CRM item form

CRM and SPA item forms have a timeline on the right side. This is where you can plan activities with clients, leave comments for colleagues, track stage changes, and more. CRM item form features and settings
Workflow events now appear in the timeline too. Complete assignments, view comments, and track workflow statuses directly in the CRM item form.
In this article:
- What workflow events appear in the timeline
- Complete assignments in the CRM item form
- Complete activities with assignments
- Delegate workflow assignments
- View comments in the workflow form
- View workflow results
- Workflow statuses and counters in Kanban
What events appear in the timeline
The timeline displays system workflow records and actions requiring the responsible person's attention.
Actions for the responsible person : These are assignments the responsible person must complete. They include approving documents, viewing comments, or checking workflow results.
Activities for these actions are automatically created in CRM and shown on a yellow background under Things to do .
System actions : These don't require the responsible person's involvement. System records show when and what actions happened to a specific CRM item.
These actions appear on a white background in the timeline.
A workflow assignment won't appear in the timeline if:
- An employee who isn't responsible for the item works on it.
- The Show assignment description only to responsible persons option is enabled in the activity settings.
Complete assignments in the CRM item form

When an employee needs to complete a workflow assignment, an activity is automatically added to the CRM item form. It includes the workflow and assignment names, status, deadline, and other details. Open the workflow form in the timeline to complete your assignment.
Assignments without a deadline . If no deadline is set, the responsible person can start working on the assignment at any time.
Click Start or Open to access the assignment, review the content, and then complete it.
Assignments with a deadline . If a deadline is set in the assignment settings, the timeline shows the due date and time.

When less than an hour remains, a red counter appears in CRM. You can set additional reminders, like one day or 30 minutes before the deadline. This will help ensure you don't miss the assignment and complete it on time. Counters in CRM
Sequential assignments . If there are several assignments in sequence, the next one appears in the timeline after completing the first.
Parallel assignments . If assignments are parallel, they both appear in the timeline at once. Select and complete one, then move to the next.
Complete activities with assignments
By default, after completing an assignment, you need to close the related activity manually in the CRM item form. Decide whether to do it immediately or later.
To complete an activity, check the box.
If there are other workflow assignments, you can keep the activity in the timeline to monitor the process. Close it when the workflow is completed.
To automatically complete activities, disable the User has to manually complete activity with assignments option in Bitrix24 settings. Bitrix24 Settings
Delegate workflow assignments
You can delegate an assignment to another employee from the timeline of a CRM item form. For example, you may need this if the responsible person is on leave or busy with other tasks.
Remember to enable this option in the activity settings. If enabled, the responsible person, their supervisor, and Bitrix24 administrators can delegate assignments.
To delegate an assignment:
1. Open the workflow form.
2. Click Delegate .
3. Select an employee from the list.
To find assignments for another employee, select them in the Responsible person filter field.
View comments in the workflow form
When a colleague leaves a new comment on a workflow assignment, an activity is created in the CRM item form. This ensures the responsible person doesn't miss important discussions.
In the timeline, you can open the assignment, view comments, and reply.
If you're waiting for a response from colleagues, avoid completing the activity. This prevents new ones from being added for each comment. Once the discussion ends, check the box.
To complete activities automatically after reading the comments, disable the User has to manually complete activity with comments option in Bitrix24 settings.
View workflow results

When a workflow is completed, an activity with its result is added to the timeline. This happens only if you started or participated in the workflow. For example, you can receive a generated document as a result.
Track workflow results to use them when working with clients. If you don't need it anymore, mark the activity as complete.
If you don't start or participate in a workflow, the CRM item form will only show a system record that the workflow is completed.
Workflow statuses and counters in Kanban
The Kanban view in CRM shows workflow statuses for different items:
- Pending: The responsible person hasn't completed the assignment yet.
- Comments added: New comments in the workflow form need attention.
- Completed: The workflow is completed.
CRM counters help the responsible person not to miss assignments and new comments:
- Red counter: Less than an hour remains before the assignment deadline.
- Green counter: A new comment has appeared in the workflow form.
In brief
- Workflow events appear in the timeline. These are system records and actions requiring the responsible person's attention.
- Complete assignments, view comments, and track workflow statuses directly in the CRM item form.
- To see workflow events, enable the Show workflow events in the timeline option in the template parameters.

- When a responsible person needs to complete a workflow assignment, an activity is automatically added to the CRM item form. It includes the workflow and assignment names, status, deadline, and other details.

- By default, after completing an assignment, you need to close the related activity manually in the CRM item form. To auto complete activities, disable the User has to manually complete activity with assignments option in Bitrix24 settings.
- You can delegate an assignment to another employee from the timeline of a CRM item form.
- When a colleague leaves a new comment on a workflow assignment, an activity is created in the CRM item form. This ensures the responsible person doesn't miss important discussions.
- The Kanban view in CRM shows workflow statuses for different items: pending, comments added, and completed.

titre: Set a workflow result
sections: Set a workflow result
In Bitrix24, you can save the result of a completed workflow for later use. For example, a contract approval workflow may generate a document to download and share with a client.
You can set a workflow result in two ways:
- Automatically – the system uses the result of the last supported activity in the workflow.
- Manually – you choose what result to display in the workflow template settings.
Set the workflow result automatically
When you use automatic mode, Bitrix24 checks all activities in the workflow template. The result is taken from the last supported activity in this list:
- Create new contact – link to the contact form
- Create new lead – link to the lead form
- Create new company – link to the company form
- Create new deal – link to the deal form
- Create CRM item – link to the CRM item
- Create SPA – link to the SPA item
- Add list item – link to the list item
- Create task – link to the task
- New element – link to the created element
- Read element – document to view or download
- Approve element – document to view or download
If the last activity in the template is not supported, the system checks earlier steps. If none of these activities are found, the result shows the employee who started the workflow.
Set the workflow result manually
Use the Set workflow result activity to define what users see. For example, you can show a created CRM item or an approval document.
To set it up:
1. Open the workflow template.
2. Click the arrow above the End block.
3. Go to Other .
4. Select Set workflow result .
5. Open the activity settings and configure the parameters.
Configure parameters
Workflow result : Choose what to show as the result:
User : Displays a specific employee. Example: show the employee approved for a business trip.
Click the three dots (...) to select a role, variable, or constant.
Item, field, or file : Select a value from the list:
- Element fields: Use a field value from the workflow form or CRM. Example: show the Order Number field.
- Extra results: Select results from activities that create items or elements. Example: choose the item created by the Create CRM item activity.
Make result visible to: Choose who can see the result:
- Workflow creator: The user who started the workflow, their supervisor, and administrators.
- All workflow participants: Everyone involved in the workflow.
- Other employees: Select specific users.
View the workflow result
The workflow result appears in the list of completed workflows and in the CRM item form.
If the result is set automatically, only users with access to the related item or element will see it. For example, if the result is a deal, only users with permission to view deals will see it.
If you set the result using the Set workflow result activity, only the users defined in the activity settings will see it.
In the workflow list
1. Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows .
2. Filter workflows by Completed status.
3. Check the result in the Status column.
If you don't see this column:
1. Open list view settings (⚙️).
2. Select the Status field.
3. Click Apply .
In the CRM item form
Open the CRM item where the workflow has completed. The result appears in the timeline. Workflow events in CRM item form
In brief
- In Bitrix24, you can view results of completed workflows and use them later.
- There are two ways to set a workflow result: automatic or manual.

- In automatic mode, the system checks all activities in the template and uses the last supported one. Only activities related to creating CRM items, tasks, or approving and reviewing elements are included.
- Use the Set workflow result activity to choose what to display, such as an item, field, file, or user.
- The result appears in the list of completed workflows and in the CRM item form.

titre: Configure workflow template parameters in CRM
sections: Configure workflow template parameters in CRM
A workflow template is a pre-configured set of actions to quickly start a workflow. To use a template, fill out its parameters.
1. Go to the Automation section.
2. Click Workflows .
3. Select Workflows in CRM .
4. Select CRM item to create a workflow template for. You can configure workflows for all CRM items and SPAs listed.
5. Click Add Template to create a new workflow template. Select Templates to edit an existing one.
6. Open the Template Parameters tab.
Specify basic information
On the General tab, complete the following fields:
Title : Enter the name to display in the list of templates.
Description : Specify the workflow's purpose to help employees choose the right workflow from the list.
Autorun : Choose how to start the workflow:
- When added: Starts automatically when a user creates a CRM item.
- When changed: Starts automatically when a user modifies a CRM item.
To start the workflow manually, disable the Autorun option.

Don't show in manual start menu : If disabled, the template is shown in the workflow list inside CRM items. If enabled, only the template creator and users with permission to edit CRM settings can view and use the template.
Sort weight : Specify the template's position on the list. Lower numbers appear higher.
Enable event logging for 7 days : Enable this option to log workflow events in workflow log. This helps test the workflow to ensure there are no errors. Workflow test log
Show workflow events in the timeline : CRM item form will display workflow events: new assignments, comments, results, etc. Workflow events in CRM item form
Once you provide the basic details, click Save .
Add parameters, variables, and constants

Parameters : Data that can't be changed after a workflow starts. These values are defined by a user before running a workflow. For example, in the Estimate Approval workflow, this could be the client name or estimate validity period.
Variables : Temporary values that can be changed after a workflow starts. For example, in the Estimate Approval workflow, this could be the total amount or responsible sales person.

Constants : Fixed values that can't be changed after a workflow starts. This could be an interest rate, date, employee role, etc. For example, create the Chief Accountant constant and select an employee with this position.
On the Parameters , Variables , and Constants tabs, click Add and fill out the fields. They are the same on each tab.
ID : Assign a unique code or number to each parameter, variable, and constant. Enter a custom value or leave the default one. This prevents duplicates and makes it easy to find and change values.
Name and Description : Specify these for a parameter, variable, or constant. For example, ask an employee to specify the estimate validity period or client name.

Type : Select the needed value type from the list, like string, number, date, etc. Depending on the type, set additional parameters. For example, to create the Chief Accountant constant, select the Bind to user type and choose an employee.
Required : Users can't start the workflow if they don't specify a value.
Multiple : Users can specify multiple values.

Default Value : Set this manually or add it using the Insert Value form. The field will be filled in automatically, but users can edit it. For example, for the Money variable, enter the estimate amount in USD. Insert Value Form
Click OK and Save .
Configure display in sales pipelines
When setting up a workflow for deals or SPAs, choose which sales pipelines to display it in.
Check the desired sales pipelines from the list. By default, employees won't see this template in other pipelines. Sales pipelines
In brief
- A workflow template is a pre-configured set of actions to quickly start a workflow. To use a template, fill out its parameters.
- Go to Automation > Workflows > Workflows in CRM and select an item to create a template for.
- Click Add Template to create a new workflow template. Select Templates to edit an existing one.
- Open the Template Parameters tab and provide basic information, such as title, description, autorun options, etc.
- Complete the Parameters , Variables , and Constants tabs.
- When setting up a workflow for deals or SPAs, choose which sales pipelines to display it in.

titre: Start workflows in CRM item form

Find a workflow template
Use filters in the workflow list to find what you need.

Filter . By default, you see workflows only for the current pipeline. In Show workflows , select All to see every workflow. Sales pipelines
In the template settings, choose which pipelines will display the workflow.

titre: Workflow test log
sections: Workflow test log
The workflow test log helps you diagnose workflows. Use it to test workflows, track each step, and find errors.
Starting August 1, 2024, you can turn the log on or off for each workflow template.
Now you can enable the workflow log manually . To record events in the workflow log, enable the log for each template. How to enable event logging in a workflow template

The log recording period has changed . The log can only be enabled for seven days, and after a week, events will stop being recorded. Logs created by the Log entry activity will also be recorded for only seven days. To adjust your workflow, enable the log again.

If you need to check the workflow execution history rather than troubleshoot, go to Automation , open Workflows , and click Journal in the Time column. It shows all the actions, participants, and effectiveness of the workflow. Workflows: new interface and features
The number of records of automation rule actions has been reduced . If the automation rule runs several times for the same entity, only the last action will appear in the workflow log.
Enable event logging in a workflow template
1. Go to Automation > Workflows .
2. Select the workflow type.
3. Open the workflow template.
4. Click Template Parameters .
5. Turn on Enable event logging for 7 days .
After seven days, logging stops automatically. To continue, turn it on again. To stop logging earlier, turn the option off.
In brief
- The workflow test log helps you diagnose workflows and find errors.
- Starting August 1, 2024, you control logging for each workflow template.
- Logs are stored for seven days.
- Logs created before August 1, 2024, will be deleted.

titre: Workflow initialization limit in CRM
sections: Workflow initialization limit in CRM

Bitrix24 limits how workflows start in CRM. You can have up to 10 incomplete workflows at the same time for one item In Bitrix24, a CRM item can be a lead, deal, contact, company, invoice, estimate, or SPA item. .
For example, if 10 workflows are already running in an Equipment purchase deal, a new workflow starts only after one of the current ones finishes.
This limit helps keep Bitrix24 running smoothly and applies to the cloud version.
How the workflow launch limit works

- The limit does not apply to automation rules created in Workflow Designer. Even if 10 workflows are already active, these automation rules launch without restrictions. Sales and marketing automation in CRM

- Workflows with the Run when created option enabled run in a queue. If a workflow has no wait actions, it finishes immediately and does not count toward the limit on simultaneously running workflows.
Keep track of how many workflows run for the same CRM item. Set priorities and prepare templates in advance. This helps avoid delays and keeps your processes running smoothly.

titre: Wait for user input in workflows
sections: Wait for user input in workflows

Workflows are a set of activities that automate routine tasks. The Wait for user input activity pauses the workflow, allowing a user to decide the next step. For example, in an Order processing workflow, this activity lets a manager decide whether to offer a customer discount.
Only users specified in the activity settings can provide input. Activities: Flow Control Workflow designer
When a workflow needs a user input, a red counter will appear in the Automation section.
1. Go to the Automation section.
2. Expand Workflows .
3. Select Workflows .
4. Click Start next to the assignment.
Assignment. Choose a value that determines the workflow's next step. For example, offer a discount, a promo code, or do nothing.
You can also leave a comment explaining your decision, like why a discount was refused.
Journal. This section shows workflow data, including:
- All completed activities
- Participants
- Efficiency, based on average execution time
Efficiency helps evaluate workflow speed and identify improvement areas. Workflows: new interface and features
Workflow element. Quickly navigate to the element where the workflow started, such as a CRM item form. The timeline shows the activity execution details. Workflow events in CRM item form
In brief

- Only users specified in the activity settings can provide input.

titre: Add a new workflow field
sections: Add a new workflow field
Workflow fields let you store extra data used during workflow execution. You can control how fields appear and whether users can edit them.
Create a new workflow field
1. Go to Automation .
2. Open the Workflows tab.
3. Select Workflows in Feed .
4. Choose a workflow.
5. Click Settings and select Customize fields .
6. Click Add field .
7. Complete the field settings and save.
Configure field settings
When creating a field, define the following options:
- Name - required. Enter a clear field name.
- Required - users must complete the field before starting the workflow.
- Multiple - allows entering more than one value.
- Type - select the field type.
- Default value - set a value that will be used automatically.

titre: Insert Value Form
sections: Insert Value Form
When you set up a workflow, use the Insert Value form to add macros and auto-generated values. These can include document fields, system variables, date and time, and more.
To add a macro:
1. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the target field.
2. Select a macro in the Insert Value form.
The form shows all macros, grouped by type:
- Template Parameters : Values you define in the workflow designer. Users can fill in some of them when they start the workflow.
- Variables : Values that can change during the workflow. For example, a number field a user enters during execution.
- Constants : Fixed values that do not change. You set them in the template parameters. Users without edit access cannot change them.
- Document Fields : Values from the document where the workflow runs, such as Created on or Created by .
- Additional Results : Outputs from workflow activities. The list includes only activities in the current template that return values.
- Users : Specific users or user groups. If you select multiple users, separate them with a semicolon.
- User categories : Departments or social network groups.
These macros are not listed in the Insert Value form, but you can still use them in workflow templates:
- {=Workflow:ID} : Inserts the current workflow ID.
- {=User:ID} : Inserts the current user ID in the format user_[system_user_ID] .
- {=Template:TargetUser} : Inserts the ID of the user who started the workflow in the format user_[system_user_ID] .
- {=System:Now} : Inserts the current date and time.
- {=System:NowLocal} : Inserts the client's current date and time (time zone is taken into account).
- {=System:Date} : Inserts the current date.
- {=Document:DETAIL_PAGE_URL} : Inserts the document page link (works only if the details page URL is set correctly).
The "printable" modifier
Add the printable modifier to make the output easier to read. If the macro supports it, the value appears in a user-friendly format. If not, it shows the default value.

Macros with this modifier are also available in the Insert Value form.

titre: Workflow designer
sections: Workflow designer

titre: Status-driven business process template
sections: Status-driven business process template

Status-driven workflows are different from sequential workflows. They work best for large, complex processes, so setup takes a little more time. Once you understand the structure, the setup is simple.
This article explains how to create and configure a status-driven workflow.
How status-driven workflow creation works
Creating a status-driven workflow includes two main stages:
1. Create statuses.
2. Configure activities within each status, define transitions between statuses, and set access permissions.
The sections below explain each stage step by step.
Create statuses
Open the template editor and click Add status .

When you create a status, you can also define access permissions for the workflow at that stage. By default, the workflow inherits the same permissions as the item it is created for. If needed, you can change these permissions.
You can grant access to individual employees, departments, or user groups.
Configure a status
After creating statuses, configure the elements inside each one.
Each element represents a separate sequential process. Once you understand how they work, setup becomes much easier.
- Status Entry Handler : Runs automatically every time the workflow enters the status.

- Status Exit Handler : Runs immediately when the workflow moves to another status. Use the Set status activity to define transitions between statuses. In most cases, the entry and exit handlers are enough. The elements below are optional but provide more flexibility.

- Command : A process that a user starts manually when needed. Use commands when the workflow path depends on the situation. For example, an order from a large wholesale customer may follow one process, while an order from an individual customer follows another.
- Delay Execution : A process that starts automatically after a specified period. Use timed execution when an activity should run without user interaction.

Keep in mind that when the workflow reaches the Set status activity, it immediately switches to the exit handler. If the entry handler already changes the status, any configured Command or Delay Execution in that status will not run.

titre: Configure workflow template parameters
sections: Configure workflow template parameters
A workflow template is a pre-configured set of actions to quickly start a workflow. To use a template, fill out its parameters.

5. Click Settings (⚙️) .

Open an existing template or create a new one. Then click Template Parameters . Create a sequential workflow template Create a status-driven workflow template
Specify basic information
On the General tab, complete the following fields:
- Title : Enter the name to display in the list of templates.
- Description : Specify the workflow's purpose.
Choose whether to automatically run the workflow or start it manually.

Add parameters, variables, and constants

Parameters : Data that can't be changed after a workflow starts. These values are defined by a user before running a workflow. For example, in the Equipment Purchase workflow, this could be the product name or a link to it.
Variables : Temporary values that can be changed after a workflow starts. For example, the purchase amount or the name of the responsible employee.

On the Parameters , Variables , and Constants tabs, click Add and fill out the fields. They are the same on each tab.

A workflow template is a pre-configured set of actions to quickly start a workflow. To use a template, fill out its parameters.
