titre: Blocking REST API: Reasons and solutions
sections: Blocking REST API: Reasons and solutions
Bitrix24 REST API is a set of tools you can use to build apps and integrations. With REST, you can automate workflows and extend your Bitrix24 using API requests.

If you send too many REST requests or configure them incorrectly, you can overload the server. For example, if an app checks all CRM activities every five minutes, it might get blocked. Alaio Inc. can limit access to the REST API due to a high load, according to clause 18.2. (e) of the Terms of Service. Bitrix24 Terms of Service
What happens when the load is too high

- Non-critical load . The first administrator receives a message asking them to contact support to identify the cause. If the admin does not respond, the source of the load (webhook, local app, or other REST integration) is blocked.
- High load . The source of the load is blocked immediately. The first administrator is notified. Contact support to find out why it was blocked and how to fix it.
Notifications about high load

Depending on the situation, the first administrator may receive one of three messages in chat. All account administrators also receive a notification with a link to the blocked app. If multiple integrations are blocked, the notification includes a link to only one of them.

- Your test.bitrix24.com is showing a dramatic increase in activity. This creates a heavy system and server load and affects other users. Did you start any resource-intensive processes such as export, import, or REST automation? Please reply to this message.
- Hello! Your webhook #WEBHOOK# has been blocked due to high server load. Contact support for more details.
- Hello! Your app #APP# has been blocked due to high server load. Contact support for more details.
You can also review REST request load in Bitrix24: Evaluate the REST load in Bitrix24

titre: Restore blocked webhooks
sections: In brief
1. Go to Applications > Developer resources > Integrations .
2. Find the blocked webhook in the list, open the Menu (≡), and select Edit .
3. Copy the new secret key from the Webhook to call REST API field and update your local app or integration with it.
In detail

When you create a webhook, a secret key is automatically generated, which opens access to your data in Bitrix24. Keep the secret key confidential and avoid using it in any webpage code or script. Alaio Inc. blocks webhooks that have a secret key or token in the public domain.
How to know if your webhook is blocked

If you see the INVALID_CREDENTIALS error, it means your webhook is blocked. Alaio Inc. can limit access to the REST API for data protection, according to clauses 4.2. and 21.3.1. of the Terms of Service. Bitrix24 Terms of Service
To reactivate your webhook, generate a new secret key.
The INVALID_CREDENTIALS error also occurs if the webhook with the specified address is missing. This can happen if:
- The webhook was deleted.
- The secret key was changed.
- The owner of the webhook changed.
- There was a mistake in the webhook address or ID.
How to get a new secret key
When a webhook gets blocked, a new secret key is generated. Here's how to find it:
1. Go to Applications > Developer resources > Integrations .
2. Find the blocked webhook in the list, open the Menu (≡), and select Edit .
3. Copy the new secret key from the Webhook to call REST API field and update your local app or integration with it.
If you want to change the webhook's owner, update the secret key. Click Generate new > Continue and save your changes.

titre: Important changes in REST API, Market, Telephony and Search
sections: Important changes in REST API, Market, Telephony and Search
We are introducing several important updates to Bitrix24 Cloud tools, including REST API, Market, Telephony, and Bitrix24 Search.
REST API and Applications
Starting January 1, 2021, Market apps and REST API are available only on commercial plans .
On the Free plan, you cannot install apps from the Market or use local apps created by you or a partner.
Migration apps from other Bitrix24 services are the only exception. These remain available on the Free plan.
To keep using apps installed or purchased before January 1, 2021, upgrade from the Free plan to a commercial plan.
You can still test Market apps and REST API in demo or integrator mode. After the trial period ends, the apps will stop working.
Telephony
Starting January 1, 2021, Bitrix24 Telephony is available only on commercial plans. This includes all connection types: rented phone numbers, REST-based apps, and the SIP connector.
You can test Telephony in demo or integrator mode.
If you do not upgrade to a commercial plan by January 15, 2021, Telephony will be disabled.
Search in Tasks and CRM
Searching large volumes of tasks and CRM records requires significant resources. Starting December 1, 2020, search limits apply to the Free plan.
If your account has more than 1,000 tasks and 1,000 CRM records (Leads, Deals, Companies, or Contacts), you can only search using standard or saved filters. Keyword search will not be available.
To restore full search functionality, upgrade to a commercial plan or delete old tasks and CRM records.
FAQ: Search
I use the Free plan and have fewer than 1,000 deals, but search still doesn’t work. What should I do?
You likely have too many completed deals, which count toward the total limit.
Switch to the CRM List view.
Apply the Closed deals filter in the search bar.
Delete unnecessary deals, starting with the oldest ones.

titre: Important! TLS 1.0/1.1 protocols: end of support
sections: Important! TLS 1.0/1.1 protocols: end of support
Starting March 1, Bitrix24 servers no longer support TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. These protocols are outdated and not secure.
What this means
Apps built by Bitrix24 partners—such as Marketplace apps and webhooks—may stop working if they run on third-party servers that do not support TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3.
What to do
If you develop or maintain these apps, check whether your server supports TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3. You can use tools like GoDaddy or SSL Labs to verify your configuration.
If your server does not support these protocols, update your configuration to enable TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3

titre: FAQ: Bitrix24 Market apps
sections: FAQ: Bitrix24 Market apps

Bitrix24 Market is a catalog of apps that expand the functionality of Bitrix24 and help your company work more efficiently. For example, you can add new payment options or set up HR analytics with just a few clicks. The catalog offers more than 600 ready-made solutions for different business needs.

Bitrix24 Settings

What the Developer resources section is for

Change your Bitrix24 address
Only Bitrix24 administrators can change the account address.

Connect your own domain
You can connect your own domain to Bitrix24, for example, example.com instead of mycompany.bitrix24.com . Only the Bitrix24 administrator can connect a custom domain on Professional and higher plans.
To keep full control over your main domain, use a third-level domain such as crm.example.com . This allows you to continue using the main domain for your website, email, and other services.
Configure DNS records
To connect your domain, add these four NS records in your domain DNS settings:
- ns-1277.awsdns-31.org.
- ns-310.awsdns-38.com.
- ns-581.awsdns-08.net.
- ns-1613.awsdns-09.co.uk.
If other records already exist for this domain, you can remove them.
After you update the DNS records, send the following to Bitrix24 Support:
- Your full domain name.
- Proof that you updated the NS records, such as a screenshot of the DNS settings.

titre: FAQ: Phishing
sections: FAQ: Phishing

Phishing is a type of fraud aimed at obtaining confidential user or company data. The Network Monitoring and Management Center analyzed the growth of phishing attacks in 2024, revealing a 425% increase.
Targeted phishing is a planned attack aimed at specific company employees to steal corporate data, gain access to internal systems, or disrupt infrastructure operations.
How fraudsters deceive:
- Research the company by reviewing social media, company structure, and communication style.
- Forge emails from managers or colleagues using cloned domains. For example, instead of name@company.com , they use name@companny.com .
- Create fake accounts in messengers and impersonate real employees, complete with profile photos.
- Send malicious files, such as requests to update software.
- Create fake login pages to steal passwords.
Test your ability to recognize phishing. Answer 10 questions.
Question 1 . You work at the company with the @mycompany.com email domain. You received an incoming email. Is it phishing?
From: CEO@MYC0MPANY.COM To: Everyone Subject: IMPORTANT. URGENT. About bonuses
Hello, colleagues!

As part of our plans to introduce a new motivation and bonus system in our company, all employees must complete a survey via the following link: HTTPS://SURVEY.MYC0MPANY.COM . Deadline: today by 4:00 PM.
Find the answer
This is a phishing email. Here are the signs:
- The email lacks specific sender and recipient details.
- The link replaces the letter O with a zero.
- The link leads to a fake website.
Question 2 . You received an email. Is it phishing?
Hello!
In response to your estimate for supplying home appliances, please complete the contractor form (attached document: card.pdf.exe) and send it back via email to continue our collaboration.
Best regards, "Company name"
Find the answer
This is a phishing email. Here are the signs:
- The email lacks a specific sender.
- The attachment is a file with an exe extension, not a pdf. File formats like exe, scr, bat, and vbs can be malicious.
Question 3 . You received an email. Is it phishing?
Hello!
As we prepare for our corporate event, please vote for the venue. Other companies are actively booking locations, so voting must be completed today.
Voting link: https://event.mycompany.co
Find the answer
This is a phishing email. The scammer changed the domain zone from com to co.
Question 4 . Is this email phishing?
From: HelpDesk@HelpDesk.com Subject: Urgent CRM update
Hello, sales department colleagues!
Due to a critical error in our CRM, there is a risk of losing all deal data. You must urgently download and run the update (attachment: update.exe).
Best regards, Paul Johson IT Lead Specialist paul@mycompany.com LLC My Company
Find the answer
This is a phishing email. The sender is forged. Instead of @mycompany.com, it uses @HelpDesk.com.
Question 5 . Which email can be used for work correspondence?
- @gmail.com
- Only corporate services
- Any services, as long as you know the recipient
Find the answer
Separate personal and work correspondence. Use only corporate services for work emails. This protects the company from sensitive information leaks.
Question 6 . Select the signs of a phishing email:
- Urgency in task completion
- Generic greeting — no name or position
- Links with character substitutions, like O replaced with 0
- Attachment with an exe file format
Find the answer
The correct answer is all the listed options indicate phishing.
Question 7 . Is this link address fake — https://googlediscover.com.xyz ?
Find the answer
Yes, this address is fake. An extra domain, xyz, is added after com. You can check site ownership on Whois services like https://www.nic.com/whois/ .
Question 8 . Is this link address fake — http://205.0.112.45 ?
Find the answer
The link may be phishing if:
- The site domain is an IP address.
- The protocol is http instead of https . Without the letter s, there is no encryption.
Question 9 . You received a message.
Hi, I can't reach your manager Paul. It's urgent to pay the invoice for equipment supply. Attachment: invoice.pdf.
Best regards, Paul Johnson paul@mycompany.com +12345678912 CEO of LLC My Company
What will you do next:

A. Call your manager Paul to confirm the task. Do nothing until he confirms. If it's phishing, immediately inform the Security Department. B. Urgent tasks from management must be completed immediately, and checking emails for phishing is the responsibility of the Security Department. C. Start following the email instructions immediately but inform your manager simultaneously.
Find the answer
The correct answer is A. Any employee can encounter phishing, so it's important to:
- Take your time — urgency in emails is often a sign of deception.
- Verify the sender — domain, name, and email style.
- Consult colleagues if something seems suspicious.
Security depends on every employee.
Question 10 . Your friend sent a file about a sale to your work laptop. You:
- Called them to clarify details
- Checked the file extension
- Scanned it with antivirus software — no threats found
- And only then opened the document
Did you do everything correctly?
Find the answer
The correct answer is no. While this wasn't a scam and you were communicating with a friend, your work laptop contains corporate data, and even accidental actions can lead to data leaks.
Follow these rules to avoid risks:
- Use your work laptop exclusively for work.
This way, you protect yourself and your company.

titre: Changes in REST 22.0.0
sections: Changes in REST 22.0.0
Starting with REST module version 22.0.0 in Bitrix24 Cloud, all REST API responses include an additional operating key in the time array. This key provides extra details about request execution time.

The key shows how long a method request runs inside the account. Bitrix24 tracks the total execution time for each method. If the combined execution time for a method exceeds 480 seconds within 10 minutes, the method is blocked for 10 minutes.
Example 1
Application 1 retrieves lead data with the crm.lead.list method.
- Each request takes 20 seconds.
- The application sends 2 requests per minute.
After 10 minutes, the total execution time is 400 seconds.
The application stays within the limit, so it continues to work normally.
Example 2
Application 2 retrieves deal data with the crm.deal.list method.
- Each request takes 15 seconds.
- The application sends 2 requests per minute.
After 10 minutes, the total execution time is 300 seconds.
This application uses a different method, so its execution time is tracked separately. The application continues to work normally.
Example 3
Application 3 starts retrieving leads with the crm.lead.list method at the same time as Application 1.
- Each request also takes 20 seconds.
Both applications use the same method. Their execution times are added together. When the total exceeds 480 seconds, both applications receive a 429 error when calling the method.

titre: Bitrix24 On-Premise editions comparison
sections: Bitrix24 On-Premise editions comparison
Bitrix24 On-Premise editions are designed for large companies and organizations that need full control over their infrastructure and data.
There are two editions available: Business and Enterprise .
The Business edition includes the following capabilities:
- More users : Supports 50–500 users.
- External users (Extranet) : Provide partners, clients, or contractors with secure access to specific workgroups. External users only see the projects and content shared with them.
- e-Learning : Create training courses, run tests, and track results. You can build unlimited courses for employees and external users. All results are recorded and available for review.
- Helpdesk : Set up an internal support system to manage service requests. Users can submit tickets through a form or by email.

- Active Directory, SSO, MS Exchange, Sharepoint Sync : Integrate Bitrix24 with your existing infrastructure. Sync calendars, contacts, and tasks with Microsoft Exchange and Outlook. Connect Active Directory or LDAP for centralized user management. CalDAV and CardDAV support allows integration with Apple and Google services.
The Enterprise edition includes all Business features, plus:
- More users : Supports 1,000–5,000 users.
- Multiple Divisions : Create separate intranet environments for different departments or branch offices. Each division can have its own structure, design, and access settings.
- Web-Cluster : Scale system performance by distributing workloads across multiple servers. Add resources as your company grows.

titre: How is Bitrix24 licensed
sections: How is Bitrix24 licensed
Bitrix24 Cloud is a SaaS solution that users subscribe to. Alaio Inc. (USA) and Alaio Cloud Limited (Europe) host, maintain, and manage the service in the cloud.
You can use your Bitrix24 account with a free subscription or a paid plan .
Before you use your Bitrix24 Cloud account and the services available in your Bitrix24, read and accept the Terms of Service (ToS) .
Bitrix24 On-Premise (Self-Hosted) uses per-user licensing. If you need more users than your current license allows, you can purchase On-Premise Edition Upgrades .
Bitrix24 On-Premise is fully customizable. You can change color schemes, layouts, menu items, headers, footers, and more. It also includes full access to the source code.
You can deploy and host Bitrix24 On-Premise on your own servers or work with Bitrix Partners .

titre: Switching Bitrix24 On-Premise license to a subscription model
sections: Switching Bitrix24 On-Premise license to a subscription model
To keep delivering regular product updates and support, Bitrix24 On-Premise moved to a subscription licensing model on September 1, 2022 .
The price of all editions stays the same. However, annual renewal is now required. The renewal cost is 50% of the edition price.
What changed
- Bitrix24 On-Premise no longer uses a one-time license with optional paid updates. All licenses now require an annual subscription renewal.
- The Bitrix24 On-Premise Enterprise Unlimited users edition is no longer available for purchase.
Starting September 1, 2022, the End User License Agreement (EULA) includes these changes:
1. We generally updated the text of the terms, added structure to the sections, and changed the order of the sections where necessary.
2. EULA was supplemented with section “Definitions” at the beginning, which is aimed to ease the general understanding of the EULA.
3. The section 2 is supplemented with special usage conditions for the Product components (please refer to §2.1.3.).
4. Transition rules for Renewals and Upgrades of your license edition and type described in §2.1.4.
5. Now you can find the description of the Updates in §2.1.7.

6. Please note that we include in EULA a new subsection 2.2. (License types and terms) dedicated to different types of licenses, which are now: (a) Subscription License, which is a license that allows you use the Product for a limited time period. When such period expires, your On-Premise Product will be locked if you don’t renew your Subscription License. This type of license reflects our new subscription model which will be effective on September 1, 2022. For details, please refer to §2.2.1. (b) Standard License. Your current commercial license will turn into Standard License on September 1, 2022 unless you renew it to Subscription License type. For details, please refer to §2.2.3. (c) Limited License is provided to the User only in case and from the date of provision of the Standard License. For details, please refer to §2.2.4. (d) NFR-License. For details, please refer to §2.2.5. (e) Trial Version. For details, please refer to §2.2.6.
7. In §2.3. you can find a description of the License Extensions.
8. §9.2. “Export Control and Compliance with Laws” was amended in compliance with regulations.
9. A clause dedicated to the changes to the EULA was amended and moved to the section 4 (please refer to §4.3).
10. In clause 7.2.2. we described measures Bitrix24 can take at its sole discretion and without any notice if you violate the terms of the EULA.
11. We clarified the ways we may use to send you legally significant notifications including connected with the EULA in section 13.
I already have an active Bitrix24 On-Premise license. What changes for me?
After September 1, 2022 all new Bitrix24 On-premise licenses are provided as a subscription license that is required to be renewed annually for 50% from the On-Premise edition price.

Licenses purchased before September 1, 2022 continue to work under the original terms. However, if you want to receive updates, support, and access to Bitrix24 cloud services, you can no longer renew the maintenance subscription separately. Instead, you must switch to a Subscription License.

titre: Why you need to update your Bitrix24 On‑Premise version
sections: Why you need to update your Bitrix24 On‑Premise version

We are going to explain why it’s essential to update your Bitrix24 On-Premise version on time. You should do this as soon as an update is released. At least updates should be installed every six months. Here’s what might happen if you ignore this simple rule.
In this case, it’s better to forget the “If it works, don’t touch it” rule.
We recommend not delaying updates. Here’s why it’s important.
Protect your data

The Bitrix24 team continually works on identifying potential vulnerabilities in the product. It is our responsibility to minimize cybersecurity risks. We promptly fix all identified issues and release new product versions. All you need to do is install them on time. This is the most cost-effective way to prevent information security risks.
Fix bugs and improve performance
We consistently fix potential errors and address reported bugs. Some of these issues are brought to our attention by you.
We want you and your team to have the best possible experience with our product. If you don’t install updates, you will encounter bugs that we have already resolved.
Support for the mobile app

We release mobile app updates several times a month. Technologies evolve, new features are introduced, and support for new devices and operating systems is added. Our team continuously works on optimizing performance and improving the interface.

The longer you delay updates on your side, the worse the compatibility between your Bitrix24 On-Premise version and our mobile app will become. It is impossible to ensure reliable interaction with all outdated versions.
Typically, issues start to arise if the On-Premise version is more than a year behind the mobile app.
Cloud features and integrations

The concept of a completely isolated On-Premise version is becoming outdated. Modern On-Premise solutions don’t operate in a vacuum: some features, including AI, rely on cloud infrastructure. The On-Premise version is becoming hybrid.
CoPilot and other AI features. Few companies connect their own models to Bitrix24. Most of them use our cloud-based LLM model.
External services (email, banks, messengers, payment systems) also update their APIs and protocols. Without updates, authorizations, webhooks, and other features stop working.
Delaying updates for too long leads to desynchronization. Certain features start to degrade or stop functioning altogether.
Access to new features
We release two major updates each year. Each release includes numerous new features, tailored to the current needs of businesses, at no additional cost.
Without updates, your team gets stuck with outdated functionality and misses out on new opportunities.
What happens if you don’t update
- Data breach risks increase with each month without patches.
- Mobile and desktop apps lose stability due to new APIs/SDKs.
- Feature gap: your team misses out on new tools.
- Performance and bugs: you are stuck with unresolved issues.
- Cloud and integration support: compatibility worsens, leading to "silent failures".
- Maintenance: it becomes costly and unpredictable over time, especially with accumulated technical debt.
FAQ

I update the On-Premise version once a year. Is that enough? No. Updates should be installed as soon as they are released, not on a fixed schedule. You might miss a critical security update, putting your entire business at risk.

The Bitrix24 partner who set up our system said their customizations might break during updates. What should we do? If the partner implemented customizations correctly, updates should proceed smoothly.

When is the On-Premise version considered outdated? Any version that isn’t up-to-date is considered outdated. However, statistics show that issues typically arise if updates are delayed for more than a year.

How do I update the Bitrix24 On-Premise version? Go to the admin panel and select Market > Platform Update . Click Install recommended updates in the Update Installation section. Choose what you want to update in the Update list tab.

How can I minimize risks when updating in production? Use a test environment, create a full backup, and have a rollback plan. Review the change log, schedule updates during low-traffic periods, and test critical scenarios.

We don’t use mobile apps. Can we update less frequently? No. Even without mobile apps, there are still factors like security, integrations (email, banks, messengers, maps, SSO), performance, and bug fixes. These alone require regular updates.

Do updates improve speed and stability? Yes. Releases often include database, caching, and interface optimizations, as well as fixes for intermittent bugs. These improvements can boost speed without hardware upgrades and reduce support requests.

titre: Bitrix24 On-Premise technical requirements
sections: Web server
Bitrix24 requires a web server with PHP support.
Supported servers
- Apache 2.4.x or later - recommended.
- nginx 1.16.x or later - requires manual configuration.
PHP requirements
Use a PHP version supported by your hosting provider or matching your local environment. For best performance and security, use the latest stable PHP release.
Required PHP extensions
- GD – used to generate images, graphs, and charts. Required for the Statistics, Advertising, and Helpdesk modules. Also used for CAPTCHA.
- PHP XML – required for the update system. Included in the standard PHP installation. XML support is built in on Windows.
- FreeType – required for CAPTCHA.
- Regular Expression support (POSIX and Perl compatible) – required by the system core.
- Zlib compression – required for data compression and system updates.
We recommend using a PHP accelerator such as OPcache or XCache to improve performance. OPcache is included in PHP 5.5 and later.
Important
- Set the XCache.cacher to Off : xcache.cacher = Off .
- eAccelerator is not compatible with PHP 5.3 or later and is no longer supported in Bitrix products starting from Kernel module version 15.0.13.
- Bitrix24 supports UTF-8 encoding for MySQL databases. To ensure proper encoding, make sure the mbstring PHP module is installed. Add the following settings to your php.ini file:
Exemple : mbstring.func_overload=0 default_charset=UTF-8
Additional PHP settings
The following PHP parameters are required:
- Memory limit
- File uploads
- PHP sessions
Memory limit
Set the maximum memory available to PHP:
Exemple : memory_limit = 256M;
You can configure this value in several ways:
- Edit the php.ini file.
- Set the value in a script using: ini_set("memory_limit", "256M"); During installation, this value is added to: /bitrix/php_interface/dbconn.php
Exemple : ini_set("memory_limit", "256M");
Exemple : /bitrix/php_interface/dbconn.php
- Add the directive to the .htaccess file: php_value memory_limit 256M
Exemple : php_value memory_limit 256M
- You use Apache (or a compatible server).
- The server allows .htaccess overrides ( AllowOverride is not set to None in httpd.conf ).
- PHP runs as an Apache module.
- Set the value in httpd.conf : php_admin_value memory_limit 256M
Exemple : php_admin_value memory_limit 256M
File uploads
Enable file uploads: file_uploads = On;
Exemple : file_uploads = On;
Configure the following parameters: upload_tmp_dir = <directory path> upload_max_filesize = <required file size limit>
Exemple : upload_tmp_dir = <directory path> upload_max_filesize = <required file size limit>
PHP sessions
Correct session configuration is required.
To prevent the PHPSESSID parameter from appearing in URLs:
- Add the following setting to php.ini session.use_trans_sid = 0[/c
Exemple : session.use_trans_sid = 0[/c
- Add the following directive to .htaccess : php_flag session.use_trans_sid off The demo site already includes this line in the .htaccess file. Uncomment it if needed.
Database requirements
We recommend using MySQL 8.x (Percona Server) .
Make sure MySQL support is enabled in PHP.
Disk space
You need at least 10 GB of free disk space for the initial installation. If you store many files or documents, additional space may be required.
RAM
- Minimum requirement: 1 GB RAM
- If you use Push&Pull server: at least 2 GB RAM
Recommended server configurations
Approximate hardware configurations based on the number of users:
- Up to 50 users Intel Xeon E3-1230v5 3.4 GHz (4 cores) 2 × 2 TB HDD for files 2 × 256 GB SSD for database 16 GB DDR4 RAM
- 50–100 users Intel Xeon E3-1230v5 3.4 GHz (4 cores) 2 × 2 TB HDD for files 2 × 256 GB SSD for database 24 GB DDR4 RAM
- 100–500 users Intel Xeon E3-1230v5 3.4 GHz (4 cores) 2 × 2 TB HDD for files 2 × 256 GB SSD for database 32 GB DDR4 RAM
- 500–1000 users Intel Xeon E5-1650v4 3.6 GHz (6 cores) 2 × 4 TB HDD for files 2 × 480 GB SSD for database 64 GB DDR4 RAM
- 1000–5000 users Intel Xeon E5-1650v4 3.6 GHz (6 cores) 2 × 4 TB HDD for files 2 × 480 GB SSD for database 128 GB DDR4 RAM
- 5000+ users Two Intel Xeon E5-1650v4 3.6 GHz servers (6 cores each) 2 × 4 TB HDD for files 2 × 480 GB SSD for database 128 GB DDR4 RAM
Supported browsers
Bitrix24 supports the latest versions of major browsers:
- Chrome 92 or later
- Edge 92 or later
- Firefox 90 or later
- Opera 77 or later
- Safari 12 or later
- Safari for iOS 12 or later
- Chrome for Android 93 or later
- Firefox for Android 92 or later

titre: Secure Bitrix24 On-Premise with external security tools
sections: Secure Bitrix24 On-Premise with external security tools

The on-premise version of Bitrix24 runs on your company's infrastructure, so you need to protect its servers, network, and employee devices. External security tools help block suspicious requests, scan uploaded files for viruses, prevent corporate data leaks, and detect cyberattacks.
In this article:
- Choose additional security tools
- Set up security tools
Choose additional security tools

The tools you need depend on your company's data, how employees access Bitrix24, and your information security requirements. Your company's information security specialist or a Bitrix24 Partner can set up security tools for Bitrix24.
Filter incoming requests with a WAF

A web application firewall (WAF) inspects incoming requests to Bitrix24 and blocks suspicious ones before they reach the server. For example, it can block attempts to inject malicious code through a web form.

Deploy a WAF in front of your web servers: users connect to the WAF, and Bitrix24 servers accept requests only from it. Your Bitrix24 architecture may include additional servers, such as Push&Pull for instant messages. Make sure traffic is routed correctly when integrating the WAF. Also consider WAF performance and set up exceptions for video calls and other bandwidth-intensive streaming services.
What you need to know:

- Start in monitoring mode. A WAF has two modes: monitoring mode only logs suspicious requests, while blocking mode rejects them. This helps you identify legitimate employee actions that the firewall mistakenly flags as suspicious and set up exceptions.

- Set up rules for login forms, the administration section, file uploads, and integrations. Rules should protect these areas without blocking file uploads, data exchange with integrations, or background tasks.
- Restrict access to the administration section. Allow access only from your company's internal network or through a secure connection (VPN).
- Keep logs of triggered rules. Collect them with other security events, for example, in a SIEM (more on this below). This makes incident investigations easier.
You can use an external WAF with the Proactive filter. The Proactive filter is built into Bitrix24 and is designed to work with it. 8 layers of protection of Bitrix24

If you can't update Bitrix24 immediately, a WAF can help block some attacks that exploit known vulnerabilities. You should still install the update: a WAF doesn't fix vulnerabilities or guarantee protection.
Scan files for viruses
Install antivirus software on the server to prevent infected files from reaching other users. It scans documents, images, and archives that employees upload to Bitrix24.
What you need to know:
- Scan uploaded files for viruses. Scanning archives can reduce performance, so set limits for scan depth and archive size.
- For Bitrix24 core files and custom code, use integrity control, change detection, and scheduled scans.
- Create exceptions only for service data, such as temporary files (cache) and logs. Only the system account should have permission to modify this data.
Prevent data leaks (DLP)

A data loss prevention (DLP) tool helps ensure that important data doesn't leave the company. For example, when integrated with Bitrix24, a DLP tool can detect or block an attempt to send an email with the customer database to a personal address.
What you need to know:
- Before choosing a DLP tool, identify the data that matters most to your company and the channels employees use to share it.
- Depending on the solution, a DLP tool can monitor outgoing emails, files saved to local devices, or data exports from Bitrix24.
- You can set up DLP using a ready-made solution from a DLP vendor or a custom solution developed by a Bitrix24 Partner.
Collect and analyze security events (SIEM)

A SIEM collects security events from different services used by your company in one place. This helps you identify suspicious activity faster, such as multiple failed login attempts, and investigate incidents.
Data you can send from Bitrix24 to a SIEM:
- Event history — Bitrix24 logs login attempts, user actions, and system errors here.
- Web server logs — these record errors that may not appear in the event history.
- Update and backup logs — these help identify unexpected file changes.
- Background task status — a stalled task may not trigger an alert.
To send this data to a SIEM, set up connectors — scripts that read log files and send the data, usually using the syslog protocol.
Manage accounts and single sign-on (SSO)
Centralized account management lets you manage user accounts in a single directory, apply consistent password rules, and quickly revoke access when an employee leaves.
Depending on your Bitrix24 version and configuration, Bitrix24 On-Premise provides the following built-in options:

- Integration with Active Directory and LDAP. Active Directory and other directory services that use the LDAP protocol store your company's employee accounts. Bitrix24 connects to a directory and synchronizes employee accounts, along with your company structure if needed. Integrate Bitrix24 with Active Directory and LDAP
- Automatic domain login (NTLM). Employees who are already signed in to their work computers with domain accounts can access Bitrix24 without entering their passwords again.
- Two-factor authentication.
For other login methods, such as a corporate single sign-on service, you can find ready-made solutions in the Market. Bitrix24 Apps
Manage mobile devices (MDM)

The Bitrix24 mobile app is a work tool, just like a corporate computer: employees use it to access messages, documents, tasks, and CRM data. You also need to secure the devices themselves. Use mobile device management (MDM) tools for this.
MDM lets you:
- Block the transfer of work data to personal apps.
- Exclude work data from device backups.
- Revoke access if a device is lost by removing VPN settings and certificates and terminating active sessions.
- Allow only Bitrix24 and other necessary apps, such as the camera and a document viewer, on corporate devices.
Configure MDM rules separately for different device groups: employees' personal devices, corporate phones, and shared terminals.
MDM doesn't replace Bitrix24 access permissions. Even if a phone runs only Bitrix24, you still need to configure access permissions in Bitrix24. Protect data in the Bitrix24 mobile app
Protect your custom code

If you have custom code in Bitrix24, protect it as well. Use the built-in security tools of Bitrix Framework, the platform Bitrix24 is built on. They help prevent common attacks, such as attempts to inject malicious code into pages or database queries.
Set up security tools

Setting up external security tools requires separate planning. There's no universal approach: the setup depends on your Bitrix24 version and edition, network, integrations, and the capabilities of the selected tool. Plan the setup with a Bitrix24 Partner who has experience with both Bitrix24 and the security tools you plan to use. Find a partner in the directory: in the Product type filter, select On-Premise . Find an implementation partner
Steps to set up security tools:

1. Gather the information your partner needs. Identify who connects to Bitrix24 and from where — via the internet or your internal network. List the data that matters most to your company and the integrations you use.
2. Choose security tools with your partner. The partner compares solution capabilities with your company's requirements and suggests suitable options.
3. Plan the integration. The partner should consider your IT environment, system configuration, legal requirements, and internal information security policies and procedures.

4. Run tests. Ensure the security tools don't block necessary actions or slow down Bitrix24. For example, keep a WAF in monitoring mode for several weeks and review all false positives. If you don't have a test server, discuss with your partner where to run the tests.
5. Launch the solution in your production environment. Review your security tool settings and rules whenever your IT infrastructure changes.
By the end of the project, you should have documentation of your security setup, test results, and instructions for administrators.
In brief

- You can add external security tools to Bitrix24 On-Premise: WAF, antivirus, DLP, SIEM, and MDM. They check requests and files, prevent data leaks, collect security events, and protect mobile devices.
- External tools complement Bitrix24 updates, access permissions, and built-in tools, such as the Proactive filter, but don't replace them.
- Start with a WAF in monitoring mode to identify false positives before enabling blocking mode.

- Bitrix24 On-Premise already includes integration with Active Directory and LDAP, domain login, and two-factor authentication. For other login methods, you can find ready-made solutions in the Market.
- Protect your custom code with the built-in tools of Bitrix Framework.
- Setting up security tools requires separate planning. Plan the setup with a Bitrix24 Partner and test it before deploying it to your production environment.

titre: Upgrade to PHP 8.1 in Bitrix24 On-Premise
sections: Upgrade to PHP 8.1 in Bitrix24 On-Premise
You may see a warning in your Bitrix24 Control Panel:
What this means
All PHP 7 versions have reached end of life and are no longer supported. They no longer receive bug fixes or security updates. Do not use PHP versions earlier than 8.1.

If you stay on an older version, you won’t be able to install Bitrix24 updates. This means you’ll miss new features, as well as important security and performance improvements. To continue updating your system, upgrade PHP to version 8.1 or later.
What to do
Upgrade your PHP version to 8.1 as soon as possible.
The process may take several steps. If needed, contact your system administrator or hosting provider.
1. Back up your site Use the built-in backup tool or create a server-level backup.
2. Install platform updates Go to Control panel > Marketplace > Platform Update .
3. Update third-party solutions Go to Control panel > Marketplace > Solution Update .
4. Upgrade PHP to version 8.1 If you use BitrixVM, open the menu and select: 1. Manage servers in the pool - 8. Update PHP and MySQL . Learn more in this course .
5. Check for updates again Install any remaining platform or solution updates.
Fix errors after upgrading PHP
- If standard Bitrix24 modules don’t work, contact Bitrix24 Support .

- If the solution name starts with bitrix.* (for example, bitrix.eshop , bitrix.sitecommunity , bitrix.sitecorporate , bitrix.siteinfoportal , bitrix.sitepersonal , bitrix.learningtemplates ), contact Bitrix24 Support.
- If a third-party module from the Marketplace doesn’t work, contact the module developer. You can find their contact details in the Support tab.
Why issues happen
After upgrading to PHP 8.1, issues usually occur if:
1. You didn’t install platform updates before the upgrade.
2. You didn’t update third-party solutions.
3. A module is not compatible with PHP 8.2 or later.
How to fix common issues
- Downgrade to the previous PHP version 7.x, get all the recommended updates, and then upgrade to PHP 8.1x again.
- If installing updates does not help to fix the issues, follow the recommendations from this section - What to do in case of errors when updating the PHP version .
- Temporarily disable the module that contains errors by moving it away from /bitrix/modules .
- Remove a third-party solution that contains errors.
These steps address specific module issues. Each case may require a separate fix.
[Ux11] Error in the "#MODULE#" module description. Cannot connect the update server. [Ux11] Error in the "#MODULE#" module description.
Cannot connect to the update server after upgrading to PHP 8.1. The site works, but updates fail.

Exemple : function ()

Connect to FTP/SFTP or log in to the hosting control panel, and enable the error output in /bitrix/.settings.php :

titre: Critical PHP vulnerabilities: what Bitrix24 clients need to do

titre: Set up two-factor authentication in Bitrix24 without the mobile app
sections: Set up two-factor authentication in Bitrix24 without the mobile app
If two-factor authentication is mandatory in your company, each employee must set it up by the deadline. After the deadline, you can't log in to Bitrix24 until you complete the setup.

You can set up two-factor authentication without the Bitrix24 mobile app. This is useful if you don't have a smartphone or don't want to install the app. Instead, you can confirm your login by email or SMS.
In this article:
- Allow login confirmation without the mobile app
- Set up two-factor authentication without the mobile app
If two-factor authentication is already enabled but you can't access the app, use another login confirmation method. Log in to Bitrix24 without the mobile app
Allow login confirmation without the mobile app
This option is enabled by default. If an administrator disables it, employees can't skip connecting a trusted device.
Open the security settings in one of two ways:
- In the left menu, click Settings (⚙️) > Bitrix24 settings and select Security
- At the top of the screen, next to the Bitrix24 logo, click the slider icon and select Security
Check the setting:
1. In the Two-factor authentication block, find Allow login confirmation without mobile app . If the option is off, turn it on. 2. If you changed the setting, click Save .

This setting doesn't disable two-factor authentication. It only lets employees skip connecting a trusted device. Employees who have already connected the mobile app can continue using it to confirm their login.
Set up two-factor authentication without the mobile app
To set up two-factor authentication without the mobile app, skip the trusted device step and confirm your email address or phone number instead.

We recommend adding both. If you lose access to one, you can use the other to confirm your login. You can also add a phone number later. How to add a phone number if you skipped this step during setup

1. Click your photo in the top-right corner. 2. Select Security . 3. Click Two-factor authentication . You can also click Enable in the Enable the new two-factor authentication banner. 4. Click Enable protection . 5. On the Connect a trusted device screen, click Skip . If you don't see the Skip button, contact your Bitrix24 administrator. 6. Enter your email address. You'll receive a confirmation code by email. To use only your phone number, click Confirm using SMS and go to step 9. 7. Click Confirm . 8. Enter the code from the email. The Backup login number screen opens. 9. Enter your phone number. You'll receive a confirmation code by SMS. 10. Click Continue . If you don't want to add a phone number, click Finish . You'll only be able to confirm your login by email. 11. Enter the code from the SMS. Two-factor authentication is now set up. 12. Close the Done! window. You can now confirm your Bitrix24 login with a code sent by email or SMS.
Save your recovery codes after setup. You'll need them if you lose access to both your email and phone. Where to find recovery codes
You can connect the mobile app later under Photo > Security > Two-factor authentication > Trusted devices > Connect .

If two-factor authentication is mandatory in your company and the setup deadline has passed, the trusted device connection screen opens when you log in to Bitrix24. Click Skip and follow steps 5–11 above.
In brief
- You can set up two-factor authentication without the Bitrix24 mobile app and confirm your login by email or SMS.
- Two-factor authentication remains active even if you don't connect the mobile app.

- Login confirmation without the mobile app is allowed by default. Administrators can check this setting under Bitrix24 settings > Security > Two-factor authentication . If you make changes, click Save .
- Employees set up two-factor authentication under Photo > Security > Two-factor authentication > Enable protection > Skip , then confirm their email or phone number.
- You can connect the mobile app or add a phone number later under Security .

titre: Alaio Vibecode: Collaborate on an app and transfer it to a colleague
sections: Alaio Vibecode: Collaborate on an app and transfer it to a colleague

Multiple employees can work on the same Alaio Vibecode app without sharing personal API keys. If the person responsible for the app changes, the owner can transfer the app to another employee along with everything needed to continue working on it.
In this article:
- Set up shared access to an app
- Publish changes when working together
- Change the app owner
Set up shared access to an app
Add employees to or remove them from the development team. The owner doesn't need to share credentials to let others work on the app — each team member uses a personal API key.
Add an employee to the development team.

1. Log in to Alaio Vibecode and open the Applications section. 2–3. Click Access > Collaboration on the app's card. 4–5. Click Add employee and start typing the employee's name in the search field. 6. Click the name of the employee you want to add to the development team. 7–8. Click the current role next to the employee's name and select an option:

- Developer : has access to app data on the server, including environment variables. Can publish changes, run commands on the server, work with files, logs, and source storage, and wake up the server.

- Administrator : has all Developer permissions and can also manage the server lifecycle, settings, security, plan, disk, backups, and domain. Can configure app access, work with the app card in the catalog, and manage app expenses.
9. Click Close . Changes to team membership and roles are saved immediately.
Remove an employee from the development team.

1–2. Open Access > Collaboration on the app's card. 3. Click Remove at the end of the employee's row. 4. In the Remove from development team window, choose whether to select the Also revoke the right to open the app checkbox:
- Checkbox cleared : the employee can't work with the app code or server but can still open and use the app. You can revoke this permission later on the Access tab of the app card.
- Checkbox selected : the employee is no longer a team member and can't open the app unless the app access settings specify otherwise.
5. Click Remove to confirm the action. 6. Click Close . Changes are saved automatically.
Publish changes when working together

You work on an app in Alaio Vibecode by chatting with an AI agent, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. The agent modifies the code and publishes it to the server. Update or remove an AI solution in Alaio Vibecode
When working on an app together, instruct the agent to follow these rules:
- Use your personal API key.
- Before making changes, retrieve the latest version of the source code and note the version number.
- Make changes without modifying the app's existing environment variables.
- Publish changes to the same server and specify the source code version used as the starting point. For example, if you started editing version v12, specify v12 as the base version.

- If publishing is rejected because a colleague has already published a newer version, retrieve the latest source code, merge your changes into it, and publish again using the new base version. Don't simply update the version number while keeping the old code.
- After publishing, verify that the app works correctly.
Example request to the agent:
Change the app owner
If the employee who led development leaves the company or moves to another project, transfer the app to a new owner.
Transfer an app. Only the app owner and the Bitrix24 administrator can transfer an app to a new owner.

1. Log in to Alaio Vibecode and open the Applications section. 2. Click Three dots (...) next to the Access button on the card for the app you need. 3. Select Transfer . 4. Check which data transfers to the new owner:
- Personal API key : reissued by default, but you can change this setting in the next step.
- Authorization key : transfers without automatic reissue. The new owner must reissue it manually if they use it.

- Server : if the server belongs to another employee, its owner doesn't change. After the transfer, Bitrix24 shows a notification and a warning on the app card about the mismatch between the app owner and server owner.
- Placements : they remain linked to the app. Their count appears in the summary before the transfer.
- People with access : the summary shows the count, and the access settings transfer with the app.

- Source snapshot : if a snapshot is saved, the right to download it transfers to the new owner. If no snapshot exists, the transfer isn't blocked, but the new owner doesn't receive it automatically. Save and transfer the source code before transferring the app.
- App : the app and its access settings transfer to the new owner.
5. Select or clear the Reissue app key checkbox:

- Checkbox selected (default): when the app is transferred, Alaio Vibecode creates a new app API key. The previous key stops working no later than 24 hours after a successful reissue. If the server supports automatic key updates, Alaio Vibecode applies the new key automatically. If the key can't be created, the app transfer still proceeds. The new owner sees a warning and can reissue the key from the app card.

- Checkbox cleared : the personal API key linked to the app transfers to the new owner without changing its value. Its full value isn't shown again. If a copy remains with the previous owner or in an integration, it continues to work on behalf of the new owner until the key expires, is revoked, or is reissued. This prevents interruptions to integrations, but doesn't block access for holders of previously issued copies. For a secure transfer, leave reissuing enabled.
If the app key can't be reissued — for example, if it's a system key or linked to a third-party app — this option doesn't appear.
6. Select the new owner — the list shows Bitrix24 employees who have already worked with Alaio Vibecode. 7. Click Transfer .
Accept an app. The new owner receives a message from the Alaio Vibecode bot and can accept the app. The app card shows the steps to complete the transfer. The steps depend on how the app is set up.
1–2. Go to Messenger and open the chat with the Alaio Vibecode bot. 3–4. Read the message, then click Open application below it.
The Alaio Vibecode website opens. Continue on the app card marked Transferred to you .

1. Click Open sources and download the current app snapshot. You'll need it if you have to redeploy the app. 2. Click Replace key and save the full key immediately in a secure location. You won't be able to view it again. Don't share the key in the chat with the agent. 3. If you need a separate API key for the agent, CI, or scripts, click Reissue keys . This step is optional. These keys don't replace the app key. 4. Update the key in the app's environment variables and redeploy the app before the date shown on the card, while the previous key is still valid. 5. Click Open in the verification block and make sure the app launches and connects to Bitrix24. 6. Once you've completed the setup, click Everything is ready, hide .
In brief
- A team can work on an app without sharing personal API keys — each team member uses their own key.
- Only the app owner or the Bitrix24 administrator can add or remove employees from the development team or transfer the app.
- The Developer and Administrator roles in the development team provide different technical permissions on the server, but neither role allows users to manage team membership or transfer the app.
- When removing an employee from the team, you can choose whether to revoke their permission to open the app.
- When publishing changes, the agent specifies the source code version it started from — this helps prevent accidental overwriting of colleagues' changes.
- Once the app transfer is confirmed, the previous owner can't undo it. The new owner completes the setup by following the instructions sent by the Alaio Vibecode bot.

titre: Use an AI agent to get data from the BI connector
sections: Use an AI agent to get data from the BI connector
Analyze Bitrix24 data with AI coding agents such as Codex or Claude Code. Describe your task, and the agent will retrieve data through the BI connector, apply filters, and prepare a response.

For example, if you want to analyze successful deals from the last six months, provide the agent with your Bitrix24 address, BI Analytics key, the documentation or a ready-made skill, and a task description. The agent will retrieve data through the BI connector, select successful deals, and present the results.
You don't need to configure request parameters manually. Describe your task, review the results, and refine your request if you need different data or a different response format.
In this article:
- Prepare to work with an AI agent
- Assign a task to an AI agent
- Refine a request
- Learn how an AI agent works with data
- Check the results
Prepare to work with an AI agent
You need the following:
Bitrix24 address. The AI agent uses this address to send requests to your Bitrix24 account. For example: https://example.bitrix24.com .
BI Analytics key. The key allows the AI agent to access Bitrix24 data. Get it in CRM > Analytics > Real time analytics > BI Analytics > BI Analytics settings > Manage keys .

Documentation or a skill. It helps the agent understand how to make requests to the BI connector. A ready-made skill explains how to list available datasets, view their fields, and retrieve rows through the BI connector. You can use the sample skill below: copy it and add it to your request.
Sample skill for the AI agent
name | bitrix-bi-connector

description | Querying the Bitrix24 BI-connector HTTP API — listing tables (gds.php?show_tables), describing columns (gds.php?desc), and fetching rows (pbi.php) with dateRange and dimensionsFilters predicate filtering (operators EQUALS, CONTAINS, IN_LIST, BETWEEN, IS_NULL, NUMERIC_GREATER_THAN/LESS_THAN with optional EXCLUDE negation). Use this skill whenever the user mentions Bitrix24, bi-connector, biconnector, bi-token, gds.php, pbi.php, or asks how to query, count, or filter leads (crm_lead), deals (crm_deal), tasks (task), contacts, companies, or smart-process entities (crm_dynamic_items_*) from a Bitrix24 portal via its BI-analytics endpoints. Also use when the user is constructing a dimensionsFilters JSON body, debugging EMPTY_SELECT_FIELDS_LIST errors, or seeing unexpected empty results from a Bitrix BI request (often a UTF-8 encoding issue or an unknown-operator silent-failure).
Bitrix24 BI-connector protocol

This skill captures the HTTP protocol for the Bitrix24 BI-analytics connector — the API that powers Power BI / Google Data Studio integrations and any custom client that reads CRM data from a Bitrix24 portal. Use it when constructing requests, helping users count/filter CRM entities, or implementing a BI client.
Endpoints overview

All three endpoints live on the client's Bitrix24 portal. Every request is HTTP POST and every body MUST include a key field — the client's bi-token. Only the path and query string vary: gds.php for metadata (list/describe), pbi.php for actual data rows.

Where the bi-token comes from: the BI-analytics key-management page of the client's own Bitrix24 portal (path varies by portal locale; on a fresh portal navigate via CRM → Analytics → BI-analytics → BI-analytics settings → Key management , or open {portal}/biconnector/key_list.php directly). Always ask the user for their own portal URL — never hardcode a reference portal (e.g. smith.bitrix24.com from sample docs) in production code.
Endpoint 1 — list tables
Exemple : POST {portal}/bitrix/tools/biconnector/gds.php?show_tables
Body:
Exemple : {"key": "<bi-token>"}
Returns [[table_name, table_description], ...] .
Endpoint 2 — describe a table's columns
Exemple : POST {portal}/bitrix/tools/biconnector/gds.php?desc&table=<table_name>
Body:
Exemple : {"key": "<bi-token>"}
Returns an array of column objects. Key fields per column:
- CONCEPT_TYPE — DIMENSION or METRIC . METRICs are typically aggregated and grouped by DIMENSIONs — preserve this distinction in any UI or query-builder code.
- ID — the identifier to use when referencing the column in subsequent requests (this is the name you pass in endpoint 3's fields ).
- NAME — human-readable label.
- TYPE — data type (e.g. NUMBER , STRING , YEAR_MONTH_DAY_SECOND ).
- AGGREGATION_TYPE , GROUP_KEY , GROUP_CONCAT , GROUP_COUNT , IS_VALUE_SPLITABLE — aggregation/grouping hints, often null .
Endpoint 3 — fetch table rows
Exemple : POST {portal}/bitrix/tools/biconnector/pbi.php?table=<table_name>
Body:
Exemple : {"key": "<bi-token>", "fields": [{"name": "<column_id>"}, ...]}

fields lists which columns to return; use the ID values from endpoint 2. Response is a 2D array where the first row is the header (column names in request order) and the rest are data rows aligned to that header. Empty cells come back as null or "" — don't treat absence as an error.
Silent-failure traps
The BI-connector has several behaviours where bad requests succeed with HTTP 200 but return misleading results. These cause real bugs because they look indistinguishable from "no data matched":

Unknown fields are silently dropped. If you request fields that don't exist on the table, the API silently drops them. If all requested fields are unknown, you get {"error":"EMPTY_SELECT_FIELDS_LIST"} with HTTP 200 — it does not name which field was wrong. Always cross-check field IDs against endpoint 2 before querying.

Unknown operators are silently ignored. Spelling an operator wrong, or guessing one that doesn't exist (e.g. IS_NOT_NULL , STARTS_WITH ), causes the server to return the unfiltered set — which looks like a successful query. Never assume an operator exists without testing it on a column with known distribution. Confirmed operators are listed below; treat everything else as unproven.

Request bodies must be UTF-8 encoded. If a filter value or URL parameter contains any non-ASCII character (in dimensionsFilters values , in a non-Latin table name, etc.), the body MUST be sent as UTF-8 bytes. A mismatched encoding does NOT produce an error — the API returns an empty result set ( Rows: 0 ), which is indistinguishable from a legitimate "no matches". PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod -Body $stringWithNonAscii is a known offender on Windows because its default body encoding is not UTF-8: pass [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($json) and Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 instead. In any language, set the HTTP client's body encoding to UTF-8 explicitly when sending non-ASCII filter values.
Date-range filtering
Add dateRange and optionally configParams.timeFilterColumn to the pbi.php body:

Exemple : { "key": "bi-token", "dateRange": {"startDate": "2018-07-19", "endDate": "2018-08-02"}, "configParams": {"timeFilterColumn": "DATE_CREATE"}, "fields": [{"name": "DATE_CREATE"}, {"name": "STATUS_SEMANTIC_ID"}] }
- startDate is treated as 00:00:00 of that day; endDate as 23:59:59.999 (inclusive).
- For a single day, set startDate = endDate .
- timeFilterColumn is the column ID to filter on. If omitted, the API uses the first date/datetime column in the table — usually safe but explicit is better.

Rule — always filter: always pass a dateRange when calling pbi.php , even if the user didn't ask. Without it, unfiltered tables can return thousands or millions of rows on real portals. Default to "last 3 months" ( endDate = today, startDate = today − 90 days) unless the user specifies otherwise. The metadata endpoints ( show_tables , desc ) don't accept dateRange — only pbi.php does. Exception: if you're using dimensionsFilters (below) and it sufficiently narrows the result (e.g. filtering by a specific ID), dateRange is optional.
Predicate filtering with dimensionsFilters

Add to the pbi.php body a key dimensionsFilters whose value is an array of arrays of condition objects. Outer arrays are joined by AND; inner conditions within one array are joined by OR. Any number of inner conditions and any number of outer groups is allowed.

Exemple : { "key": "bi-token", "fields": [{"name": "ID"}, {"name": "CREATED_BY_ID"}], "dimensionsFilters": [ [ {"fieldName": "ID", "values": ["2"], "type": "INCLUDE", "operator": "EQUALS"}, {"fieldName": "ID", "values": ["12706"], "type": "INCLUDE", "operator": "EQUALS"} ], [ {"fieldName": "CREATED_BY_ID", "values": ["1"], "type": "INCLUDE", "operator": "EQUALS"} ] ] }
Above: (ID=2 OR ID=12706) AND CREATED_BY_ID=1 .
Condition object fields
- fieldName — column ID from endpoint 2.
- values — always a list of strings, even for numeric columns (e.g. "1" , not 1 ).

- type — "INCLUDE" (apply the operator) or "EXCLUDE" (invert it). EXCLUDE works as a universal negator on top of any operator: EXCLUDE + EQUALS = "not equal", EXCLUDE + CONTAINS = "doesn't contain", EXCLUDE + IN_LIST = "not in list", EXCLUDE + IS_NULL = "not null" (the stand-in for the missing IS_NOT_NULL ).
- operator — confirmed values:
- "EQUALS" — exact match; values is a single-element list, e.g. ["1"] .
- "CONTAINS" — substring match, e.g. {"fieldName":"TITLE","values":["CRM:"],"operator":"CONTAINS"} .

- "IN_LIST" — field value is any of the listed strings, e.g. {"fieldName":"ID","values":["1","2"],"operator":"IN_LIST"} . Prefer this over OR-ing multiple EQUALS conditions for the same field — cleaner and one condition object instead of N.

- "IS_NULL" — null check; values MUST be an empty list ( [] ). For non-null, use EXCLUDE + IS_NULL (there is no standalone IS_NOT_NULL operator — the server silently ignores it and returns all rows unfiltered). Caveat: the desc metadata does NOT expose which fields are nullable, so there's no way to verify at runtime. Only use this when you already know from data inspection or domain context that the field can hold null.

- "BETWEEN" — value in range, both endpoints inclusive. values MUST be a 2-element list [low, high] (as strings, like all other operators). Behaviour on non-numeric columns is unspecified — treat it as numeric/date-only and test before applying to strings.

- "NUMERIC_GREATER_THAN" / "NUMERIC_GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL" / "NUMERIC_LESS_THAN" / "NUMERIC_LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL" — > , >= , < , <= . Single-element values , e.g. ["2"] . Behaviour on non-numeric columns is unspecified — use on numeric/date columns and verify before applying to strings.

- Anything else (e.g. STARTS_WITH , ENDS_WITH , REGEX ) is unproven. Per "Silent-failure traps" above, an unknown operator returns the full unfiltered table — which looks like a wide-open match. Test on a known-distribution column before relying on it.
Useful pattern — fetch a single row by ID
Exemple : "dimensionsFilters": [[{"fieldName":"ID","values":["19244"],"type":"INCLUDE","operator":"EQUALS"}]]
Success/failure semantics in CRM entities
Bitrix24 uses a one-letter "semantic" code to indicate where an entity sits in its lifecycle. Same codes, different field names across entities — easy to mix up:
- P — in progress (non-terminal)
- S — successful terminal state
- F — failed terminal state
Entity (BI table) | Lifecycle concept | Semantic field
crm_lead | Status | STATUS_SEMANTIC_ID (raw) / STATUS_SEMANTIC (label)
crm_deal | Stage | STAGE_SEMANTIC_ID (raw) / STAGE_SEMANTIC (label)

To count "successful" leads or deals, filter on the _SEMANTIC_ID field equal to S . To count "completed" (any terminal state), include both S and F . The text-label variants ( STATUS_SEMANTIC , STAGE_SEMANTIC ) come back as localized strings in the portal's UI language — use them for display, not for filtering. The single-letter _ID codes are stable across locales and should always be the key you filter on. Smart-process entities ( crm_dynamic_items_* ) likely follow the deal convention (stages) — verify via endpoint 2 before assuming.

Non-CRM entities like task may use a completely different schema (e.g. a raw STATUS column holding a localized human-readable string, with no semantic code at all). Always check endpoint 2 before generalizing — don't assume STATUS_SEMANTIC_ID exists outside the CRM tables documented above.
Credential handling

The bi-token is a credential. Treat it as you would any API key: never log it, never commit it to source control, never echo it back in error messages or stack traces. When building configuration scaffolding for an implementation, read the token from an environment variable or a gitignored config file — never a hardcoded constant in committed code.

Your task. Describe the result you need in business terms rather than technical instructions. For example: “Show successful deals for the last six months” or “Find leads from the last 30 days and group them by assigned employee.”
Assign a task to an AI agent

To assign a task, send a request to the AI agent in the chat. A complete request includes all the required details: your Bitrix24 address, BI Analytics key, the documentation or a skill, and the task description.
Example request:
Exemple : My Bitrix24: https://example.bitrix24.com My BI Analytics key: your_BI_Analytics_key. Show successful deals from the last six months.
Add the documentation or a ready-made skill to the request, for example, the sample skill from the previous section.

The agent then completes the task and returns a table of the selected data along with an analysis. The example shown is only one possible response format. The actual results depend on the data available in Bitrix24 and the fields accessible through the BI connector.
Refine a request
The first response may be too general. Refine the task directly in the chat: ask the agent to show only the metrics you need, group the data, or provide a short conclusion.
For example, use requests like these:
- Show the total amount of successful deals — “Show only the total amount of successful deals for the last six months and the number of deals.”
- Group deals — “Group successful deals by assigned employee. Show the number of deals and the total amount for each employee.”
- Break down deals by month — “Break successful deals down by month. Show the number of deals and the amount for each month.”
- Draw a conclusion from the data — “Give me a short conclusion: which month had the most successful deals, and which employee has the highest total deal amount?”
Refining your request helps you get the results you need. The AI agent not only retrieves data but also tailors the results to your business task.
Learn how an AI agent works with data

An AI agent works with the BI connector under the same rules as a regular application. It sends HTTP requests to Bitrix24 and receives responses in JSON format. The BI connector doesn't return all data in a single request. The process involves several steps:
1. First, the agent determines which data it can request through the BI connector. BI Builder: Datasets
Sample request to get a list of available data
Request address:
Exemple : POST https://example.bitrix24.com/bitrix/tools/biconnector/gds.php?show_tables
Request body:
Exemple : { "key": "your_BI_Analytics_key" }
Sample response:
Exemple : [ [ "crm_lead", "Leads" ], [ "crm_deal", "Deals" ], [ "task", "Tasks" ] ]
2. Next, the AI agent checks which fields are available in the required dataset. The response includes field descriptions: technical name, display name, data type, and additional parameters.
Sample request to retrieve field descriptions
Request address:
Exemple : POST https://example.bitrix24.com/bitrix/tools/biconnector/gds.php?desc&table=crm_lead
Request body:
Exemple : { "key": "your_BI_Analytics_key" }
Sample response:

Exemple : [ { "ID": "ID", "NAME": "Unique key", "TYPE": "NUMBER" }, { "ID": "TITLE", "NAME": "Lead Title", "TYPE": "STRING" }, { "ID": "DATE_CREATE", "NAME": "Created", "TYPE": "DATETIME" }, { "ID": "STATUS_ID", "NAME": "Status", "TYPE": "STRING" }, { "ID": "ASSIGNED_BY_ID", "NAME": "Responsible", "TYPE": "NUMBER" } ]
3. After the AI agent selects the required fields, it requests the data rows.
Sample request to get data
Request address:
Exemple : POST https://example.bitrix24.com/bitrix/tools/biconnector/pbi.php?table=crm_lead
Request body:
Exemple : { "key": "your_BI_Analytics_key", "fields": [ { "name": "ID" }, { "name": "TITLE" }, { "name": "DATE_CREATE" }, { "name": "STATUS_ID" }, { "name": "ASSIGNED_BY_ID" } ] }
Sample response:

Exemple : [ [ "ID", "TITLE", "DATE_CREATE", "STATUS_ID", "ASSIGNED_BY_ID" ], [ "125", "Consultation request", "2026-05-12 10:15:32", "NEW", "17" ], [ "126", "Equipment order", "2026-05-13 14:42:10", "IN_PROCESS", "21" ] ]
Check the results
An AI agent helps you retrieve and process data, but you still need to review the results. Check:
- Whether the correct time period was used.
- Whether the results include the relevant data.
- Whether the filters were applied correctly.
- Whether the results contain unnecessary fields.
- Whether the conclusions match the data in the table.

For example, if you requested successful deals for the last six months, make sure the results don't include deals that are still in progress or were lost. If you need only closed successful deals, specify this in your request.
In brief
- You can analyze Bitrix24 data with AI agents such as Codex or Claude Code.
- Describe your task, and the agent will use the BI connector to retrieve data, apply filters, and prepare a response.
- You need your Bitrix24 address, BI Analytics key, and the documentation or a ready-made skill.
- If the first response is too general, refine your request in the same chat: show only the metrics you need, group the data, or ask for a short conclusion.
- Check the results: the time period, filters, fields, and conclusions.
- Don't share the BI Analytics key publicly or store it in a public repository. It provides access to Bitrix24 data.

titre: Alaio Vibecode course
sections: Alaio Vibecode course

Alaio Vibecode is an app development platform and is part of the Bitrix24 ecosystem. It allows you to build apps by simply describing what you want to create: AI does the programming while Vibecode securely hosts and connects your solution to your Bitrix24.
In this article, you will find video tutorials that cover the basics of vibe coding and how you can use Alaio Vibecode to build apps for your Bitrix24.
- What is vibe coding?
- First vibe coding project
- Vibe coding security
- Building a real business tool
- Taking your app online

Lesson 1. What Is Vibe Coding?

Here, we introduce the concept of vibe coding for complete beginners and explain how AI makes it possible to create software, web pages, scripts, and business tools simply by describing what you want in everyday language.
Lesson 2. Your First Project

Using Claude for vibe coding, we show how a non-technical user can give AI simple instructions, turn raw Excel data into a visual dashboard, and even ask AI to generate useful insights from the results.

You don't need to be a cybersecurity expert to vibe code safely – but you do need to understand a few simple rules and know when to be cautious. In this lesson, we cover the basic security habits every beginner should know before building with AI.

We go deeper into the Alaio Vibecode platform and build three practical AI-powered tools connected to Bitrix24. Instead of starting from scratch, we use Vibecode's ready-made solutions and prompts to quickly create apps that work with real CRM and knowledge base data.

titre: Email address requirements for Bitrix24 employee invitations
sections: Email address requirements for Bitrix24 employee invitations

To make sure an employee receives the invitation and can sign in to your Bitrix24 on their first try, enter their email address in the correct format. First, check whether the employee already has a Bitrix24 account, as this determines how you should enter their email address.
If the employee already has a Bitrix24 account

Enter the email address associated with the employee's account — for example, ann.smith@gmail.com . Do not remove periods, hyphens, or other characters from the address, even for Gmail or Proton addresses. Bitrix24 may not find the employee's account if you change the address.
If you sent an invitation to the wrong email address, delete it and send a new one. FAQ: Log in to your Bitrix24 account
If the employee does not have a Bitrix24 account

When you invite an employee by email or register them yourself, remove characters that are not allowed in the email address. Bitrix24 does not support the + sign in email addresses when registering employees, and additional restrictions apply to Gmail and Proton addresses. Follow the rules below when entering the email address.

All email addresses — remove + and everything between it and @ . Many email services, including Gmail and Proton, use + to create email aliases. Emails sent to an alias arrive in the main inbox. For example, enter annsmith@gmail.com instead of annsmith+work@gmail.com . If + is part of the mailbox name, ask the employee for a different email address.

Gmail — remove all periods before @ . This rule applies to addresses on gmail.com and googlemail.com. Enter annsmith@gmail.com instead of ann.smith@gmail.com . Gmail ignores periods in email addresses, so messages sent to either address arrive in the same inbox. If the address contains both periods and a + sign, apply both rules: enter annsmith@gmail.com instead of ann.smith+work@gmail.com . Gmail help

Proton — remove periods, hyphens, and underscores before @ . This rule applies to addresses on proton.me, protonmail.com, pm.me, and protonmail.ch. Enter annsmith@proton.me instead of ann.smith@proton.me . Proton ignores these characters in email addresses, so messages sent to either address arrive in the same inbox. Proton help

Other email services and work email addresses — you can keep periods, hyphens, and underscores. You do not need to change addresses such as ann.smith@yahoo.com or ann.smith@company.com : Gmail and Proton restrictions do not apply to them.

Do not use disposable email addresses. Disposable email services provide temporary inboxes that expire after a short time. Bitrix24 may reject these addresses. Ask the employee for a personal or work email address they use regularly.

If you invite an employee to Bitrix24 using a link, they enter their own email address during registration. The same restrictions apply, so let the employee know about them in advance. Invite new users to Bitrix24 Join Bitrix24 via invitation link

titre: Vibecode bot
sections: Vibecode bot
The Vibecode bot is a system bot for the Alaio Vibecode platform. It sends important notifications to your Bitrix24 account.

The bot appears automatically the first time you open the Alaio Vibecode dashboard. Each Bitrix24 account can have one active bot. When the bot starts for the first time, it sends a welcome message to the employee who connected the platform. Other employees receive a welcome message when they first interact with the bot.
The Vibecode bot reports important platform events:
- Your trial period or paid access to Alaio Vibecode is about to expire. The bot sends reminders 7, 3, and 1 day before expiration.
- Your Vibe package is about to expire. The bot sends warnings 30 and 7 days before expiration.
- Your balance is insufficient. Server operation will be suspended and restored after you top up your account.
- A server goes offline, becomes unavailable, or requires recovery. The owner of the key connected to the server receives a notification.
- Access to a server, app, or key changes. For example, an employee receives access to a server, a management key changes, or an app is transferred.
- A bot created on the platform goes offline because of authentication errors. The owner of the bot's key receives a notification.
- A connected feature requires action. For example, you need to reconnect an integration, confirm an operation, or open a support inquiry.
The Vibecode bot does not:
- Read employee or customer conversations
- Send messages on behalf of employees or clients

Buttons in bot messages open the corresponding section in Alaio Vibecode. For example, To the Vibecode platform opens the Dashboard Dashboard — this is the main Alaio Vibecode page where you manage servers, bots, and billing. .

You can turn off some notifications, such as billing reminders, directly in the chat with the bot. Click one of the buttons: Snooze for 3 days or Snooze for a week . The bot stops sending these notifications for the selected period. The snooze resets after you top up your account.
Disable the Vibecode bot
The Vibecode bot is disabled automatically if you disconnect Bitrix24 from the Alaio Vibecode platform.
You can also delete the bot manually in Bitrix24.
1. Go to Applications > Developer resources . 2. Select Integrations . 3. Click Menu (≡) next to the Vibecode bot. 4. Select Delete .
Without the bot, you will not receive system notifications from the Alaio Vibecode platform. The next time you open the dashboard, the bot will be registered again.
Create a bot for your own task

The Vibecode bot sends only platform service messages. For your own tasks, create a Hermes AI agent. When you create an agent, the platform registers a separate bot in Bitrix24. Create the Hermes AI Agent in Alaio Vibecode
In brief
- The Vibecode bot is a system bot for the Alaio Vibecode platform.
- It appears automatically the first time you open the Alaio Vibecode dashboard. Each Bitrix24 account can have one active bot.
- The bot sends system notifications such as billing and server status updates.
- It does not read conversations, send employee messages, or send tokens.
- You can create your own bot with the Bots API and Managed Bots tools.
- If you delete the bot manually, it will register again the next time you open the Alaio Vibecode dashboard.

titre: Black Hole servers
sections: Black Hole servers
